title: ARCHITECTURE: fork-without-exec plus one shared uid leaves no isolation between executions
description:
FOUND by adversarial validation of genetics-results-suite-4h6.39 (the supervisor skeleton), 2026-08-17. EVERY CLAIM BELOW WAS DEMONSTRATED against the real supervisor forking real children, not argued. Probe scripts were left in the session scratchpad; reproduce before acting, they will not survive.

THIS IS A DESIGN DECISION, NOT A BUG FIX. Do not patch around it. Three separate isolation failures share ONE root cause, and the fix has to be chosen deliberately because each candidate costs something the epic currently depends on.

=== ROOT CAUSE: THE POD'S ISOLATION IS ONE UID AND ONE ADDRESS SPACE ===
Two decisions, each individually justified, combine into no isolation between executions:
- 4h6.7 FORCED one shared uid 65532 for supervisor and child. drop:[ALL] + allowPrivilegeEscalation:false leave no CAP_SETUID/SETGID/CHOWN; setuid(65533) and chown(65533) were MEASURED to return EPERM. Not revisitable at the pod level.
- 4h6.39 forks WITHOUT exec, deliberately - an exec throws away the prewarmed interpreter, which is the entire return on sandbox/prewarm.py.
Concurrency is 1, so the epic reasoned that cross-user exposure was bounded. IT IS NOT: the QUEUE holds up to two waiting requests, retention holds completed ones, and the child inherits everything.

=== FINDING 1 (the one that decides the design): A CHILD READS OTHER USERS' TOKENS, CODE AND SESSION IDS OUT OF INHERITED MEMORY ===
The fork copies the supervisor's entire address space. Nothing is cleared or scoped first. FOUR INDEPENDENT ROUTES, all demonstrated with one execution queued behind another:
1. module global: sys.modules[...].SUPERVISOR._waiting -> the QUEUED victim's full ExecuteRequest: their user, their session id, THEIR SOURCE CODE, and both raw JWTs (claims decoded and printed).
2. frame walk: sys._getframe() up to Supervisor._execute / run / _Handler._execute -> job.req.tokens in three frames, plus THE RAW REQUEST BODY BYTES still live in the handler frame.
3. gc.get_objects() filtered on ExecuteRequest -> live request objects with tokens.
4. RAW ADDRESS SPACE: scan /proc/self/mem via /proc/self/maps for the JWT pattern -> recovered subjects from a queued execution, a running one, AND AN EXECUTION THAT HAD ALREADY COMPLETED AND BEEN RELEASED.
ROUTE 4 IS WHY THIS CANNOT BE PATCHED. A sanity probe confirmed a string explicitly dropped and gc.collect()-ed BEFORE the fork is still recoverable in the child. Python strings are immutable and freed objects stay in arenas that COW hands over. So clearing references, __slots__, `del`, or any "overwrite the token" attempt CANNOT WORK. Only never letting token bytes into the forking process, or exec(), removes it.
CONSEQUENCE FOR 4h6.43: THE READ-ONCE TOKEN FILE BUYS NOTHING against the process it is protecting from. The child already holds its own token; the file's value was bounding exposure, and memory reading bypasses it. 4h6.43 should still be implemented - the child needs SOME way to receive the credential - but it MUST NOT be documented as an exposure bound until this bead is resolved.

=== FINDING 2: A CHILD READS AND OVERWRITES OTHER EXECUTIONS' ARTIFACTS ===
Same uid, one flat /scratch, and nothing is deleted until 4h6.46 lands. Demonstrated from inside a child: listed /scratch, found a previous user's execution directory, READ artifacts/private.csv, OVERWROTE it, and PLANTED a new file in that user's artifacts directory.
read_artifact's descriptor discipline (4h6.15) does not help - the inode is legitimately inside the other execution's artifacts/, so the retention window SERVES ATTACKER-CONTROLLED CONTENT UNDER ANOTHER USER'S EXECUTION ID. The docs acknowledge mkdir 0o700 protects nothing under one uid, but treat that as a TOKEN problem only. It is equally an ARTIFACT INTEGRITY problem.

=== FINDING 3: A RESIDENT DETACHED PROCESS DEFEATS THE TOKEN FILE AND SURVIVES EVERY GROUP KILL ===
Demonstrated: execution A forks a grandchild that setsid()s, dup2s /dev/null over 0/1/2 and CLOSES fd 3, then returns. A looks perfectly normal to chat-backend - status ok, 60 ms. The resident then polls /scratch, sees the NEXT execution's directory appear, and READS ITS mode-0600 TOKEN FILE INSIDE THE READ-ONCE WINDOW (victim wrote it and unlinked 400 ms later). Captured output shows the victim's bearer token.
Section 4 anticipates this shape for /proc/<pid>/environ and prescribes the file as the fix. The file is exactly as exposed, for the same reason: same uid plus a process nothing kills.
The same resident can also write into a LIVE execution's artifacts/ before build_manifest runs, injecting attacker-controlled files into another user's manifest.
AND IT DEFEATS THE REAPER 4h6.41 IS ABOUT TO BUILD: job.pgid = pid is ASSERTED, never read back with os.getpgid(pid), never re-validated before signalling. Measured: killpg(pgid, SIGTERM) and SIGKILL both returned ESRCH while the grandchild survived. Two hazards for 4h6.41 - any descendant calling setsid()/setpgid() leaves the group and is unreachable; and once waitpid reaps the child the pgid is STALE AND THE PID IS RECYCLABLE, so a later killpg can hit an unrelated group, plausibly THE NEXT EXECUTION'S CHILD.

=== THE THREE CANDIDATE FIXES, WITH WHAT EACH COSTS ===
(a) EXEC AFTER FORK. Removes finding 1 completely and nothing else. COST: throws away the prewarmed interpreter, which is the whole justification for sandbox/prewarm.py and a measurable part of the latency budget. Does NOT address findings 2 or 3.
(b) A FORK SERVER STARTED BEFORE ANY REQUEST IS PARSED, which never sees a token - it receives only (code, dirs) over a pipe and forks children from a pristine address space. Removes finding 1 while KEEPING prewarm, which is why it is the most attractive on paper. COST: a second long-lived process, a new IPC surface to get right, and the supervisor must hand the credential to the child by a route that does not pass through the forking process. Does NOT address findings 2 or 3.
(c) NAMESPACES: a PID namespace per execution (child as PID 1 of its own namespace) plus a mount namespace for /scratch. This is the ONLY mechanism found that kills finding 3 as a CLASS - a pgid-based reaper structurally cannot - and a mount namespace is the clean answer to finding 2. COST: needs to work under gVisor and inside the pod's dropped-capability set, WHICH IS UNVERIFIED AND IS THE FIRST THING TO ESTABLISH. If unprivileged user namespaces are unavailable there, this option collapses and (b) plus a weaker containment for 2 and 3 is what remains.
These are not exclusive. (b)+(c) is probably the real answer; (a) is the fallback if prewarm turns out to be worth less than it looks.

=== WHAT IS AND IS NOT BLOCKED ===
NOT BLOCKED: local single-user development and testing. Every finding here is CROSS-USER, and the local path (4h6.40 Docker, 4h6.49 end-to-end) is one developer running their own code against their own tokens. The user's stated order of operations is local first, and that stands.
BLOCKED: anything that puts this in front of more than one user. 4h6.50 (wiring the supervisor into the manifest, which clears deploy.sh's refusal) and 4h6.51 (deploy-window verification) both now depend on this bead.
ALSO WEIGH: the epic's whole premise is that co-tenancy inside the pod is removed by concurrency 1 plus replicas 1 plus strategy Recreate. Findings 1-3 show that premise is FALSE AS BUILT - the queue and the retention window are the co-tenancy. Section 2's reasoning needs revisiting whichever fix is chosen, not just the code.

FIRST STEP, before choosing: establish empirically whether an unprivileged PID namespace and mount namespace can be created inside the sandbox pod as it is configured - gVisor runtime class, drop:[ALL], allowPrivilegeEscalation:false, uid 65532. That single measurement decides whether (c) is on the table, and everything else follows from it. It is a LIVE-CLUSTER measurement and therefore sits behind the zg6 phase gate; it may be approximable under a local gVisor/runsc container as part of 4h6.40.
notes:
--- MEASUREMENT ADDED 2026-08-17 by genetics-results-suite-4h6.40, PENDING INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION. This changes option (c)'s analysis. ---
This bead said the FIRST STEP was to establish whether unprivileged PID and mount namespaces can be created inside the pod's constraint set, and that the answer decides whether option (c) is on the table. A local approximation now exists.

MEASURED FROM INSIDE A REAL EXECUTION IN THE ACTUAL IMAGE (CapEff: 0, NoNewPrivs: 1, Seccomp: 2): unshare(NEWNS), unshare(NEWPID), unshare(NEWUSER), the combination, and setuid(65533) ALL RETURN EPERM.

THE CONTROL EXPERIMENT IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. Same uid, same --cap-drop ALL, same no-new-privileges, ONLY seccomp=unconfined changed: unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER) SUCCEEDS, and nested inside it unshare(CLONE_NEWNS|CLONE_NEWPID) ALSO SUCCEEDS.
SO THE BLOCKER IS THE SECCOMP PROFILE, NOT THE CAPABILITY SET AND NOT no_new_privs. That distinction is easy to get backwards, because the profile's EPERM is INDISTINGUISHABLE from the capability check unless you vary the profile - which is why the naive reading ("capabilities are dropped, therefore namespaces are impossible, therefore option (c) is dead") is wrong.

WHAT IT COSTS, and why this does not simply unblock (c): relaxing the profile means a CUSTOM SECCOMP PROFILE, which docs/code-execution-security.md already lists under REJECTED CONTROLS because it needs a DaemonSet-distributed localhostProfile. That rejection was cheap when nothing depended on it; it is not cheap now. Re-opening it is a real decision with a real operational cost, and it must be weighed against options (a) and (b), which need no profile change at all.

CRITICAL CAVEAT: THIS SAYS NOTHING ABOUT gVISOR, which is what will actually run in the pod. runsc implements unshare in the SENTRY, not the host kernel, so its answer can differ in either direction, and runsc is not installed on the dev machine. The pod also uses containerd RuntimeDefault rather than Docker's default seccomp profile - a different profile, measured here only by proxy. THE REAL MEASUREMENT IS STILL OWED and is a live-cluster or local-runsc question.

REVISED READING OF THE OPTIONS:
(a) exec after fork - unchanged, still costs prewarm, still closes only finding 1.
(b) fork server that never sees a token - unchanged, still the cheapest complete answer to finding 1, still does nothing for 2 or 3.
(c) namespaces - NOT dead, but its price is now known to include re-opening a control the doc rejected on operational grounds. Do not treat "namespaces work" as free.
Nothing here changes the recommendation to weigh (b)+(c) together; it changes what (c) actually costs.

--- PARKED 2026-08-20 by the ralph-wiggum loop. NOT abandoned; it cannot be executed from this seat. ---
MEASURED THIS SESSION on the dev machine: `command -v runsc` -> not found; docker's registered runtimes are
runc and io.containerd.runc.v2 only. So the local-runsc approximation this bead's own notes offered as the
way to settle option (c) IS NOT AVAILABLE HERE. `unshare --user --map-root-user true` succeeds on the bare
host, which re-confirms the earlier finding that the blocker is the seccomp profile rather than the
capability set - and equally re-confirms that a bare-host result says nothing about gVisor. THE REAL
MEASUREMENT IS STILL OWED and is still a live-cluster question behind genetics-results-suite-zg6.

WHY PARKED RATHER THAN WORKED: choosing among (a), (b) and (c) is not a coding task. Option (c)'s price is
now known to include re-opening the custom seccomp profile that docs/code-execution-security.md lists under
REJECTED CONTROLS - a DaemonSet-distributed localhostProfile with a real operational cost. That is a
decision for whoever owns the deploy, and it must NOT be made by implementing whichever option is cheapest
to code.

WHAT WOULD UNPARK IT, in order of cost:
1. A user ruling on (a) / (b) / (c) / (b)+(c). Option (b) - a fork server started before any request is
   parsed - needs NO seccomp change and NO live measurement, and closes finding 1 completely. If the user
   picks (b) this bead becomes executable immediately, and findings 2 and 3 split out as separate work.
2. Otherwise the live-cluster (or local-runsc) namespace measurement, which zg6 gates.
Nothing in the epic's frontier depends on this bead except 4h6.50 and 4h6.51, which are already blocked on
it and are themselves deploy-window work.

--- USER RULING 2026-08-20: OPTION (b). Recorded by the ralph-wiggum loop. ---
The user selected option (b): a fork server started BEFORE any request is parsed, which never sees a
token and receives only (code, dirs) over a pipe, forking children from a pristine address space.
Rationale as stated when the options were put to them: (b) needs no seccomp profile change and no
live-cluster measurement, and closes finding 1 completely while KEEPING prewarm.

THIS BEAD IS NOW SCOPED TO FINDING 1 ONLY, via option (b). It is no longer the whole architecture
question.

WHAT (b) DOES NOT DO, and why that is now tracked elsewhere rather than dropped:
(b) closes finding 1 (a child reading other users' tokens, source code and session ids out of the
inherited address space). It does NOTHING for finding 2 (cross-execution artifact read/overwrite under
one uid on a flat /scratch) or finding 3 (a setsid() resident that reads the next execution's token file
and survives every process-group kill). Those two were split out so that scoping this bead to (b) does
not silently weaken the deploy gate:
  finding 2 -> genetics-results-suite-4h6.82
  finding 3 -> genetics-results-suite-4h6.83
4h6.50 and 4h6.51 were blocked on THIS bead because it carried all three findings. They are now blocked
on .82 and .83 as well, so "front of more than one user" still cannot ship until all three are answered.
Do not close .82/.83 by pointing at this bead's fix.

STILL TRUE AND STILL UNMEASURED: whether unprivileged PID/mount namespaces work under gVisor in the pod
(option (c)). runsc is not installed on the dev machine (measured 2026-08-20), so that stays a
live-cluster question behind genetics-results-suite-zg6. Option (c) remains the only mechanism found that
kills finding 3 as a CLASS; .81 should record that its own best answer may be (c), at the price the
notes above describe.
close_reason:
LANDED as option (b), per the user's ruling. genetics-results-suite 78cc9db.
SCOPED TO FINDING 1. Findings 2 and 3 are 4h6.82 and 4h6.83 and remain open; both gate 4h6.50/4h6.51.
Do not read this closure as closing them.

WHAT LANDED: a fork server forked in bring_up() after prewarm() and before ready, so it is a snapshot of a
supervisor that has never read a request. It gets one {"op":"fork"} plus four descriptors over
SOCK_SEQPACKET and reads none of them; code/env/cwd travel in an anonymous memfd THROUGH it to the child.
So it holds no user data at all - stronger than the bead's "(code, dirs) over a pipe", since the source
code finding 1 named never enters it either. Vocabulary is three ops, pinned by an AST check.
MEASURED by two independent validators: all four leak routes (module global, frame walk, gc.get_objects,
/proc/self/mem) return nothing for a RELEASED victim and a QUEUED victim. Prewarm is genuinely inherited
(numpy/scipy/polars/matplotlib in the child's sys.modules), not re-done. The child's credential route is
4h6.43's read-once token file, unchanged - which is exactly what makes it load-bearing now rather than
redundant: it is the supervisor->child route that does not pass through the forking process.

SECTION 2'S PREMISE CORRECTED as the bead required: concurrency 1 + replicas 1 + Recreate does NOT remove
in-pod co-tenancy. The queue and the retention window ARE the co-tenancy. Doc says so and names .82/.83.

CAUGHT IN REVIEW, NONE BY TESTS - the suite was green after implementation and after each fix round:
1. THE CONTROL SOCKET DESYNCHRONISED on any failed round trip and was not poisoned, so the next execution
   read the previous request's reply. Measured: a timed-out WAIT left {"ok":true} queued for the next
   REAP. The dangerous ordering was fork - the supervisor would take a stale {"pid": N} and apply limits
   to, watchdog, killpg and reap THE PREVIOUS USER'S CHILD while its own ran unwatched. Now poisoned
   inside the lock; every later call raises.
2. A ForkServerError out of _reap left the child running for the pod's lifetime with same-uid /scratch
   access while later users executed. The finally now kills the group.
3. A DEAD FORK SERVER WAS INVISIBLE: /health answered 200 ok forever while every /execute 500'd, and
   sandbox.yaml has readiness but deliberately no liveness - a permanently Ready black hole. health() now
   reports forkserver-down via a LOCK-FREE alive() (the first attempt took a lock wait_nowait holds for
   the child's whole lifetime, which blocked every health check during an execution). NO in-process
   restart, deliberately: re-forking from a supervisor that has served requests reopens finding 1.
4. A PRE-READY POST /execute was fully parsed before the readiness check, so tokens/code/session reached
   the arenas the fork server snapshots - MEASURED recoverable, with a post-fork negative needle correctly
   absent. _execute now refuses 503 NotReady before _read_body.
5. THREE OF THE FOUR LEAK SEARCHES HAD NO POSITIVE CONTROL. Found by sabotage: killing scan_refs left the
   suite GREEN because `found = found | in_mem`. Now asserted separately; re-verified by sabotage.
6. A LOST FORK REPLY STRANDED A CHILD the supervisor could not name - a REGRESSION THIS CHANGE INTRODUCED
   (the supervisor used to fork directly and always knew the pid). The fork server now tracks pids it
   forked and was never asked to reap, and kills those groups before exiting.
7. Six descriptors leaked when _payload_fd raised - the same leak this change set out to remove, moved
   five lines up. ECHILD was reported as "waitid unsupported", sending _reap into a poll loop under
   kill_lock.

KNOWN RESIDUAL, FILED AS 4h6.87 AND GATING 4h6.50: rbufsize = -1 means BaseHTTPRequestHandler's header
parse does an 8 KiB buffered recv BEFORE _execute is entered, so a body sharing a TCP segment with its
headers (any body under ~8 KiB; http.client concatenates) is in the heap before the readiness check. No
Python object is built and the reference routes stay clean, but the raw bytes were recovered at full
fidelity when the fork landed promptly. A/B: one segment -> token/source/session recovered; separate
segments -> nothing. The realistic-window null result is ARENA REUSE, not exclusion. Every claim in the
tree - two supervisor.py comments, code-execution-security.md, project-spec.md - was corrected to state
the enforced property (no Python object holding a token/body/source is constructed before the fork)
rather than an absolute.

TWO FIX ROUNDS WERE USED, which is the cap; 4h6.87 exists because a third was not started.

TESTS: scripts/test-supervisor.py 252 -> 289 checks, 2 skipped. The skips are the freed-arena control and
are report-only - the leak assertion is independent and unconditional - but note that control skipped in
100% of observed runs, so the "reference-clearing cannot work" evidence rests on the bead's original
measurement, not on this suite. Every new check has a verified negative control.
NOT RUN, preconditions absent: test-sandbox-docs.py (no staged SDK), test-network-policies.py (no
cluster), test-e2e-local.py (no dev stack), build-checks.py (no built image).

title: Write the sandbox threat model and security design doc (GATE)
description:
Nothing else in the sandbox track may start until this is written and reviewed. The user explicitly asked for code execution to be carefully examined security-wise.

Must cover, concretely:
- Why in-process execution is unacceptable: chat-backend runs as ROOT (suite docs/project-spec.md:362 - it raises ulimit and owns root-owned chat-data PVC files), and ENABLE_SCRIPT_EXECUTION is false in production today. sandbox_tools.py:21 _ALLOWED_ENV_KEYS is an allow-list precisely because a deny-list previously leaked INTERNAL_API_SECRET.
- Isolation boundary: separate pod, non-root, read-only rootfs, drop ALL capabilities, RuntimeDefault or stricter seccomp, no shell, gVisor/sandboxed-node evaluation, memory/CPU/pid limits, wall-clock timeout, output size caps.
- Egress: deny by default. The sandbox reaches db-api and results-api ONLY, never the internet, never the chat-data PVC, never the Keycloak/postgres services.
- Credentials: the sandbox must NOT hold INTERNAL_API_SECRET. Design a short-lived per-request scoped token. Note the precedent problem at suite docs/project-spec.md:237 - mcp-server sits on both sides of the db-api NetworkPolicy, so a NetworkPolicy alone is not a boundary.
- MCP exposure: per explicit user requirement, code execution must NOT be reachable via /mcp. Enumerate every layer enforcing this (tool registration, NetworkPolicy, and a test).
- Abuse cases: crypto mining, data exfiltration via db-api, resource exhaustion starving chat-backend on a shared node, prompt-injected scripts from user-supplied attachments or tool results.

Deliverable: docs/code-execution-security.md in genetics-results-suite, plus a new documentation-ownership row in CLAUDE.md.
close_reason:
Design of record written: docs/code-execution-security.md (892 lines), plus a CLAUDE.md documentation-ownership row and the docs/ tree entry in project-spec.md. Committed 6f7f520.

Two reviewers (codebase-accuracy + adversarial security), two fix rounds. Round 1's fixes introduced two new breaks which round 2 closed; stopped at two rounds per policy rather than a third.

WHAT REVIEW CAUGHT THAT NOTHING ELSE WOULD HAVE:
- The central isolation claim was unsound. Dedicated KSA with no Workload Identity binding only holds under GKE_METADATA node mode; a pool built from the first spec would default to GCE_METADATA + the Compute default SA, exposing the raw metadata server. GKE_METADATA needs cluster-level WI, which gke.tf gates on manage_iam, so it fails at APPLY not plan - and the cheap escape re-introduces the hole.
- results-api accepts a forged X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email from any namespace pod (from-less ingress rule + header fallback). Filed as genetics-results-suite-fad; .8/.9 blocked on it.
- Routing JWTs by dot-count would have 401'd every Google Identity Token. Now discriminates on the JOSE alg header.
- Pod-level /tmp emptyDir was a sequential cross-conversation channel; concurrency 1 bounds concurrent leakage, not sequential.
- read_artifact reusing SUBAGENT_ALLOWED_PATHS (=/data) would have handed the model a read primitive over chat_history.db and llm_config.db.
- The db-api ingress policy admits only chat-backend and mcp-server, so the sandbox egress allow-list alone left the primary data path dead. Both reviewers found this independently.
- The TOOL_PROFILE argument for MCP exclusion was backwards: mcp-server passes no profile, tool_profile=None means NO filtering, so _mcp_disabled membership is the sole registration-layer control.

DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS FROM THE TICKET:
- DNS eliminated (hostAliases as v1 default) rather than allowed with tunnelling booked as residual. Rationale: ~200 KB/s sustained exfiltration falsified two load-bearing controls. Reversible - the doc carries an explicit revert clause. USER HAS NOT RULED ON THIS.
- gVisor on a separate pinned 1-node pool. USER HAS NOT RULED ON THIS EITHER; it is a permanent extra node.

LEFT UNDONE: wording/stale-count/citation drift batched as genetics-results-suite-5r2. The doc's node-pool sizing assumes a pinning that is not actually in effect - genetics-results-suite-262 blocks .10.

CAVEAT FOR IMPLEMENTERS: 892 lines of design that has never met an implementation. Expect .6/.7 to find over-specification; prefer amending the doc over silently diverging.

title: read_artifact is authorized by client-supplied session_id alone, so one user can read another's artifacts
description:
FOUND by the probe for genetics-results-suite-r0v, which asked a narrower question (is a client-minted session id safe?). This is a DIFFERENT and pre-existing defect that the probe turned up on the way. r0v does NOT cause it and is not blocked by it.

THE DEFECT. genetics-mcp-server tools/executor.py _ArtifactManifests (~408-414, map at ~466) is keyed on `sid` ALONE. Its own docstring calls itself 'THE AUTHORIZATION STATE for read_artifact (genetics-results-suite-4h6.52)' and says 'A name recorded under another sid is not merely refused, it is invisible'. record() (~468) and resolve() (~487) take only session_id; THERE IS NO `sub`/user TERM IN THE KEY.

AND session_id IS FULLY CLIENT-SUPPLIED AND UNVALIDATED. It arrives in the /v1/chat body (chat_api.py:320), is passed straight through (chat_api.py:615), and becomes the token's `sid` claim verbatim (sandbox_token.py:101-110). executor.py:6087 states it flatly: 'session_id is client-supplied'. No code in chat_api.py checks it against the authenticated user or against the sessions table. The MODEL cannot inject it - llm_service.py:1650-1656 strips and overwrites any model-emitted session_id - but THE CLIENT SETS IT DIRECTLY, and that is the whole attack.

THE SUPERVISOR WILL NOT SAVE YOU, deliberately. sandbox/supervisor.py:3514-3518: 'There is no per-session check here, and there is not meant to be one: the sid-scoped resolution genetics-results-suite-4h6.52 specifies belongs in chat-backend, the only side that knows which session owns which execution.' So chat-backend is the ONLY place this can be enforced, and it is not enforcing it.

THE ATTACK, all conditions required:
1. User B puts user A's session_id in B's own /v1/chat request body.
2. B prompts their model to call read_artifact("<name>").
3. resolve(A_sid, name) returns A's execution_id; the fetch goes to the supervisor by that id.
4. B receives A's bytes.
Preconditions: B must LEARN A's session id; A must have run run_analysis in the last ARTIFACT_RETENTION_S = 300 s (executor.py:405); B must know or guess an artifact filename. chat-backend is replicas: 1, so 'same pod' is automatic rather than a limiting factor.

WHAT PROTECTS THE REST, and why this is specifically about artifacts: `sub` IS server-derived - get_authenticated_user (auth/core.py:210-235) honours the proxy identity header ONLY from a caller presenting the internal secret, and run_analysis has the additional gateway_asserted gate (executor.py:6079-6095). `jti` is a server-minted uuid4. Budgets and rate limits are keyed on jti, not sid (results-api app/core/sandbox_budget.py:209, db-api _jti_bytes). So a chosen sid cannot forge identity, cannot spend another execution's budget, and cannot address anything outside the artifact manifest. THE ARTIFACT MANIFEST IS THE ENTIRE EXPOSURE - and it is enough.

NOT EXPLOITABLE TODAY, AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY THIS IS P1 RATHER THAN ICED. SANDBOX_ENABLED is "false" on every manifest, so run_analysis is not in the resolved tool list and no artifact is ever recorded. THIS GOES LIVE THE MOMENT SANDBOX_ENABLED IS FLIPPED, which is the deploy genetics-results-suite-4h6 exists to make. Shipping the epic without fixing this ships a cross-user read.

THE FIX, most likely: key the manifest on (sub, sid) rather than sid, so a stolen or guessed session id resolves to nothing for a different user. That is a small change to _ArtifactManifests.record/resolve plus their call sites, and read_artifact already has `user` in scope on the same path that mints `sub`. CHECK BEFORE ASSUMING: whether fetch_artifact/_fetch_analysis_images share the same resolution path, and whether the supervisor's fetch-by-execution-id needs a matching term (per its own comment above it deliberately does not - so the whole fix should stay in chat-backend).

TWO THINGS TO SETTLE THAT AFFECT SEVERITY, neither established here:
1. HOW GUESSABLE IS A PERSISTED SESSION ID? Secret chats mint crypto.randomUUID (browser ChatPage.tsx:307), which is infeasible to guess. If PERSISTED session ids are sequential or otherwise low-entropy, the precondition 'B must learn A's session id' collapses and severity rises sharply. Check what the sessions table uses as its id.
2. DOES THE CHAT-HISTORY API HAVE THE SAME PATTERN? The probe explicitly did NOT audit chatHistoryApi (browser src/features/chat/chatHistoryApi.*) and its backend route. It is not on the sid/token path, but if it also trusts a client-supplied session id on save/load it is a second instance of the same defect and should be fixed alongside.

RELATED: genetics-results-suite-4h6.91 already cut RETENTION_S 900 -> 300 to shrink the 'same-uid artifact exposure window', so the exposure of artifacts has been thought about before - but that bead reduced a WINDOW, it did not add an OWNER to the key.
close_reason:
LANDED. genetics-mcp-server 4dcfbb5, genetics-results-suite b19e777. One fix round.

THE FIX: _ArtifactManifests is keyed on (sub, sid) instead of sid alone, and BOTH halves fail closed -
_is_identity requires a non-empty str, so a missing, empty OR MALFORMED identity stores nothing and
resolves to nothing. There is no session-only fallback anywhere. The malformed case matters more than it
looks: a non-str identity previously raised TypeError out of the tuple lookup, which is a DIFFERENT
RESPONSE SHAPE from ArtifactNotFound and therefore an oracle, even though get_authenticated_user can only
return str|None today.

NON-DISCLOSURE WAS TREATED AS PART OF THE FIX, NOT A NICETY. A cross-user denial is byte-identical to a
name that never existed - same error text modulo the caller's own name, same error_type, same key set,
same retryable - and nothing is sent downstream in either case. Blind validation compared them under
json.dumps(sort_keys=True) and confirmed identity, and confirmed no log line, exception type or manifest
side effect distinguishes them either.

*** THE FIRST CUT WAS INCOMPLETE, AND THIS IS THE PART TO CARRY FORWARD. *** Keying on `user` is worth
nothing while `user` is forgeable, and on the READ path it was. run_analysis has refused a
non-gateway-asserted identity since 4h6.84 - a holder of INTERNAL_API_SECRET can send
X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email and be "indistinguishable from a browser session", and mcp-server holds
that secret and is admitted to chat-backend:8000. read_artifact had NO SUCH GATE.
MEASURED, with the victim's key planted:
    run_analysis  gw=False -> success=False
    read_artifact gw=False -> success=True   content="VICTIM-SECRET"
THE WRITE PATH WAS GATED AND THE READ PATH WAS NOT. Both validators found this INDEPENDENTLY, which is
the strongest signal either of them produced. read_artifact now carries the identical condition, placed
ABOVE the name check so the refusal cannot vary with whether the name exists.
NOBODY LOSES ACCESS, and the argument is structural rather than empirical: the ONLY writer of the manifest
is _record_artifact_manifest, called from exactly one site - run_analysis, AFTER its own gate. So the set
of (sub, sid) keys that can ever hold a row is a SUBSET of callers who already satisfied this gate. Any
caller the new gate refuses could never have produced a row to read.

TWO SMALLER THINGS THE SAME ROUND CLOSED:
- The display/log strip that keeps a model-emitted `user` out of the operator log and the client-visible
  tool disclosure covered run_analysis ONLY, so read_artifact could put a forged identity into a log join -
  the exact hazard that branch's own comment names. Execution was never affected; this is log integrity.
- session_id, now half a security key, had NO max_length while message_id directly below it was capped at
  64 with a comment that the service has no request-body-size middleware. Bounded to 64: every producer
  emits a uuid4 at 36 chars (str(uuid.uuid4()) for persisted, crypto.randomUUID for secret chats, no third
  producer found), so 64 cannot truncate a real id and matches its neighbour rather than inventing a
  second number.

A DOC SENTENCE THIS BEAD ITSELF WROTE HAD TO BE CORRECTED, which is worth stating plainly: the first cut
added "`sub` is the half that cannot be chosen", justified by a gate read_artifact did not have. Five
OTHER cross-references still claimed sid-alone authorization after the read_artifact subsection had been
rewritten - including the 4h6.15 as-built summary row, which is precisely what a reader checking the
boundary would find. All swept.

BOTH OPEN QUESTIONS ANSWERED, both reassuring:
A. PERSISTED SESSION IDS ARE NOT GUESSABLE. db/chat_history_db.py create_session uses str(uuid.uuid4())
   behind Depends(auth_required) - 122 random bits, nothing sequential, no timestamp component. So "B must
   learn A's session id" remains a real precondition requiring disclosure, not enumeration. Severity is as
   the bead assumed, not higher.
B. THE CHAT-HISTORY API IS NOT A SECOND INSTANCE - do not file one. Every /chat/sessions/{id} route
   authorizes the path id in the SQL predicate (WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?), with 404 on miss and an
   explicit 403 for a non-owner on share. get_messages has no user term but is only ever reached after
   get_session_for_access succeeds. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE LESSON: chat-history ids ride in the PATH of
   routes that check ownership, while session_id rode in the /v1/chat BODY, where nothing did.

TESTS: 2006 -> 2029 passed, 74 deselected (+23 across both rounds); test_code_execution_tools.py 140.
NOT MERELY ADDED - the cross-user tests were confirmed to catch the defect by reverting the key to
session-only under a throwaway shim: 7 OF THE 8 original new tests die, and the single survivor is the
same-user positive control, which MUST survive. An earlier, narrower shim reported 6/4; the stricter shim
is the honest number and says the tests are stronger than first measured.

RECORDED, NOT FIXED (4h6.98 items 100-103): the LRU is refreshed by writes but not reads, so a manifest
being actively read can be evicted by another tenant's writes - availability only, matches the docstring's
own "LRU by last write" framing, throughput-bounded by real sandbox runs; record() caps rows but not names
per row; the _MAX_SESSIONS bounds prose still says "sessions" where it now means (sub, sid) keys; and
db.get_messages' missing user term is safe by call-site discipline only.
NOT MINE: /scratch is enumerable at the shared uid 65532 during retention, so another user's UNSEALED
artifacts are readable off disk regardless of this key. That is genetics-results-suite-4h6.88 and is open.
This bead closes the read_artifact authorization hole; it does not close 4h6.88.

title: The staging host is staging.genegenie (a subdomain of production), not staging-genegenie; five doc sites are wrong and the cookie relationship changed
description:
CONFIRMED BY THE USER 2026-08-22. The staging host they actually created is
`staging.genegenie.broadinstitute.org` (a DOT). The repo says `staging-genegenie.broadinstitute.org`
(a HYPHEN) in five places and the dotted form appears NOWHERE. The real value lives in an uncommitted
per-environment tfvars (`domains`, terraform/variables.tf:33) on the admin machine, so the repo cannot
self-correct and a reader following docs/environments.md today would configure the wrong hostname.

THE FIVE SITES, all docs/environments.md: line 10 (the DEPLOY_ENV table's primary host), 107 and 111 (the
DNS A record step and its `dig +short` verification), 118 (the Keycloak Google IdP endpoint URL), 172 (the
final sign-in step). Re-derive by grep rather than trusting this list.

WHY IT IS NOT A TYPO FIX - THE TWO FORMS HAVE DIFFERENT SECURITY PROPERTIES:
`daly` production is `genegenie.broadinstitute.org` (docs/environments.md:10). So
  - the HYPHENATED form is a SIBLING of production: a separate registrable host, no cookie
    relationship, no way for one to set cookies the other will send.
  - the DOTTED form is a SUBDOMAIN OF PRODUCTION. A subdomain can set a cookie with
    `Domain=genegenie.broadinstitute.org`, and PRODUCTION WILL THEN SEND IT. That is a real
    cross-environment channel from the less-trusted environment to the more-trusted one, and it did not
    exist under the name the repo was written for.
MEASURED 2026-08-22: no `--cookie-domain` / `cookie_domain` / `COOKIE_DOMAIN` setting exists anywhere in
k8s/, terraform/ or scripts/, so oauth2-proxy's cookies are host-only by default and staging and
production do NOT share a session today. THAT IS A DEFAULT, NOT A CONTROL - nothing asserts it, and
setting a cookie domain later, on either side, would silently create the channel.

REQUIRED:
1. Correct the five doc sites to the dotted host. Re-derive the list; do not trust the five above.
2. State the subdomain relationship explicitly in docs/environments.md, next to the isolation discussion
   at :60-98 which already enumerates what daly and daly-staging share (project, and therefore every
   project-scoped resource, disambiguated by resource_suffix). Cookie scope now belongs in that list.
3. Add a line to the "Bringing up daly-staging" checklist to verify the managed certificate's SAN matches
   the dotted host, since the cert is issued for whatever `domains` says and a mismatch produces a login
   loop rather than an obvious error.
4. Check whether `__Host-` prefixed cookies (which forbid a Domain attribute and so cannot cross) are
   available on the oauth2-proxy / Keycloak versions in use. If they are cheap to adopt, say so; do not
   adopt them here - that is a separate decision.

DO NOT change any tfvars or apply anything: genetics-results-suite-zg6 forbids live-cluster action, and
the tfvars are not in this repo anyway. This is documentation and one checklist item.

BLOCKS the staging bring-up, which the user has stated is where this epic deploys FIRST - so it blocks
genetics-results-suite-4h6.50 in practice.
close_reason:
LANDED. genetics-results-suite a48b6f4. Docs-only, one file, one fix round.

THE HOSTNAME: all 5 sites corrected to `staging.genegenie.broadinstitute.org`. The site list was
RE-DERIVED BY GREP over the whole tracked tree rather than taken from this bead's line numbers - there was
no sixth site, and no .sh/.tf/.tfbackend/.yaml file contained the hostname at all. The real value lives in
the gitignored per-environment tfvars (`domains`), so the operator's machine is authoritative and
docs/environments.md was the only copy in the repo. Verified afterwards: zero `staging-genegenie`
occurrences remain except one deliberate historical reference inside the new cookie bullet.

MY OWN ANALYSIS OF THE COOKIE RELATIONSHIP WAS WRONG AND REVIEW CORRECTED IT. Carry the corrected version:
I told the user, and the first draft of the doc said, that a genuinely separate hostname "could never" send
a cookie to production. FALSE. `broadinstitute.org` IS NOT A PUBLIC SUFFIX, so the old hyphenated
`staging-genegenie.broadinstitute.org` could have set `Domain=broadinstitute.org` and production would have
sent it. THE RENAME DID NOT CREATE THE CHANNEL. What it narrowed is the VALUE needed to open it: under the
hyphen, `Domain=broadinstitute.org` - which also leaks to every other Broad host and reads as obviously
over-broad in review; under the dot, `Domain=genegenie.broadinstitute.org` - literally the correct value
for the production deployment, so a tfvars or manifest copied from prod produces it verbatim and SURVIVES
REVIEW. Smaller delta than I claimed, and the one that is actually true.

REVIEW'S SECOND FINDING, which is the one worth remembering methodologically: THE BULLET REASONED ABOUT
ONE COOKIE-SETTER WHEN THERE ARE TWO, AND HAD CHECKED THE SAFER ONE. The negative grep for
--cookie-domain/cookie_domain/COOKIE_DOMAIN was TRUE and INSUFFICIENT.
- oauth2-proxy (k8s/deployments/oauth2-proxy.yaml): --cookie-secure, --cookie-httponly,
  --cookie-samesite=lax, no --cookie-domain.
- KEYCLOAK IS ON THE SAME HOST under /auth - scripts/deploy.sh:176 builds KEYCLOAK_HOST from DOMAIN +
  KEYCLOAK_PATH - k8s/deployments/keycloak.yaml sets NO cookie attributes at all, and scripts/deploy.sh:188
  ALREADY REWRITES those cookies: `proxy_cookie_flags ~ secure samesite=none`, deliberately, for the Apple
  form_post callback. So AUTH_SESSION_ID / KEYCLOAK_IDENTITY / KEYCLOAK_SESSION / KC_RESTART are the
  SameSite=None half - the fully cross-site-usable half if a Domain is ever introduced - and they are the
  half the first draft did not mention.
The doc now names both setters and BOTH ways the channel could be opened: an oauth2-proxy cookie-domain
setting, and nginx's `proxy_cookie_domain` - the sibling directive to the proxy_cookie_flags ALREADY IN
USE, living inside a shell printf in deploy.sh and therefore the site least likely to be found by anyone
grepping manifests for `--cookie-domain`.
The claim is written as "no component sets an explicit cookie Domain, so cookies are host-only" - A
DEFAULT, NOT A CONTROL - rather than "staging and production do not share a session", which is a property
of the deployments the measurement does not establish.

REVIEW'S THIRD FINDING: MY CERTIFICATE-SAN ITEM CONTRADICTED LINE 118 OF THE FILE IT WAS ADDED TO. I wrote
that a stale `domains` value "still reaches Active - just for the wrong host". The DNS step 60 lines
earlier already says a Google-managed cert cannot provision until the record resolves and one that starts
FAILED_NOT_VISIBLE needs a delete/recreate. Follow the checklist as written - A record for the DOTTED host,
stale hyphenated `domains` - and the cert does not provision AT ALL. It reaches Active for the wrong name
only if the stale host ALSO resolves to that IP, which nothing checks and the checklist never asks for.
Now stated that way, plus the consequence that IS unconditional: domains[0] also drives KC_HOSTNAME and the
ingress host rules (terraform/outputs.tf:34), so a mismatch surfaces as a redirect/login loop either way.
The item also separates `kubectl describe managedcertificate`, which merely ECHOES the spec.domains
generated from the same tfvars value being validated, from the openssl branch, which is the only one that
reads an ISSUED SAN.

DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED: the reserved global IP object name `staging-finngenie-broadinstitute-org-ip`.
terraform/main.tf:72 REFERENCES that address by var.static_ip_name and does not derive it from the
hostname, so matching it to the new host would break the lookup. Do not "fix" it.

ITEM 4 OF THIS BEAD (report on __Host- cookie availability, do not adopt) WAS ANSWERED AND THE ANSWER IS
RECORDED ON genetics-results-suite-4h6.50, not here, because that is the deploy bead somebody will read.
Short version: oauth2-proxy v7.14.3 already meets all three preconditions (Secure, Path=/, no Domain) so
adopting the prefix there is a one-value --cookie-name change and would convert this cookie-domain hazard
from "nothing checks it" into "the browser refuses it"; Keycloak 26.5 names its session cookies internally
with no supported rename, so prefixing those needs a custom SPI or a Set-Cookie rewrite that would also
have to change Path and risks the Apple callback. Recommendation recorded: do oauth2-proxy only.

ALSO PRODUCED BY THIS CYCLE, recorded not filed as frontier work: genetics-results-suite-4h6.94 (iced) -
three keycloak-*.sh scripts hardcode the PRODUCTION issuer/audience as their default, which stamps
production values into a STAGING realm during bring-up. Also summarised on 4h6.50, which is where the
person doing the bring-up will actually be looking.

title: docs/code-execution-security.md claims RuntimeDefault blocks ptrace; measured, it does not, and 4h6.82's integrity property depends on what actually does
description:
FOUND 2026-08-20 by the feasibility probe for genetics-results-suite-4h6.88 (encrypting retained
artifacts), while establishing whether a same-uid child can steal a key out of supervisor memory. It is not
about encryption - it is a FALSE SECURITY CLAIM about a control that ALREADY-SHIPPED work depends on.

THE FALSE CLAIM, docs/code-execution-security.md:509:
    "RuntimeDefault already blocks the escape-relevant set (add_key, keyctl, bpf, mount,
     PTRACE BEYOND SELF, namespace clone flags)"
MEASURED in the shipped image under docker's default seccomp profile (~= RuntimeDefault), by attaching to
one's OWN DESCENDANT - a case Yama permits and seccomp would not:
    ptrace ATTACH on own descendant rc=0 errno=0(Success)
So ptrace is ALLOWED by the profile. seccomp is not what stops a same-uid child attaching to the
supervisor. (MEASURED under docker's default profile; INFERENCE that containerd's RuntimeDefault matches -
both have allowed ptrace unconditionally since the same upstream change. Worth confirming.)

WHAT ACTUALLY PROVIDES THE PROTECTION - Yama, alone. MEASURED, same image, uid 65532, child forked from a
parent holding a canary:
    environ_read=531 bytes                     <-- READABLE (PTRACE_MODE_READ, Yama does not restrict)
    mem_open=ERR PermissionError(13)           <-- /proc/<pid>/mem needs PTRACE_MODE_ATTACH
    ptrace_attach rc=-1 errno=1(EPERM)
    process_vm_readv n=-1 errno=1
    yama_ptrace_scope=1
Yama scope 1 refuses ATTACH because the supervisor is the child's ANCESTOR, not its descendant.
Sibling-to-sibling (a resident from execution A against execution B's child) fails for the same reason.
NOTE the doc is RIGHT that the child can read the supervisor's /proc/<pid>/environ - that is
PTRACE_MODE_READ and is a different gate. The two must not be conflated in the correction.

WHY THIS IS BLOCKING RATHER THAN A WORDING NIT, and it is the second-order consequence that matters:
4h6.82's ARTIFACT INTEGRITY PROPERTY RESTS ON THIS. supervisor.py:900-903 (build_manifest) says the digest
map "is kept in the SUPERVISOR'S MEMORY - never on the filesystem, because the whole failure it answers is
that /scratch is writable by the process being defended against." A child holding PTRACE_ATTACH forges the
digest map and 4h6.82 evaporates. So the doc currently attributes that protection to seccomp, which does
not provide it, instead of to Yama, which does - and Yama's behaviour is UNVERIFIED UNDER gVISOR
(genetics-results-suite-4h6.51; runsc is not installed on the dev machine, measured 2026-08-20).
A reader following this doc would conclude 4h6.82's foundation is enforced by the seccomp profile and is
therefore as solid as the rest of that list. It is not; it is one unmeasured gVisor fact.

THE EPIC HAS SHIPPED A MEASURABLY FALSE SECURITY ABSOLUTE TWICE ALREADY (4h6.55's pre-fork claim, and
4h6.83's "nothing an execution leaves behind outlives it"). The standing rule that came out of those is
that a doc which OVERCLAIMS a security property is blocking, not a wording nit. This is that.

REQUIRED:
1. Correct :509 - remove "ptrace beyond self" from the RuntimeDefault list, or mark it explicitly as NOT
   provided by the profile. Re-derive the rest of that list rather than trusting it; if one entry was
   wrong, check the others (add_key, keyctl, bpf, mount, namespace clone flags) rather than assuming.
2. State what DOES enforce it: yama/ptrace_scope=1, MEASURED under runc, UNVERIFIED under gVisor, and say
   which 4h6.82 property depends on it.
3. Preserve the correct existing claim that /proc/<pid>/environ IS readable - do not "fix" that into a
   blanket statement that the child cannot read the supervisor's /proc.

NOT about encryption. This wants fixing whether or not 4h6.88 is ever implemented.
close_reason:
LANDED. genetics-results-suite bc38dfc. Filed and closed in the same cycle - it was found while
probing 4h6.88 and fixed immediately, because a false security claim in the normative doc is blocking under
this epic's standing rule.

THE FIX: :509's "RuntimeDefault already blocks ... ptrace beyond self" is corrected. The profile ALLOWS
ptrace (MEASURED: attach to one's own descendant returns rc=0, a case Yama permits and seccomp would not).
Yama (kernel.yama.ptrace_scope=1) is what refuses a same-uid child attaching to the supervisor, because the
supervisor is the child's ANCESTOR; sibling-to-sibling fails identically.

THE REST OF THE LIST WAS RE-DERIVED RATHER THAN TRUSTED - the point of the bead's instruction, since one
entry being wrong is reason to doubt the others. No moby/containerd default.json exists on this machine, so
it was settled by A/B measurement instead of by reading upstream: a raw syscall() probe run twice with ONLY
`--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` varied, which is what separates a seccomp ERRNO denial from a capability
denial. That is the same control the doc's 4h6.55 section already uses.
    add_key                EPERM / EFAULT     blocked by profile   MEASURED
    keyctl                 EPERM / EINVAL     blocked by profile   MEASURED
    bpf                    EPERM / EINVAL     blocked by profile   MEASURED
    mount                  EPERM / EFAULT     blocked by profile   MEASURED
    unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER) EPERM / SUCCEEDS   blocked by profile   MEASURED  (corroborates 4h6.55 at :1737)
    ptrace(ATTACH)         rc=0  / rc=0       NOT BLOCKED          MEASURED
FIVE OF SIX STAND, and they are now measured rather than asserted - which is a better outcome than the
correction alone. The docker-default ~= containerd-RuntimeDefault step is labelled INFERENCE, reusing the
doc's existing caveat wording rather than a new formulation.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS NAMED, which is why this mattered: 4h6.82's integrity property rests on this. The
build_manifest docstring keeps the digest map in supervisor memory precisely because /scratch is writable
by the process being defended against, so a child holding PTRACE_ATTACH forges the map and 4h6.82
evaporates. The doc credited that to seccomp. It now credits Yama, MEASURED under runc and UNVERIFIED under
gVisor (4h6.51), and says so at the site as well as in both docs. The gVisor phrasing deliberately matches
4h6.83's existing disclaimer rather than inventing a second formulation.

A CORRECT CLAIM WAS PRESERVED ON PURPOSE: the child CAN still read the supervisor's /proc/<pid>/environ -
PTRACE_MODE_READ, which Yama does not restrict, is a DIFFERENT GATE from PTRACE_MODE_ATTACH. The doc says
so explicitly rather than collapsing into "the child cannot read the supervisor's /proc". Three existing
places already asserted the environ read (:208, :2165, :3033) and all three remain true.

ALSO RECORDED, marked INFERENCE not measured: the pod cannot write /proc/sys/kernel/yama/* under
readOnlyRootFilesystem with no CAP_SYS_ADMIN, so the value is the NODE's. A node at ptrace_scope=0 voids
the property and k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml neither asserts nor checks it. That is a real gap and it is
deliberately left as a documented INFERENCE rather than turned into work.

GREP CONFIRMED :509 WAS THE ONLY INSTANCE - no other doc or code comment asserts seccomp blocks ptrace, and
sandbox.yaml sets seccompProfile: RuntimeDefault while making no claim about it.

Doc ownership satisfied: sandbox/** changed (the build_manifest docstring), so both
docs/code-execution-security.md and docs/project-spec.md were updated in the same commit.

TESTS: scripts/test-supervisor.py 325 passed, 2 skipped - unchanged, as a doc correction should be.

title: Encrypt retained artifacts with a per-execution key held only in supervisor memory, closing the cross-execution read of completed executions
description:
SPLIT OUT OF genetics-results-suite-4h6.82 on 2026-08-20 when the user rescoped that bead to the
integrity half. THIS IS THE CONFIDENTIALITY HALF, AND IT IS NOT FIXABLE BY ANY MECHANISM CURRENTLY
AVAILABLE. It is filed so that the deploy gate stays honest, not because there is work to do.

THE EXPOSURE, MEASURED 2026-08-20 from inside a second execution's child:
    listdir(/scratch) -> ['.supervisor', '<victim-uuid>', '<own-uuid>']
    peer_entries: ['private.csv']   read: 'SECRET-VICTIM-DATA'   stat mode: 0o40700
Every live and retained execution directory is enumerable, and every file in it is readable, by any
process at uid 65532. mkdir 0700 protects nothing when there is one uid. The window is 900-930s for
artifacts/ after completion (RETENTION_S 900 + REAPER_POLL_S 30) and the full duration for a live
execution.

WHY IT IS NOT WORK, i.e. why every option is closed:
- A MOUNT NAMESPACE per execution is the clean fix. That is option (c) from 4h6.55: it needs a custom
  seccomp profile, which docs/code-execution-security.md lists under REJECTED CONTROLS because it requires
  a DaemonSet-distributed localhostProfile, AND its behaviour under gVisor is UNMEASURED - runsc is not
  installed on the dev machine (measured 2026-08-20), so this stays behind genetics-results-suite-zg6.
- A SECOND NON-ROOT UID for the child is the real non-namespace fix and is DECIDED AGAINST: it needs
  CAP_SETUID/CAP_SETGID/CAP_CHOWN, which k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml drops. See
  docs/code-execution-security.md:130 and 4h6.7, where setuid(65533) and chown(65533) were MEASURED to
  return EPERM.
- Encrypting retained artifacts with a per-execution key held only in supervisor memory would bound
  reading of RETAINED artifacts, but not the live window - the child writes plaintext into its own
  artifacts/ - and it buys nothing against a resident that reads during execution.
- chmod 0300 on the /scratch root bounds naive enumeration only; the child owns the directory and can
  chmod it back.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS FOR: it gates genetics-results-suite-4h6.50 so that no multi-user deploy happens without
somebody CONSCIOUSLY ACCEPTING this residual or paying for option (c). It is labelled `human` because the
only two ways to close it are a risk acceptance and a rejected control - neither is an autonomous
decision, and an agent must not close it by implementing a partial measure and calling the class handled.

RELATED: 4h6.82 (integrity half, in progress), 4h6.83 (the same-uid resident that reads the NEXT
execution's token file - same root cause, different asset), 4h6.87, 4h6.55 (where the option analysis
lives).
notes:
--- DOC ERROR FOUND 2026-08-24 while probing the runsc question. It is in the SECURITY DOC, it bears on
    this bead's own residual analysis, and it should be corrected by whoever does this bead. ---
docs/code-execution-security.md:575-578 records as INFERENCE that "a node booted with ptrace_scope=0
removes this protection entirely". sandbox/supervisor.py:950 carries the same claim.
UNDER GVISOR THAT LOOKS WRONG, and the direction matters: it UNDERSTATES the protection rather than
overstating it, so it is not the blocking class - but it is still false and it is load-bearing for how
4h6.82/.83/.88 assess their residuals.
WHY: gVisor's YAMAPtraceScope is SENTRY STATE, initialised to linux.YAMA_SCOPE_RELATIONAL unconditionally
at kernel init (pkg/sentry/kernel/kernel.go:576). It is NOT read from the node's sysctl. The node's value
governs the SENTRY PROCESS ON THE HOST, not the guest's ptrace checks. So a node booted with
ptrace_scope=0 does not, by that route, void the in-sandbox refusal.
DO NOT COPY THIS STRAIGHT INTO THE DOC. It is a probe reading gVisor master on GitHub, not a measurement
of the build GKE Sandbox actually ships, and two residuals are open: whether GKE's runsc flags override
the default, and whether /proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope is WRITABLE FROM INSIDE THE SANDBOX (a child
lowering it to 0 would void the protection by a different route entirely). Re-verify before editing, and
write the claim at the strength the evidence supports - this epic has shipped a measurably false security
absolute three times, and the fix for that is not to ship a true-sounding one in the other direction.
Full triage on genetics-results-suite-4h6.51's notes.

=== DECIDED BY THE USER 2026-08-24: ENCRYPT. This bead becomes WORK. ===
The user was given the accept-or-fix choice with the recommendation to encrypt, and answered "4h6.88:
encrypt". The description above says encryption "would bound reading of RETAINED artifacts, but not the
live window" - THAT REMAINS TRUE and is not superseded. What changed is that the residual is being paid
down rather than accepted whole. Un-deferred and the `human` label dropped.

WHAT ENCRYPTION ACTUALLY BUYS, stated so nobody later reads this bead as closing the class:
  BEFORE: any same-uid process can listdir /scratch and read every LIVE and every RETAINED execution's
          artifacts. Retained window 300-330s (RETENTION_S 300 + REAPER_POLL_S 30, both re-read
          2026-08-24 - the 900s in the description above is STALE, 4h6.91 changed it).
  AFTER:  the retained window is closed. The LIVE window is not: the child writes plaintext with a raw
          open() into its own artifacts/, so a resident reading DURING an execution is untouched.
          Live window = up to timeout_s (1-120, default 60) + KILL_GRACE_S 2, plus an unmeasured
          reap-to-encrypt tail.
  So this removes the CROSS-EXECUTION read of COMPLETED executions - the attack that was actually
  demonstrated (listdir /scratch -> peer_entries -> read SECRET-VICTIM-DATA) - and leaves a same-execution
  -window race. Whoever writes the docs MUST say that and must not write "artifacts are encrypted" as
  though it were unqualified. This epic has shipped a measurably false security absolute three times.

=== PROBED 2026-08-24 BEFORE SPECCING. All of the following is MEASURED, not recalled. ===

THERE IS NO CHOKEPOINT IN THE CHILD. There is no SDK artifact-writing helper - the child writes with a raw
open() to $SANDBOX_ARTIFACTS_DIR, and the shipped SDK/stubs expose no artifact function at all. So
encryption CANNOT live on the write side; it has to be a supervisor-side encrypt-in-place after the reap.
(NOTE: docs/code-execution-security.md:4912 calls artifacts/ "the one subdirectory the SDK writes named
outputs into" - that wording is WRONG today. Doc finding, recorded on e8e, fix it while you are in there.)

THE HOOK POINT IS UNAMBIGUOUS - supervisor.py:3417-3433 inside _execute_inner:
    os.unlink(dirs.tokens)
    trimmed = self._retain(job)                                  <- deletes all but artifacts/, trims

title: The supervisor's socket read buffer admits a request body before the readiness check, so the fork server can still snapshot raw token bytes
description:
FOUND by blind re-validation of genetics-results-suite-4h6.55 (option (b), the fork server), 2026-08-20,
AFTER that bead's two fix rounds. It is the residual left when .55's startup-window bypass was closed, and
it is narrower and one layer lower than the one .55 fixed.

.55's bar: "the process that calls os.fork() must NEVER, at any point in its lifetime, for any execution,
have held a token, a request body, or another user's source code in its address space." .55 now refuses a
pre-ready POST /execute with 503 BEFORE _read_body, so no Python string is ever built and the
module-global / frame-walk / gc routes stay clean. THE RAW BYTES ARE STILL THERE.

THE MECHANISM: _Handler inherits rbufsize = -1, so BaseHTTPRequestHandler's request-line and header parse
does an 8 KiB BUFFERED recv BEFORE _execute is entered at all. A body sharing that segment with the
headers - i.e. any body under ~8 KiB from a normal client, and http.client concatenates them - is already
in the supervisor's heap when the readiness check runs. _read_body and parse_execute_request never run;
the bytes get there underneath them.

MEASURED, with the A/B that isolates it (prewarm gated so ForkServer.start() runs milliseconds after the
503, removing the arena churn a multi-second prewarm provides):
  headers+body in ONE segment (679-byte body):
     mem_found=['control-prefork','early-code','early-header','early-session','early-token']
  headers and body sent as SEPARATE segments (body arrives after the 503):
     mem_found=['control-prefork']        <- nothing else
Under a REALISTIC startup window (prewarm ~3.06s, request at +10ms) nothing was recovered - but that is
ARENA REUSE, not exclusion, and it is not a property anything enforces.

REACHABILITY is the same as .55's original: an in-place container restart keeps the pod in endpoints for
failureThreshold x periodSeconds (~30s) while the new supervisor is already accepting, and anything the
network policy admits can reach the pod IP directly. It additionally requires the fork to land promptly
after the refusal, which a fast prewarm or a warm page cache makes more likely.

CANDIDATE FIXES, neither free, which is why this is a bead and not a third fix round on .55:
(a) rbufsize = 0 on the handler, so headers are read without slurping the body. Closes it at the source.
    COST: unbuffered header reads on every request - a real HTTP read-performance change on the hot path
    that wants measuring, not assuming.
(b) Restate the bar honestly and bound the exposure instead: the enforced property is that no Python
    object holding a token/body/source is built before the fork, with raw socket-buffer bytes a residual
    bounded by arena churn. Cheap, but it is a weaker claim than the epic has been making.
(a) is the real fix if the measurement supports it.

DO NOT close this by pointing at .55. .55's fix is correct and its own bypass stays closed - verified by
re-running the original probe unchanged, with the post-fork negative needle correctly absent.

BLOCKS the deploy gate for the same reason .55 did: 4h6.50.
notes:

(a) STILL PRESENT (READ). sandbox/supervisor.py ~:4250-4253 - _Handler sets protocol_version,
server_version and sys_version, and NO rbufsize, so it still inherits -1. bd415f9 changed nothing here.

(b) THE COST OF CANDIDATE FIX (a), rbufsize = 0, MEASURED. n=5000 per arm, keep-alive, TCP_NODELAY and
disable_nagle_algorithm in BOTH arms (without that a 40ms delayed-ACK stall swamps the signal - the first

    unbuffered  real _Handler GET /health      mean= 996.1us p50= 979.0us p99= 1688.6us recv_into= 75.17/req

title: MCP can still reach sandbox dispatch by asserting an identity header alongside the marker
description:
FOUND by BOTH reviewers independently while validating genetics-results-suite-4h6.27, 2026-08-20.
4h6.27 asked for the marker-ALONE service identity to be refused at sandbox dispatch. That landed and is
correct. THIS BEAD IS THE RESIDUAL IT DOES NOT COVER, and it is the difference between a convention and a
property.

THE HOLE, with the exact request that exercises it:
auth/dependencies.py case 1 beats case 3. Marker PLUS an asserted identity header wins. So any holder of
INTERNAL_API_SECRET - mcp-server included, by the same NetworkPolicy admission to chat-backend:8000 that
4h6.27 cites - reaches sandbox dispatch as a real user with:

    POST /chat/v1/chat
    X-Internal-Auth: <INTERNAL_API_SECRET>        (or Authorization: Bearer <INTERNAL_API_SECRET>)
    X-Goog-Authenticated-User-Email: anyone@finngen.fi
    {"messages":[...], "session_id":"anything", "tool_profile":"code"}

get_authenticated_user accepts any address passing _email_allowed, the run_analysis guard passes because
the identity is no longer 'mcp-tool', and BOTH per-execution JWTs are minted with sub = that asserted
address. session_id is client-supplied and unvalidated, so the artifact scope and the audit trail both
attribute the execution to a person who never made the request.
WORSE: _email_allowed's own docstring records that the allow-list FAILS OPEN when unconfigured, in which
case any string is accepted.

WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY BROKEN: mcp-server's only call to chat-backend today is POST /v1/tokens/validate.
So the AUTOMATIC transitive path is closed. What remains is that the boundary rests on mcp-server
choosing not to assert an identity, not on chat-backend being unable to be told one. The user's stated
requirement is that code execution not be reachable via MCP - as a property, that is not yet true.

CANDIDATE FIX, and it is cheaper than it looks: the two marker transports are ALREADY distinguishable.
auth/core.py:67-75 shows auth-gateway uses X-Internal-Auth while mcp-server and results-api use
Authorization: Bearer. Requiring the GATEWAY transport specifically for sandbox dispatch would make the
