title: A setsid() resident reads the next execution's token file and survives every group kill (4h6.55 finding 3)
description:
SPLIT OUT OF genetics-results-suite-4h6.55 on 2026-08-20, when the user ruled option (b) for that
bead. (b) is a fork server that never sees a token; it closes .55's finding 1 and does NOTHING for this
one. Split so that scoping .55 to (b) does not silently weaken the deploy gate.

THE FINDING, demonstrated end to end, not argued:
Execution A forks a grandchild that setsid()s, dup2s /dev/null over fds 0/1/2 and CLOSES fd 3, then
returns. A looks perfectly normal to chat-backend - status ok, 60 ms. The resident then polls /scratch,
sees the NEXT execution's directory appear, and READS ITS mode-0600 TOKEN FILE INSIDE THE READ-ONCE
WINDOW (the victim wrote it and unlinked it 400 ms later). Captured output shows the victim's bearer
token.

CONSEQUENCE FOR 4h6.43: the read-once token file is exactly as exposed as /proc/<pid>/environ, for the
same reason - same uid plus a process nothing kills. The file must NOT be documented as an exposure
bound while this is open.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REAPER (4h6.41), two distinct hazards, both measured:
- job.pgid = pid is ASSERTED, never read back with os.getpgid(pid) and never re-validated before
  signalling. killpg(pgid, SIGTERM) and SIGKILL both returned ESRCH while the grandchild survived. Any
  descendant calling setsid()/setpgid() leaves the group and is unreachable.
- Once waitpid reaps the child the pgid is STALE AND THE PID IS RECYCLABLE, so a later killpg can hit an
  unrelated group - plausibly THE NEXT EXECUTION'S CHILD.

CANDIDATE ANSWER from .55's analysis: a PID namespace per execution (child as PID 1 of its own
namespace) is THE ONLY MECHANISM FOUND that kills this as a CLASS - a pgid-based reaper structurally
cannot. That is option (c), and its price is a custom seccomp profile (listed under REJECTED CONTROLS in
docs/code-execution-security.md) plus an unmeasured gVisor question behind genetics-results-suite-zg6.
runsc is not installed on the dev machine, measured 2026-08-20.

RELATED: 4h6.62 and 4h6.66 are the narrower reaper defects and are already open; this bead is the class,
they are instances. Do not close this one by fixing those.

BLOCKS: anything putting the sandbox in front of more than one user - 4h6.50 and 4h6.51 are blocked on
this bead as well as on .55.
notes:
--- CORRECTION 2026-08-20. TWO OF THIS BEAD'S CLAIMS WERE FALSE WHEN IT WAS FILED. Verified against the tree. ---
This bead was split out of 4h6.55 by copying that bead's finding-3 text. That text was written against an
older tree and was NOT re-verified before filing. It has now been checked line by line. What is wrong:

WRONG #1 - "job.pgid = pid is ASSERTED, never read back with os.getpgid(pid)".
There is no pgid slot. Job.__slots__ (supervisor.py:1923) omits it, with the comment at :1920-1921 "NO
pgid SLOT. The design point is that no pgid is ever cached (see _resolve_pgid)". Resolution is LIVE:
_resolve_pgid (:2777) -> _own_pgid (:1459) -> os.getpgid(pid), returning None when the pgid equals the
caller's own group. `git log -S"_resolve_pgid"` dates this to 09ed48d, i.e. genetics-results-suite-4h6.41
- so it was already true before this bead existed. 4h6.55 only EXTRACTED _own_pgid so the fork server
could share the guard; it did not introduce it.

WRONG #2 - "once waitpid reaps the child the pgid is STALE AND THE PID IS RECYCLABLE, so a later killpg
can hit an unrelated group".
Guarded. _signal_group (:2807-2811) takes job.kill_lock and returns _SIGNAL_GONE if job.reaped or
job.pid is None BEFORE resolving a pgid; _kill_group's grace loop re-checks under the lock (:2770-2772);
_fire_limit checks (:2732); and _reap's waitid(WNOWAIT)-then-waitpid-under-lock split (:2854-2867) keeps
the pid un-recyclable until the flag and the reap happen together. A killpg cannot fire on a reaped or
recycled pid today.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE BEAD - NOTHING KILLS A setsid() ESCAPEE.
MEASURED 2026-08-20 after a NORMALLY-COMPLETING execution (status ok):
    SURVIVORS:  1197089 1197084 PRB-INGRP    <- plain fork, stayed in the pgid
                1197090 1197090 PRB-DETACH   <- setsid escapee
The only /proc scan is _group_members (:2870-2900), which matches the job's pgid and is the pid-budget
counter, not a sweep. No cgroup kill, no same-uid scan, no subreaper. _kill_group's own docstring says so
(:2746-2750). The token-file read primitive is live for the same reason .82's is: same uid, and
tokens.json sits under an enumerable directory (the file-access half MEASURED; the timing race itself
read, not re-run).

THE NAMESPACE-FREE MECHANISM THAT ACTUALLY REACHES THIS CLASS, and it was not in the original analysis:
PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER on the fork server, plus killing and reaping everything reparented to it at
execution end. setsid() does NOT change parentage, so an escapee whose parent exits still reparents to
the nearest subreaper rather than to PID 1. This does NOT need a seccomp profile change and does NOT need
option (c). It does not bound the INTRA-execution window (a resident is alive while its own execution
runs), it needs the fork server to distinguish its own live child, and it is unverified under gVisor.
A same-uid /proc sweep at execution end reaches the same class without prctl, but is pid-reuse racy and
one misclassification kills the fork server.

RELATED, both re-verified: 4h6.62 STILL TRUE as written. 4h6.66's "only from _fire_limit" is imprecise -
there are two _kill_group call sites (:2740 _fire_limit, :2523 the stranded path) - but its DEFECT STANDS,
because a normal completion has reaped=True so neither fires, which is exactly what PRB-INGRP above
demonstrates.
close_reason:
LANDED. genetics-results-suite bd415f9. Closes the INTER-execution half only - see the bound below.

WHAT LANDED: PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER on the fork server, plus an FS_OP_SWEEP that enumerates the fork
server's children BY PARENTAGE through /proc and subtracts its own live child. Parentage is the entire
point and is why this reaches a class nothing else here could: setsid() does NOT change parentage, so an
escapee whose parent exits reparents to the nearest subreaper. A pgid-based reaper structurally cannot see
it - which is what the bead's own measurement showed (PRB-DETACH survived every existing mechanism).

THE FIRST IMPLEMENTATION WAS WRONG AND VALIDATION CAUGHT IT. THE SUITE WAS GREEN AT 315/2 WHEN IT WAS
FOUND, and both an independent sighted review and a blind validation found it separately; the blind one
measured it and measured the fix.
_fs_sweep enumerated the fork server's children ONCE and then worked over that frozen set. So a DEPTH-2
setsid() chain survived: at scan time the survivor's parent is still alive, so the survivor is not yet a
child of the fork server and is not enumerated; the parent is killed and reaped; the survivor reparents
AFTER the snapshot; nothing re-enumerates. It also escaped the collateral killpg that caught the shallower
probes, because its own setsid() put it outside its parent's group.
MEASURED before the fix:
    PROBE4 double-setsid status=ok pids={'A': 1213980, 'B': 1213981} A=None B='S'
    PROBE4 after ONE more execution: B=None
B was in state S (running) for the ENTIRE next execution - precisely the "resident sitting in front of the
next user" this bead exists to close, for one extra fork()+setsid().
WHY THE TESTS DID NOT CATCH IT: both probes were exactly the two shapes the bead had measured
(PRB-DETACH, PRB-INGRP). The tests were honest and their negative controls genuinely bite; they inherited
the BEAD's blind spot, not a testing failure. The lesson is that a test written from a finding tests the
finding, not the class.

THE FIX: bounded re-enumeration - loop until a pass finds nothing, capped by FS_SWEEP_MAX_ROUNDS = 4 AND
FS_SWEEP_BUDGET_S = 10s. The wall-clock bound is load-bearing: the sweep runs inside an FS_OP_SWEEP round
trip, so overrunning FS_CONTROL_TIMEOUT_S = 30s would poison the control socket and KILL THE FORK SERVER,
turning a containment mechanism into a self-kill primitive. Worst case is the budget plus ONE round (the
budget is tested at the END of a round) = 10 + 2*KILL_GRACE_S = ~14s, a 16s margin. A round cannot exceed
2*KILL_GRACE_S because _fs_kill_set uses one batch grace per signal, not one per pid. Worst OBSERVED 8.5s.

RE-VALIDATED, all MEASURED:
- depth-2 no longer survives; test_survivor_chain covers it with a negative control (FS_SWEEP_MAX_ROUNDS=1
  patched in before the fork server is forked, so the fork server's own copy is the patched one) that was
  confirmed from the suite log rather than from the implementer's transcript.
- depth-5 clears exactly ONE LEVEL PER ROUND, remainder LOGGED, remainder cleared by the next execution's
  sweep - so the doc's "four levels per execution" is measured, not assumed.
- a SIGTERM-ignoring stray that forks a fresh setsid() decoy each time it is signalled is a FIXPOINT: never
  eliminated, taxes every later execution ~8.2s (the ROUND cap binds, not the budget). The fork server
  survives and the following execution still works. Recorded on e8e as the worst case.
- the loop cannot kill the fork server's own live child or itself: `pending` is never mutated across
  rounds (each round consumes a copy), and _child_pids cannot return the caller.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, and the docs say so rather than implying otherwise:
- THE INTRA-EXECUTION WINDOW. A resident is alive while its own execution runs. Unbounded here.
- The sweep bounds chain DEPTH per execution. It is NOT a guarantee of an empty pod - see the fixpoint.
- UNVERIFIED UNDER gVISOR. runsc is not installed on the dev machine; behind 4h6.51.
- If prctl is unavailable the sweep is INERT and fails OPEN, logged once at startup only - there is no
  per-execution signal that it is doing nothing. Stated in _fs_become_subreaper's docstring and both docs.
- Reading another execution's data is a different asset and is 4h6.88.

THREE DOC ABSOLUTES WERE MEASURABLY FALSE and were corrected in the same commit: project-spec.md's
"nothing an execution leaves behind outlives it"; code-execution-security.md's "a grandchild of execution A
is dead before execution B's token file is written" (in the TOKEN FILE section, which made it the worst of
the three); and "the escaped-process route is closed across executions". Replaced with the enforced
property and its bound - a process reparents only when its parent exits, depth n needs n rounds, four
levels per execution, remainder logged. THIS EPIC HAS NOW SHIPPED A FALSE SECURITY ABSOLUTE TWICE, so the
same sentence was also removed from test prose (test_survivors' docstring and skip label) to stop it being
copied back into the docs.

ALSO: reparented ZOMBIES no longer trip the ERROR that tells operators a control failed - they go to INFO.
A raw os.fork() orphan produces one routinely. NOTE for whoever reads that log: a subprocess.Popen the
script never waits on does NOT produce one, and the reason is subtle - the execution child exits via
os._exit() and never reaches interpreter shutdown or GC finalization at all; what reaps it is exec()
returning, the throwaway globals dict releasing the last Popen reference, and refcounting running
waitpid(WNOHANG) right there. Recorded on e8e.

RESIDUAL, recorded on e8e not filed: the LAST round's collateral killpg victims are left as zombies until
the next execution's sweep, because reaping a round's victims is what the NEXT round's enumeration does.
Bounded by the pod pid budget, persists one execution, and the "cannot claim the pod is clear" line fires,
so it is observable rather than silent.

title: Retained artifacts can be overwritten or planted by any same-uid process, so read_artifact serves attacker-controlled content under another user's execution id
description:
RESCOPED 2026-08-20 BY THE USER to the INTEGRITY half plus the missing test. The confidentiality
half - a same-uid process READING another execution's artifacts - is genetics-results-suite-4h6.88 and is
NOT this bead's work. Do not close .88 by pointing here.

WHY THE SPLIT: under one uid NO FILESYSTEM MECHANISM BOUNDS ACCESS. Only discovery, window and detection
can be bounded. Reading is therefore not closable without a mount namespace (option (c), which needs a
custom seccomp profile and carries an unmeasured gVisor question behind genetics-results-suite-zg6) or a
second non-root uid (decided against by 4h6.7: it needs CAP_SETUID/SETGID/CHOWN, which
k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml drops). Integrity IS closable, because the supervisor can bind what it
served to what it built.

=== IN SCOPE 1: ARTIFACT INTEGRITY ===
THE FAILURE THIS CLOSES, measured 2026-08-20 from inside a second execution's child:
    listdir(/scratch) -> ['.supervisor', '<victim-uuid>', '<own-uuid>']
    peer_entries: ['private.csv']   read: 'SECRET-VICTIM-DATA'
    overwrote: true   planted: true
The overwrite and the plant are the integrity half: THE RETENTION WINDOW SERVES ATTACKER-CONTROLLED
CONTENT UNDER ANOTHER USER'S EXECUTION ID. read_artifact's descriptor discipline (4h6.15) cannot help -
the inode is legitimately inside that execution's artifacts/.
REQUIRED: hash each artifact at build_manifest and re-verify in read_artifact, so a modified or planted
file is REFUSED rather than served. A planted file that was never in the manifest must also be refused,
not just a changed one.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, and the doc must say so: reading (that is .88); planting into a LIVE execution
BEFORE build_manifest runs, which is inside the window the manifest is built from; and deletion/DoS.

=== IN SCOPE 2: THE MISSING TEST ===
Cross-execution artifact isolation is UNTESTED. test_isolation (scripts/test-supervisor.py:2336) is MEMORY
isolation only - /proc/self/mem, gc, frame-walk and module-global routes against token/code/session
needles. Its only filesystem assertion is `set(os.listdir(tmp)) == before`, i.e. "no stray dirs in the
harness tmp". test_startup_wipe (:2135) and test_artifact_scoping (:468) do not cover it either.
REQUIRED: a test that a second execution's child overwriting or planting into a first execution's
artifacts/ makes read_artifact REFUSE, with a working negative control (disable the verification and the
test must fail).

=== IN SCOPE 3: ONE DOC WORDING FIX, because it is measurably false ===
read_artifact's docstring (supervisor.py:2075-2077) says the execution id "cannot be guessed and cannot be
walked". Names are uuid4 (EXECUTION_ID_RE :299) so unguessable is right, but /scratch IS FULLY ENUMERABLE
by any same-uid process - measured above. The claim is true of the HTTP surface only. Say that.

CONTEXT that is current: 4h6.46 has landed, so _retain (:2198-2247) deletes everything under
/scratch/<id> except artifacts/ at completion, and artifacts/ is removed 900-930s later (RETENTION_S 900,
REAPER_POLL_S 30). The exposure window is that 900-930s, not "forever" as this bead originally said.
notes:
--- VERIFIED AND UPDATED 2026-08-20 against the tree. The finding REPRODUCES IN FULL; one clause was stale. ---
STALE CLAUSE: "nothing is deleted until 4h6.46 lands". 4h6.46 is CLOSED. _retain (supervisor.py:2198-2247)
now deletes everything under /scratch/<id> EXCEPT artifacts/ at completion - so tmp, home, mplconfig,
cache, pycache and tokens.json go - then trims artifacts/ to ARTIFACT_QUOTA_BYTES (64 MiB). artifacts/ is
retained RETENTION_S = 900s (:238) and removed by reap_expired (:2317-2358) on a REAPER_POLL_S = 30s tick,
so it is gone somewhere in [900, 930)s.
THE CORRECT STATEMENT IS THEREFORE "the exposure window is 900-930s for artifacts/, and ends at completion
for tokens/tmp/home/caches" - NOT "forever". 4h6.46 shortened the window; IT DID NOT TOUCH THE ACCESS.

MEASURED 2026-08-20, from inside a second execution's child - the primitive is unchanged:
    listdir(/scratch) -> ['.supervisor', '<victim-uuid>', '<own-uuid>']
    peer_entries: ['private.csv']   read: 'SECRET-VICTIM-DATA'
    stat mode: 0o40700   overwrote: true   planted: true   uid == supervisor's
Directory names are the execution_id, a lowercase uuid4 (EXECUTION_ID_RE :299, validated :597-601) that
must equal both tokens' jti (:628-636). So the name is NOT GUESSABLE but IS FULLY ENUMERABLE - and
read_artifact's docstring (:2075-2077) claiming the id "cannot be guessed and cannot be walked" is true of
the HTTP surface ONLY, and is misleading if read as a filesystem property. Fix that wording when this bead
is worked.

UNTESTED: no test asserts cross-execution artifact isolation. test_isolation
(scripts/test-supervisor.py:2336) is MEMORY isolation only; its single filesystem assertion is
`set(os.listdir(tmp)) == before`, i.e. "no stray dirs in the harness tmp". test_startup_wipe (:2135) and
test_artifact_scoping (:468) do not cover it either.

THE HARD CEILING, and it is what makes this bead not straightforwardly fixable: UNDER ONE UID NO
FILESYSTEM MECHANISM BOUNDS ACCESS. Only discovery, window, or detection can be bounded. Enumerated
options that need neither namespaces nor a second uid:
- HASH artifacts at build_manifest and re-verify in read_artifact -> bounds the INTEGRITY half (serving
  attacker-modified bytes under another user's execution id). Does NOT bound reading, planting into a LIVE
  execution before build_manifest runs, or deletion/DoS. THIS IS THE ONE WITH REAL SECURITY VALUE.
- Encrypt retained artifacts with a per-execution key held only in supervisor memory -> bounds reading AND
  silent modification of RETAINED artifacts; does not bound the live window or deletion.
- Shorten/eliminate retention -> bounds the post-completion window only.
- chmod 0300 on the /scratch root -> bounds naive enumeration only; the child owns the dir and can chmod
  it back.
- A second non-root uid is the real non-namespace fix and is DECIDED AGAINST: it needs CAP_SETUID/SETGID/
  CHOWN which k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml drops (docs/code-execution-security.md:130, by 4h6.7).

LANDED as the INTEGRITY half, per the user's 2026-08-20 rescope. genetics-results-suite bd415f9.
THE CONFIDENTIALITY HALF IS NOT CLOSED and is 4h6.88 (labelled human, deferred, gates 4h6.50). Do not read
this closure as closing reading.

WHAT LANDED: sha256 every artifact at build_manifest, verify in read_artifact. The digests live IN
SUPERVISOR MEMORY ONLY, which is the load-bearing design point - a manifest written to /scratch would be
forged in the same breath as the file it describes, by the same uid, so an on-disk manifest would have
bound nothing. A name the manifest never listed 404s BEFORE the file is opened; changed bytes give 409
ArtifactModified. TOCTOU is structurally closed because the verify hashes the bytes that would be
RETURNED, not a re-read of the file - there is no window between hash and response.

MEASURED by blind validation over the real GET /artifact wire, tampering at the same uid from outside the
supervisor, 10 attack shapes:
    untouched -> 200 (control)          same-byte-length overwrite -> 409
    planted name -> 404                 listed name -> symlink to /etc/passwd -> 404 (O_NOFOLLOW)
    hardlink outside (nlink=2) -> 404   then drop the other link (nlink=1) -> 409
    exact byte restore -> 200           <- correct: restored bytes are not attacker-controlled
    over the read cap, truncated -> 409 <- digest None is REFUSED, never made servable
    artifacts/ dir itself swapped for a symlink to an attacker dir with BYTE-IDENTICAL content -> 404
    retained execution with no manifest -> serves nothing (empty map serves nothing)

THE MISSING TEST (scope item 2) landed as test_artifact_integrity, with a negative control that was
independently confirmed to bite: with the binding disabled the same reads hand back 'ATTACKER-OWNED-YOU'
and 'PLANTED'.

SCOPE ITEM 3, the doc wording: read_artifact's "cannot be guessed and cannot be walked" is corrected.
execution_id is now described as authorisation ON THIS HTTP SURFACE - it is a uuid4 so it is unguessable,
but /scratch is FULLY ENUMERABLE by any same-uid process, which is measured in 4h6.88.

FOUND IN VALIDATION AND FIXED HERE, because the change created it: _artifact_digests was bounded per
execution (<= ARTIFACT_ENTRY_BUDGET = 1024 entries) but NOT across retained executions, and
_name_is_retrievable imposes no name-length cap. ~0.5 MB per execution, retained for RETENTION_S = 900s,
against a 512 Mi pod - and RETAINED_ARTIFACTS_CEILING_BYTES could not evict it because it is charged
st_size and 1024 ZERO-BYTE files measure 0. A ~2500x amplification of an already-uncapped row count.
Fixed by charging the map to the retained-state accounting (RETAINED_STATE_CEILING_BYTES 4 MiB, 512 B per
row plus len(name)+320 per entry), chosen over a row cap (would shorten retention for legitimate rapid
users) and a name-length cap (halves a per-entry cost, leaves the row count uncapped). FAIL-CLOSED BY
CONSTRUCTION: eviction is _forget_retained, which drops directory, id and digest map in ONE step, so
"readable but unverifiable" is unreachable. Verified: 24 executions x 1024 x 200-byte names at st_size 0
stay under the ceiling with rows actually dropped, and the raised-ceiling negative control retains all 24.

ALSO FIXED: expected_digests no longer defaults fail-open. It was `= None` (verification DISABLED); the
single production caller always passed a map so nothing was broken, but a future caller omitting the kwarg
would have silently served unverified bytes with no log line. Now a sentinel that raises on omission.

KNOWN RESIDUAL, FILED AND ICED AS 4h6.89: a FIFO planted over a name the manifest LISTED hangs a handler
thread forever - os.open blocks before the fstat that would reject it. This change NARROWS it (a planted
name now 404s before the open) but cannot close it, because a listed name must be opened before it can be
verified. Same attacker class as .88, but a LIVENESS failure of the supervisor rather than a data failure,
so no fix to .88 would resolve it. Iced because the fix is a real design call: O_NONBLOCK changes
regular-file semantics, and fstatat-before-open reintroduces the TOCTOU the current ordering avoids.

TESTS: 315 -> 325 checks with .83/.66, 2 skipped (pre-existing freed-arena controls, unchanged).

title: Scripts cannot import the SDK by the only name they are told: genetics is not importable
description:
MEASURED in the dev stack, 2026-08-19. Every run_analysis session opens by burning executions on the wrong import:

  10:54:59  import genetics as g                 -> ModuleNotFoundError   (audit records=0)
  10:55:04  from genetics import genetics as g   -> ModuleNotFoundError   (audit records=0)
  10:55:11  pkgutil.iter_modules() probe
  10:55:14  genetics_mcp_server probe
  10:55:18  genetics_mcp_server.sdk probe
  10:55:24  import genetics_mcp_server.sdk as g  -> works                 (audit records=3)

Six executions and ~5 model roundtrips before the first line of real work. The same sequence appears in an unrelated session from a different day, so it is the normal opening, not a one-off.

NOT a missing analysis library: the scripts that follow do `import matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg"); import matplotlib.pyplot as plt` and run past it. matplotlib, numpy and polars are all present and importable.

WHY: the real import path is `genetics_mcp_server.sdk`, and every surface the model can read calls it `genetics`:
- run_analysis description: "Write the script against the `genetics` SDK"
- list_capabilities description and enum: modules 'genetics', 'client', 'errors'
- executor.py _SDK_MODULES = ("genetics", "client", "errors")
- the shipped stub is named genetics.pyi
- the shipped schema README says "Query them with genetics.sql(...)"

The single place the true import line exists is sdk.__doc__ ("import genetics_mcp_server.sdk as genetics"), and list_capabilities DELIBERATELY strips module docstrings (executor.py ~6209: they describe the deployment, env vars and services, and the tool is MCP-reachable). So a model that obeys run_analysis's own "call list_capabilities first" instruction is STILL never told how to import. pkgutil probing is the only discovery path, which is what it does.

DECIDED FIX (user, 2026-08-19), both halves:
1. Ship a real top-level `genetics` module in the sandbox venv aliasing genetics_mcp_server.sdk, so `import genetics` works like any package and every string above becomes true. Must be added to sandbox/prune_venv.py's allowlist (it deletes everything outside the SDK closure) and asserted in sandbox/build-checks.py.
2. Prepend the exact import line to list_capabilities' output. The module docstring stays stripped - only the import statement is added, not the deployment detail it was stripped for.

Files: genetics-mcp-server/src/genetics_mcp_server/sdk/, tools/executor.py; sandbox/prune_venv.py, sandbox/build-checks.py; docs/code-execution-security.md, docs/project-spec.md.

title: First turn of an inline-started chat sends session_id: null, so run_analysis refuses it
description:
MEASURED in the dev stack (~/.cache/genetics-dev-stack/chat-api.log):

  10:38:41.393  Executing tool: run_analysis with input: {'code': '...matplotlib...
  10:38:41.438  ERROR run_analysis called without an authenticated identity (user=True session=False)
  10:39:15.436  Chat complete: iterations=5
  10:39:15.813  Chat session created by anonymous: d16eff64-94cf-46be-bf72-be097ed4f01f

The session row is created 377 ms AFTER the turn it belongs to finished. The whole turn logs [session=unknown]. user is fine (dev-mode 'anonymous' fallback in auth/dependencies.auth_required); session_id is None.

WHY: ChatPage.handleFirstExchange (ChatPage.tsx:~472) calls createSession() only after onStreamingComplete, and LLMChat sends session_id: sessionId || null. So the FIRST turn of a chat started by typing (rather than by pressing New chat) has no session id. ToolExecutor.run_analysis refuses that with _sandbox_operator_error and retryable: False, because the per-execution sandbox token's sid claim is what scopes artifact retention, the GET /artifact fetch and the db-api/results-api per-jti budgets to one conversation. Failing closed is correct; the missing id is the defect.

NOT AFFECTED, which is why it reads as intermittent: handleNewChat (ChatPage.tsx:~257) creates the session eagerly, and secret chats mint crypto.randomUUID() client-side (ChatPage.tsx:~307). Every turn after the first works too.

USER-VISIBLE SYMPTOM: the agent says it cannot render a plot because 'the plotting sandbox has no authenticated session in this context', then falls back to an ASCII rendering. Every other tool works, so nothing else signals the fault.

DECIDED FIX (user, 2026-08-19): create the session BEFORE the stream starts, so a conversation always has an id on the wire. No API change. Accepts that an abandoned first turn leaves an empty session row — handleNewChat already produces those, so it is not a new class of row.

CONSTRAINT the current code encodes and the fix must keep: handleFirstExchange sets inlineSessionIdRef.current and avoids setChatKey precisely so that adopting the new id does not remount LLMChat mid-send. Creating earlier must not reintroduce that remount.

title: The benchmark cannot be quality-judged: it writes nothing (secret=true) and analyze_conversations reads a chat-history DB
description:
FOUND by reading replay_benchmark.py against genetics-results-suite-4h6.23 (2026-08-18). THE SINGLE BIGGEST GAP BETWEEN THAT BEAD AND THE CODE.

4h6.23's gate includes "LLM-judge quality via analyze_conversations --force, which must not regress" - and names quality as HALF the kill criterion: "if the code arm does not beat the baseline on cost AND does not regress quality, keep it behind the profile rather than defaulting it on."

THERE IS NO PATH BY WHICH THE JUDGE CAN SCORE BENCHMARK OUTPUT. These are two disconnected programs:
- analyze_conversations.py reads a CHAT-HISTORY SQLITE DB and scores conversations recorded there.
- replay_benchmark.py sends `secret: True` on EVERY request - hard-coded and non-negotiable - and secret chat writes no chat_messages and no chat_turn_metrics row. The benchmark deliberately leaves NO TRACE in any DB.
So the benchmark produces transcripts the judge cannot see, and the judge scores conversations the benchmark did not produce.

THE secret FLAG IS CORRECT AND SHOULD NOT BE REMOVED to fix this - a benchmark that pollutes real users' conversation history with replayed turns would corrupt the very dataset the next eval_dataset.json is sampled from. Fixing this by turning secret off would be a self-poisoning loop.

WHAT TO BUILD, two shapes, both real work:
(a) PERSIST REPLAY TRANSCRIPTS somewhere the judge can read - a separate SQLite file with the same schema, written only by the harness, pointed at by analyze_conversations --db. Keeps the two programs separate and reuses the judge unchanged. Probably the right answer.
(b) ADD A JUDGING PASS to the harness itself, calling the same scoring prompts on the in-memory transcripts. Fewer moving parts, but duplicates scoring logic that already exists and would drift from it.

COST NOTE: judging is its own Opus-5 spend on top of the benchmark's ~2 USD/turn x 2 arms. Budget it explicitly rather than discovering it.

UNTIL THIS EXISTS, 4h6.23 CAN MEASURE COST AND LATENCY BUT NOT QUALITY, so its kill criterion is only half-computable and the honest outcome of any run is "keep it behind the profile" by default.

Related: genetics-results-suite-4h6.23.
notes:
--- USER CONSTRAINT AND DESIGN DIRECTION, 2026-08-18. READ BEFORE STARTING; IT NARROWS THIS BEAD SUBSTANTIALLY. ---

THE USER STATES: analyze_conversations is NOT run in this dev environment, automatically or manually. So THE SELF-POISONING CONCERN THIS BEAD WAS BUILT AROUND DOES NOT APPLY HERE, and the elaborate isolation it proposed is not worth building. What is still wanted, unchanged, is LLM JUDGING OF THE RESULTS OF THE DIFFERENT TOOL PROFILES.

WHAT THAT RULES OUT: option (a) as originally framed - standing up a separate SQLite file with the chat-history schema purely so the existing judge can read benchmark output - is now over-engineering for the case at hand. It was justified only by keeping replayed turns out of a DB that feeds the next eval_dataset.json sample. In dev nothing samples that DB.
STILL DO NOT REMOVE `secret: True` from the benchmark requests. It costs nothing to leave, and the reason it exists survives the dev case: the moment this is pointed at anything whose history IS sampled or IS judged, writing replay turns into it corrupts the sample. Keep the benchmark write-free and add judging as its own step.

=== THE DESIGN POINT THAT MATTERS MOST, AND IT IS NOT A DETAIL ===
analyze_conversations JUDGES ONE CONVERSATION AT A TIME AND SCORES IT ABSOLUTELY - topic, quality, success_score, issues. That instrument was built for SAMPLING (top and bottom per topic for eval_dataset.json) and for tracking quality over time. IT WAS NOT BUILT TO COMPARE TWO ANSWERS TO THE SAME QUESTION.

For this bead the question is not "how good is this conversation" but "for THIS turn, is the code arm's answer worse than the all-tools arm's". Those need different instruments:
- ABSOLUTE SCORING EACH ARM AND COMPARING MEANS is a weak test. Rubric scores are coarse and noisy, the difference between arms is expected to be small, and 4h6.23's own harness will already be flagging p90/p95 as unreliable at the n a local run produces. A real regression can easily sit inside the noise.
- A PAIRED, SIDE-BY-SIDE JUDGE - same question, both answers, which is better and by how much - is far more sensitive at small n, because it removes the per-question difficulty that dominates absolute scores. This is the standard reason A/B evaluations are done pairwise.
THE HARNESS ALREADY PRODUCES EXACTLY THE RIGHT INPUT FOR THIS: matched_pairs() already keeps only (case_id, turn_index) keys that came back ok on BOTH arms. That set IS the paired-judge input, already computed.

REQUIREMENTS FOR THE PAIRED JUDGE, all of which are about not fooling ourselves:
1. BLIND. The judge must not be told which answer came from which arm, and the arm labels must not leak through the transcript (a run_analysis tool call is a dead giveaway - decide deliberately whether tool traces are shown to the judge at all, and record the choice; judging FINAL ANSWERS ONLY is the defensible default and should be the starting point).
2. ORDER-RANDOMISED, and the order recorded. Position bias in pairwise LLM judging is large and well documented. Consider judging each pair BOTH WAYS and treating a disagreement as a tie - it doubles cost and is the single cheapest defence against position bias.
3. TIES MUST BE EXPRESSIBLE. Forcing a winner on two equally good answers manufactures signal.
4. REPORT THE DISTRIBUTION, not just a win rate: wins / losses / ties with the count, and per-case detail so a human can read the disagreements. 4h6.23's kill criterion is "must not REGRESS quality", which is a question about the LOSS tail, not about the mean.
5. COST IS ITS OWN LINE ITEM. Judging is Opus-5 spend on top of the benchmark's ~2 USD/turn x 2 arms. Print an estimate before spending, the way --dry-run already does for the benchmark, and make the judge independently skippable.

WHETHER TO ALSO REUSE analyze_conversations' ABSOLUTE RUBRIC is a secondary question. It gives comparability with historical production numbers, which the paired judge cannot. Worth having, NOT worth blocking on, and it is the half that needs the chat-history schema.

WHAT THIS BEAD SHOULD DELIVER, restated: a judging pass over the harness's OWN matched pairs, blind and order-randomised, reporting wins/losses/ties with per-case detail, skippable, and priced before it spends. Option (b) from the original description, with the pairwise design above - not option (a).

genetics-results-suite-4h6.72: pairwise blind judging of the benchmark's own matched pairs

The quality half of 4h6.23's kill criterion, which was previously not computable
at all. Implementation + sighted review + INDEPENDENT blind validation + one fix
round. Suite 1649 -> 1686 -> 1700 passed / 74 deselected. No billed judging pass
and no benchmark run: every judge call goes through a stub client.

WHY PAIRWISE AND NOT THE EXISTING JUDGE. analyze_conversations scores ONE
conversation at a time, ABSOLUTELY - an instrument built for sampling and for
tracking quality over time. Scoring each arm absolutely and comparing means is a
weak test here: the rubric is coarse, the expected between-arm difference is
small, and the harness already flags p90/p95 unreliable at the n a local run
produces, so a real regression sits inside the noise. 4h6.23's criterion is
"must not REGRESS quality", which is a question about the LOSS TAIL. A paired
judge cancels the per-question difficulty that dominates absolute scores, and
the harness already computes the right input - matched_pairs() keeps only the
turns that came back ok on BOTH arms, so build_pairs() reuses it through a shim
rather than re-deriving the rule.
The user confirmed analyze_conversations is not run in this dev environment, so
the SQLite-mirror approach the bead originally proposed was dropped as
over-engineering. `secret: True` stays on benchmark requests regardless: the
moment this points at anything whose history is sampled or judged, replayed
turns corrupt the sample.

THE DESIGN. Every pair judged BOTH WAYS; a win requires both presentation orders
to agree, and disagreement becomes tie_position_flip - the run measuring its own
position bias rather than hiding it. Order seeded sha256(case_id|turn_index),
deliberately not hash() (per-process salt) and not a global RNG (the draw would
depend on how many pairs preceded). The judge sees the user question, the
earlier USER turns (identical across arms - each arm's own assistant replies are
withheld), and two answers labelled only Answer 1 / Answer 2. NO TOOL TRACE AT
ALL: a run_analysis call carrying Python identifies the code arm outright, so
showing the trace to a "blind" judge is theatre. Exact two-sided sign test over
decisive pairs, ties excluded not split, and below MIN_DECISIVE_PAIRS no p-value
is printed at all.

=== THE DEFECT THAT MOVED THE VERDICT, FOUND BY THE SIGHTED REVIEWER AND MISSED
=== BY THE BLIND ONE
final_answer_text took text blocks after the LAST tool_use. Measured:
  [table][tool][more analysis][tool]["In summary, yes."] -> "In summary, yes."
  answer entirely before the tool call                    -> ""
THE CODE ARM MAKES ONE TOOL CALL, EARLY, so nearly all its prose is post-tool and
survives whole; THE ALL-TOOLS ARM'S LAST CALL IS LATE, so substantive content
produced BETWEEN calls was silently discarded before the judge saw it. A
systematic handicap on the baseline arm, in the direction that makes the
candidate win - and nothing detected it, because answer_chars and the whole
length diagnostic were computed on the already-sliced text.
The slicing rule is unchanged; ITS EFFECT IS NOW VISIBLE. final_answer_split
returns the dropped character count, it is persisted per turn so a saved report
carries it, and the per-arm MEDIAN prints as a `slicing loss:` line directly
under the length check. If the arms' medians differ materially the verdict is
measuring the slicing rule rather than quality, and a reader can see it.
A better rule is proposed but NOT shipped: slice per iteration rather than once
at the last global tool_use, keeping the "let me query X" drop while preserving a
table written three iterations earlier. It changes what every arm is judged on
and needs real-transcript validation, which costs benchmark spend. The
dropped-char medians are the instrument that will say whether it is worth doing.

=== AN UNEXTRACTED ANSWER WAS SCORED AS A LOSS, AND COULD DRIVE A SIGNIFICANT
=== HEADLINE
Reproduced by the blind validator: eight pairs whose final_answer is ""/None
produced `wins all 8 (100.0% of decisive)`, `SIGN TEST p=0.008 ...
distinguishable from chance`, and a loss-tail line naming the kill criterion.
The footnote four lines below correctly said a one-sided empty count is a bug
report rather than a quality finding, AND NEITHER RESTRICTED NOR RECOMPUTED THE
HEADLINE. That inverts this harness's own standard: an answer that could not be
extracted is NOT MEASURED, and it was being scored.
Empty-answer pairs now get the same full restricted table provenance already
gets, and empty_answers_with_dropped_text_per_arm separates "the model said
nothing" from "the slicing rule ate it".
THE GUARD AGAINST EXACTLY THIS USED `and` WHERE IT NEEDED `or` - it fired only
when BOTH arms were empty on EVERY pair, so the catastrophic half-missing case
was the one it did not catch.

=== TWO DIAGNOSTICS DESCRIBED SOMETHING OTHER THAN WHAT HAPPENED ===
Truncation was a pair count, so one arm at 40,000 chars against another at 500
printed "elided for both arms alike" when only one was touched. Now per-arm.
The LENGTH-CONFOUND diagnostic - the one whose job is to warn that the judge is
rewarding length - used RAW lengths. After elision both answers are 11,999 chars,
IDENTICAL, while the report announced a 2x median difference. Now computed on the
shown post-elision text, with the raw figure kept and labelled.

=== THE BLINDING AUDIT WAS MORE REASSURING IN PRINT THAN THE CODE BELIEVED ===
Both reviewers, independently. The marker list's asymmetry was confessed only in
a source comment - grepping the rendered report for "asymmetr" returned nothing,
so the printed restricted table invited exactly the mistake it exists to prevent.
marker_counts was ARM-BLIND at the summary level, printing (python_fence=7,
sandbox=7) with no sign they were all one arm's, when one-sidedness IS the
argument. The restricted table carried a quotable p-value with no power guard, so
THE PRINTED REPORT AND THE SAVED JSON DISAGREED ABOUT WHETHER THAT NUMBER WAS
QUOTABLE. `[Max tool iterations reached]` passed through as the judged answer,
matched no marker, and is a near-perfect tell for the many-roundtrip arm. And
`\bartifacts?\b` fired on ordinary genetics prose - "a batch artifact of
imputation", "an artifact of population structure" - shrinking the clean control
subset on BOTH arms for a non-provenance reason.
All five fixed; the asymmetry is now a printed line and a JSON field.

ALSO: the win share printed as a solid number when underpowered (100.0% over
n=1, above the NOT CONCLUSIVE line), against the module's own stated rule and the
spec's claim of "never a bare win rate"; an unrecognised margin word vanished,
printing three numbers that did not sum; the loss-tail sentence hard-coded
arms[1] as the candidate and named the wrong arm when the arms were swapped; and
the prompt told the judge "both answers had the same conversation history" when
only the USER turns were - an instruction to the judge, not a comment, so it was
fixed rather than batched.

=== VERIFIED SOUND UNDER ATTACK, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-LITIGATED ===
The sign test was independently recomputed against an exact two-sided binomial
over every (wins, losses) in 0..12 x 0..12 with ZERO mismatches, including the
clamp at w==l. MIN_DECISIVE_PAIRS = 6 is right: n=5 gives 0.0625 > 0.05, n=6
gives 0.03125 <= 0.05. Both adversarial judges were BUILT - always-pick-first and
always-pick-second - and each produces all tie_position_flip, zero decisive, no
p-value: A MAXIMALLY POSITION-BIASED JUDGE CANNOT NET A WIN FOR EITHER ARM.
Seeding is stable across processes and varies across pairs; a failed or
unparseable call is unresolved, in neither wins nor ties, with the second call
skipped; the cost preflight is an upper bound priced from the real prompts, an
unpriceable model reports NOT PRICED rather than guessing, and judging spend is
never folded into an arm's cost_usd.

TWENTY MUTATIONS, ALL VERIFIED RED. Two came back GREEN on the first pass and
were treated as the tester's bug rather than as a pass: one mutation was a no-op
because setdefault re-added the key, and one perturbed only rendering the test did
not read. Both were replaced with genuine mutations AND the tests strengthened -
the empty-answer test now uses 8 unextractable pairs plus 4 measured ones, so the
headline is a significant sweep while the restricted table shows ties over 4
pairs, and the assertion reads those numbers.

WHAT IS STILL NOT NEUTRALISED, and is stated in the report rather than hidden:
length (the prompt forbids it, the diagnostic measures it); the marker list's
asymmetry, which cannot be fixed because no phrase reliably marks "many small
tool calls", so a full-vs-restricted gap is evidence about the JUDGE rather than
the arms; iteration-ceiling notices, which are genuine quality facts that also
correlate with arm behaviour; and self-preference, since the judge is the same
model family being benchmarked - which both-ways judging does not remove.
A large tie_position_flip count means THE INSTRUMENT COULD NOT HAVE DETECTED a
regression of that size, not that there was none, and the tie block now says so.

title: Nothing emits the script_result SSE chunk, so the code arm's script-failure and retry-loop rates are unmeasurable
description:
FOUND by reading replay_benchmark.py against genetics-results-suite-4h6.23's stated gate (2026-08-18). THE HARNESS IS HONEST ABOUT THIS - it prints NOT MEASURED rather than 0 - which is exactly why it needs a bead rather than being left to be discovered mid-benchmark.

THE CODE ARM'S CHARACTERISTIC FAILURE MODE IS CURRENTLY UNPRICED. The whole premise of the code profile is that it trades many tool calls for ONE SCRIPT THAT MIGHT FAIL AND BE RETRIED. 4h6.23's gate names "script failure rate and retry-loop count" as two of its six criteria. Neither can be computed today.

THE MECHANISM IS WRITTEN AND DORMANT. replay_benchmark.py looks for an SSE chunk of type `script_result` carrying exit_code / timed_out / exception, and has the retry-loop logic ready (a failed script followed by another `usage` chunk = one retry loop). NOTHING EMITS THAT CHUNK. When none is seen the harness reports null and prints NOT MEASURED with the reason - deliberately NOT 0, which would hand the code arm a free win on a criterion it was never scored against.

WHAT TO BUILD: emit a `script_result` SSE chunk from the chat backend when a run_analysis call completes, carrying at minimum exit_code, timed_out and exception. The data already exists - sandbox_client.py already logs `sandbox execution <id> finished: status=... duration_ms=... artifacts=...` from the supervisor's response body, and executor.py already surfaces duration_ms into the rendered run_analysis result. So this is plumbing an existing signal onto the wire, not new measurement.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE BENCHMARK: a script that fails and is retried costs a full extra model iteration at full context. That is the single most expensive failure shape in the code arm and the one most likely to erase its cost advantage. Shipping the profile without being able to see it means the rollout decision is made blind on its main risk.

BLOCKS A COMPLETE 4h6.23. A benchmark can be RUN without this - four of the six criteria work - but the gate as written cannot be fully evaluated, and the report will say so.

Related: genetics-results-suite-4h6.23, genetics-results-suite-4h6.16 (shipped the profile).

Landed as genetics-mcp-server 756d19a (both beads, one commit - they share the usage-chunk seam).

genetics-results-suite-4h6.71 + 4h6.73: per-iteration timing, exact USD, and the script_result chunk

Two beads landed together because they share one seam: the per-iteration `usage`
SSE chunk and the harness that parses it. Implementation + sighted review +
INDEPENDENT blind validation + two fix rounds. Suite 1620 -> 1638 -> 1646 ->
1649 passed / 74 deselected. No billed benchmark run: everything is verified
with fabricated streams, unit drivers and a fake Anthropic stream.

THESE NUMBERS DECIDE A ROLLOUT (4h6.23), so the standard held throughout is the
harness's own: it prints NOT MEASURED rather than 0 so as not to hand an arm a
free win.

=== WHAT IS NOW MEASURABLE ===
The `usage` chunk gains `turn_elapsed_ms` (cumulative from turn start, sharing
the monotonic zero with chat_turn_metrics.wall_ms), `model_ms` (that iteration's
model call alone) and `model_attempts`. A new `script_result` chunk is emitted
per completed run_analysis. Cost becomes `cost_usd` + `cost_basis`
(exact/interval/unpriced) using the cache_read/cache_create split that
genetics-results-suite-n3p had already put on the wire and the harness had
simply never consumed.

=== THE DORMANT CONSUMER HAD NEVER EXECUTED, AND WAS WRONG ===
replay_benchmark.py already looked for `script_result` and already had the
retry-loop logic, but nothing had ever emitted the chunk, so none of it had run.
Treating it as suspect rather than as a contract found three defects:
- `exit_code` DOES NOT EXIST. The bead, the dormant harness and a pre-existing
  test all specified exit_code/timed_out/exception. The supervisor answers with a
  `status` string of ok/error/timeout/limit. Emitting an exit_code would have
  meant inventing a constant and reporting it as measurement.
- chat_api.py's SSE dispatch is an if/elif chain with NO DEFAULT, so the chunk
  would have been emitted and silently dropped - NOT MEASURED forever with the
  work apparently done. Now has a branch and a test that fails without it.
- The retry-loop logic itself was correct and was kept.

=== THE DEFECT BOTH REVIEWERS FOUND INDEPENDENTLY, AND IT FLATTERED THE ARM ===
`ran = isinstance(status, str)` treated "no status key" as "transport fault, says
nothing about the model's script". FALSE for two shapes, both measured against
the real executor:
- a blank/non-string `code` from the model, which arrived as a bare
  status "unknown" INDISTINGUISHABLE IN THE JSON from a genuine transport fault;
- SandboxRejected, whose own comment reads "a caller bug ... Actionable, because
  the model chose the value" - raised for a model-supplied timeout_s outside
  1..120 and for oversize code.
Both were removed from the numerator AND the denominator and printed as "sandbox
faults (not script failures)". Measured consequence: a model asking timeout_s 300
twice per case yields `script runs=N failures=0 rate=0.000, sandbox faults=2N` -
a reader concludes the scripts never fail and the sandbox is flaky. THIS IS THE
DIRECTION NOBODY HOPING THE SMALL ARM WINS WOULD CATCH.
Now classified on the `status` already on the wire via five disjoint categories;
blank code carries a real `EmptyScript` error_type; both are script failures on
both sides of the rate.

THE TWO REVIEWERS DISAGREED ON TurnBudgetExceeded - one called it the arm's
characteristic risk, the other genuinely infrastructural - AND THAT IS DISSOLVED
RATHER THAN DECIDED. Every shape is counted verbatim and individually, the rate
prints its numerator and denominator inline, and TurnBudgetExceeded sits in its
own bucket on neither side, on its own line. Either classification is
recomputable from numbers on the page.

=== THE LOCALISATION FEATURE POINTED ONE ROUNDTRIP TOO LATE ===
Found by the blind validator and measured. `iteration_ms[N]` was
`turn_elapsed[N] - turn_elapsed[N-1]` = model[N] + THE TOOL PHASE OF N-1, printed
on the same row as tool_phase_ms[N], which belongs to N. Ground truth
iter1 model=1000 / iter1 tools=5800 / iter2 model=2000 named iteration 2 as the
bottleneck at 7.8 s when its own work was 2.0 s, and slowest_iteration_ms is in
_TURN_DISTRIBUTIONS so it propagated per-arm.
Now `iteration_ms = model_ms[N] + tool_phase_ms[N]` - the row sums and
slowest_iteration names the roundtrip to go and look at. The old quantity
survives as `segment_ms`, epoch-honest, because pre_model_ms derives from it.
NOTE the reviewers did NOT contradict each other here: tool_phase_ms's own
attribution was independently verified CORRECT and untouched. Different field.

=== THE FINAL ITERATION IS NOT AN ABSENCE, AND ALMOST BECAME ONE ===
The first fix made iteration_ms None on the final iteration, citing "absence is
never imputed as 0". But two cases were collapsed: a turn that ended BECAUSE the
model stopped calling tools has a tool phase that is genuinely ZERO, while a turn
that hit the iteration ceiling ran tools that were never timed.
Enumerating every exit from the agentic loop shows the split is clean - the
max_tokens and unfilled-result continuations `continue` rather than `break`, so
they always emit another usage chunk and are never final. Therefore
tools-after-the-final-usage-chunk implies the ceiling, and the ceiling is exactly
what appends the notice. The imputation is additionally gated on status == "ok",
so an error, timeout or disconnect mid-turn yields None.
This mattered rather than being tidiness: ~36% of production turns are
single-iteration and would have contributed NOTHING, and the final iteration is
where the answer is generated against the largest context (median 39k -> 117k
tokens by iteration 7+, uncached share 11% -> 52%). A metric that structurally
cannot see it would systematically name the wrong roundtrip - the same defect
class as the off-by-one above.
`tool_phase_ms` deliberately stays None in both cases: the column means "a tool
phase that was measured", and seeding one 0 per turn would drag every by-index
median toward zero for a reason unrelated to how long tools take.
Version skew was the one real false-negative risk and is closed: the notice text
is hoisted to llm_service.MAX_ITERATIONS_NOTICE, the harness keeps its own
literal (it parses a REMOTE stream, so importing would be wrong), and the two are
pinned together by a test.

=== ALSO FIXED ===
The timeline silently merged across an untimed iteration; it now resets the
baseline and reports None. It printed one `n` per row while tool_phase_ms has a
different denominator, and never printed the unreliable_percentiles the harness
already computes - so a p90 over n=1 rendered as an ordinary number, in exactly
the tail rows a reader cares about. Now per-column n with a `*` flag.
`model_ms` is printed under a header that says what it contains: the timed span
encloses retry backoff and, being an async generator, downstream SSE
serialisation. `model_attempts` went on the wire so a retry-inflated figure is
IDENTIFIABLE rather than merely disclaimed.
retry_loops splits into script / disputed / infra, summing to the total. The
parallel-script over-count is documented as the safe direction rather than
solved.
The footer's ">12x" is restored to a true statement: the two cache CLASSES differ
>12x in price; the bracket is narrower because output and uncached input sit in
both endpoints.

=== VERIFIED SOUND UNDER ATTACK, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-LITIGATED ===
The exact cost is algebraically closed and was derived independently twice: the
usage chunk's context is input + cache_read + cache_create, so the harness's
subtraction-derived cached total is identically read+create; min prices all at
the read rate, max at the create rate, read < create, so cost_usd is ALWAYS
inside its bracket. The two cannot disagree. Mixed turns are demoted whole -
one chunk without the split and the turn is not exact - and absence is never
imputed as 0.

Ten source mutations across the two fix rounds, each failing exactly its intended
tests and nothing else. Two assertions are deliberately real rather than
decorative: one drives the REAL run_analysis through a transport that calls
pytest.fail if reached, proving no request leaves the process and therefore that
the sandbox cannot be blamed for either shape; another raises a real
APIConnectionError and asserts model_ms >= 900, so the 1 s backoff demonstrably
sits inside the figure.

title: run_analysis is in the default chat profile and will fail for every user until the sandbox is deployed
description:
FOUND by the review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.48. NOT A DEFECT IN THAT CHANGE - a deployment-ordering hazard it creates, which nothing currently prevents. Behind the zg6 phase gate, so there is time to decide.

THE SITUATION: run_analysis is now in the DEFAULT chat tool profile. get_anthropic_tools() with profile=None contains it, and TOOL_PROFILES puts `orchestration` in the `api` and `bigquery` profiles too. Its description tells the model "Use this instead of chaining data-access tools" - i.e. the model is instructed to PREFER it.

WHAT HAPPENS ON A DEPLOY FROM THIS BRANCH, as things stand:
- chat-backend HAS SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY (k8s/deployments/chat-backend.yaml), so minting succeeds and the fail-closed path does NOT fire.
- chat-backend has NO SANDBOX_URL, so sandbox_client falls back to its default 127.0.0.1:8080 - see genetics-results-suite-6um - and gets ConnectError.
- That classifies as SandboxUnavailable with retryable: True and a message telling the user to wait and try the same script again.
So EVERY CHAT USER GETS A TOOL THE MODEL IS TOLD TO PREFER, WHICH ALWAYS FAILS AND INVITES RETRIES. The failure is the most expensive shape available: it looks transient, so the model retries; and it is the tool the model reaches for FIRST.

WHY IT IS NOT OBVIOUSLY WRONG: this is how genetics-results-suite-4h6.15 landed list_capabilities and read_artifact - definition first, backend later - so it may be deliberate. The difference is that neither of those is a tool the model is instructed to prefer over the alternatives, so their pre-backend failure mode was rare rather than default.

THE OPTIONS:
(a) GATE THE DEPLOY on the sandbox Deployment existing and serving. Natural fit with 4h6.50, which already gates on the manifest declaring args:, and with 4h6.51's deploy-window verification.
(b) SHIP THE DEFINITION BEHIND A SETTINGS FLAG, defaulting off, so the tool is absent from the chat list until the sandbox is reachable. Most robust, and it makes the ordering explicit rather than implicit in deploy sequencing.
(c) Fix 6um so the default URL is not a wrong service, and accept that the tool fails cleanly as "not configured" rather than "temporarily unavailable". Necessary but NOT SUFFICIENT on its own - it improves the message, it does not stop the model preferring a tool that cannot work.
(b) plus (c) is probably right. Decide before anything from this branch reaches chat-backend.

DEPENDS ON: nothing in code. This is a release-ordering decision, so it belongs to whoever runs the deploy window. Related: genetics-results-suite-6um (the default URL), genetics-results-suite-4h6.50 (the wiring bead), genetics-results-suite-zg6 (the phase gate).

title: hla_associations_v column names differ between dev and production, so get_hla_by_allele 400s against prod
description:
FOUND while validating genetics-results-suite-4h6.53, by driving the real MCP executor against BOTH datasets. PRE-EXISTING and independent of that change - the table resolves fine and then column resolution fails.

THE DEFECT: `hla_associations_v` HAS DIFFERENT COLUMN NAMES IN DEV AND PRODUCTION.
  genetics_dev:     mlog10p, se, af, af_cases, af_controls
  genetics_results: mlogp,   sebeta, af_alt, af_alt_cases, af_alt_controls
The MCP server's `get_hla_by_allele` targets the DEV naming, so against production it returns:
  HTTP 400 - Unrecognized name: mlog10p; Did you mean mlogp?
Measured: `get_hla_by_allele("DRB1*15:01")` returns 112 rows against genetics_dev and 400s against genetics_results.

WHY THE TWO DIVERGED, and this is the part that matters: the dev dataset was built from the schemas in the genetics-results-db WORKTREE (branch worktree-db-only-architecture), which carry the NEW column names. Production's deployed views still carry the OLD ones. SO THE WORKTREE SCHEMAS REPRESENT A PENDING VIEW MIGRATION THAT HAS NOT BEEN APPLIED TO PRODUCTION - the dev dataset is not a subset of production, it is a subset of a FUTURE production.

CONSEQUENCES TO WEIGH BEFORE FIXING:
1. `get_hla_by_allele` IS BROKEN AGAINST PRODUCTION RIGHT NOW, wherever the MCP server points at the production dataset. Establish whether that is the deployed state - if so this is a live user-visible failure, not just a dev annoyance.
2. It means anything else built or tested against genetics_dev may silently assume the new schema. Check the other views for the same drift rather than fixing only this one - the same probe that found this (drive each executor method against both datasets and compare) will find the rest cheaply.
3. Applying the view migration to production is a LIVE BigQuery change and is therefore behind the phase gate genetics-results-suite-zg6. The MCP-side fix (targeting whichever naming is canonical) is file-only and is not.

DECIDE FIRST which naming is canonical - the worktree schemas or the deployed views - because that determines whether the fix is "migrate production" or "revert the schemas". Do not fix the MCP query to the old names without establishing that, or the pending migration will break it again.

RELATED: genetics-results-suite-eyg (the credible_sets clustering swap) is a similar already-known case of the worktree schemas being ahead of deployed production, and genetics-results-suite-g08's close reason records that production's `credible_sets` predates the clustering swap and stores neither `resource` nor `variant`. This is the same phenomenon in a different view, which suggests checking ALL of them.
