title: A CTE aliased to a view or table name is silently rewritten by db-api, returning the wrong rows
description:
FOUND by the blind validator during genetics-results-suite-bee, and CONFIRMED BY RUNNING IT. Pre-existing in shape, but bee makes it REACHABLE, so it belongs to this epic now.

THE HAZARD, measured against a live db-api:
    WITH datasets AS (SELECT 1 AS x) SELECT * FROM datasets   -> HTTP 200, total_rows=889
    WITH g        AS (SELECT 1 AS x) SELECT * FROM g          -> HTTP 200, total_rows=1
The first returns 889 rows of `datasets_v` - THE WRONG DATA, WITH NO ERROR. genetics-results-db api/main.py's `_QUALIFY_TARGETS` contains the 15 views PLUS the 15 bare base names (`datasets`, `phenotypes`, `mpra`, `credible_sets`, ...), and `_qualify_tables` rewrites any bare name after FROM or JOIN that matches one. A CTE whose alias collides with a view or table name is silently rewritten into a table reference.

THIS IS THE SAME SILENT-WRONG-ANSWER CLASS the FROM/JOIN anchor was introduced to fix. `_qualify_tables`' docstring documents the string-literal residual it accepted; it does NOT document this one.

WHY bee MAKES IT MATTER. Before bee, the MCP server emitted fully-qualified names, so the rewrite was a no-op on everything it generated and only model-written SQL could trip it. bee makes bare names the NORMAL, INSTRUCTED form - the system prompt, the tool descriptions, the SDK docstring and all 16 shipped schema docs now tell the model to write them - so the rewrite is on the hot path for every query. Nothing shipped is affected today: the executor's own SQL uses only the CTE alias `g`, and a test now pins that every emitted FROM/JOIN referent is bare. THE EXPOSURE IS MODEL-AUTHORED AND SDK-AUTHORED SQL, which is precisely what the code-execution sandbox exists to run.

`datasets` and `phenotypes` are the dangerous aliases - short, generic, and exactly what a model names a CTE.

OPTIONS, and this needs a decision rather than a patch:
1. TEACH `_qualify_tables` ABOUT CTEs: parse the WITH clause and exclude those names from rewriting. Correct, and the parse is not hard (a paren-depth scan accepting `<name> AS (` only at depth 0 - the bee test guard already does exactly this and can be lifted). Cost: the rewrite stops being a regex over text.
2. STOP REWRITING BARE BASE-TABLE NAMES, keeping only the 15 `_v` views in `_QUALIFY_TARGETS`. Much cheaper, and it removes the realistic collisions (`datasets`, `phenotypes`) since a model is far less likely to name a CTE `credible_sets_v`. Check first whether anything legitimately relies on bare base names being rewritten.
3. REJECT RATHER THAN REWRITE a bare name that collides with a CTE alias, so the caller gets an error instead of wrong data. Fails loudly, which beats both above on safety, but breaks any query that legitimately shadows.

WHOEVER TAKES THIS: the fix is in genetics-results-db api/main.py (`_QUALIFY_TARGETS` ~L528, `_qualify_tables` ~L547-554). Pin it with a test that asserts a CTE named `datasets` is NOT rewritten - the failure returns 200 with plausible-looking rows, so nothing else will catch it. Update `_qualify_tables`' docstring, which currently enumerates the residuals it accepts and is now incomplete.
close_reason:
Landed as genetics-results-db 05571dc. Probe, implementation, blind validation, TWO fix rounds, an APPROACH CHANGE, then a cross-repo validation and a polish pass. db suite 138 -> 142 passed / 17 skipped without live credentials, 159 passed with. FILE-ONLY; no BigQuery writes.

THE OUTCOME IS A DELETION, NOT A FIX. `_qualify_tables` and its six helpers - 131 lines - are gone. db-api now sets `default_dataset` on the job config and BigQuery resolves bare names itself.

WHY, AND THIS IS THE DURABLE LESSON: the rewrite was a REGEX EMULATING SQL SCOPING, and three rounds each closed one lexical case and revealed the next, EACH PRODUCING THE IDENTICAL 889-ROW HTTP 200 WRONG ANSWER:
1. A CTE aliased to a view or base-table name was rewritten into a table reference. `WITH datasets AS (SELECT 1 AS x) SELECT * FROM datasets` served 889 rows of datasets_v.
2. Fixed by parsing the WITH clause - but a BACKTICKED declaration was erased by the literal-blanking that exists to stop parens inside literals skewing the depth count, so the CTE was missed. Same 889 rows.
3. Fixed by reducing identifier CONTENTS instead of blanking the span - but BIGQUERY DECODES ESCAPE SEQUENCES INSIDE BACKTICKS, so `\u0064atasets` declares a CTE genuinely named `datasets` while the scan sees `u0064atasets`. And an escaped backtick desynchronised the pairing, swallowing an arbitrary later span including real declarations. Same 889 rows, twice over.
The class is not exhaustible by patching. The rewrite was emulating a grammar whose owner was one API call away, and in SQL a CTE alias shadows a table - BigQuery is the thing that defines when. Recorded in the spec as "db-api no longer parses SQL, and must not start again".

THE GATE IS UNCHANGED AND WAS RE-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY. authorize_query still rejects non-SELECT and any table outside _ALLOWED_TABLE_IDS, because BigQuery reports referencedTables FULLY QUALIFIED whether the name was written bare or qualified - that was the load-bearing fact, established by probe before anything was deleted and re-confirmed by the implementer before deleting it. Both job configs carry the default dataset and the dry-run probe DERIVES IT FROM THE CALLER'S CONFIG rather than a module constant, so probe and execution cannot diverge; a divergence would be a bypass. Verified structurally: authorize_query has exactly one call site and nothing reassigns job_config.default_dataset.

INFORMATION_SCHEMA IS THE ONE GENUINELY NEW SURFACE and it is closed. A bare `FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES` now RESOLVES where before it could not - but BigQuery reports it in referencedTables so the allow-list 403s it. Verified for TABLES, COLUMNS, VIEWS, SCHEMATA, backticked and dataset-qualified forms. Wildcards (`credible_sets*`, _TABLE_SUFFIX) are refused by BigQuery itself. genetics_dev contains exactly the 30 allow-listed objects, no routines, no models.

ONE EXCEPTION BRANCH WIDENED, AND IT HAD TO BE. With a default dataset an unknown bare name stops being a MALFORMED reference (BadRequest) and becomes a WELL-FORMED reference to a nonexistent table (NotFound), which escaped the handler - the first acceptance run hung for 120s. Now both are caught and return the same 400. The gate logic is byte-for-byte unchanged; this is plumbing. NOTE this also resolves the query path of the separately-filed NotFound-to-500 bead.
A THIRD exception type, Forbidden from the dry run, would still escape as a 500. It fails CLOSED (nothing executes) so it is a status-code issue, and it could not be triggered live because the SA has project-level dataViewer. Left as-is and recorded.

ACCEPTANCE RAN AGAINST BOTH DATASETS: the three previously-broken shapes - plain, backticked, and escaped-backtick CTE names - each return the CTE's SINGLE ROW, with an 889-row control proving the assertions are not passing by coincidence. Explicit out-of-allow-list table 403; unknown bare name 400; non-SELECT 400.
THE CROSS-REPO CHECK WAS THE ONE THAT MATTERED: genetics-results-suite-bee (mcp 7712f45) had just made the MCP server emit BARE names ON THE ASSUMPTION THAT DB-API WOULD QUALIFY THEM, and this deletes the thing that did. All six executor methods re-driven against genetics_dev through the new db-api: 67-500 rows each, no failures. The validator initially got 0 rows for all five by-gene methods with APOE and DID NOT ACCEPT IT - genetics_dev is chr22-only and APOE is chr19; re-running with SMARCB1 gave rows. Worth remembering when testing against the dev subset.

TESTS RESTRUCTURED, and the honest part is that the deep ones do not run by default. The 31 old tests asserted on rewritten SQL TEXT and became meaningless - deleted, file renamed test_query_qualification.py -> test_query_name_resolution.py. 17 new ones assert on ROWS RETURNED against live BigQuery, but they SKIP unless LIVE_BQ_PROJECT_ID/LIVE_BQ_DATASET_ID are set, and THIS REPO HAS NO CI AT ALL. A regression that has recurred three times cannot be guarded by a suite nobody runs.
So the guard that actually runs is tests/test_no_sql_rewriting.py (4 tests, no BigQuery, no env vars): no parsing helper has been reintroduced; /query hands authorize_query the caller's SQL BYTE FOR BYTE, driven through a recording stub with a query all three deleted rewrites got wrong; both configs carry a default dataset; and the probe's value comes from the caller's config. It pins the invariant rather than the symptom, and its docstring says why so it is not deleted as redundant.
They need their own env vars rather than the app's PROJECT_ID/DATASET_ID because setting those globally breaks 9 tests in test_query_caps.py, which mocks BigQuery with referenced tables hardcoded under `test-project`. Pre-existing, reproduced against HEAD, not caused here. (The implementer's docstring said eleven; measured nine; corrected.)

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, documented rather than hidden: the rewrite used to turn `FROM credible_sets` into `credible_sets_v`. A bare base-table name now resolves to the BASE TABLE, which is NOT column-identical to its view - credible_sets_v adds `maf` and reorders columns - so a human writing `FROM credible_sets` on /query silently loses `maf`. Data is correct, reach is unchanged (base tables were always allow-listed), MCP is unaffected since it emits only `_v` names. The _BASE_TABLES comment claimed base names are "accepted as aliases for their views", which is now true only for /schema and /tables/{name}/sample lookups; corrected.

FILED SEPARATELY: hla_associations_v's column names differ between dev and production (mlog10p/se/af vs mlogp/sebeta/af_alt), so get_hla_by_allele returns 112 rows against genetics_dev and 400s against genetics_results. That is not this change - the table resolves and then COLUMN resolution fails - and it means the worktree schemas represent a PENDING VIEW MIGRATION not applied to production, i.e. the dev dataset is a subset of a FUTURE production rather than of the current one. Same phenomenon as eyg and as g08's note about credible_sets predating the clustering swap, which suggests checking all the views.

title: genetics-mcp-server hardcodes `genetics_results`, so MCP tools 403 against the dev dataset
description:
FOUND while verifying the dev dataset (genetics-results-suite-g08). IT BLOCKS THE POINT OF THE DEV DATASET FOR THE CHAT PATH, so it is worth doing before much local development happens.

THE PROBLEM: genetics-mcp-server HARDCODES the production dataset name. `genetics_results.<view>` is baked into tools/executor.py's generated SQL, the `run_sql` tool description, config/defaults.py, and the shipped schema docs. Meanwhile genetics-results-db's `authorize_query` (api/main.py) builds `_ALLOWED_TABLE_IDS` from the DATASET_ID it was started with, and the BigQuery dry run resolves the unqualified `genetics_results.x` against the default project.

CONSEQUENCE, verified: against a db-api pointed at `genetics_dev`, every MCP-generated query is REJECTED 403. It FAILS CLOSED, which is the right direction and is not a security problem - but it means THE MCP TOOLS AND THEREFORE THE CHAT PATH DO NOT WORK AGAINST THE DEV DATASET AT ALL. Local development of anything that goes through chat-api's data tools is limited to production data until this is fixed.

The other two siblings are clean: genetics-results-api and genetics-results-browser name no BigQuery dataset (their `dataset_id` hits are datasets.yaml registry keys, unrelated).

WHAT TO DECIDE FIRST, because it shapes the fix: should the mcp server learn the dataset from configuration, or should it stop qualifying the dataset at all and let db-api resolve it? The second is cleaner - db-api already owns the allow-list and the dataset identity, and an unqualified view name would work against whatever db-api was started with - but it changes the generated SQL and the tool descriptions the model reads, and the schema docs shipped into the sandbox image would need regenerating.
NOTE THE SHIPPED SCHEMA DOCS ARE A SANDBOX ARTEFACT: sandbox/schema/ and sandbox/stubs/ are the trees the suite CLAUDE.md deliberately does NOT exempt from doc-drift checking, and genetics-results-suite-4h6.34 is already open about them being stale. Coordinate with it rather than regenerating twice.

CHECK WHILE FIXING: whether anything else in the suite assumes the production dataset name by literal. The db repo's own scripts/setup_bigquery.sh does a blind global `sed s/genetics_results/.../`, which is why the dev dataset had to be named `genetics_dev` rather than `genetics_results_dev`.

ACCEPTANCE: with db-api started with DATASET_ID=genetics_dev, an MCP query tool returns rows rather than 403, and the same code still works against production when DATASET_ID is unset. Add a test that pins it, since the failure mode is a 403 that reads like an auth problem rather than a configuration one.
close_reason:
Landed as mcp 7712f45 + suite d14ea47. Probe, implementation, blind completeness validation, one fix round. mcp suite 1487 -> 1494 passed / 74 deselected. ruff clean. Batched with 4h6.34 because both regenerate the same trees.

THE DECISION: MCP STOPS QUALIFYING ENTIRELY rather than learning the dataset name from config. Making it configurable would put the name in TWO places that must agree - point mcp at genetics_dev while db-api is on genetics_results and you get the same 403 with a knob on it. db-api already owns the dataset identity and the allow-list, so it is the single source of truth and the dev/prod difference collapses to the one variable that already existed.

DB-API NEEDED NO CHANGE AT ALL, which the probe established and I had not expected. `_qualify_tables` already rewrites bare view names using db-api's own DATASET_ID, and it runs as the FIRST statement of the query handler, before authorize_query - so the gate still compares fully-qualified ids either way. Verified the gate holds rather than assuming: explicitly naming a table outside the allow-list is still 403'd, and an unknown bare name 400s inside the dry run before anything executes.

THE BACKTICK TRAP WAS THE REAL RISK AND IT IS NOW PINNED. The rewrite is anchored on \b(FROM|JOIN)(\s+)<name>\b and does NOT match a backtick, so a bare-BUT-BACKTICKED name would sail past db-api unqualified and fail at BigQuery. Every emitter used backticks, so they had to come off WITH the prefix. Both failure modes were measured rather than reasoned about: backticked-bare gives 400 "must be qualified with a dataset", the old qualified form gives 403. The guard extracts every FROM/JOIN referent from all seven SQL-building methods and asserts each is bare and un-backticked, deriving CTE names by parsing the WITH clause instead of hardcoding the one alias in use.
The first draft of that guard COULD NOT REACH get_hla_by_allele - it parametrized over method names and called each with a positional "APOE", so the one method taking an allele was silently uncovered despite being one of the rewritten sites. Restructured to carry per-method arguments.

MY FILE LIST WAS INCOMPLETE IN THE WAY THAT MATTERED. I listed the mcp sites and said "regenerate the sandbox trees". But the 64 occurrences in sandbox/schema/*.md are generated from the SUITE's configs/datasets.yaml (69 sites), not from the SDK - so regeneration alone could never have removed them. That pulled datasets.yaml and gen-sandbox-docs.py's own README preamble into scope, and with them the doc-ownership obligations for datasets-yaml-schema.md and adding-datasets.md.

THE TOOL THE MODEL IS TOLD TO CALL FIRST WAS HANDING IT 69 COUNTER-EXAMPLES. The system prompt says "always call get_database_schema first"; that returns db-api's /schema, whose worked examples come from DB-API'S OWN COPY of datasets.yaml, which is a generated sibling and was not regenerated. Measured: 120,859 bytes containing 69 `genetics_results.<view>` examples, each of which 403s against genetics_dev. So the model was told "bare names" and then shown 69 qualified ones. Fixed by regenerating the sibling copies; /schema is now 119,993 bytes with ZERO occurrences and 13 bare `FROM credible_sets_v` examples.
NOTE FOR NEXT TIME: scripts/sync-datasets.sh resolves siblings next to the MAIN checkout via --git-common-dir, so running it bare from a worktree would have overwritten the copies the user's RUNNING dev servers use. It exposes SUITE_SIBLING_ROOT for exactly this; the fix used it with symlinks into the worktrees and verified both main checkouts stayed clean. The sibling copies are gitignored generated artifacts, so nothing from that half is committed.

A DOC RATIONALE WAS STALE AND IT WAS THE RATIONALE FOR THE THING BEING CHANGED. suite docs/project-spec.md justified qualifying with "db-api's unqualified-name fallback is a regular expression that cannot tell a table position from a string literal". `_qualify_tables` anchors on FROM/JOIN and its own docstring says that defect was the PREVIOUS implementation. The same stale claim was baked into gen-sandbox-docs.py's README preamble and therefore SHIPPED IN THE SANDBOX IMAGE. Both rewritten.

ACCEPTANCE, run rather than argued: ONE BINARY, TWO DATASETS, NO CODE CHANGE BETWEEN. `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM credible_sets_v` returned 525,271 against genetics_dev and 115,076,906 against production, each matching bq independently. All six public SQL-building methods exercised live against the dev dataset for two genes each; all 15 views plus 3 base-table aliases probed directly - 18/18 with rows, no errors, no 403s. Auth used db-api's documented fail-open branch with INTERNAL_API_SECRET unset, so the sandbox-token path remains untested here.

MODEL-FACING TEXT WAS TREATED AS PART OF THE CHANGE: the system prompt and its worked example, both tool descriptions, the SDK sql() docstring, the database_analysis skill and all 16 shipped schema docs now say the same thing, and the SDK docstring says WHY - one script serves dev and prod. A model told to qualify in one place and not another writes queries that pass in prod and fail in dev.

LEFT DELIBERATELY, with a note so nobody "fixes" it: genetics_results.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS in four suite files. Those are maintainer `bq` queries run straight against BigQuery, which has no default dataset and must name one. Not emitted SQL. (Correction to the implementation report, which placed these in the mcp repo - they are all in the suite repo.)
Also left: four mcp test fixtures, including a SQL-injection payload that find-and-replacing would have weakened.

FILED, and it is the more interesting finding: a CTE aliased to a view or base-table name is SILENTLY rewritten by _qualify_tables and returns the wrong rows with HTTP 200. `WITH datasets AS (...) SELECT * FROM datasets` gives 889 rows of datasets_v. Pre-existing in shape, but bee makes bare names the INSTRUCTED form, so the rewrite is now on the hot path for exactly the model-authored SQL the sandbox exists to run.

title: Wire the supervisor into the image and the manifest, clearing the deploy refusal
description:
LAST IN THE CHAIN, DELIBERATELY. scripts/deploy.sh REFUSES to apply k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml while that manifest declares neither command: nor args:, keyed on the manifest itself rather than on a ticket number so it self-clears the moment this lands. That refusal is what stops a Deployment with no supervisor being applied, SCHEDULING (it is not the Pending case) and CrashLoopBackOffing behind a kubectl apply that returned 0 - nothing rollout-statuses the sandbox, so the deploy would report success over a pod that can never serve. Do not clear it until the supervisor actually works locally.

Scope:
- Add args: to the sandbox container (or a CMD in the image) naming the supervisor module. The image ENTRYPOINT is the bare interpreter and ships NO CMD on purpose, so that a placeholder could never be mistaken for a real supervisor at runtime.
- COPY the supervisor into the final stage of sandbox/Dockerfile with --chown=65532:65532, and confirm sandbox/build-checks.py and sandbox/prune_venv.py still pass with it present (the prune allow-list and the placeholder gate both run over the staged trees).
- Re-run scripts/test-network-policies.py: it discovers the sandbox workload by file name OR object name OR pod labels and gates deploy.sh, and it asserts SANDBOX_ENABLED is literal true on BOTH db-api and results-api whenever a sandbox workload is discoverable.
- DOCUMENTATION OWNERSHIP, per CLAUDE.md: k8s/** and scripts/deploy.sh both require docs/project-spec.md and README.md IN THE SAME COMMIT; sandbox/** requires docs/code-execution-security.md. Re-derive the services table and any counts rather than trusting them.
- rollout.sh has no sandbox entry - genetics-results-suite-4h6.37 owns that. Do not duplicate it here.
- FILE-ONLY. genetics-results-suite-zg6 forbids applying anything to the live cluster, and the apply stays gated on ENABLE_SANDBOX derived from sandbox_pool_enabled in terraform.tfvars.

Files: k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml, sandbox/Dockerfile, docs/project-spec.md, docs/code-execution-security.md, README.md.
notes:
--- ADDED 2026-08-20 by the ralph-wiggum loop, from genetics-results-suite-4h6.85. ---
FLIP THREE MANIFESTS, NOT TWO. 4h6.85 added an explicit SANDBOX_ENABLED: "false" to
k8s/deployments/chat-backend.yaml and extended scripts/test-network-policies.py to assert it there
alongside db-api.yaml and results-api.yaml, on the SAME discovery path (file-name OR object-name OR
pod-label over k8s/deployments/, with the ENABLE_SANDBOX-keyed live relaxation).

WHY THIS BEAD IS THE ONE THAT HAS TO KNOW: chat-backend was previously SILENT on this flag, and the
preflight only inspected the two verifiers - so the deploy that creates the sandbox would flip two, the
preflight would report GREEN, chat-backend would default false, and run_analysis would be withheld from
every tool list with no signal anywhere. That is exactly what 4h6.85 closed. The preflight now FAILS if
chat-backend is left "false" or left undeclared once a sandbox workload is discoverable, so the failure is
loud rather than silent - but it will fail YOUR deploy if you flip only the two verifiers.

The docs that enumerate this were corrected in the same commit (docs/project-spec.md and
docs/code-execution-security.md's deploy-ordering table both said "db-api and results-api"). If you are
reading an older copy, do not trust the pair.

NOTE chat-backend is NOT a verifier - it mints sandbox tokens and gates the run_analysis tool rather than
authorizing requests, so it does not key require_sandbox_config(). It still has to track the flag.

--- NEW DEPLOYMENT TARGET, reported by the user 2026-08-22. Read this before planning the deploy. ---
The user has set up a SEPARATE STAGING DOMAIN in the daly environment, managed from a DIFFERENT MACHINE,
and states the intent plainly: "we will use another terraform/kube deployment for that domain name first",
i.e. the epic's first real deploy goes to STAGING, not to the production domain.

WHAT THIS CHANGES: the deploy at the end of this epic is no longer a single-shot against the only live
system. There is a staging target to prove it on first. That materially de-risks 4h6.50 and everything
gated behind it, and it means the deploy sequence should be written as staging-then-production rather than

--- TWO MORE STAGING BRING-UP ITEMS, recorded 2026-08-22 from the 4h6.93 review. ---

1. THE KEYCLOAK HELPER SCRIPTS DEFAULT TO PRODUCTION. scripts/keycloak-register-client.sh:50-51,
   keycloak-register-brainzzz.sh:24 and keycloak-get-token.sh:29 default OAUTH_ISSUER and
   OAUTH_RESOURCE_URL to https://genegenie.broadinstitute.org/... Registering a client during staging
   bring-up WITHOUT setting them writes the PRODUCTION audience into the STAGING realm, and staging logins
   then fail with an audience error naming a hostname that looks right. The scripts target the current
   kubectl CONTEXT (kubectl exec into the keycloak pod), so they do NOT mutate production - except
   keycloak-get-token.sh, which curls OAUTH_ISSUER directly and so drives a PRODUCTION login.
   SET BOTH VARIABLES EXPLICITLY when bringing up staging. Full analysis in the iced bead genetics-results-suite-4h6.94.

2. __Host- COOKIE PREFIXES, reported and NOT adopted (4h6.93 asked for the answer, not the change).
   oauth2-proxy is pinned at v7.14.3 (k8s/deployments/oauth2-proxy.yaml:18) and ALREADY MEETS all three
   preconditions the prefix requires - Secure (--cookie-secure=true), Path=/ (no --cookie-path set, so it
   defaults) and no Domain. Adopting it there is a one-value change to --cookie-name, and it would make
   the host-only property BROWSER-ENFORCED rather than merely default - i.e. it converts the cookie-domain
   hazard documented in docs/environments.md from "nothing checks it" into "the browser refuses it".

   (AUTH_SESSION_ID, KEYCLOAK_IDENTITY, KEYCLOAK_SESSION, KC_RESTART) are chosen internally by the server

   gateway. Note the gateway ALREADY rewrites those cookies at scripts/deploy.sh:188

   rewrite would have to change the path too and that risks the Apple callback this line exists to fix.

description:

- The SDK request APPEARS IN results-api sandbox_budget execution map. A 200 is not evidence - an INTERNAL_API_SECRET caller is also served, with no accounting at all. This is the exact check whose absence hid genetics-results-suite-0lf.
- The audit lines carry the real sub, sid and jti rather than unknown, are visible in docker logs, and a script that writes forged [user=...] text or a megabyte line onto the audit fd cannot produce a record that parses as genuine.

- An unset SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY FAILS THE EXECUTION rather than falling back to the shared secret or to no credential.
- Artifacts survive to the 15-minute retention boundary and are gone after it.

title: Add the run_analysis tool definition, handler and its MCP exclusion
description:
The single tool that replaces the data-access grid. TOOL_DEFINITIONS entry plus register_mcp_tools block in genetics-mcp-server tools/definitions.py, handler in tools/executor.py, following the shape list_capabilities and read_artifact landed in with genetics-results-suite-4h6.15.

Category orchestration, matching the two 4h6.15 tools, AND check the subagent exclusion BY NAME. 4h6.15 measured that a category-only exclusion left both new tools live in three of five subagent skills, including the skill.extra_tools fallback path that re-derives tools from settings.disabled_tools.

FAILURE HANDLING MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE HAPPY PATH. The benchmark counts script failures and retries because a failing script costs a full model roundtrip, and the measured distribution is bimodal - most turns at 1-2 roundtrips with a tail at 8+ from debugging loops, and that tail burns 35 percent of spend. Return STRUCTURED, ACTIONABLE errors: exception type, the traceback tail, WHICH limit fired when one did (wall clock, memory, output cap, artifact quota, pid budget), and the relevant SDK stub signature, so the model repairs in one attempt rather than three.

RETURN THE ARTIFACT MANIFEST - name, size, content_type per file, no paths and no execution id. read_artifact resolution depends on chat-backend recording that manifest against the jti and sid; without it the tool has nothing to resolve a name against.

notes:
--- ADDED 2026-08-17 from the genetics-results-suite-4h6.47 review. TWO HAZARDS THIS BEAD WILL WALK INTO ---

1. THE HOUSE ERROR-HANDLING STYLE WILL SWALLOW THE FAIL-CLOSED SIGNAL. tools/executor.py wraps essentially every tool method body in `except Exception as e:` returning an error dict - 40+ sites. `SandboxTokenUnavailable` is a plain RuntimeError. A run_analysis handler written in the house style WILL CATCH IT.
This cannot produce either forbidden fallback - no credential is ever sent, the client fails before the request - so it is not a security hole. What it does is turn an OPERATOR-VISIBLE MISCONFIGURATION (SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY unset) into a MODEL-VISIBLE "tool failed", which the model then RETRIES, repeatedly, against a sandbox that can never work. Let it propagate, or catch it specifically and surface it as an operator error that is not retryable.

2. THERE IS NO TOTAL DEADLINE ACROSS RETRY ATTEMPTS, and this bead owns the chat-turn budget. Each individual attempt is bounded correctly, but the sum is not: worst case for ONE execute() call is 5 (connect) + 10 (body write) + 255 (read) + 60 (Retry-After sleep) + 270 = about 585 SECONDS. The client offers no knob for this and does not document the number.
Decide here whether a ~10 minute worst case fits a chat turn. If it does not, the cap belongs at this layer - do not push it back into the client's per-attempt timeouts, which are correct as they stand and are derived from the supervisor's own worst-case hold time (max queued wait 120 + timeout_s 120 + margin 15).

3. FOR AWARENESS, not a defect: the client returns the supervisor's 200 body UNCHANGED, including unknown fields, and treats error.type as an OPEN STRING. Do not switch on a closed enum when rendering, and do not crash on a type you do not recognise - the contract reserves the supervisor's names as a MINIMUM, not an exhaustive set.

The reviewer's explicit verdict: it COULD NOT get run_analysis onto the MCP surface by any configuration, env var, empty-disabled-set, category, profile or dynamic-registration path it could construct.
TWO INDEPENDENT REGISTRATION-LAYER CONTROLS, both asserted against the ENUMERATED FastMCP tool list rather than against a constant:
1. membership of mcp_server._mcp_disabled - and the wider set was checked for INERT members (named but registered anyway); there are none, so the layer is real rather than decorative.
2. NO @mcp.tool() block for run_analysis at all. register_mcp_tools is a HAND-ENUMERATED LIST OF DECORATED CLOSURES and never iterates TOOL_DEFINITIONS; disabled_tools is only ever used to SUBTRACT. So no configuration can put it back. Measured: 54 tools on /mcp; 66 registrable blocks with an empty disabled set, still without this one; exactly one definition with no block, and it is run_analysis.
The `orchestration` CATEGORY is not used for bulk selection on the MCP path - it appears only in TOOL_PROFILES, read by get_anthropic_tools (chat and subagent), never by register_mcp_tools, which takes no profile. THE FORGERY WAS ONE LAYER OVER, ON A PATH THIS CHANGE TOUCHED BUT DID NOT COVER - the most valuable finding of the cycle. subagent.py dispatches with getattr(executor, name)(**tool_input) and had NO ALLOW-LIST: it would call ANY executor attribute the model named. DEMONSTRATED LIVE, not theorised: _execute_subagent_tool("run_analysis", {"code": ..., "user": "attacker@evil.example", "session_id": "other-sid"}) reached the handler with that identity, which would have become the sub/sid of BOTH per-execution JWTs and of every audit record. run_analysis is excluded from the subagent's DECLARED list, but the dispatcher never consulted the declaration - and the subagent's task text is written by the parent model, which DOES have run_analysis declared.
FIXED WITH AN ALLOW-LIST, NOT A SECOND STRIP: the dispatcher now refuses any tool_name not in the set _get_tool_definitions(skill) produced, before any branch. getattr is no longer the authorization decision, and the by-name `disabled` set becomes ENFORCEABLE rather than advisory. Verified: the reviewer's exact call now logs a refusal and the handler is never awaited.
EVIDENCE THE GUARD BITES: three PRE-EXISTING tests used invented tool names (some_tool / my_tool / fail_tool) and are now correctly refused; they were repointed at real declared names.

IDENTITY IS INJECTED, NEVER ACCEPTED. llm_service._execute_tool strips any model-supplied user/session_id and substitutes the authenticated pair into a NEW dict (so tool_input is not mutated), unconditionally setting both keys even when None so a model value cannot survive; both call sites pass them; run_analysis's parameters are keyword-only so nothing can be smuggled positionally. This wiring was OUTSIDE the bead's file list and is load-bearing - tool_input is splatted verbatim, so without it a model-invented user reaches the minter.
The DISPLAY AND LOG path now mirrors the strip too, and truncates the inlined script. A stripped-but-logged address still reads as identity in a log join, which is exactly what the 4h6.12 join exists to make trustworthy; and the block was putting up to 256 KiB of script on one log line and into the streamed markdown.

Pinned three ways: behaviourally; end-to-end with the signing key unset asserting ZERO REQUESTS SENT (the MockTransport WOULD have returned 200, so catch-and-fallback fails that assertion and catch-and-continue fails the error_type one); and structurally by an AST test asserting one try, no Exception, no bare clause, first handler SandboxTokenUnavailable - reordering fails it.

title: chat-backend: sandbox HTTP client that mints the tokens per execution
description:
New module in genetics-mcp-server, e.g. src/genetics_mcp_server/sandbox_client.py, called by the run_analysis handler. genetics-results-suite-4h6.9 implemented the minter and NONE of the transport; this is the transport.

MINTING CONTRACT (src/genetics_mcp_server/sandbox_token.py):
    from genetics_mcp_server.sandbox_token import mint_execution_tokens
    minted = mint_execution_tokens(user=<authenticated email>, session_id=<chat session id>)
    minted.execution_id  # uuid4, the jti of BOTH tokens
    minted.db_api        # aud db-api
    minted.results_api   # aud results-api
    minted.expires_at    # iat + 300
An optional execution_id= kwarg exists for when the caller has already chosen the /scratch directory name. THE TWO MUST BE THE SAME VALUE - execution_id IS the /scratch/<id> directory name, and that identity is what makes the 4h6.12 log join close across chat-backend, the sandbox SDK and db-api.

FAIL CLOSED: mint_execution_tokens RAISES SandboxTokenUnavailable when SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY is unset. That is deliberately an exception and not a None. DO NOT catch it and continue - every fallback from no-sandbox-token is either send no credential or send the shared secret, which are the two outcomes the whole mechanism exists to prevent. Fail the execution and surface it.

Scope:
- POST the contract body (code, execution_id, both tokens, user, session id, timeout) to the sandbox base URL, read from ONE configuration value that points at the in-cluster Service in production and at the local Docker container in dev. NO local/prod branch in the request flow.
- Client-side deadline above the supervisors 120s ceiling, and a DISTINCT error when the sandbox is unreachable: strategy Recreate plus terminationGracePeriodSeconds 130 means a deploy landing on an in-flight execution leaves no sandbox for up to ~130s, and that must not read as a script failure.
- Return the supervisors structured result unchanged for the tool layer to render.
- Never log the tokens.

Files: genetics-mcp-server/src/genetics_mcp_server/sandbox_client.py (new), src/genetics_mcp_server/config/settings.py.
close_reason:
Landed as genetics-mcp-server c56aa0c. Implementation + review + one fix round. Suite 1494 -> 1564 passed / 74 deselected, ruff clean. FILE-ONLY; nothing deployed, nothing on the cluster.

BUILT BLIND AGAINST THE CONTRACT, IN PARALLEL WITH THE SERVER, and that is the result worth recording. 4h6.38's §2 is the only thing binding the two sides - they cannot share a module, because the sandbox image installs only the SDK import closure and prune_venv.py deletes the rest. Review cross-read both as-built implementations: the same six-field set, constants matching ONE FOR ONE (1 MiB body, 256 KiB code, 60/120s, depth 2, 120s max wait, Retry-After 60), the same error.type names, and a supervisor Content-Type parser that accepts the bare application/json this client sends. Driving the supervisor with byte-for-byte the request this builds round-trips 200. WRITING THE CONTRACT FIRST PAID FOR ITSELF.

FAIL-CLOSED HOLDS, verified structurally rather than by inspection. mint_execution_tokens is OUTSIDE the try and INSIDE the retry loop; there is no `except Exception` anywhere in the module; and SandboxTokenUnavailable and SandboxError are SIBLING hierarchies, so the retry loop's `except SandboxError` structurally cannot catch it - with a test asserting the non-subclassing. The fail-closed test is load-bearing: it asserts both the raise AND zero requests sent, so catch-and-continue fails the first assertion and catch-and-fallback the second.

THE CONTRACT WAS WRONG ABOUT THE CLIENT DEADLINE AND THIS TASK FOUND IT. §2 said twice "above the 120s ceiling", but the supervisor may hold a request for the full 120s queued wait AND THEN run it for the full timeout_s - 240s worst case. A client following that literally times out on executions the supervisor is about to answer, and because a running child is deliberately not killed on disconnect, the retry then queues BEHIND THE CHILD IT ABANDONED. Implemented as max queued wait + timeout_s + margin = 255s; §2 corrected in the same cycle. Verified to REACH THE WIRE (the test reads request.extensions["timeout"]["read"]), not merely to be configured. Also verified no path can send an expired token: every attempt mints inside the loop, both retry branches fall through to a fresh mint, and worst case mint-to-response is 270s against the 300s TTL.

TWO MORE CONTRACT DEFECTS REPORTED AND FIXED IN THE DOC: Content-Type was ambiguous between the Transport paragraph (charset form) and the 415 row (bare form), so an exact string compare at either end would have 415'd every request - the supervisor parses the media type and a sentence now says so. And 409 TokenExpired's stated justification was wrong: the doc claimed the 429 retry was the only route, but the retry re-mints and 120s max wait cannot exhaust a 300s TTL. The defensive check stayed; the reason was corrected.

THE ONE REAL LEAK, found by review and not by tests: `error.type` was NOT passed through the redactor while `error.message` was, and was uncapped. Demonstrated with a mock supervisor echoing the minted db-api JWT in `type` - the full token reached the exception string AND the exception attribute, both of which 4h6.48 renders into model context. _redact's own docstring says it exists for "a misbehaving or impersonating peer", which is exactly the peer that would put a token in `type`. Now redacted and capped BEFORE `detail` is built, so every downstream error_type= kwarg gets the scrubbed value. Verified by deletion: removing the line fails the new test with the full JWT visible.
The rest of the leak surface was already closed BY THE CONTRACT'S DESIGN: tokens are body-only, and neither httpx nor httpcore logs bodies, which is a direct consequence of the nothing-in-a-header rule. No exception chain carries a body; a non-JSON error body yields nothing at all.

SandboxUnavailable is a distinct class from a script failure because strategy Recreate plus terminationGracePeriodSeconds 130 leaves no sandbox for ~130s when a deploy lands on an in-flight execution. Classification verified: ConnectError/ConnectTimeout and 502/503/504 unavailable, residual TransportError unavailable, residual TimeoutException deadline; catch ordering correct since ConnectTimeout subclasses both. Script errors arrive as 200 and never enter this path.

title: Supervisor: /scratch sub-quotas, artifact retention and the reaper
description:
Exceeding an emptyDir sizeLimit does NOT fail the write - THE KUBELET EVICTS THE POD. That kills the in-flight script and destroys every retained artifact from every earlier execution in the window, and a script triggers it deliberately with one 512Mi write. /scratch is 512Mi COMBINED artifact-plus-temp for all live and retained executions (there is no pod-level /tmp), so the supervisor must hold the budget and the kubelet must never be the thing that fires. Section 2, Staying under sizeLimit.

Scope:
- PER-EXECUTION ARTIFACT QUOTA of 64Mi on /scratch/<id>/artifacts. Over quota is a CLEAN ERROR RETURNED TO THE MODEL, not an eviction.
- PER-EXECUTION TOTAL QUOTA over all of /scratch/<id> (artifacts + temp + caches + inputs), sized so one execution plus the full retained set cannot approach 512Mi.
- AGGREGATE RETAINED-ARTIFACT CEILING across all retained artifacts/ directories, with OLDEST-FIRST EVICTION when a new execution would breach it, so retention degrades gracefully instead of accumulating until the kubelet intervenes.
- Enforcement by POLLING actual usage, not by trusting the child - the child writes straight to the filesystem and there is no syscall interposition available. Poll often enough that a fast writer is killed before 512Mi; the child is CPU-limited to 1500m, which bounds how fast it can get there.
- LIFECYCLE: on completion delete everything under /scratch/<id> EXCEPT artifacts/, which is retained 15 minutes so read_artifact has something to return and is then deleted unconditionally whether or not it was ever read. 15-minute TTL for executions that never complete. Retention does not survive a pod restart, and the startup wipe (skeleton bead) removes unrecognised entries.
- DO NOT put artifacts on a second emptyDir. It reads like the cleaner fix and does not work: sizeLimit eviction is a POD-LEVEL action, so a second volume changes which volume is over budget, not whether the pod survives, and the second volume dies with the pod anyway.

Landed as genetics-results-suite 09ed48d, batched with the other three because all four edit the same paths in sandbox/supervisor.py. In-process harness 90 -> 184 checks (identical across two consecutive runs); container mode 59 passed / 1 skipped -> 106 passed / 3 skipped. REVIEW FOUND NINE BLOCKING DEFECTS IN ROUND 1 AND ONE MORE IN ROUND 2, and the pattern is the one this epic keeps repeating: every one was a control that LOOKED enforced. The blind validator - deliberately not told what the change was for - independently reproduced the two worst.

/SCRATCH SUB-QUOTAS, ARTIFACT RETENTION AND THE REAPER.
64 MiB per-execution artifact quota, 192 MiB per-execution total, 256 MiB aggregate retained ceiling with oldest-first eviction, and a 15-minute reaper with two mechanisms - a registry pass and an orphan sweep that excludes live and queued ids by name. On completion everything under /scratch/<id> except artifacts/ is deleted; artifacts/ is retained 15 minutes and then deleted unconditionally whether or not it was ever read. Accounting on st_blocks with follow_symlinks=False, so the sparse-file bypass and symlink traversal are both closed. Artifacts stayed on the one emptyDir, for the reason the bead gives.

BLOCKING, REPRODUCED: ZERO-LENGTH FILES WERE FREE. _dir_bytes summed st_blocks*512 only and an empty file is 0 blocks, so NEITHER QUOTA COULD FIRE. 300,000 of them: status=ok, no limit, 8.6 MB charged against a 192 MiB quota, a 19.8 MB response, supervisor RSS 22 -> 166 MB, and the slot held 58.7s for a 34.9s child - 23.8s of it AFTER the reap, in build_manifest and _retain's rmtree, neither under a deadline, against a client deadline of 255s the supervisor could not honour. At 3M files the child kills the supervisor without tripping any limit. Now charged per-entry as well as per-block, with entry budgets the watchdog enforces (1024 artifacts, 20000 execution entries), a capped streaming manifest, and retained sizes measured once and cached instead of re-walked on every completion.

BLOCKING: THE BUDGET ARITHMETIC CONTRADICTED ITSELF IN TWO COMMENTS - one sizing the poll overshoot at ~200 MiB, the other budgeting 64 MiB for it. 256 + 192 + 200 = 648 MiB against a 512 MiB sizeLimit whose breach EVICTS THE POD, which is the single thing this bead exists to prevent. Both numbers were copied into the doc. Now stated ONCE: 256 + 192 = 448 <= SCRATCH_AGGREGATE_CEILING 480 = 512 - 32 reserve. _retain TRIMS artifacts/ back to quota before build_manifest runs (a burst killed at 64 MiB had been leaving 93 MiB retained, 46% over, in 0.31s); the len(sizes) > 1 guard is gone; and the watchdog gained an AGGREGATE retained+live check, because nothing had been measuring the total during a run and the total is the invariant that matters.

AND THE SECOND REVIEW CAUGHT THE FIX CARRYING ITS OWN VERSION OF THE SAME DEFECT. _trim_artifacts - the thing that MAKES the tree small - bounded its own enumeration by EXECUTION_ENTRY_BUDGET, the budget it exists to restore, then derived the cached retained size from that truncated sample. Measured on 25,000 files: 6,024 entries survived against a 1,024 budget, and the cached size was a 6x undercount (0.5 MiB reported vs 2.9 MiB real), scaling linearly. So _retained_total undercounted, the new aggregate check never fired, and _enforce_retained_ceiling summed fiction - four such retentions being ~548 MiB on a 512 MiB emptyDir. Reachable, not marginal: ArtifactQuota fires above 1024 entries and KILL_GRACE_S is 2s against a measured 13,000-14,000 file creations/s. Now drains in bounded passes; a pass that cannot see the whole directory drops its sample rather than ordering it against an unseen remainder, with three independent termination bounds.

A HARNESS CHECK WAS NONDETERMINISTIC AND WOULD HAVE MISLED 4h6.49. The trim check wrote 24 x 8 MiB UNPACED; on a fast tmpfs the whole 192 MiB completed inside the watchdog's first 200 ms scan gate, so the execution answered "ok" and the check failed - reproduced failing and passing on the same tree with no edits. A control assertion that flips on filesystem speed is not evidence the control works. Now paced so the write spans >=1.2s across >=12 scans while still exercising the over-quota trim path.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. The steady-state budget is exact; the TRANSIENT PEAK against a SIGTERM-trapping writer through KILL_GRACE_S is not bounded by the 32 MiB reserve, and the doc says so rather than implying the arithmetic covers it. build_manifest's artifacts_omitted is a FLOOR past the scan limit, not an exact count, and logs that it is. TRIM_ENTRY_CEILING is justified by reasoning, not measurement.
CONTRACT-VISIBLE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, deliberate and in the doc's budget table: a script writing more than 1024 artifacts or more than 20,000 files under /scratch/<id> is now KILLED with a limit rather than succeeding.
NEW TEST-ONLY KNOB: SANDBOX_RETENTION_S, same standing as SANDBOX_SCRATCH_ROOT - loud warning every start, may only SHORTEN, a larger value REFUSED at startup rather than clamped, never set by the image or the manifest. It exists so the reaper can be watched deleting a directory inside a test run; the harness takes --retention-s N and skips the check BY NAME otherwise.
NOTE FOR 4h6.49: REAPER_POLL_S is 30, so the 15-minute TTL is 15 min + up to 30s. This bead's dependent is instructed to assert the boundary exactly. Filed as part of 4h6.59.

title: Supervisor: read, cap, re-frame, stamp and forward the SDK audit stream
description:
This is the written specification handed over by genetics-results-suite-4h6.12, not a suggestion. 4h6.12 established BY RUNNING ATTACKS that no in-process mechanism can make these records trustworthy: a script forged records by calling logging.getLogger("genetics_mcp_server.sdk.audit").info(...) directly and by os.write to the audit fd number it reads from its own environment, and suppressed them via logger.disabled, the level, filters and handler removal. As long as the audited code and the emitter share an address space that is a property of where the code runs, not a list of gaps. Enforcement has to move out of the process, which means here.

Scope:
- Give the child a dedicated audit fd - GENETICS_SDK_AUDIT_FD, which sdk/client.py already reads - and hold the READ END in the supervisor.
- Apply the RATE, BYTE and PER-LINE caps ON THE READ END, where the child cannot reach them. The in-SDK refusal budget stays as it is; 4h6.12 measured that a per-execution ceiling keyed on a script-writable variable was both bypassable (19,622 lines/s after id rotation) and a SUPPRESSION PRIMITIVE (50ms of refusals silenced every genuine read afterwards). Do not reintroduce that shape on the read end: bound the stream, never silence a class of records on demand.
- TREAT THE CHILDS FRAMING AS UNTRUSTED INPUT. Re-parse and RE-FRAME every record before recording it. A child writing newlines, chosen [user=...] text, or megabyte lines must not be able to manufacture a record an operator reads back as genuine.
- STAMP [user=] [session=] [execution=] FROM THE TOKENS sub, sid and jti CLAIMS, which the supervisor holds. Do not ask the child who it is. sdk/client.py reads SANDBOX_USER, SANDBOX_SESSION_ID and SANDBOX_EXECUTION_ID from the childs own environment, which the script can rewrite, and today all three render unknown.
- FORWARD THE RESULT TO THE PODS STDOUT. The cluster logging agent collects the pods stdout and nothing else. The childs streams go into the supervisors pipe and nothing forwards them, so the control currently produces records nothing ingests.
- Keep the format compatible with the parser in genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/scripts/analyze_conversations.py. A test pins the analyzers marker constant as a substring of what the SDK writes.

DOC AND CODE DISAGREE HERE, DO NOT SILENTLY PICK ONE: section 6.2 of docs/code-execution-security.md and sdk/client.py both still describe the identity fields as read from the childs environment, written before 4h6.12 landed. The supervisor stamp is the intended answer; state in the doc which is authoritative once this lands, and say what the child-side values then mean (untrusted, or not set at all).

--- ADDED 2026-08-17 while discharging 4h6.44's cross-repo doc obligation. ---
docs/project-spec.md CLAIMED THE SUPERVISOR ALREADY FORWARDS THE SDK AUDIT STREAM TO THE POD'S STDOUT. It does not - sandbox/supervisor.py marks it STUB (genetics-results-suite-4h6.45) in two places and says "one hole remains". The bullet was corrected in place in commit a4a2e23, but RE-TRUING IT IS PART OF THIS BEAD: when the forwarding lands, that bullet and control 3 in docs/code-execution-security.md both change from "attributable now, still not collected" to collected.
ALSO: 4h6.44 deliberately left sdk/client.py almost untouched (one constructor docstring) BECAUSE THIS BEAD EDITS IT NEXT. Nothing there is reserved against you.
AND: the supervisor DOES already set SANDBOX_USER, SANDBOX_SESSION_ID and SANDBOX_EXECUTION_ID in the child's environment from the token's sub/sid/jti (ExecutionDir.child_env). That contradicts the older claim that all three render "unknown". They are still NOT trustworthy - the child owns its environment - which is exactly why this bead stamps from the tokens the supervisor holds rather than from what the child reports. The env prefix and the signed claims are not the same evidence.
close_reason:
Landed as genetics-results-suite b7cdbb4 and genetics-mcp-server 3f323ae. Implementation + sighted review + INDEPENDENT blind validation + one fix round. THIS WAS THE LAST STUB IN sandbox/supervisor.py.

THE DESIGN, AND WHY IT COULD NOT BE DONE IN-PROCESS: 4h6.12 established BY RUNNING ATTACKS that no in-process mechanism can make these records trustworthy - a script forged records by calling the audit logger directly and by os.write to the fd number it reads from its own environment, and suppressed them via logger.disabled, the level, filters and handler removal. While the audited code and the emitter share an address space that is a property of where the code runs, not a list of gaps. So: a third pipe created pre-fork, dup'd onto fd 4, named by GENETICS_SDK_AUDIT_FD, drained on a third thread sharing the reaped event and 4h6.39's deadline. Every line matched WHOLE against three admitted shapes; everything before the marker - INCLUDING THE CHILD'S OWN [user=...] PREFIX - discarded; the record re-emitted stamped from the tokens' sub/sid/jti, which only the supervisor holds. Caps on the READ end: 4 KiB per line (drop, never truncate), 1 MiB per execution, 100 records/s with a 200 burst. Past the byte budget it KEEPS READING AND DISCARDS, because stopping would block the child inside a successful data call.
NOT THE SHAPE 4h6.12 MEASURED AS BROKEN: budgets are per-execution objects keyed on nothing the child can write, no class of record is silenced on demand, a flooder spends only its own budget, and every drop is counted and announced.

A LATENT BUG THE SECOND FD EXPOSED, worth remembering: dup2(status_w, 3) silently closes the audit write end whenever the kernel hands one pipe fd 3 or 4. Unreachable with a single fixed fd; reachable the moment there were two. _relocate_above is load-bearing rather than defensive noise - review exercised ALL 20 orderings of the two pipe fds across 3-7 and confirmed fd 3 is always status and fd 4 always audit.

SIX BLOCKING DEFECTS. The best was found by the BLIND validator and broke this file's own rule:
1. THE BYTE BUDGET TRUNCATED A RECORD AND FORWARDED THE FRAGMENT AS GENUINE. The child controls every byte on the fd, so it controls where the boundary falls. Reproduced end-to-end with a real fork and real stdout: pad to budget-63 with oversize lines (which cost NO rate tokens, because length was checked before the token was taken), then write a record ending `rows: 999999999`. Pod stdout carried `rows: 9` under the real user's stamp, COUNTED AS records=1 - forwarded, not dropped - with nothing indicating alteration, and the shipped analyzer parsed it. The same trick shears a trailing ` error: X` off a real record. AUDIT_LINE_MAX_BYTES' own comment states the rule this broke: replace-don't-truncate.
2. THE REGEX DROPPED A RECORD THE SDK GENUINELY EMITS - found by the SIGHTED reviewer, in the OPPOSITE direction to everything else. _summarize_arguments returns the bare string <unavailable> (no braces) when bind_partial raises TypeError. Reproduced: forwarded=0, dropped_unparseable=1. Reachable by any ordinary buggy script - one extra positional, one unknown kwarg - and an operator reading dropped_unparseable=1 would conclude tampering.
3. THE CHARSET WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS while the comment claimed it was derived from the SDK. The SDK's real bound is pure ASCII; the class excluded only {}[]\, C0 and DEL, so up to 1024 bytes of chosen text passed per record. Reproduced as forwarded verbatim: U+2028, U+2029, U+0085 (each making the record TWO lines under str.splitlines(), which the harness itself uses), U+202E, U+00A0, fullwidth brackets. ATTRIBUTION HELD THROUGHOUT - brackets cannot get through, so no forged [user= and the analyzer cannot be fooled - but "cannot put arbitrary text on an operator's stream" was false.
4. _drain's SINK-FAILURE RECOVERY KILLED THE DRAIN THREAD: after sink=None the next block hit `sum(...) >= limit` with limit=None (reproduced TypeError), so the rest of the stream was not READ and a still-running child would fill the 64 KiB pipe and block in os.write inside a successful data call - exactly what keep-reading-and-discard exists to prevent. A defensive path strictly worse than no recovery.
5. "NO SDK CALLS" WAS NOT DISTINGUISHABLE FROM CHILD-SIDE SUPPRESSION and four places claimed it was. Reproduced: the two summaries are BYTE-IDENTICAL. What actually holds is narrower - SUPERVISOR-SIDE drops are distinguishable from "no calls". Child-side suppression remains fully available and silent, including simply rewriting GENETICS_SDK_AUDIT_FD to 1 so the SDK opens the stdout pipe instead. Scoped in all four places; making it detectable is 4h6.55's.
6. THE COPIED ANALYZER REGEX COULD NOT DETECT THE DRIFT IT CLAIMED TO. Byte-identical to analyze_conversations.py's SDK_CALL_RE today, but only the supervisor side was watched - if the analyzer moved, the harness kept testing its stale copy and passed. Now reads the sibling repo's literal with ast when present and SKIPS BY NAME when not, since the repos cannot import each other.
ALSO: _line spent a rate token before checking parseability, so junk consumed the bucket genuine records need (200 pad lines -> dropped_rate=63, records=0); dropped_over_budget counted newlines only; `rows: \d{1,12}` used Unicode \d so `rows: <arabic-indic digits>` was forwarded and int() read 123; the refusal-notice count is child-chosen while the comment claimed it could not be a channel for chosen text; one stdout stream carried two timestamp shapes.

14 OF THE 15 NEW CHECKS WERE VERIFIED FAILING against a mechanically reverted copy rather than merely added. WORTH REMEMBERING: the first draft of the truncation check PASSED pre-fix, because the cut happened to land on the space before the first digit. It was re-anchored at `rows: ` plus one digit, which is the real attack. A check that passes against the bug is worse than no check.

ONE DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE FIX BRIEF, accepted: oversize lines still do not spend a rate token. Charging them would recreate exactly the starvation being removed - an oversize flood would push GENUINE records into dropped_rate instead of forwarding them - and the forward it was meant to mitigate is now impossible, since the fragment is discarded rather than truncated-and-forwarded. The implemented rule is "nothing that is dropped spends a token", with junk volume bounded by the byte budget.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: nothing here holds against a setsid() escapee or a /proc/self/mem scan - 4h6.55 bounds those and the docs say so explicitly. Attribution and framing are bounded; TRUTH IS NOT, and endpoint_access is what holds under compromise. The env prefix and the signed claims are NOT the same evidence: the supervisor does set SANDBOX_USER/SANDBOX_SESSION_ID/SANDBOX_EXECUTION_ID in child_env for the SDK's own rendering, and the child owns them, which is exactly why the read end stamps from the claims.

THE RE-TRUING OBLIGATION IN THIS BEAD'S NOTES IS DISCHARGED: docs/project-spec.md's forwarding bullet (corrected in a4a2e23 while still false) is now true, and control 3 in docs/code-execution-security.md moves from "attributable now, still not collected" to collected. No STUB( markers remain in sandbox/supervisor.py.

title: SDK: send the per-execution token instead of INTERNAL_API_SECRET
description:
genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/sdk/client.py. Today the client attaches INTERNAL_API_SECRET from the environment to every request and its own docstring says so.

WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC - handoff from genetics-results-suite-0lf, MEASURED against the real ASGI app: results-api charges its four per-execution counters only when _sandbox_principal resolves an HS256 sandbox token. is_internal_caller ACCEPTS the shared secret, so such a request is served with NO ACCOUNTING AT ALL: 200, user_email mcp-tool, sandbox_budget._executions == {}. Closing the omit-the-header case left send-the-other-header open, and while the sandbox path uses the shared secret every quota control above it is inert.

Scope:
- Read the token file the supervisor wrote (path from the env var the supervisor sets), ONCE, and UNLINK it immediately. Read-once-and-unlink IS the entire mitigation under the one-shared-uid decision; leaving the file readable for the executions lifetime discards it.
- Select the token BY DESTINATION: aud db-api for BIGQUERY_API_URL, aud results-api for GENETICS_API_URL. They are audience-bound and not interchangeable - a cross-audience token is a hard 401 at both validators (db api/sandbox_auth.py, results-api app/core/sandbox_token.py).
- Stop attaching INTERNAL_API_SECRET on the sandbox path.
- ACCEPTANCE: a request from the SDK must APPEAR IN results-api sandbox_budget execution map. A boolean auth-works check is exactly the test shape that let this bypass through unnoticed in the first place; assert on the map.
- A TEST WILL FAIL WHEN YOU GET THIS RIGHT, deliberately: genetics-results-api tests/test_anonymous_surface.py::test_an_internal_secret_caller_is_served_but_not_accounted. It encodes todays behaviour on purpose. Update it in the same commit rather than working around it.
- SITTING DIRECTLY ON THIS PATH: genetics-mcp-server tools/executor.py builds an Authorization header only if api_secret is set and otherwise sends NO header (around line 304-312) - a silent fallback that becomes a bare 401 with no local signal once the anonymous surface is closed. Fix it or explicitly account for it here.

No cluster access.

THIS BEAD NAMED THE WRONG FILE AND THAT WAS A FINDING, NOT AN OBSTACLE. It says sdk/client.py attaches INTERNAL_API_SECRET; client.py never built an Authorization header. Across the entire SDK import closure there are exactly three Authorization sites, all in tools/executor.py, and review confirmed no other path attaches the secret on the sandbox path. client.py got ONE edit - a constructor docstring asserting the now-false behaviour - deliberately minimal because 4h6.45 edits that file next.

THE ACCEPTANCE IS A MEASUREMENT, WHICH IS THE ENTIRE POINT OF THIS BEAD. is_internal_caller accepts the shared secret and is served 200 with an EMPTY accounting map, so a status code proves nothing - that test shape is what hid 0lf. Measured end-to-end across two processes over real sockets: real minter -> supervisor-shaped O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW 0600 tokens.json -> real GeneticsClient -> captured Authorization bytes replayed into the real results-api ASGI app. jti present in sandbox_budget._executions with requests=1 and in_flight=0; token file gone after the first call; the db-api token 401s at results-api leaving the map empty. Review confirmed admit() runs in middleware BEFORE routing, so the measurement covers unmatched paths too.

THE CONTRACT WAS DERIVED FROM supervisor.py RATHER THAN FROM A DOC, as instructed: SANDBOX_TOKEN_FILE carries the PATH in the child's environment only; the file is /scratch/<execution_id>/tokens.json, pre-fork, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, 0600; the shape is flat and keyed by audience. Two children forked with different token files each got their own and the parent memo stayed False/None. The double-checked locking is correct - the loaded flag is published last.

title: Supervisor: deliver the per-execution tokens to the child by a read-once file
description:
Token transport inside the pod. Section 4 of docs/code-execution-security.md plus the minting contract recorded in the notes of genetics-results-suite-4h6.14.

1. The two tokens arrive in the BODY of chat-backend POST. The supervisor places them in the FORKED CHILD only and NEVER in its own environment - the supervisor holds no credentials at any point (residual 7).
2. Preferred over the childs environment: a mode-0600 file under /scratch/<execution_id>, whose path is named to the child by an environment variable. /proc/<pid>/environ is readable by any process with the same uid, and supervisor and child SHARE uid 65532, so a helper process the script spawns can read a token out of a siblings environment.
3. UNDER THE SHARED UID, MODE 0600 IS NOT THE PROTECTION - it does not exclude the child at all. THE PROTECTION IS LIFETIME: the SDK reads the file once and unlinks it (that half is the SDK bead), and /scratch/<id> is wiped regardless. DO NOT chown the file to 65533 and DO NOT set 0400. That is section 2 Permission contract for option (a), which is marked NOT IN EFFECT and returns EPERM here.
4. The supervisor RETAINS the sub, sid and jti claims from the token for the audit-stamping bead. It is the only component that both holds the token and sits outside the childs address space, which is why 4h6.12 assigned the stamping to it.
5. Nothing about the tokens is written to the pod spec, a ConfigMap or a Secret. k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml must keep receiving NEITHER INTERNAL_API_SECRET NOR SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY - exactly three Deployments mount the signing key (chat-backend signs, db-api and results-api verify) and the sandbox must not become a fourth.
6. Reject an execution whose token set is incomplete or whose audiences are wrong, rather than running it uncredentialed. An uncredentialed run is the case where db-api pre-existing fail-open branch (unset INTERNAL_API_SECRET disables auth with only a startup warning) becomes reachable.

title: Supervisor: stdout capture with the 8 MiB pipe cap and 64 KiB head-and-tail return
description:
The output cap row of docs/code-execution-security.md section 2. Two different limits, and conflating them loses one of them.

- PIPE CAP: the supervisor stops reading at 8 MiB from the childs pipe and kills the child (whole process group). This exists so that while True: print(...) cannot consume the SUPERVISORS memory before the wall clock fires - the wall clock alone does not bound it.
- RETURN CAP: 64 KiB back to the model, as first 32 KiB plus last 32 KiB with an EXPLICIT ELISION MARKER between them. Head AND tail because the model needs the traceback, which is at the tail; a head-only truncation is the single most expensive failure shape, because the model then debugs against output it cannot see and burns another roundtrip. The 64 KiB figure is a CONTEXT-BUDGET decision as much as a security one: the epics justification is the context-accumulation curve (39k to 117k tokens per turn) and an unbounded stdout defeats it.
- Cap by BYTES, and do not slice a multi-byte character in half when cutting the head and tail.
- Truncation must be VISIBLE in the returned payload, never silent.
- stderr: decide and record whether it is interleaved into the same stream or returned separately. The audit stream is a SEPARATE dedicated fd (owned by the audit bead) and must not be mixed into stdout here.

title: Supervisor: wall clock, RLIMIT_AS, oom_score_adj and process-group pid policing
description:
The per-execution resource controls the supervisor owns, all specified in docs/code-execution-security.md section 2 and its handoff row for 4h6.14.

- WALL CLOCK: 60s default, 120s HARD CEILING, not overridable by the model. terminationGracePeriodSeconds is 130 in the manifest precisely so the supervisor has room to reap the child, answer the in-flight request and wipe the execution directory.
- MEMORY: set RLIMIT_AS on the child below the 3Gi cgroup limit with explicit supervisor headroom, so an over-large allocation gets a clean MemoryError inside the child rather than an OOM kill. The cgroup OOM killer is NOT a guarantee about which process dies: the kernel picks by oom_score, a heuristic over RSS, and gVisor changes the accounting because the sentry holds memory on the applications behalf.
- oom_score_adj: supervisor low (about -500), child high (about +500), so if the OOM killer does fire it aims at the child.
- PID BUDGET IS THE SUPERVISORS JOB, NOT RLIMIT_NPROC. This is the direct cost of the one-shared-uid decision (4h6.7, option (b)): RLIMIT_NPROC is a limit per REAL UID across the pid namespace, so a child forking to its limit also stops the SUPERVISOR forking - the fork bomb takes out the supervisor instead of being contained. Put the child in its own process group (setsid/setpgid), watch the group size, and kill the WHOLE GROUP above a threshold sized from what a legitimate script needs (tens of processes, not hundreds). Treat RLIMIT_NPROC as advisory only. The kubelet pod_pids_limit of 1024 is the outer backstop and is explicitly not a substitute.
- EVERY kill path - timeout, pid budget, output cap, quota - must kill the whole PROCESS GROUP, not just the direct child. A spawned grandchild that outlives the execution shares the pod with the next user, and concurrency 1 plus replicas 1 guarantees there IS a next user in the same pod.

NOT PROVABLE IN LOCAL DOCKER: whether oom_score_adj is writable and whether process-group inspection through /proc behaves the same under runsc. Implement and test locally, and leave those two to the deploy-window verification bead rather than asserting them.

notes:

1. A PGID-BASED REAPER CANNOT DO THE JOB. Measured: a grandchild that calls setsid() leaves the group; killpg(job.pgid, SIGTERM) and SIGKILL both returned ESRCH while the grandchild survived and kept running. See genetics-results-suite-4h6.55 - a PID namespace is the only mechanism found that closes this as a class.
2. job.pgid = pid is ASSERTED, NEVER READ BACK with os.getpgid(pid) and never re-validated before signalling. Once waitpid reaps the child the pgid is STALE and the pid is RECYCLABLE, so a later killpg can hit an unrelated process group - plausibly THE NEXT EXECUTION'S CHILD. Re-validate before every signal.
3. THE WALL CLOCK ALONE DOES NOT FREE THE SLOT. Measured before the 4h6.39 fix round: a reaped child whose detached grandchild held the output pipe's write end kept the slot for 40s and made a second user wait 36s, because the drain join had no deadline. 4h6.39 added a drain deadline; do not remove it, and do not assume "child reaped" means "execution over".

WALL CLOCK, RLIMIT_AS, oom_score_adj, PID POLICING.
One watchdog thread per execution owns the wall clock, the pid budget and both quotas. RLIMIT_AS 2560 MiB child-side. Child oom_score_adj +500. Kill path SIGTERM to the group, 2s, SIGKILL.

NO PGID IS CACHED, AND THE REASON IS A MEASURED DEFECT THE BEAD DID NOT PREDICT. Reading os.getpgid(pid) immediately after the fork returns THE SUPERVISOR'S OWN GROUP - the parent routinely wins the race against the child's setsid(). title: Local execution backend: run the sandbox image in plain Docker
description:
The user requires an implementation that RUNS IN THE LOCAL DEV ENVIRONMENT BEFORE ANYTHING IS DEPLOYED, and this is the bead that makes every later sandbox bead developable and testable without a cluster. Decided approach: the supervisor speaks HTTP, and locally the SAME image runs in a plain Docker container instead of a gVisor pod. Highest fidelity available - same image, same entrypoint, same caps, same /scratch path - minus the gVisor syscall boundary and the NetworkPolicy.

THE PROD/DEV DIFFERENCE MUST BE A DEPLOYMENT DETAIL, NOT A SECOND CODE PATH. chat-backend reads one sandbox base URL from configuration and does exactly the same thing in both environments. Do not add a local/in-process branch to the request flow: a fork in the code is the shape that leaks into production config later. What runs locally must be the same program that runs in the pod.

Scope:
- A script (e.g. scripts/run-sandbox-local.sh) that builds sandbox/ and runs the container. The build needs a staged genetics-mcp-server checkout at sandbox/.sdk-src - see the sandbox/Dockerfile header and scripts/build.sh, which already stages it; a bare docker build sandbox/ fails by design.
- Run it with --read-only, --cap-drop ALL, --security-opt no-new-privileges, --user 65532:65532, a writable mount at exactly /scratch, and memory/cpu limits mirroring the manifest (3Gi, 1500m).
- /scratch MUST be at that exact path. read_artifact refuses any artifacts dir that does not resolve under a HARDCODED /scratch/ prefix (executor.py, 4h6.15), and that prefix is the structural safety property, not a configurable.
- PORT COLLISION: the container port is 8080 and so is the local db-api (see genetics-results-suite-r9e for the running dev stack). Publish a DIFFERENT HOST PORT and keep the container port at 8080 so the manifest and the local run agree.
- The container must reach the LOCAL db-api and results-api, not cluster ClusterIPs. Set GENETICS_API_URL and BIGQUERY_API_URL to host-reachable addresses (host.docker.internal with --add-host on Linux). The manifest values are cluster FQDNs pinned by hostAliases and do not resolve locally.
- RECORD WHAT FIDELITY IS LOST, in docs/code-execution-security.md: no gVisor sentry, no NetworkPolicy so no egress allow-list at all, no kubelet pod_pids_limit, and Docker default seccomp rather than the RuntimeDefault profile. Any control whose ONLY enforcement is one of those is not exercised locally and must be verified at deploy time.

Files: scripts/run-sandbox-local.sh (new), docs/project-spec.md, docs/code-execution-security.md, README.md. Coordinate with genetics-results-suite-r9e, which owns bringing the rest of the dev stack up from the worktree branches.
