Landed as genetics-results-suite a97d47c. Implementation + review + one fix round. In-process harness 90 checks unchanged; new container mode 59 passed / 1 skipped. LOCAL DOCKER ONLY - no kubectl, no gcloud mutation, no terraform apply, nothing near a cluster.

THE SANDBOX NOW RUNS ON THIS MACHINE. scripts/run-sandbox-local.sh builds sandbox/ and runs THE SAME IMAGE, SAME ENTRYPOINT, SAME SUPERVISOR under plain Docker, published on 127.0.0.1:8081. The supervisor is passed as the container's command at `docker run` time - NO CMD was added to the image and k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml is UNTOUCHED, verified (`Cmd=null`, `Entrypoint=["/usr/bin/python3"]`), so deploy.sh's refusal still fires and 4h6.50 is still the bead that clears it.

THE SDK IS STAGED FROM A LOCAL CHECKOUT, not cloned from GitHub as build.sh does, because MASTER OF genetics-mcp-server HAS NO src/genetics_mcp_server/sdk - only the worktree does. Each candidate is gated on that directory existing, so the main checkout is rejected on its merits rather than by ordering luck; review confirmed it cannot silently build with an absent or stale SDK, and that the failure when none is found is loud. This is the check-worktree-paths failure class and it was written not to have it.

WHAT ONLY BECAME VISIBLE IN A CONTAINER, and it is the reason this bead exists before 4h6.49: in-process the harness ALWAYS ran with SANDBOX_SCRATCH_ROOT set, which the supervisor itself warns is test-only. This is the first run where /scratch is really /scratch, the rootfs is really read-only and prewarm() actually executes. NO WIRE-CONTRACT OR SUPERVISOR DEFECT SURFACED - every shared check answered identically in both modes, which is real evidence for 4h6.39's fidelity rather than an absence of testing.
18 of the 59 container checks are image properties in-process cannot see at all: read-only rootfs, no writable /tmp, no pip/setuptools/google-auth, the SDK importing, matplotlib producing a PNG from the baked font cache, no credential in the child's environment, and the child running as 65532 rather than the 65533 the image advertises.

THE FIDELITY REPORT IS THE DELIVERABLE, NOT A COURTESY. The failure this task can cause is a developer verifying something locally, believing it holds in the pod, and being wrong. Every unreproduced control is printed on every start and listed in the doc: gVisor (runc not runsc), no NetworkPolicy so egress is unrestricted - review MEASURED the metadata server returning a live ya29 access token for the dev VM's node service account, so that warning is not theoretical - --pids-limit per container not per pod, Docker's default seccomp rather than containerd RuntimeDefault, ordinary Docker DNS instead of dnsPolicy None plus hostAliases, ephemeral-storage which has NO LOCAL FORM AT ALL, and restartPolicy.

REVIEW FOUND ONE OMISSION AND IT WAS THE DANGEROUS KIND. /scratch is a tmpfs, therefore page cache IN THE CONTAINER'S OWN MEMORY CGROUP - measured 113 MiB -> 414 MiB after writing 300 MiB. The pod's emptyDir carries no medium: Memory, is node-disk-backed, and is charged to ephemeral-storage (1Gi/2Gi), NEVER to limits.memory 3Gi. 4h6.41 is the next bead and must size RLIMIT_AS below the 3Gi cgroup with headroom: tuned locally it is up to 512 MiB more conservative than the pod needs, and a script holding 2.6 GiB RSS while /scratch holds 400 MiB is cgroup-OOM-killed locally and sails through in the pod. 4h6.46 polls /scratch against a 512 Mi budget and would never see the interaction locally at all. Now stated with the measurement and both consumer beads named.

terminationGracePeriodSeconds 130 was REPRODUCED rather than listed: --stop-timeout 130, and --stop now uses docker stop plus docker rm rather than rm -f, because rm -f SIGKILLs and would skip exactly the drain-reap-answer-wipe the 130s exists to buy.

THE HARNESS OVERCLAIMED ITS OWN COVERAGE, which matters because 4h6.49 reads its output. It said everything unavailable is "reported as skipped, never silently dropped" - but container mode reported ONE skip while never invoking FIVE WHOLE GROUPS, about 46 checks, so "59 passed / 1 skipped" read as near-complete coverage of the 90. Container mode now prints the NOT RUN groups with the reason each is unreachable over the wire, plus a partial-coverage line saying the total is not a fraction of the in-process run. skip()'s narrower claim - a check INSIDE a group that ran - is retained and stated as such.

THE 4h6.55 MEASUREMENT, taken from inside a real execution in the actual image and INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED IN REVIEW (CapEff 0, NoNewPrivs 1, Seccomp 2): unshare(NEWNS), (NEWPID), (NEWUSER), the combination and setuid(65533) ALL return EPERM. THE CONTROL EXPERIMENT IS THE RESULT: same uid, same --cap-drop ALL, same no-new-privileges, ONLY seccomp=unconfined changed -> unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER) SUCCEEDS and nested NEWNS|NEWPID also succeeds. THE BLOCKER IS THE SECCOMP PROFILE, NOT THE CAPABILITY SET, and the distinction is invisible unless you vary the profile because both produce the identical EPERM. The naive reading - "capabilities are dropped, therefore namespaces are impossible, therefore option (c) is dead" - is WRONG.
Two refinements from review, both recorded because they constrain how the fix must be written: NEWNS and NEWPID ALONE still return EPERM even unconfined, so ONLY the CLONE_NEWUSER-first route works and a fix calling unshare(CLONE_NEWPID) directly fails anyway; and setuid's blocker really is the capability set, so it was moved out of the seccomp table.
CAVEATS THAT KEEP THIS FROM BEING AN ANSWER: it says NOTHING about gVisor, which is what actually runs - runsc implements unshare in the sentry and is not installed here - and the pod uses containerd RuntimeDefault rather than Docker's default profile. Relaxing the profile also means a custom seccomp profile, which the security doc lists under REJECTED CONTROLS because it needs a DaemonSet-distributed localhostProfile. Option (c) is not free.

FILED THIS CYCLE: genetics-results-suite-6um (P2) - sandbox_client defaults SANDBOX_URL to 127.0.0.1:8080, which on this machine IS THE LOCAL db-api, so a chat-backend started without SANDBOX_URL POSTs /execute at db-api and gets a confusing sandbox error instead of "nothing is listening". 4h6.40 published on 8081 precisely because 8080 was taken. And genetics-results-suite-e96 (P3) - run-sandbox-local.sh is in neither CLAUDE.md's doc-ownership table nor check-doc-drift.sh, so changing it will never warn that the two docs it now owns have gone stale.

LEFT NON-BLOCKING, recorded in review: the NetworkPolicy bullet discusses only egress while the pod's ingress admits chat-backend alone; --regen --no-build now exits 2 rather than silently no-opping; and rev-parse now uses --path-format=absolute so a plain checkout run from another cwd no longer misdiagnoses as "no checkout found".

title: Supervisor: process skeleton, /health, /execute and the per-execution fork
description:
The process the sandbox pod actually runs, and the thing whose absence makes k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml unapplyable today. New file under sandbox/ in this repo (e.g. sandbox/supervisor.py), part of the image build context. It may import ONLY the standard library plus what sandbox/requirements.txt already ships: sandbox/prune_venv.py deletes pip and everything outside the SDK import closure, so a new third-party dependency has to be added there deliberately and asserted in sandbox/build-checks.py.

Scope:
- Serve 0.0.0.0:8080. GET /health (the readinessProbe already points at it). POST /execute per the contract bead.
- ONE execution at a time, queued beyond that. With replicas 1 and strategy Recreate this is the cluster-wide bound, and it is what removes cross-user co-tenancy inside the pod.
- Per execution create /scratch/<execution_id>/ with artifacts/ and tmp/, and set the CHILD environment: TMPDIR, HOME, MPLCONFIGDIR, XDG_CACHE_HOME, PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX all inside that directory, plus SANDBOX_ARTIFACTS_DIR=/scratch/<id>/artifacts. sandbox/Dockerfile deliberately leaves all of these unset because they are per-execution; a fixed pod-wide value recreates the cross-execution shared directory that removing the pod-level /tmp was meant to prevent.
- Copy the baked font cache from $GENETICS_MPLCACHE (/genetics/mplcache) into the per-execution MPLCONFIGDIR before the child runs. The root filesystem is read-only.
- Startup assertions BEFORE accepting any execution, both required by the handoff table in docs/code-execution-security.md: /etc/nsswitch.conf exists and lists files before dns for the hosts database; and prewarm() ($GENETICS_PREWARM, sandbox/prewarm.py) called before the first fork, letting PrewarmError crash the pod rather than catching it.
- At startup, wipe any /scratch entry that does not belong to a live or still-retained execution. A crash mid-execution must not leave a readable directory behind.

MUST NOT setuid AND MUST NOT chown. Supervisor and child share uid 65532 - option (b), DECIDED and FORCED by 4h6.7. drop ALL plus allowPrivilegeEscalation false leave no CAP_SETUID, CAP_SETGID or CAP_CHOWN, and setuid(65533) / chown(65533) were MEASURED to return EPERM in this pod shape. The image advertises SANDBOX_CHILD_UID=65533; it names a uid nothing can switch to. A supervisor written against option (a) fails at runtime, not at review. Section 2 Permission contract is retained in the doc but marked NOT IN EFFECT.

DO NOT add command: or args: to k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml in this bead. scripts/deploy.sh refuses to apply that manifest while it declares neither, and that refusal is the only thing stopping a Deployment with no working supervisor being applied, scheduling and CrashLoopBackOffing behind a kubectl apply that returned 0. The wiring bead at the end of this chain clears it.

Deliberately NOT here, each owned by a named sibling bead: wall clock and rlimits, output caps, token delivery, audit forwarding, quotas and the reaper.

Files: sandbox/supervisor.py (new), sandbox/requirements.txt and sandbox/build-checks.py only if a dependency is unavoidable, docs/code-execution-security.md.
close_reason:
Landed as genetics-results-suite 45b3670. Implementation + TWO parallel validators (contract conformance and adversarial isolation) + one fix round. Harness 77 -> 90 checks, no cluster and no credentials needed. FILE-ONLY; k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml deliberately untouched, so scripts/deploy.sh still refuses to apply and nothing can reach a cluster.

WHAT LANDED: sandbox/supervisor.py, ~1000 lines, STDLIB ONLY (prune_venv.py deletes everything outside the SDK import closure, so a third-party import fails at runtime rather than at review). /health and /execute per §2, one execution at a time with at most two waiting, per-execution scratch directory and child environment, startup assertions (nsswitch, prewarm before the first fork with PrewarmError left uncaught), startup wipe of unrecognised /scratch entries, fork and reap. NO setuid and NO chown anywhere - 4h6.7 forced one shared uid and both were MEASURED to return EPERM in this pod shape, so a supervisor written against the documented-but-not-in-effect permission contract would pass review and fail at runtime.

CONVERGENT WITH THE CLIENT, built blind against the same document. Driving this supervisor with byte-for-byte the request 4h6.47 builds round-trips 200 with every response field present and correctly typed. No interop failure found on any path.

THE CONTRACT'S ONE OPEN QUESTION IS SETTLED: the child reports its exception on a DEDICATED STATUS PIPE, not through stdout - the traceback is exactly what the 64 KiB tail cap elides, and stdout parsing lets a script forge its own error object by printing one.

FIVE DEFECTS FOUND BY VALIDATION, each MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER rather than argued:
1. THE STATUS PIPE ONLY HALF-CLOSED THE FORGERY IT WAS BUILT FOR. fd 3 is open and writable in the child because the fork is not followed by an exec. A script writing a status record, printing, and exiting 0 came back as status "error" with exit_code 0 - a combination the contract's status table declares IMPOSSIBLE, and the client returns the body unchanged, so the model is told a successful analysis failed. Prompt-injection reachable per §6.4. FIXED: the supervisor's own observation wins - exit 0 and no signal is `ok` and the record is ignored, which costs nothing legitimate because an uncaught exception implies a non-zero exit.
2. THE DRAIN HAD NO DEADLINE, so a reaped child did not end the execution. A detached grandchild holding the output pipe's write end kept the slot for 30s and MADE A SECOND USER WAIT 28s, with duration_ms reporting 30016ms for a child that lived 16ms. CRITICALLY, landing 4h6.41's wall clock as specified would NOT have fixed this: the process group was already gone (killpg returned ESRCH) and the slot was held by A PIPE JOIN, not by the child. FIXED: a grace period after the reap, the supervisor closes the read ends itself, duration_ms measured at waitpid. Second user now waits 0.2s; duration_ms is 16.
3. EXECUTION_ID_RE ACCEPTED A TRAILING NEWLINE - `re.match` with `$` matches before a final newline - on the ONE field whose own comment calls it strict "because this value names a filesystem path". It created a directory literally named with the newline and echoed it in the response: a log-injection primitive. Now \A..\Z with fullmatch. THE CLIENT INDEPENDENTLY HIT THE IDENTICAL HOLE the same day; the anchoring convention was the trap, not either implementation.
4. TWO STUB SEAMS DESCRIBED THEMSELVES FALSELY - the exact failure class 4h6.54 had just spent a cycle removing. `_audit_pipe` was DEFINED AND NEVER CALLED while the section header claimed every seam was wired, and it is not a drop-in: 4h6.45 must create the pipe BEFORE the fork, pass the fd into _child_main and extend the _close_inherited_fds keep-set. `_apply_limits` promised RLIMIT_AS on the child and a LOWERED oom_score_adj on the supervisor, neither possible from the parent after the fork without CAP_SYS_RESOURCE, which is dropped; now split into a parent-side half and an in-child half that is actually called, with both docstrings naming the capability. `_drain`'s docstring claimed it blocks the child at the cap when it actually discards to EOF - THE CODE WAS THE SAFER OF THE TWO, so the comment was corrected rather than the behaviour, since 4h6.42 would otherwise have been written against a false premise.
5. The harness never asserted Retry-After reached the wire, which the client's retry loop depends on. Now driven over real HTTP with three concurrent executions.

VERIFIED CORRECT AND NOT TO BE RE-LITIGATED: fd hygiene in the child (/proc/self/fd enumeration, not close-on-exec, which would be a no-op without an exec - no listening socket or client connection reaches the child); the duplicate-id admission race (six concurrent same-id requests give one 200 and five 409); manifest filtering (symlink, FIFO, subdirectory, trailing-space name and hardlink all omitted); status "timeout" and "limit" genuinely unreachable by exhaustion with no fabricated limit values; the Dockerfile COPY introducing no third-party import and lying outside prune_venv's reach; and docs/project-spec.md NOT re-importing contract figures §2 owns.

UNILATERAL RESOLUTIONS OF CONTRACT GAPS, all judged right by review: duplicate-id checked at accept AND dequeue (strictly better than the doc - two identical ids in the QUEUE would both pass a pure filesystem test, since directories are created at dequeue); chunked or absent Content-Length refused with 400 (the 1 MiB cap's whole value is refusing before reading, which chunked forbids); aud accepted as a single-element list (a harmless superset, and it is a consistency check not authentication); child cwd = /scratch/<id>/tmp (pointing at artifacts/ would promote every scratch file into the manifest).
WEAKEST OF THEM, recorded for 4h6.46: retention state is IN MEMORY, so a restart both deletes artifacts the 15-minute window promised and frees the id early - the bijection the contract calls for is only per-process. _retained_ids also grows without bound today.

NOT FIXED HERE, ESCALATED AS genetics-results-suite-4h6.55 (P0, blocking 4h6.50 and 4h6.51): FORK WITHOUT EXEC PLUS ONE SHARED UID LEAVES NO ISOLATION BETWEEN EXECUTIONS. A child was measured recovering a QUEUED user's tokens, source code and session id by four independent routes, including a raw /proc/self/mem scan that also recovered an ALREADY-COMPLETED execution's - which no amount of clearing references can close, since freed Python strings stay in arenas COW hands over. Also measured: a child reading and OVERWRITING another execution's artifacts, and a detached setsid() grandchild reading the NEXT execution's mode-0600 token file inside its read-once window while its own execution looked perfectly normal to chat-backend. Local single-user development is deliberately NOT blocked, because every finding is cross-user.

title: Sandbox HTTP contract: define the POST /execute and /health wire shape
description:
The seam between chat-backend and the sandbox supervisor, written down because it cannot be shared as code. The image pip-installs only the genetics SDK import closure from genetics-mcp-server and sandbox/prune_venv.py deletes everything else, so the two sides cannot import one module. Two implementers building each side against different assumptions is unrecoverable without redoing both.

Write it into docs/code-execution-security.md as a new subsection (section 2 or 4) and mirror the essentials into docs/project-spec.md. Specify:

- POST /execute request body: the Python source, execution_id, the two tokens (db-api and results-api audiences), the user and chat session id, and an optional timeout BOUNDED by the 60s default / 120s hard ceiling that the model cannot raise.
- execution_id IS the /scratch/<id> directory name AND the jti of both tokens. One value everywhere. That identity is what closes the log join across chat-backend, the sandbox SDK and db-api (4h6.9, 4h6.12).
- Response: exit status, capped stdout (64 KiB head+tail with an explicit elision marker), a structured error object (exception type, traceback tail, and which limit fired if one did), and the ARTIFACT MANIFEST - name, size, content_type per file, NO paths and NO execution id - which section 6 read_artifact resolution depends on.
- GET /health, already named by the readinessProbe in k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml.
- Tokens travel in the BODY only. Never pod env, never a ConfigMap, never a Secret: chat-backend cannot set env on a running pod, and a pod-spec value turns a 300s per-execution credential into a static pod-lifetime one.

Files: docs/code-execution-security.md, docs/project-spec.md.
close_reason:
Landed as 5b02b6c. Implementation + review + one fix round. FILE-ONLY, docs only - no code, and the contract is written before either side is built, which is the point of the bead.

PLACED AT THE END OF SECTION 2 of docs/code-execution-security.md, because every value on the wire is a section 2 decision row's WIRE FORM - the 60s/120s wall clock, the 64 KiB output cap, concurrency 1, /scratch/<execution-id> and its quotas, the artifact manifest. Section 4 owns the CREDENTIAL, which the contract carries but does not re-decide; it cross-references rather than restating. docs/project-spec.md carries a POINTER ONLY: the first draft mirrored the port, the queue depth, the timeouts and the manifest fields, and the depth is the number the security doc itself calls "the one tunable number here" - having it in two files is exactly the enumeration rot CLAUDE.md warns about. All figures were removed from the spec.

DECIDED, NOT OMITTED: NO HTTP-LAYER AUTH. The pod holds no credential to verify against, and giving it one would violate section 4. The ingress allow-list (cluster) and loopback bind (docker) ARE the authentication. Everything travels in the body; the supervisor decodes the tokens UNVERIFIED purely to check the caller's own consistency, and never holds a signing key. Written down as a decision with its reason so nobody "fixes" it later.

THE CONTRACT IS IDENTICAL UNDER KUBERNETES AND PLAIN DOCKER, which 4h6.40 needs. Nothing on the wire touches the downward API, a service account or cluster DNS, and the four deployment-only differences (gVisor + pool, NetworkPolicy, hostAliases, emptyDir) are enumerated so nobody adds a wire field to compensate for one.

THE VALUE WAS IN THE STATE QUESTIONS, NOT THE FIELD LIST. The review's framing was the right one - not "is it well written" but "would an implementer of ONE side, who cannot see the other, build something that interoperates". Seven gaps were found where two implementers would each pick something reasonable and incompatible:
- A REPEATED execution_id had NO SPECIFIED BEHAVIOUR, and it is a NORMAL event rather than an edge case: the contract itself specifies a 429 retry path, artifacts are retained 15 minutes, and section 4 explicitly supports passing execution_id= back in. RULED: REFUSE, 409 DuplicateExecutionId. It is the only one of the three options that keeps one id -> one directory -> one manifest -> one audit trail a BIJECTION. Reuse merges two runs' artifacts into a manifest chat-backend already recorded; wipe-and-rerun deletes artifacts read_artifact may still be serving - both leave the jti/sid join that 4h6.52 will build on pointing at content that is not what was recorded. Made coherent by fixing directory creation at DEQUEUE, so a 400/429/409 leaves nothing behind, and requiring a fresh id on the 429 retry.
- CLIENT ABANDONMENT was unspecified. RULED: split on whether the child was forked. A QUEUED request whose connection closed is dropped at dequeue - nobody is waiting, and running it spends the only slot and 120s of a doomed credential while the retry queues behind itself. A RUNNING child is NOT killed: it completes, is reaped, its manifest is written, artifacts are retained the usual 15 minutes, and the undeliverable response is discarded. Killing would destroy artifacts the retention window promises and a rerun may not reproduce, and disconnect detection while not reading the socket is unreliable enough that a false positive kills live executions. The slot is held at most timeout_s, the same bound the max wait is derived against.
- THE PIPE CAP HAD NO OUTCOME, and this one would have silently violated section 2. Section 2 says the reader stops at 8 MiB and KILLS THE CHILD; the response section never said so and never mapped it to a status. One supervisor kills and answers status "limit" / OutputLimit; another drains, discards and answers "ok" with error null. Now specified: SIGTERM the process group, SIGKILL after the same 2s grace as the timeout path, 200 with status "limit", and status stays "limit" regardless of how the process actually ended because it records that the SUPERVISOR'S limit fired.
- QUEUE DEPTH did not say waiting-only or total, so one side accepts 1 running + 2 waiting and the other 1 + 1, and a client treating queued < 2 as safe gets unpredicted 429s. Now "at most two WAITING, not counting the one executing", with /health's `queued` given the same definition.
- error.type was ambiguous between a closed enum and an open string while the doc elsewhere says "a field not listed here does not exist", AND had no vocabulary for a non-zero exit with no exception - which the contract itself makes a status "error" case. Now an OPEN string with the supervisor's names as a reserved minimum, plus NonZeroExit.
- /health's 503 CONTRADICTED the uniform error-shape rule inside the same subsection; a client parsing it by the stated rule would KeyError. /health is now the single named exception, with status restricted to starting/draining/ok.
- THE MANIFEST COULD ADVERTISE A NAME read_artifact CANNOT OPEN: executor.py strips before validating, so "plot.png " passes every listing rule, gets listed, and is then unretrievable behind the indistinguishable "Artifact not found". "No leading or trailing whitespace" added to the criteria.

ONE ARITHMETIC ATTRIBUTION WAS WRONG IN A WAY THAT WOULD HAVE MISLED THE NEXT PERSON. The draft said depth 2 was "the one tunable number" constrained by `max wait + timeout_s < 300`. DEPTH DOES NOT APPEAR IN THAT INEQUALITY - the MAX WAIT does. Someone raising the depth is safe and would have been warned; someone raising the wait, which the inequality actually guards, would not have been. Fixed, and the arithmetic itself verified against the real TTL (mint_execution_tokens' TTL_SECONDS = 300; 120 + 120 = 240).
RECORDED ALONGSIDE IT: the queue EATS SECTION 4'S SLACK. Section 4 justifies the 300s TTL partly by "a slow BigQuery job started at the last moment and clock skew"; a full 120s wait then a full 120s run leaves ~60s of token life, not the ~180s section 4 assumes.

EVERY CLAIM ABOUT LANDED CODE WAS CHECKED and all but one were true - read_artifact's validation chain, the hardcoded /scratch/ prefix, the 4 MiB cap, mimetypes-derived content type, mint_execution_tokens' execution_id= kwarg and claims and TTL, and the manifest's port, probe, emptyDir sizeLimit, replicas, Recreate and 130s grace. The exception was the pipe cap above.

OWNERSHIP ERROR CORRECTED: the implementation said the artifact-retrieval hop "belongs to no bead in this chain that I could find". genetics-results-suite-4h6.52 owns exactly it - open, P2, filed when 4h6.14 was split. Fixed in three places, including section 6's paragraph which still attributed the HTTP path to the CLOSED 4h6.11, with a line added saying not to read that closure as evidence the work landed.

DELIBERATELY LEFT UNSETTLED, and both are the right ones: how the child reports exception type and traceback to the supervisor (4h6.39-internal; the contract fixes only the emitted shape and requires clients to tolerate type "Killed" with a null traceback), and the absence of any artifact-retrieval endpoint (4h6.52's). Implementers should build /health and /execute and nothing else.

FILED: genetics-results-suite-4h6.54, because the review's sweep found that the CLOSED 4h6.14 and 4h6.11 are still named as live owners in about 40 places across docs, the k8s manifest, deploy.sh, the Dockerfile, prune_venv.py, prewarm.py and two mcp source files. The failure mode is "closed bead => the work is done", which is false in both directions here - and the two worst sites are in the file that implements the local artifact read, telling the next reader the HTTP proxy is somebody else's finished business.

title: Run the dev stack from the worktree branches against the dev dataset
description:
UNTRACKED until now. The user's order of operations (2026-08-14): first an implementation that RUNS LOCALLY, then further local development and testing, and only then deployment and live-cluster changes.

CURRENT STATE, measured from ss/ps and /proc/<pid>/cwd - all five dev servers run from the PLAIN CHECKOUTS on master, none from the db-only-architecture worktrees:
  8080 db-api        python3 api/main.py                       genetics-results-db (master)
  2000 results-api   python3 run_server.py 2000                genetics-results-api (master)
  4000 chat-api      python3 -m genetics_mcp_server.chat_api   genetics-mcp-server (master)
  5000 browser BFF   tsx watch bff/server.ts                   genetics-results-browser (master)
  3000 frontend      vite --host --port 3000                   genetics-results-browser (master)
The user has authorised terminating them and re-running from the worktree branches.

THE TRAP THAT WILL BITE WHOEVER DOES THIS: the config that makes these servers work is GITIGNORED AND LIVES ONLY IN THE MAIN CHECKOUTS. genetics-mcp-server/.env (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANALYZE_* models) and the browser's .env.dev / .env.local (VITE_API_URL, VITE_CHAT_URL, VITE_TARGET) do NOT exist in the worktrees. A worktree started fresh has neither, and the failure will look like an application bug rather than missing config. configs/datasets.yaml is also per-checkout.
Also note the documented start commands DIFFER from what is actually running: the mcp README says `cd src; uvicorn genetics_mcp_server.chat_api:app --port 8000`, while the running process is `python -m genetics_mcp_server.chat_api` on its argparse default of 4000. Follow what runs, not what is documented, and fix the doc.

WHAT THIS TASK SHOULD PRODUCE: a repeatable way to bring the stack up against the WORKTREE branches and the dev dataset - a script or documented sequence covering all five services, the ports, the env each needs, and how to point db-api at DATASET_ID=genetics_dev. It must be obvious how to switch back to master, since these are the user's working dev servers and this is their machine.

DO NOT start or stop anything until the dev dataset exists, or the worktree stack will come up pointing at production exactly like the current one.

DEPENDS ON the dev-dataset task. Files: likely a new scripts/dev-*.sh in the suite repo plus README/docs/project-spec.md updates (doc-ownership rule).
close_reason:
Landed as genetics-results-suite 509aa05. Implementation + review + one fix round. THE STACK IS UP AND SERVING FROM THE WORKTREE BRANCHES AGAINST genetics_dev, and was left running for the user.

scripts/dev-stack.sh drives all five services as one unit: up / down / status / logs, --tree worktree|main, per-service subsets. Both trees use the SAME FIVE PORTS, so one tree serves at a time by construction, and every `up` prints the switch-back line as its last output.

VERIFIED SERVING, NOT MERELY STARTED, which is the distinction that matters here:
- db-api: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM credible_sets_v -> 525,271. Production is 115,076,906, so the number itself proves the dataset. DATASET_ID=genetics_dev read from /proc/<pid>/environ.
- results-api: startup smoke query passed after full GCS file verification.
- chat-api: /status reports 62 tools, anthropic available, SANDBOX_URL on 8081 and BIGQUERY_API_URL on 8080. No paid chat message was sent.
- BFF and frontend: the browser's REAL path, :3000 vite proxy -> BFF -> results-api, returns 200 and 22,434,945 bytes for SMARCB1 - byte-identical to the same call against the master stack beforehand.
- An MCP tool driven from the worktree SDK against the local stack returns 7,819 credible sets.
--tree switching was exercised in BOTH directions on db-api, so the switch-back path is tested rather than merely written down.

SECRETS ARE REFERENCED, NEVER COPIED. genetics-mcp-server/.env is sourced BY PATH from the main checkout into the chat-backend subshell only. Verified rather than trusted: no secret in argv, ZERO occurrences of the key across the log directory, no set -x, nothing copied into a worktree, and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY present only in chat-api's environment and in no other service. Because the file is sourced BEFORE the script's defaults, values there WIN - which is the documented place for what the script deliberately does not set.

THE BEAD'S RECORDED TRAP WAS HALF WRONG, and checking cost less than working around it. .env.dev is TRACKED and present in the worktrees; only .env.local is gitignored. It makes no difference either way, because VITE'S DEFAULT MODE IS `development`, WHICH LOADS .env.local AND NOT .env.dev - so the master frontend was using the gitignored file. The three VITE_* values are passed as environment variables instead and no worktree file is needed at all.

THREE BLOCKING PROBLEMS FOUND IN REVIEW, ALL FIXED AND ALL VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY:
1. THE PORT-FREEING LOGIC KILLED WHATEVER HELD THE PORT - socket -> pid -> PROCESS GROUP, SIGKILL after ten seconds, with NO check on cwd, argv or owner - and then printed "stopped <service>", the name it WANTED rather than what it killed. The group kill is the RIGHT mechanism (it is what lets the script take over hand-started servers and kill a whole npm->sh->node tree rather than letting tsx watch respawn its child) but it needed a guard. Now a holder is signalled only when its cwd is inside the expected repo or its argv names it; anything else prints pid, pgid, cwd and argv and is LEFT RUNNING unless --force, and the message names what was actually signalled. Verified with throwaway listeners on an unused high port: cwd outside the suite refused, cwd inside killed, --force overrides; the live stack confirmed still resolvable as ours WITHOUT sending a signal.
THE HAZARD WAS NOT HYPOTHETICAL: the leftover g08 db-api on :8791 has PGID != its own pid, i.e. it sits in a group led by another process. Interactive job control gives each hand-started server its own group (which is why the tmux servers were safe), but anything started from a wrapper or `bash -c '... &'` inherits the invoking shell's group.
2. `up` FREED PORTS BEFORE VALIDATING TREES, so one missing .venv killed a running server and exited, leaving two services on the worktree, one dead and two still serving the OLD tree - half on each, unwarned. Every selected service is now preflighted before any port is touched, aborting with nothing started or stopped.
3. THE HLA GUIDANCE WAS INVERTED. The doc said an HLA query failing against DEV is expected. Measured, it is the reverse: genetics_dev carries the house spelling (mlog10p, se, af), production still carries the old (mlogp, sebeta, af_alt), and the worktree MCP code selects the house names. So worktree+dev WORKS, --tree main WORKS, and HLA fails only in the MIXED mode the doc itself advertises - worktree code against genetics_results, because 94c's expand phase has not been applied to production. Written the wrong way round it dismissed an unshipped production migration as a dev artefact and contradicted this repo's own project-spec.md. THIS IS THE SECOND TIME THIS INVERSION HAS APPEARED IN THIS EPIC; dev is the FIXED state, production is what has not had the migration.

Also fixed: `up` exited 0 with services down, which 4h6.49 would have believed; pidfiles written and never read, recording the socket holder rather than the group leader; lexicographic sort -u on pids; no `command -v ss` preflight, whose absence made every port look free; no root refusal or pgid<2 skip, so one sudo made kill -- -1 reachable; the launching terminal's group not skipped; and pid->pgid re-resolved just before SIGKILL, exactly when a recycled pid would name an unrelated group. The usage fix uses a SENTINEL range rather than the literal line number I specified, because the header had already grown from 35 to 41 lines - the enumeration-rot rule applying to the fix itself.

TWO BEHAVIOURAL CHANGES FOR THE USER, both flagged rather than silently accepted: the master chat-api had EXTERNAL_MCP_SERVERS set by hand in tmux including a PRIVATE gnomad Cloud Run URL, and the script defaults to opentargets only rather than hardcoding a private URL into a tracked file - `export EXTERNAL_MCP_SERVERS=...` before `up` restores it. PERPLEXITY_API_KEY and TAVILY_API_KEY are not in .env and were not in the shell, so literature and web search fail until exported. Both, plus the four chat storage paths, are now documented as belonging in genetics-mcp-server/.env.

LEFT RUNNING, NOT KILLED: pid 386742, a db-api from the db worktree on :8791, started 2026-08-14 - g08's "temporary instance was killed" was not. It conflicts with nothing.
NEEDS FILING AGAINST genetics-mcp-server: its own README still documents `cd src; uvicorn genetics_mcp_server.chat_api:app --port 8000` while the process actually runs `python -m genetics_mcp_server.chat_api` on 4000. This repo's docs/local-dev-vm.md was already correct.

title: Create and populate a dev BigQuery dataset so the local stack stops reading production
description:
USER-AUTHORISED 2026-08-14 as an explicit carve-out from the phase gate genetics-results-suite-zg6: "The BigQuery dev database however can be created and populated in europe-west1-b because we will need that in dev too." Everything else in zg6 still stands.

WHY IT IS NEEDED: THE LOCAL DEV STACK CURRENTLY READS PRODUCTION. Measured from /proc/<pid>/environ on the running dev servers: db-api runs with PROJECT_ID=phewas-development and DATASET_ID UNSET, so api/main.py:147 defaults it to `genetics_results` - the production dataset - and every query builds `phewas-development.genetics_results.<view>`. chat-api points BIGQUERY_API_URL at localhost:8080, so the whole local chain terminates in production data. Switching is a ONE-VARIABLE change: export DATASET_ID before starting db-api. Nothing else in the stack names a dataset.

LOCATION: `europe-west1`, NOT `europe-west1-b`. The user named the GKE zone; BigQuery takes a region. All three existing datasets (genetics_results, genetics_api_logs, genetics_chat_logs) are `europe-west1`, verified with `bq show`. A mismatch cannot be fixed by ALTER - it needs a recreate-and-reload - and cross-dataset queries against production would fail outright.

NAME IT `genetics_dev`, AND NOT ANYTHING CONTAINING `genetics_results`. scripts/setup_bigquery.sh rewrites every schema file with a BLIND GLOBAL `sed "s/genetics_results/${PROJECT_ID}.${DATASET_ID}/g"`, so a dataset called `genetics_results_dev` would mangle itself.

THE SCRIPT ALREADY DOES THIS AND IS PARAMETERISED, but read the hazard first: genetics-results-db/scripts/setup_bigquery.sh takes PROJECT_ID / DATASET_ID / LOCATION from the environment and creates 13 tables from schemas/*.sql plus 13 views from schemas/*_v.sql. **ITS DEFAULT DATASET_ID IS PRODUCTION.** Run with no env set and `--recreate`, it does `bq rm -f -t` on every PRODUCTION table. The dev invocation must set all three variables explicitly, and --recreate must never be used without them.

SCOPE DECIDED BY THE USER: full schema, SMALL SUBSET of data - enough to exercise every view, not a full copy. scripts/load_data.py takes --project and --dataset and the 13 scripts/load_*.sh wrappers pass them through, but they read source data from GCS and do a FULL-SIZE load unless subsetted, and some tables are large (gene_burden_results ~343M rows). Work out the subsetting mechanism before loading anything; if the loaders cannot subset, say so rather than loading everything.

ACCEPTANCE:
- `genetics_dev` exists in phewas-development, location europe-west1, with all 13 tables and all 13 views.
- Every view returns rows for at least one query, so nothing is silently empty.
- Production `genetics_results` is UNTOUCHED - verify table count and a row count before and after.
- The DATASET_ID that makes the local stack use it is written into whatever we use to start the dev servers, so nobody has to remember it.
- Record the actual load cost/time, so the benchmark work later knows what it is measuring against.
close_reason:
Dev dataset `phewas-development:genetics_dev` EXISTS, location europe-west1, 15 tables + 15 views, populated and VERIFIED SERVING THROUGH db-api. Docs committed with the code. Cost: $0.04 for the whole session including probes; the dataset is 3,574,998 rows / 611.7 MB against production's 1,100,942,887 rows / 224 GB - about 1/370th.

PRODUCTION IS PROVABLY UNTOUCHED, checked three times by two different agents, before and after every write: credible_sets 115,076,906 / gene_burden_results 327,363,096 / open_chromatin 232,773,819 / coloc_credsets 30,460,655, identical throughout, and `bq ls` shows the same 18 tables + 15 views. Every statement against genetics_results was a SELECT; all DML targeted genetics_dev. `--recreate` was never passed - the setup ran behind a guard that asserted DATASET_ID before invoking the script, because setup_bigquery.sh DEFAULTS DATASET_ID TO PRODUCTION and `--recreate` does `bq rm -f -t` on every table it knows.

MY OWN BEAD WAS WRONG ABOUT THE SCHEMA COUNT and following it would have produced a broken dev DB. I wrote "13 tables / 13 views" from the master checkout. The db worktree has 15 of each - it adds `datasets` and `phenotypes` (commit 52e9175, bead 4h6.19) - and api/main.py's `VIEWS` literal at :524 lists 15, with `_ALLOWED_TABLE_IDS` derived from it. A dev DB built from master's schemas would have been missing exactly the two views the API expects, and `/schema` and `/stats` iterate the whole list. Verified independently from git rather than taken on the implementer's word.

THE LOADERS CANNOT SUBSET, which the bead assumed they might. load_data.py and the 13 load_*.sh wrappers take --project/--dataset but no row limit, chromosome filter or partial-source selection; they load whole GCS files (~218 GB). So population used the sanctioned fallback: INSERT ... SELECT from production into dev, chr=22, with caps. Column lists were read from `bq show --schema` per table so column ORDER could not silently shift.

TWO SOURCING QUIRKS THAT MUST SURVIVE ANY RELOAD:
- `credible_sets` MUST be sourced from production's `credible_sets_v`, NOT the base table. Production's base table predates the clustering swap and stores neither `resource` nor `variant`, while the dev schema clusters on both. Only the view exposes the full dev column set.
- Reloads use TRUNCATE + INSERT with an explicit column list, NOT CTAS. schemas/credible_sets.sql documents that a CTAS flattens every column to NULLABLE, which would flip /schema from REQUIRED to NULLABLE for variant and resource; truncate+insert preserves the modes, the RANGE_BUCKET partitioning and the clustering keys.

THE FIRST LOAD LEFT ONE CORRELATED GROUP ACTIVELY MISLEADING, and it was fixed rather than documented away. A blind LIMIT 500000 meant 25.5% of `colocalization` rows referenced a credible set that was never loaded (cs2_id resolved 30,631/41,131). Reloaded seeded from the cs_ids the dev colocalization slice actually references, with the cap applied to the REMAINDER so seeded rows cannot be evicted by an arbitrary slice. Now 41,131/41,131 = 100% on both cs1_id and cs2_id.
The shared-cs_id count only moved 426 -> 518, and THAT IS PRODUCTION'S CEILING, not a dev shortfall: the dev coloc slice references 3,908 distinct cs_ids, every production credible_sets_v row for all of them was loaded, and only 518 of those ids exist in genetics_results.credible_sets at all. The two tables use largely disjoint cs_id namespaces upstream. Recorded in the spec so nobody re-opens it as a dev bug.

ACCEPTANCE VERIFIED BY A SEPARATE AGENT, not by the implementer: a temporary db-api started from the db WORKTREE with DATASET_ID=genetics_dev served /health, /schema, /scstats, /query and /tables/{t}/sample - all 200, 15 views, `warnings: []`, non-zero row counts for every view, and no view that answers `bq` but 500s through the API. That temporary instance was killed and the five running dev servers were confirmed untouched. The auth path used was the documented fail-open branch with INTERNAL_API_SECRET explicitly unset - so the sandbox-token path was NOT exercised and remains untested here.

DATA QUALITY, so nobody mistakes these for dev artefacts:
- The subset is genuinely usable for variant, gene, phenotype and annotation work: 98.5% of credible-set rows carry an annotation, 97.4% of gene_burden rows resolve a gene symbol, 124 of 125 datasets resolve.
- phenotypes_v coverage is 13% and that is NOT a subset artefact - most of the chr22 slice is QTL data whose trait_original is a gene, not a registry phenotype.
- peak_to_gene -> open_chromatin returns ZERO matches, and this is a PRODUCTION DEFECT confirmed on production chr22, not a subset artefact: the peak_id formats differ (chr22-23263950-23264449 vs 22-20750312-20751112). Filed genetics-results-suite-dwp.

FILED, and it limits what the dev dataset is good for: genetics-mcp-server hardcodes `genetics_results.<view>`, so against a dev-pointed db-api every MCP-generated query is REJECTED 403 by authorize_query. It fails CLOSED, which is correct, but the chat path cannot be developed against dev data until that is fixed. genetics-results-api and genetics-results-browser are clean - they name no dataset. This corrected an unverified absolute in the docs ("no other service names a dataset"), which was false.

DOCS record the region-vs-zone trap (the user said europe-west1-b, a GKE zone; BigQuery took europe-west1 and a mismatch needs a recreate-and-reload), that DATASET_ID defaults to PRODUCTION, the naming constraint from setup_bigquery.sh's blind sed, and that timings measured here are meaningless for the benchmark work in 4h6.23.

title: PHASE GATE: no live-cluster changes until the epic is done and tested locally
description:
PHASE GATE, not a work item. Nothing here is implemented; this bead exists so that live-infrastructure tasks stop appearing in `bd ready` while the epic is still being built.

USER INSTRUCTION, 2026-08-14, verbatim in substance: "we don't want to touch the live cluster at all before we're finished here. So we are going to test on a live cluster only after everything is done and we've tested it locally."

THE RULE WHILE THIS BEAD IS OPEN: no kubectl apply, no rollout, no terraform apply, no BigQuery schema swap or data migration, no Keycloak mutation - against the live cluster or project. There is only ONE cluster and ONE project (gke_phewas-development_europe-west1-b_finngenie / phewas-development); the name is historical and it IS production. There is no development environment to try things in, which is exactly why this gate exists.
READ-ONLY INSPECTION REMAINS ALLOWED AND IS OFTEN NECESSARY: kubectl get, bq ls/show, bq query --dry_run, gcloud ... list, gsutil ls/cat. The line is mutation, not access.

WHAT DEPENDS ON THIS: every bead marked OPERATOR is now blocked by it. They are NOT blocked by a missing dependency - they are ready in every technical sense and blocked by PHASE. Do not "unblock" them by removing the dependency; that would silently discard the instruction above.

TO CLOSE THIS GATE, in order:
1. All file-only work in the epic is complete and committed.
2. It has been tested locally - the test suites green, and whatever local verification the individual operator beads name in their own descriptions.
3. The user explicitly says to proceed to live testing. This step is NOT optional and is NOT inferable from the queue being empty.
Then close this bead, and its dependants become ready together - which is also the point at which their ORDERING matters, because several of them interact (the auth-gateway reconciliation and the NetworkPolicy replacement in particular must be sequenced deliberately, not applied in whatever order `bd ready` happens to list them).

WHOEVER CLOSES THIS: re-read each dependant before applying it. They were written earlier in the epic and some record live state that will have been measured months prior; live state drifts, and several of these beads exist precisely BECAUSE the live cluster did not match the committed manifests.
notes:
--- SCOPE WIDENED 2026-08-14, after the first pass missed three ---
THE FIRST PASS KEYED ON THE LITERAL STRING "OPERATOR" IN THE TITLE and therefore gated only afw, unj, 94c, eyg and 3sm. Three live-work beads carry no such marker and were left ready, one of them P1 and newly unblocked by 4h6.7 landing:
- 4h6.26 Deploy-window live verification of the sandbox NetworkPolicy - four checks that NEED A LIVE POD and cannot be faked (mcp-server -> sandbox must fail; metadata-server egress from the sandbox; etc.).
- 4h6.23 Run the paired benchmark and decide the rollout on the numbers - needs the code arm actually running.
- 4h6.20 Apply the stored-column and clustering fix to the other view-derived tables - a BigQuery migration, and it also waits on eyg's measurement.
All three now depend on this gate.
NOT GATED, deliberately, because they are file-only despite live-sounding titles: 4h6.37 (add an IMAGE_MAP entry to rollout.sh) and 4zd (open the chat DB read-only - a one-line source change to a CronJob that runs against live data, but the CHANGE is file-only).
LESSON FOR THE NEXT SWEEP: gate on WHAT THE TASK DOES, not on a title convention. A bead that merely mentions production may be file-only; a bead titled "verification" may need a live pod.

--- POLICY CLARIFIED BY THE USER 2026-08-14, SUPERSEDES THE BLANKET READING ABOVE ---
ORDER OF OPERATIONS IS NOW EXPLICIT: (1) an implementation that RUNS LOCALLY in the dev environment, (2) test and develop it further locally, (3) only then deployment and live-cluster changes. Deployment work is not merely deferred - it is the LAST phase, and local runnability is the current goal.

THE DEV ENVIRONMENT EXISTS AND I HAD THIS WRONG. Earlier notes in this epic assert "there is NO development environment". That is true of the CLUSTER - there is one cluster and one project and it is production - but NOT of the developer machine: dev servers are currently running locally, from the master branch. The user has authorised terminating them and re-running them from these worktree branches if needed. Treat "no dev environment" as meaning "no dev CLUSTER" wherever it appears in this epic's notes.

ONE CARVE-OUT FROM THE GATE, AUTHORISED EXPLICITLY: the BigQuery DEV DATABASE MAY BE CREATED AND POPULATED, because it is needed for local development too. That is a real GCP mutation and it is permitted; everything else in this bead still stands.
CHECK BEFORE CREATING, do not guess: the user named "europe-west1-b", which is a GKE ZONE. BigQuery datasets take a LOCATION (a region such as `europe-west1`, or a multi-region such as `EU`), not a zone. Establish what the EXISTING datasets use and match it - a mismatched location cannot be fixed by an ALTER, it needs a recreate-and-reload, and cross-location queries fail outright.
The carve-out covers creating and populating a DEV dataset. It does NOT extend to touching production datasets, and it does NOT extend to the gated BigQuery migrations (94c, eyg, 4h6.20), which remain blocked.

STILL BLOCKED, unchanged: kubectl apply, rollout, deploy.sh, terraform apply, Keycloak mutation, and any change to production BigQuery datasets.

--- ORDERING CONSTRAINT ADDED 2026-08-16, from the ad3 audit ---
THE CODE HALF OF THE hla_associations_v RENAME MUST NOT SHIP BEFORE THE VIEW EXPAND PHASE (genetics-results-suite-94c). Nothing is broken in deployed production today - the old view, the old mcp image and the old ConfigMap are self-consistent, and every half of the rename lives only on worktree-db-only-architecture. Deploying the code half first would CREATE an outage that does not currently exist.
This is a phase-ordering constraint on this gate's release, not a separate task: when this gate is closed and work moves to the cluster, 94c's EXPAND step goes FIRST, then the three code artifacts (mcp image, the SEPARATE sandbox image, and the datasets-config ConfigMap that only deploy.sh recreates), then 94c's CONTRACT step - and per docs/project-spec.md the contract phase is sequenced after eyg is verified.
The runbook already exists at docs/project-spec.md:1445-1500 with the literal expand SQL. Do not improvise it: the `CASE ... AS resource` block is load-bearing and an improvised `SELECT *` plus five aliases drops it.

--- PARKED 2026-08-20 by the ralph-wiggum loop. THE GATE IS STILL IN FORCE - this is scheduling only. ---
DEFERRED so that `bd ready` stops serving it. This bead is a MARKER, not work: it can never be "done" by
an agent, so it sat at the head of every `bd ready` and was re-evaluated once per loop iteration for
nothing.
DEFERRING DOES NOT WEAKEN IT. `bd defer` affects `bd ready` only; the DEPENDENCIES that make this bead
block the live-infrastructure tasks are unchanged, so those tasks stay blocked exactly as before, and
`bd list` and `bd blocked` still show this one.
TO LIFT THE GATE the user un-defers and closes it - that is a human decision by construction, per the
verbatim instruction in the description. An agent must NOT close this to unblock its own work.

--- NEW DEPLOYMENT TARGET, reported by the user 2026-08-22. Read this before planning the deploy. ---
The user has set up a SEPARATE STAGING DOMAIN in the daly environment, managed from a DIFFERENT MACHINE,
and states the intent plainly: "we will use another terraform/kube deployment for that domain name first",
i.e. the epic's first real deploy goes to STAGING, not to the production domain.

WHAT THIS CHANGES: the deploy at the end of this epic is no longer a single-shot against the only live
system. There is a staging target to prove it on first. That materially de-risks 4h6.50 and everything
gated behind it, and it means the deploy sequence should be written as staging-then-production rather than
as one apply.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS IN THE REPO, verified 2026-08-22 rather than assumed:
- scripts/lib/env.sh knows DEPLOY_ENV=daly-staging (one of daly, daly-staging, finngen).
- terraform/daly-staging.tfbackend exists alongside daly.tfbackend and finngen.tfbackend.
- docs/environments.md already documents daly-staging in full: project daly-finngenie, cluster
  finngenie-staging, resource_suffix "-staging", its own state prefix, and a "Bringing up daly-staging"
  CHECKLIST including the DNS A record, the Keycloak IdP endpoint and a final sign-in step.
- daly and daly-staging SHARE the daly-finngenie project, so every project-scoped resource is
  disambiguated by resource_suffix (Artifact Registry repo, Workload Identity GSA, snapshot policy,
  Keycloak backup bucket, log sinks / BQ datasets). docs/environments.md:60-70 is the table.
So the staging path is largely BUILT, not new work - the remaining question is which checklist steps the
user has already completed on their admin machine.

AN OPEN DISCREPANCY THE USER MUST SETTLE - DO NOT GUESS:
The user wrote the domain as `staging.genegenie.broadinstitute.org` (a DOT). The repo uses
`staging-genegenie.broadinstitute.org` (a HYPHEN) in 5 places - docs/environments.md lines 10, 107, 111,
118, 172 - and the dotted form appears NOWHERE. The real value lives in an uncommitted per-environment
tfvars (`domains` in terraform/variables.tf), i.e. on the user's admin machine, so the repo cannot settle
it. These are different hostnames and the difference is load-bearing: it changes the DNS A record, the
managed TLS certificate, the Keycloak redirect URIs and the Google IdP endpoint, and oauth2-proxy's
config. Getting it wrong produces a cert that does not match and a login loop, not an obvious error.
ASKED 2026-08-22; awaiting the user's answer. If the dotted form is correct, those 5 doc sites need
updating and the checklist's dig/cert steps re-verifying.

NOTE ALSO, unresolved and NOT ruled on here: zg6's text says "There is only ONE cluster and ONE project
(gke_phewas-development_europe-west1-b_finngenie / phewas-development)", while docs/environments.md
describes daly / daly-staging / finngen across daly-finngenie and other projects. Those two statements do
not obviously describe the same world. Somebody who knows the estate should reconcile them before the
deploy, because zg6's whole justification for the phase gate rests on its version being true.

--- RESOLVED 2026-08-22: the DOTTED form is correct. See genetics-results-suite-4h6.50's notes for the
full write-up; do not re-derive it here. Short version: staging is
`staging.genegenie.broadinstitute.org`, which makes it a SUBDOMAIN OF PRODUCTION rather than a sibling,
so a cookie scoped to the parent domain would cross between them. Measured: no cookie-domain setting
exists anywhere, so they are separate today BY DEFAULT, NOT BY CONTROL. Docs corrected under
genetics-results-suite-4h6.93.
THE ONE-CLUSTER-ONE-PROJECT DISCREPANCY ABOVE IS STILL OPEN and is the more important of the two.

--- THE ONE-CLUSTER DISCREPANCY IS RESOLVED, 2026-08-24, by the user. It was never a contradiction: the
    two statements are scoped to different things, and NEITHER doc said which. ---
THE USER'S ANSWER, verbatim in substance: "There is and will be only one cluster (finngen profile) managed
from this machine. There is currently one cluster (daly) managed from another machine. But now we will be
able to use staging in daly so we can deploy this first there. So we need to switch to that daly machine
at some point when we are ready to try deploying."

SO THE RECONCILIATION IS BY MACHINE, NOT BY ESTATE:
- THIS MACHINE reaches exactly ONE cluster: `gke_phewas-development_europe-west1-b_finngenie`, project
  `phewas-development`, which is the `finngen` profile (identified, not assumed - docs/bigquery-dev-dataset.md:11-16
  gives project_id=phewas-development with domains finngenie.finngen.fi, and docs/environments.md's
  `finngen` row gives cluster `finngenie` / host `finngenie.finngen.fi`). It IS production and there is no
  second context here. zg6's description is therefore TRUE OF THIS SEAT and its justification survives
  intact - there is still no cluster here to try anything in.
- THE ESTATE has three deployments (daly, daly-staging, finngen). docs/environments.md is correct.
  docs/project-spec.md:1473-1484 already states this correctly and explicitly handles daly-staging: it is a
  second GKE cluster inside the DALY project, a rehearsal ground for the daly brand, "not for this project".
  That paragraph was right all along.
- daly and daly-staging are managed from a DIFFERENT ADMIN MACHINE. docs/environments.md:13 already says
  "daly and daly-staging are managed from the same admin instance; finngen is managed elsewhere" - read
  from the daly machine's point of view. From HERE the sentence inverts.

THE CONSEQUENCE THAT IS NOT WRITTEN DOWN ANYWHERE AND MATTERS MOST FOR THIS EPIC:
**THE EPIC'S DEPLOY TARGET IS NOT REACHABLE FROM THIS MACHINE AT ALL.** daly-staging lives in
`daly-finngenie` and is administered from the other instance. Lifting this gate therefore does NOT mean
"an agent in this session starts deploying". It means the work MOVES MACHINES. Whoever lifts it should
plan for a handoff, not for a next task in the queue.

AND A CORRECTION TO HOW THE OPERATOR BEADS SHOULD BE READ:
`genetics-results-suite-afw` and `-unj` record live-vs-committed DRIFT that was measured on context

They are about a different cluster and they stay open on their own terms.
CONVERSELY, THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT FOR STAGING-FIRST IS EXACTLY THIS: daly-staging is being brought up
fresh, so committed == live there BY CONSTRUCTION. It is the only environment in the estate where the
manifests this epic has been writing are what actually runs, with no accumulated delta to ship by accident.
That is precisely the failure mode afw warns about on the finngen cluster.

WHAT IS STILL A HUMAN DECISION, UNCHANGED: closing this gate. Step 3 of the description ("the user
explicitly says to proceed to live testing") is not satisfied by the estate question being answered.

title: Design a BigQuery dev dataset so the five DDL beads can be rehearsed before they touch live data
description:
USER DECISION 2026-08-13: asked whether we could finish all remaining work without touching live infrastructure, so they could "try first in development and then touch the live infra". A read-only survey established the premise is FALSE - there IS no development environment - and the user then chose to have a BigQuery dev dataset designed as part of the remaining file-only work.

WHAT THE SURVEY ESTABLISHED, all read-only, so this does not need re-deriving:
- ONE cluster. `kubectl config get-contexts` returns exactly one row, gke_phewas-development_europe-west1-b_finngenie. No staging context, no second kubeconfig entry.
- The project name is a HISTORICAL ACCIDENT. `gcloud projects list --filter="projectId:*phewas*"` returns exactly one project, phewas-development, and there is no companion phewas-production. terraform.tfvars sets project_id = "phewas-development", domains = ["finngenie.finngen.fi", "finngenie.fi"], and the live results-api carries DEPLOY_ENV=prod and LOG_SOURCE=finngenie_prod. phewas-development IS production.
- ONE application namespace, `genetics`. No genetics-dev.
- `bq ls` in phewas-development returns exactly THREE datasets: genetics_api_logs, genetics_chat_logs, genetics_results. There is no dev dataset and no dev project.
- No compose file, no kind/minikube config, and no dev-first workflow described anywhere in the docs. There never was one (docs/project-spec.md:428 mentions a historical log_source value genetics-results-api-dev1, so one existed at some point; it does not now).
- The `daly` profile is a SECOND PRODUCTION BRAND, not a staging copy - its own project, region, domain (genegenie.broadinstitute.org), Keycloak broker and users. Using it as a canary would mean testing on Broad's live users. GAP, not established read-only: gs://genetics-results-terraform-daly returns 403/may-not-exist under this account, so whether the daly target has ever been stood up is UNKNOWN.

WHY THIS BEAD IS THE HIGHEST VALUE PER UNIT OF EFFORT: FIVE open beads are BigQuery DDL against the single live genetics_results dataset that live db-api reads -
  94c    CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW hla_associations_v (expand phase)
  eyg    the credible_sets clustering table swap
  4h6.20 stored-column/clustering fix for coloc_credsets, exome_variant_results, asm_qtl
  4h6.21 backfill gene expression and gene-disease
  4ci    DROP TABLE x3, ~27 GB each, IRREVERSIBLE - and credible_sets_exp_drvp is the verification reference for eyg, so dropping it before eyg is verified destroys the only means of confirming the swap worked
There is nowhere to rehearse any of it.

SCOPE - FILE-ONLY. Produce everything needed so that ONE later command from the user stands the dataset up. Do NOT create the dataset, do not run DDL, do not copy or clone anything.
Deliverables:
1. A script that creates and populates a dev dataset, idempotently, and can tear it down.
2. A runbook doc describing the expand/verify/contract cycle to follow for each of the five beads, and how to promote a verified change to the live dataset.
3. Notes on each of the five beads pointing at the runbook.

DESIGN QUESTIONS TO RESOLVE ON EVIDENCE, not taste - these are what make this non-trivial:
- HOW TO POPULATE IT CHEAPLY. The tables are large (three at ~27 GB). BigQuery table CLONES are zero-copy and writable, which is almost certainly the right primitive - but verify clone support, cost semantics and any same-region/same-project constraint against the actual dataset rather than assuming. Snapshots (read-only) and plain CTAS copies (full storage cost) are the alternatives.
- REGION. The dev dataset must match the source dataset's location or nothing will join. Establish the real location with `bq show --format=prettyjson`.
- THE VIEWS. genetics_results holds views as well as tables, and views embed fully-qualified table references. A cloned/copied dataset needs its view DDL rewritten to point at the dev dataset, or the views silently read PRODUCTION tables while the tables around them are dev copies - which would make a rehearsal actively misleading. This is the single most important correctness issue in the whole bead.
- WHICH TABLES. Cloning everything may be unnecessary; each of the five beads touches a specific set. Decide whether the script takes a table list or clones wholesale, and justify it.
- HOW db-api AND THE SDK WOULD POINT AT IT, if at all - is there a dataset name in configs/datasets.yaml or an env var, and would a dev rehearsal need one, or is running the SQL directly enough?
close_reason:
Landed as suite (see the 44g commit). Validated at FULL tier - sighted review plus a blind validator in parallel, then a re-verification pass and a final targeted fix. NOTHING WAS EXECUTED against BigQuery beyond read-only bq ls/show/query --dry_run; every exercise of the script ran against a stub bq proven first on PATH with command -v.

DELIVERED: scripts/bq-dev-dataset.sh (check/create/verify/rewrite/teardown) and docs/bigquery-dev-dataset.md, plus pointers in project-spec, adding-datasets and datasets-yaml-schema. Dry run is the DEFAULT; --apply executes; teardown additionally needs --yes AND the dataset name typed at a tty. Non-overridable refusals: the three protected dataset names, a target without a `dev` segment, target==source, cross-region.

DESIGN ANSWERS, each on evidence:
- CLONE, verified not assumed: `bq query --dry_run 'CREATE TABLE ... CLONE ...'` validates at an upper bound of 0 bytes. Snapshots are READ-ONLY and so useless for rehearsing DDL; CTAS would bill all 224.42 GB (exact, per-table figures verified).
- LOCATION europe-west1, maxTimeTravelHours 168. This bit: a dry run against the not-yet-existent dev dataset returns "not found in location US" because the CLI defaults to US when it cannot infer, so every call passes --location explicitly.
- VIEWS, the crux. All 15 embed a fully-qualified phewas-development.genetics_results reference, so verbatim copies would read PRODUCTION while the tables around them were dev clones - a rehearsal that looks right and proves nothing. Rewritten on copy, and verify re-reads every dev view back OUT of BigQuery rather than trusting what was written.
- WHOLESALE, all 18 tables: clones are zero-copy so 18 costs what 3 costs, and a partial clone leaves views over missing base tables - the exact silent-failure class this exists to eliminate. --tables/--exclude for deliberate narrowing.
- NO SERVICE PLUMBING NEEDED and none added: all five beads are SQL plus SQL acceptance tests, and genetics-results-db/scripts/setup_bigquery.sh already takes PROJECT_ID/DATASET_ID/LOCATION and substitutes into every schemas/*.sql.

BOTH VALIDATORS INDEPENDENTLY FOUND THE SCRIPT HAD NEVER WORKED - not once, in any mode. `python3 - ... <<'PY'` makes the HEREDOC python's stdin (that is how python3 - receives its program), so the rewriter's sys.stdin.read() returned the empty remainder and the piped SQL was discarded. MEASURED: `rewrite < in.sql > out.sql` produced ZERO BYTES and exit 0; `create --apply` issued all 18 CLONEs and then died at the first view with a bare BrokenPipeError, exit 120, zero views created - 24 of 30 dry runs, the other 6 printing `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW ... AS` followed by a bare `;`. The REGEX had been tested offline against all 15 real definitions; the SHELL PATH around it had never emitted a byte. That is the gap a green-looking offline test leaves, and only running it found it. Now `python3 -c`, the form the three working neighbours already use, plus a `[ -n "$q" ] || die` so an empty body can never be issued.

VERIFY PASSED VIEWS THAT READ PRODUCTION - the precise failure this script exists to prevent, and it was live in the thing meant to catch it. The grep required the dot to IMMEDIATELY follow the dataset name, so `phewas-development`.`genetics_results`.`asm_qtl` (per-part backticks) and a reference split across a NEWLINE both passed as "references only genetics_results_dev". Both are ordinary BigQuery style, and the rehearsal REQUIRES the operator to hand-write new views (94c's expand, 4h6.21's two new views, eyg's credible_sets_v). Demonstrated by planting dev views, not by reading. FIXED STRUCTURALLY: the rewriter and both residue checks are now ONE PROGRAM IN TWO MODES, so what is rewritten and what is detected cannot drift apart - that divergence was the actual root cause, not the regex.

A --tables TYPO BUILT A DATASET OF 15 VIEWS OVER ZERO TABLES AND REPORTED SUCCESS: `die` inside $(...) consumed by a `for` list exits only the subshell, and set -e does not propagate. The list is now assigned first, where set -e does apply, and before the dataset is created - the earlier placement still fired bq mk first.

THE TOKENIZER WAS THE RISKIEST THING ADDED, since a bug there CORRUPTS SQL instead of failing loudly. It masks comments and string literals so a reference inside them is neither rewritten nor flagged. Attacked with 43 cases across escaping, quote/comment confusion in both directions, doubled backticks, CRLF and unterminated constructs. It survived all but one: BIGQUERY RAW STRINGS DO NOT TREAT BACKSLASH AS AN ESCAPE, so r'a\' is a COMPLETE string, and the escape-aware body ran on to the next quote and swallowed a real table reference - neither rewritten nor reported, the silent-production-read class again. Fixed for EVERY quote form, not only the single-quote one demonstrated. Byte offsets provably cannot shift (the rewrite concatenates an exact partition; residue masks with a length- and newline-preserving substitution). All 15 live definitions round-trip dev->src BYTE-IDENTICALLY and validate under real bq --dry_run with no error other than the dev dataset not yet existing.
DELIBERATE ASYMMETRY, confirmed intact: rewrite is conservative (will not touch otherproj.genetics_results.t) while detection is liberal (does flag it), so a cross-project reference makes create DIE and demand a human rather than being silently created.

TWO DOC CLAIMS WOULD HAVE COST MONEY OR DATA: clone storage is ALSO billed once the BASE table is replaced or dropped, which is exactly what eyg (23.75 GB) and 4ci (3 x 26.96 GB) do - the runbook said to tear down only at the end of the batch, which would have put ~105 GB into billed storage at promotion; it now says to drop each dev clone as its counterpart is promoted. And time travel DOES cover a dropped table via UNDROP within the 168-hour window, contrary to the runbook, which matters in a document governing irreversible DROPs.
The runbook also asserted the rewrite "was tested against all 15 live view definitions before this landed". The regex was; the script could not have been. Replaced with what was actually run, after the fix.

A CLAIM ABOUT THIS REPO'S OWN CONFIG WAS FALSE and I filed a bead on it before checking: configs/datasets.yaml was said to describe 12 of the 15 views with no entry for peak_to_gene_v. IT HAS ALL 15 - peak_to_gene_v at line 1412, plus phenotypes_v, datasets_v, gene_annotations_v and variant_annotation_v. Verified directly. genetics-results-suite-lxz is withdrawn and the false sentence removed from adding-datasets.md. What survives is only that ALL_VIEWS (genetics-results-db/scripts/generate_resource_sql.py:22-34) has 11, omitting gene_annotations_v and variant_annotation_v - already owned by genetics-results-suite-fml, which now carries the correction.

ORDERING re-derived from the beads, not copied: 4ci strictly after eyg is verified (credible_sets_exp_drvp is eyg's reference); 94c's expand safe while applying schemas/hla_associations_v.sql is the CONTRACT phase that breaks consumers; 5p5 and 4h6.30 correct today and wrong only after eyg; 4h6.20 after eyg is measured. 94c's premise re-confirmed by dry run: the HLA examples still fail with "Unrecognized name: mlog10p; Did you mean mlogp?".

WHAT WAS NOT DONE, stated rather than glossed: THE SCRIPT HAS STILL NEVER RUN AGAINST A REAL bq. Every claim above rests on a stub plus read-only dry runs. `bq mk`'s flag ordering is the one command that could not be exercised at all - bq query accepts the same ordering, so it very likely works, but it is unverified. Cross-project clone semantics are unverified and the script refuses cross-project rather than guessing. genetics-results-db/docs/credible-sets-clustering-swap.md, which eyg's rehearsal needs, is NOT on the sibling checkout's current branch - it exists only on its db-only-architecture worktree.
FIRST COMMAND FOR THE USER: `scripts/bq-dev-dataset.sh check` - read-only, touches nothing. Then create (prints the plan, executes nothing), create --apply, and verify, which must print VERIFIED before anything is rehearsed.
NIT LEFT FOR THE BATCH: docs/bigquery-dev-dataset.md says "the remaining 8" where it is 9.

title: OPERATOR: the live auth-gateway is a single root nginx container - eau, a7n and the whole render-config/INTERNAL_API_SECRET gate are not deployed
description:
Found by the BLIND validator on genetics-results-suite-a7n while establishing what a rollout of that change would actually ship. Read-only kubectl only; nothing was applied.

MEASURED on the live cluster (context gke_phewas-development_europe-west1-b_finngenie, namespace genetics, Deployment auth-gateway at generation 30):
  - ONE container. No `render-config` initContainer at all.
  - securityContext: {} - i.e. NONE of genetics-results-suite-eau's hardening is in effect. The nginx master runs as root with the full 14-capability Docker runtime default and NoNewPrivs 0.
  - ONE volume, the configMap. None of the emptyDirs.
  - The live ConfigMap contains NO X-Internal-Auth header and no INTERNAL_API_SECRET substitution ANYWHERE.

CONSEQUENCES, in descending order of how much they should worry you:
1. THE SHARED-SECRET GATE BETWEEN THE GATEWAY AND THE BACKENDS IS NOT LIVE. The committed ConfigMap injects X-Internal-Auth: ${INTERNAL_API_SECRET} on the proxied routes and the initContainer renders it. Neither exists on the cluster. Several beads in this session reason about that header as an existing control - notably the is_internal_caller path in results-api (genetics-results-suite-0lf, rhh, 618) and the mcp-server require_internal_api_secret work. Whatever those beads concluded about defence in depth, THIS layer is currently absent in production. Re-check any claim that rests on it.
2. The internet-facing nginx master is root with a full capability set, today. eau and a7n both describe a posture the cluster does not have.
3. Applying the committed manifest now ships the ENTIRE accumulated delta in one rollout - eau's hardening, the render-config initContainer, the secret gate AND a7n - not just the most recent change. That is a much larger blast radius than any single bead's rollout note describes, and each of those beads' close reasons assess their own change in isolation.

THE ROUTE SET IS UNCHANGED. The validator diffed the live ConfigMap's location blocks against the committed one: same routes, so nothing is lost by applying. It also ran the preflight read-only - genetics-secrets/internal-api-secret exists, length 44, and passes the initContainer's whitelist (value never printed) - so the init gate will not stall on a missing or malformed secret.

THIS IS THE SECOND live-vs-committed drift found this session; see genetics-results-suite-unj, where the enforced NetworkPolicies are not the committed ones either and have generation 1 since 2026-04-08. Same root cause: no full scripts/deploy.sh run in months. Treat them together - deciding to reconcile one without the other leaves an inconsistent cluster.

NOT AN AGENT TASK. Requires applying manifests to the live internet-facing gateway, which the user has forbidden for the whole of this session. Needs a human to decide sequencing, choose a window, and WATCH the rollout - deploy.sh runs `kubectl rollout status ... || true`, so a stalled init is silent and the deploy exits 0 regardless.
notes: PARKED 2026-08-27 by the ralph-wiggum loop: requires a PRODUCTION rollout, which this seat may not perform. UNPARK WHEN: an operator is ready to deploy to gke_phewas-development_europe-west1-b_finngenie. title: OPERATOR: live NetworkPolicies are not the committed ones and admit every source on port 4000
description:
Found while validating genetics-results-suite-rhh. UNRELATED to that change, and more serious than it.

THE ENFORCED NETWORK POLICY IS NOT THE COMMITTED ONE, AND THE ENFORCED ONE IS WIDE OPEN.

MEASURED, read-only, 2026-08-13:
  kubectl get networkpolicy allow-ingress-results-api -n genetics -o yaml
    creationTimestamp: "2026-04-08T12:53:06Z"
    generation: 1
    ingress:
    - ports: [{port: 4000}]              # <-- NO `from:` - admits EVERY source
    - from: [chat-backend, mcp-server]
      ports: [{port: 4000}]
The committed k8s/network-policies/policies.yaml has ONE rule with FIVE podSelectors. The live object has a from-less rule that admits everything on 4000, plus a narrower one that is therefore redundant.

`generation: 1` since 2026-04-08 means the object has NEVER BEEN MODIFIED since creation. scripts/deploy.sh:424 is what applies these policies, so NO FULL deploy.sh RUN HAS HAPPENED IN FOUR MONTHS, and the committed policy has never been in effect.

THE SAME SHAPE APPEARS ON allow-ingress-frontend, allow-ingress-bff AND allow-ingress-chat-backend - all ports-only, i.e. effectively unrestricted ingress.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS:
1. Several documents in this repo cite k8s/network-policies/policies.yaml as THE bound on who can reach a service. Those citations describe a policy the cluster is not enforcing. genetics-results-suite-rhh's first draft did exactly this and had to be reworded to argue from the actual pod inventory instead.
2. scripts/test-network-policies.py validates the COMMITTED union and exits 0. It cannot detect that the committed union is not what is live - it reads manifests, never the cluster. genetics-results-suite-r22 closed ten fail-open paths in that harness; this is a different gap, outside it by construction.
3. The sandbox rollout (genetics-results-suite-4h6.7, 4h6.26, 4h6.27) rests on NetworkPolicy as the isolation boundary. If policies are not actually applied, that boundary does not exist at deploy time.

TO DO:
1. Diff every live policy against the committed one and record the drift. Read-only; do this first.
2. Work out WHY they were never reapplied - whether deploy.sh has genuinely not run in four months, or whether something makes the apply a no-op or skips it.
3. Apply the committed policies. This is a LIVE CLUSTER OPERATION and the user has held those back, so it needs their go-ahead - flag it rather than doing it.
4. Add a check that compares live policies against committed ones, or make test-network-policies.py able to run in a live mode. A harness that validates a file nobody applied is a harness that reports green on an unenforced control.
5. Then re-check every doc that cites policies.yaml as a bound.

DO NOT let this ride along with a feature bead - it needs its own window and its own verification.
