title: Scoped short-lived credential for sandbox to db-api
description:
The sandbox must never hold INTERNAL_API_SECRET. That secret authenticates the service, not the request, and a script that can read it can reach db-api directly and forever.

Design and implement a per-request, short-lived, audience-scoped token minted by chat-backend and injected into the sandbox execution environment for the lifetime of one script. db-api validates it alongside the existing shared secret. Include an expiry short enough that a leaked token is worthless (minutes), and make the token carry the session id so db-api logs attribute queries to a conversation.

Note the fail-open behaviour in db-api today (docs/project-spec.md: unset INTERNAL_API_SECRET disables auth with a startup warning) - the new path must NOT inherit fail-open.

Files: genetics-results-db/api/main.py, genetics-mcp-server sandbox client, k8s manifests.
close_reason:
Landed as suite cbd2165, mcp-server e26fd82, db 2dc03be, results-api c70f7ee. Files only; NOTHING applied to any cluster, per the standing hold. Full tier: review + blind validation + test runner in parallel, one fix round, then a targeted re-review. No blocking findings survived.

WHAT LANDED. chat-backend mints one HS256 token per destination per execution -- audience-bound so a results-api token cannot be replayed at db-api, 300s TTL, carrying sub, the chat session id, and an execution id that is also the /scratch/<id> directory name so logs join across chat-backend, the sandbox SDK and both backends. db-api and results-api validate offline. SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY is deliberately NOT INTERNAL_API_SECRET; exactly three Deployments mount it (chat-backend signs, the two verifiers verify), mcp-server does not, and the sandbox holds neither.

Tests: MCP 1274 -> 1285 passed / 74 deselected; db-api 65 -> 102 passed; results-api 482 -> 516 collected with 87 auth tests green (that suite cannot run green on this VM - ~282 pre-existing data-dependent failures needing GCS or local data, spot-checked as unrelated).

ATTACKED WITH 30 HAND-ROLLED TOKENS against both validators with real PyJWT, not just the repo's own tests. Closed and confirmed: alg none; RS256/HMAC confusion; HS384/512 with the correct key; wrong key; empty signature; every required claim missing or null; missing/null/empty scope; cross-audience replay both directions; foreign iss; expiry; and a far-future exp with an ancient iat. That last is why the age check exists independently of exp - effective lifetime is 300s from iat regardless of what exp claims, boundary confirmed at 299 accept / 301 reject.

TWO MINTER INVARIANTS THE VALIDATORS WERE TRUSTING RATHER THAN ASSERTING, both found independently by two reviewers, neither forgeable without the key but both undercutting the attribution this credential exists to produce: an EMPTY-STRING sub, sid or jti validated (PyJWT's require option rejects only missing and null), and aud as a LIST validated (PyJWT treats list aud as membership), so one token could have been valid at BOTH backends - single-destination binding was a minter property, not a validator one. Both asserted now.

ZERO FORWARD CLOCK-SKEW TOLERANCE, fixed with leeway=5. PyJWT >= 2.10 raises ImmatureSignatureError when iat > now and leeway defaulted to 0, so any positive skew between chat-backend and a verifier rejected a freshly minted token. The doc's argument that the short TTL makes skew a non-issue covers exp, not iat. The 300s age bound is separate and stays exact - re-verified after the change - so the acceptance window grew only on the not-yet-valid side, to 305s of verifier wall-clock.

THE FAIL-OPEN IS ROUTED AROUND, NOT REMOVED. db-api still disables auth entirely with a startup warning when INTERNAL_API_SECRET is unset; that is pre-existing and out of scope. The sandbox branch sits AHEAD of that early return, so a malformed sandbox token can never degrade into the shared-secret comparison or into no-auth. require_sandbox_config() sys.exit(1)s when SANDBOX_ENABLED is true and either secret is missing, both-unset included, and a reviewer confirmed both calls are on the REAL startup path - db-api's main.py IS the entrypoint given CMD ["python","main.py"] over COPY api/ ., and results-api's runs at import of app.server, where run_server.py's except Exception does NOT swallow SystemExit.

THE OPERATIONAL HAZARD WAS THE SECRET ORDERING, NOT THE CODE ORDERING. The code claim held up under checking (the path is entirely new; minter-only and validators-only are both safe; a token meeting an old validator 401s). But the new secret gate made create-secrets.sh mandatory before the next deploy on every existing cluster, and that script implements reuse-or-generate for only five keys - an operator re-running it with just ANTHROPIC_API_KEY exported, exactly what the old error message invited, would have blanked admin-users, external-mcp-servers, the Slack webhook and four API keys. The gate now emits a targeted kubectl patch for the single missing key and names the clobber. Script untouched; -4pj owns fixing it.

SANDBOX_ENABLED IS NOW COUPLED TO THE SANDBOX EXISTING. test-network-policies.py, already a deploy gate from 4h6.8, asserts sandbox.yaml present => both verifier manifests set it true. Without that, landing 4h6.7 with the flags still false silently voids the whole fail-closed guarantee. IMPORTANT FOR 4h6.7: both flags must flip in the SAME commit that adds sandbox.yaml or every deploy aborts with exit 1 - verified both ways on a scratch copy, and recorded in 4h6.7's notes because the first symptom is an aborted deploy with no obvious cause.

DELIBERATE SCOPE SPLIT: the design doc's per-credential BigQuery caps (50 GB/query, 200 GB per jti, row and response-byte ceilings, plus a defaults-not-penalty inversion that changes behaviour for EVERY caller of both services) are NOT implemented. No bead owned them and the blast radius is far wider than a credential. Filed as 4h6.28; this bead ships the request.state hook they need. So the credential lands WITHOUT the spend controls the doc pairs it with.

OTHER DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS, all recorded in an 'As built' subsection of the doc: iss is required rather than optional; iat age is checked explicitly because PyJWT accepts an ancient iat when exp is future; scope is required-present but kept out of the decoder's require list so its absence logs distinctly; results-api reports sandbox:<user> rather than the bare email so a script is never mistaken for a verified human.

ACCEPTED RESIDUALS, now written down rather than implicit: the symmetric key means a compromise of db-api OR results-api can MINT tokens impersonating chat-backend (Ed25519 with the private half at chat-backend would remove this while keeping offline validation); rotation is NOT atomic across the three Deployments, so every sandbox execution 401s across a rolling restart; jti is recorded but not consumed, so a leaked token is replayable within its 300s window; and @is_public routes skip auth_required entirely, which is an ATTRIBUTION gap as well as an authorization one - no principal, no sid/jti on endpoint_access for those five routes, and 4h6.28's caps will not key there.

ONE REAL BUG FOUND IN THE LOGGING: the sandbox authorization line passed a string message, so GCPJsonFormatter copied only names in EXTRA_LOG_FIELDS and none of sub/sid/jti reached jsonPayload - the line went nowhere. Added the three names rather than dropping the extra, since endpoint_access does not cover the @is_public set. Verified there is exactly one extra= call site in the whole service and no dependency collides on those names.

NOT WIRED TO ANYTHING YET, by design: mint_execution_tokens has no caller. Transport into the sandbox - the POST body, the mode-0600 /scratch/<id> file, the chown-before-fork rule - is 4h6.14, handoff recorded in its notes. So 'the sandbox gets this instead of the shared secret' is unproven end to end until 4h6.7 and 4h6.14 land.

LEFT UNDONE, filed: 4h6.28 (the caps), 4pj (create-secrets.sh blanks eight optional secrets on re-run, plus its silent-regeneration-on-kubectl-failure path), zyi (db-api compare_digest on str - the last known instance of the bug fad and th2 each fixed elsewhere - and PyJWT being the only unpinned validator dep). Nits unfiled: the harness routes an unanticipated manifest shape to exit 1 rather than exit 2, and two stale docstring lines about where Google tokens are handled.

title: NetworkPolicy: sandbox egress allow-list, and mcp-server must not reach it
description:
Two directions, both required.

Egress FROM sandbox: db-api (8080) and results-api (4000) only. Deny all other egress including DNS-to-internet, so a script cannot exfiltrate query results or fetch code. Deny access to keycloak, keycloak-postgres, chat-backend and rag-service.

Ingress TO sandbox: chat-backend ONLY. mcp-server must be denied at the network layer, not just by omitting the tool - this is the user's explicit requirement that code execution not be reachable via MCP, and the suite spec already warns (docs/project-spec.md:237) that mcp-server sits on both sides of the db-api policy, so a tool-registration omission alone is not a boundary.

Add a test that asserts the mcp-server pod cannot open a connection to the sandbox Service.

Files: k8s/network-policies/sandbox-policy.yaml (new), docs/project-spec.md (Security section).
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-10.

Files: k8s/network-policies/sandbox-policy.yaml (new, 2 objects: allow-ingress-sandbox and
sandbox-egress), k8s/network-policies/policies.yaml (allow-ingress-db-api and
allow-ingress-results-api each gained an explicit 'app: sandbox' peer),
scripts/test-network-policies.py (new, offline), scripts/check-doc-drift.sh (sandbox ->
code-execution-security.md row, which CLAUDE.md's ownership table already declared but the
script did not mirror), docs/project-spec.md (Security section) and
docs/code-execution-security.md (three amendments, below).

LABEL CONTRACT (recorded in the policy file header, project-spec, and 4h6.7's notes):
app: sandbox / containerPort 8080/TCP / Service 'sandbox' 8080 -> targetPort 8080.

deploy.sh needed NO change: it already runs 'kubectl apply -f network-policies/' on the
whole directory.

DOC AMENDMENTS, each because the design doc was written before fad/k4t landed:
1. The doc said to edit ONLY allow-ingress-db-api and warned against copying
   allow-ingress-results-api because it was from-less (admitting everything). fad closed
   that hole, so results-api now needs the sandbox added EXPLICITLY or the path is dropped
   at the receiving end. Doc corrected.
2. The doc claimed 169.254.169.254 was 'covered by default-deny'. That over-claims:
   link-local/node-local traffic is the exact class proven EXEMPT from NetworkPolicy on this
   dataplane in the ingress direction (kubelet probes from 169.254.4.6). Egress enforcement
   to a link-local address is UNVERIFIED here. Doc now says no coverage should be assumed;
   4h6.26 carries the live test.
3. Recorded the auth reality: both reverse-direction entries are REACHABILITY ONLY. db-api
   401s without Bearer INTERNAL_API_SECRET; results-api 401s post-fad without the marker or
   a valid bearer (REQUIRE_AUTH=true in prod, get_verified_user -> None -> 401). The sandbox
   holds neither by design, so every sandbox request 401s until 4h6.9. Expected, not a bug.

DNS: doc and policy AGREE - no kube-dns rule, hostAliases instead. No contradiction found.

TESTING: scripts/test-network-policies.py runs offline (no cluster, no network) and asserts
across ALL files in k8s/network-policies/ (union semantics) that no rule selecting the
sandbox admits mcp-server or the monitor, no sandbox rule is from-less, egress is exactly
db-api:8080 + results-api:4000 with no ipBlock and no port 53, and db-api/results-api admit
the sandbox on the right ports. Negative-tested by mutating a copy: it fails correctly.
Manifests also validated with kubectl apply --dry-run=client.
The LIVE mcp-server -> sandbox connection test the bead asks for could not be run (nothing is
deployed); it is filed as genetics-results-suite-4h6.26 for the deploy window, along with the
metadata-server question and a check that Cilium translates ClusterIP -> pod IP before egress
policy evaluation (sandbox-egress uses podSelector and depends on that ordering).

NOT DONE HERE (owned elsewhere): the sandbox Deployment/Service (4h6.7), the node pool
(4h6.10), the scoped credential (4h6.9), the MCP tool-registration exclusion and its test
(4h6.16).
close_reason:
Landed as 191489a. Files only; NOTHING applied to any cluster, per the standing hold. Full tier: review + blind validation in parallel, then two fix rounds and a targeted re-review, then a third round of three one-liners.

WHAT LANDED. k8s/network-policies/sandbox-policy.yaml (allow-ingress-sandbox + sandbox-egress), an app: sandbox peer added to allow-ingress-db-api and allow-ingress-results-api, scripts/test-network-policies.py as an offline manifest harness now gating deploy.sh, a check-doc-drift.sh row, and the project-spec Security section. Egress is db-api:8080/TCP and results-api:4000/TCP only; ingress is chat-backend:8080/TCP only.

Two SEPARATE egress rules, not one: `to` x `ports` cross-products within a rule, so a merged form would also have permitted db-api:4000 and results-api:8080. No ipBlock anywhere, which is the ONLY thing closing pl.write_parquet('s3://...') -- 4h6.6 established polars ships the Rust object_store with its own HTTP/TLS stack, so no image-level control touches it. Both rules pin TCP, so all UDP including DNS is denied, matching the doc's hostAliases decision.

THE REVERSE DIRECTION WAS REQUIRED AND IS EASY TO MISS: an egress allow-list alone leaves the data path dead, because each destination's own ingress policy must admit the sandbox too. Both amended inside the from: lists -fad and -k4t just scoped; neither became from-less, no port widened.

BOTH HALVES 401 TODAY. results-api requires -fad's marker, db-api requires the same bearer, and the sandbox deliberately holds neither. Reachability is in place; authorization is not, until 4h6.9. Recorded in both policy files and both docs rather than left to be rediscovered. The sandbox was NOT given the internal secret.

NO METADATA COVERAGE IS CLAIMED, and the doc's previous claim that default-deny covered it was an over-claim, now corrected. Nothing permits 169.254.169.254 so standard semantics deny it, but link-local is the same class already PROVEN exempt in the ingress direction on this dataplane, and egress enforcement to link-local has never been tested here. THE LOAD-BEARING CONTROL IS 4h6.10's GKE_METADATA POOL, so 4h6.10 must land before the sandbox ever runs untrusted code. 4h6.26 was widened to cover the node IP and 169.254.4.6, not just the metadata IP.

A LABEL MISMATCH IN 4h6.7 FAILS OPEN, ASYMMETRICALLY, and this is the most important thing for whoever does .7. This is the namespace's first and only egress policy -- 17 live policies, all Ingress -- so a pod missing the selector has NO egress policy applying and gets the allow-all default: full internet, DNS, metadata, API server, no event, no log. Ingress meanwhile fails closed and loudly, which invites precisely the wrong fix (relax ingress to match the pod, leaving egress uncovered). Contract is app: sandbox, containerPort 8080/TCP, Service sandbox 8080->8080, pinned in the policy header, project-spec and 4h6.7's notes, and the harness cross-checks the Deployment the day it appears.

THE HARNESS SHIPPED WITH TWO WAYS TO PASS WHILE mcp-server COULD REACH THE SANDBOX. Both found independently by two reviewers, both reproduced by mutation, both closed:
- policyTypes is OPTIONAL and Kubernetes INFERS it, so a policy admitting mcp-server with the field omitted was fully enforced by the API server and wholly invisible to the harness. Now inferred per SetDefaults_NetworkPolicy: Ingress ALWAYS, Egress only when egress is NON-EMPTY. The truthiness matters -- `egress: []` with no policyTypes would otherwise pass the deny-by-default check while the cluster left egress unrestricted.
- peer_selects returned False for any peer carrying a namespaceSelector, with an inline comment stating the wrong inference. `namespaceSelector: {}` matches every pod in every namespace, mcp-server included. Now fails closed on namespaceSelector, ipBlock and missing podSelector alike, via a raise the @check wrapper records as a normal failure.
It catches 11 of 13 mutations, including ones planted in a DIFFERENT policy file, which is the property that matters given union semantics.

IT WAS ALSO WIRED TO NOTHING -- no CI, and -rxw records no installed git hooks -- so the label-contract check would never have fired. Now gates deploy.sh before the network-policies apply AND before any deployment, so an abort cannot leave a sandbox pod running without its policy. Blocking on exit 1, warning on exit 2. Exit 2 had to be fixed in a third round: sys.exit(<str>) exits 1, so a machine without PyYAML would have aborted a production deploy while blaming a security control.

THE CILIUM QUESTION IS SETTLED, and the file's own hedge was the dangerous part. cilium-config sets bpf-lb-sock-hostns-only true, so pod->ClusterIP is translated in the pod's veth eBPF program and bpf_lxc DNATs before resolving destination identity and before egress policy evaluation; to: podSelector is correct, no Service-CIDR ipBlock needed (Cilium v1.18.7-gke1.35). The hedge had suggested exactly such a block, and 10.20.0.0/20 is every Service in the cluster INCLUDING kube-dns -- following it would have reopened the DNS exfiltration path the design exists to close. Now stated as settled with a /32-per-Service contingency and an explicit prohibition. Reasoned from config, not observed, because no pod in the cluster currently carries an egress policy; empirical confirmation is in 4h6.26. Also confirmed no other policy engine can widen any of this: enable-cilium-network-policy false, no CRD.

DOC OF RECORD FIXED: it contradicted itself between section 3 and its own summary table on whether allow-ingress-results-api was still from-less. Section 3 is right; -fad scoped it.

LEFT UNDONE, filed: 4h6.27 (P1, the transitive mcp-server -> chat-backend -> sandbox path -- the network layer closes one hop only, and section 5 now says so in prose; the run_analysis dispatch must reject the marker-alone mcp-tool identity, which mcp-server can produce since it holds the secret), r22 (three residual harness fail-opens, none reachable on today's manifests), 4h6.26 (live deploy-window verification, widened). The 'no signal anywhere' wording overstates the case since ingress dying IS a signal -- nit, unfiled.

title: Build the paired A/B replay benchmark harness
description:
New scripts/replay_benchmark.py. POSTs recorded turn sequences to /chat/v1/chat with secret=true (chat_api.py:295, so nothing is persisted) under two tool_profile arms in a PAIRED design - both arms in one execution so model drift cannot confound the comparison.

Report DISTRIBUTIONS, not just medians: production is heavily tail-weighted (median 2 iterations but p95 8, max 25). Metrics per arm: iterations/turn, tool calls/turn, wall-clock to first token and to done, input/output/cache tokens, USD. Plus code-execution-specific counters: script failure rate (non-zero exit, timeout, exception) and retry-loop count, since a failing script costs a full roundtrip.

Baseline to beat, measured 2026-08-07 over 916 turns since 2026-05-01: iterations median 2 / p90 6 / p95 8; tool calls per turn median 4 / p90 12; mean 2.01 USD per turn; 13.5% of turns >5 iterations consuming 35% of spend; median context 39k tokens at iteration 1 growing to 117k at iteration 7+ with uncached share rising 11% -> 52%.

Files: genetics-mcp-server/scripts/replay_benchmark.py (new).
notes:
HANDOFF from .1 (2026-08-07): .4's plan is to POST with secret=true 'so nothing is persisted' (chat_api.py:295). With .1 landed, secret=true ALSO means no chat_turn_metrics row is written — .1 deliberately skips metrics entirely for secret chat because secret chat is a privacy promise to the user. So the replay harness CANNOT read its numbers out of chat_turn_metrics when running secret.

Two options, pick one and record it: (a) read iterations/tokens/cost off the SSE stream itself — llm_service.py already yields a 'usage' StreamChunk per iteration carrying iteration, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_input_tokens, total_output_tokens, context_window, context_percent; or (b) run non-secret against a throwaway copy of chat_history.db and read chat_turn_metrics.

(a) is probably better: it needs no DB at all and works against any deployment.

ENVIRONMENT TRAP: in a fresh genetics-mcp-server worktree, 'uv run pytest' resolved to the pyenv shim rather than the worktree venv and imported genetics_mcp_server from the MAIN CHECKOUT, silently testing unmodified source. Run 'uv sync --extra dev' first, then assert the module resolves inside the worktree before trusting any test result.
close_reason:
Paired A/B replay harness built. genetics-mcp-server worktree fbf121e. Suite 1165 -> 1194 passed, 74 deselected, 0 failed. One reviewer, one fix round.

BUILD ONLY - running it against a deployment is task .23, separately gated. Default base URL is localhost, --dry-run issues zero requests, secret=true is a hard-coded literal with no flag or env override.

THREE PREMISE CORRECTIONS:
1. The usage chunk's input_tokens is the WHOLE CONTEXT (input_tok + cache_read + cache_create), not billed input. Cached tokens are derived by subtracting total_input_tokens.
2. COST CANNOT BE COMPUTED EXACTLY FROM THE STREAM. Cache reads and creations are folded into one number and never separated, yet they differ by exactly 12.5x in price. The harness reports an INTERVAL (all-cached-as-reads to all-cached-as-creations) rather than fabricating a figure; since every per-token price lies between those, the true cost is provably inside it. This weakens the metric .23 gates on - production data shows the cache-read share swinging 11% to 52% across a turn, so the interval will not be narrow. Fix filed as genetics-results-suite-n3p: emit cache_read/cache_create on the usage chunk. Both are already computed and already logged one line away.
3. An unpriceable --model was silently priced as Sonnet by cost.py's fallback. Now warns and returns null.

CAUGHT IN REVIEW - either would have INVERTED the result:
- Replayed history dropped tool_results. Production pushes them back as a user turn (LLMChat.tsx ~595-599); without them _sanitize_tool_blocks strips every tool_use block from the replayed assistant turn as orphaned, so from turn 2 the model saw an answer from thin air. Tool results are the BULK of the context growth this epic exists to measure (39k -> 117k, uncached 11% -> 52%), and the bias was ASYMMETRIC - the arm making more tool calls lost more context, compressing the measured gap toward zero. A code-execution arm would have looked no better than the status quo.
- The paired design was never used in the ANALYSIS. Distributions were built per arm independently over ok turns, so an arm failing on the hard, late, expensive turns kept only its cheap early ones and its medians dropped BECAUSE it failed. Recording failures is not excluding them from the comparison. Matched subset (ok in both arms) is now the headline; marginals survive explicitly labelled not-comparable.

ALSO FIXED: a wedged stream could keepalive past the per-turn timeout forever (httpx read timeout is per-read and sse-starlette comments reset it, so the TimeoutError handler was dead code); a whole-case exception collapsed N turns into 2 records; a turn with no usage chunk contributed a fake tool_calls=0, which EVERY turn would do against a deployment defaulting to OpenAI (--provider added); MIN_N_FOR_PERCENTILE[90] was 11 not 10 through float error.

VERIFIED CORRECT BY REVIEW: tool calls counted from real tool_use blocks never the prose markers (.2's imitation finding); the cost interval is a true bound computed the right way round; semaphore scope makes arms of one case non-overlapping; arm alternation recorded per case; per-turn failure aborts only that case+arm.

DESIGNED-IN GUARDS: percentiles flagged unreliable when n(1-p) < 1 so a p90 from 9 cases is not presented as stable; script_runs/script_failures/retry_loops look for a chunk that does not exist yet and stay None with an explicit NOT MEASURED reason, so the eventual code-execution arm cannot win trivially on a silent zero.

LEFT UNDONE: wording nits - UNMEASURED_REASONS missing script_runs, the doc's section heading path, arm_order_per_case keyed on case_id (two cases sharing a session_id would collide), two different Ns on one screen, and no test asserting --dry-run issues zero requests. Fold into genetics-results-suite-5r2.

chat_turn_metrics table landed. genetics-mcp-server worktree commit 18f919d. Suite 993 -> 999 passed, 74 deselected, 0 failed.

THE TICKET'S KEYING PREMISE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED. (session_id, message_id) is unavailable at write time: PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON (chat_history_db.py:90) and the assistant chat_messages row is POSTed by the client only AFTER the stream ends, so an FK always aborts; and ChatPage.tsx handleFirstExchange creates the session only after the first exchange completes, so EVERY conversation's opening turn streams with session_id null. - Cross-user overwrite: the upsert keyed on client-supplied message_id with no ownership scope. Reproduced empirically - user B overwrote user A's row, cost zeroed 9.99 -> 0.0, session reassigned, silently. Fixed with a user_id column (from auth_required, never the request body) guarding the DO UPDATE; a conflicting write from another user inserts nothing and logs.

title: ChatRequest.system_prompt lets any authenticated user replace the entire system prompt
description:
Flagged during planning of the Instructions epic (genetics-results-suite-s5y) and deliberately left out of its scope. Now in scope on its own.

genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/chat_api.py:215 declares ChatRequest.system_prompt, used verbatim at ~line 458:
    system_prompt = request.system_prompt or default_system_prompt(settings.app_name)
There is no allow-list, no admin gate, no length bound. Any authenticated caller can replace the ENTIRE system prompt for their turn - discarding every grounding, citation, truncation and out-of-scope rule the default prompt establishes.

This is a strictly larger hole than the feature built next to it. The Instructions epic went to some length to make user-authored text safe: the body is resolved server-side by id so it never travels on the request, it is capped, it is wrapped in an envelope with a trailing guardrail, and it is scoped to presentation only. All of that is bypassed by a field sitting two lines away that accepts arbitrary prompt text with no constraints at all.

SCOPING ALREADY DONE - nothing in the suite sends it:
- genetics-results-browser: zero references in src/ or bff/
- the only senders anywhere are tests (tests/test_chat_api.py:356 test_chat_custom_system_prompt, and the stream-truncation harness which passes system_prompt=None)
- llm_service.stream_chat(system_prompt=...) is a separate INTERNAL parameter that chat_api populates with the assembled default+verbosity prompt. That stays; only the request-level override is the hole.

Preferred fix: remove the field from ChatRequest entirely. Pydantic ignores unknown fields by default, so a caller still sending it is silently ignored rather than 422'd - a graceful removal with no client breakage.

Before removing, confirm there is no external consumer: the chat API is also reachable with a bearer API token (see the Authorization: Bearer path that bypasses the BFF), so check whether any script, notebook or sibling repo drives it directly. If a legitimate need exists, the fallback is an admin gate plus a length bound rather than leaving it open.
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit f8302b9. Suite 935 passed / 74 deselected across two seeds.

Removed rather than gated, after confirming across all six repos that nothing sends it - not the browser, not the BFF, not any script; only a test. Pydantic ignores unknown keys, so a caller still sending it is ignored rather than 422'd. A side benefit: block 0 of the two-block cached system prompt is now unconditionally identical across users, which its cache design already assumed.

THE SAME CAPABILITY EXISTED IN A SECOND FORM, found independently by both reviewers and fixed here too: the Anthropic path filtered client-sent system-role messages but the OpenAI path did not, and provider is client-selectable with OPENAI_API_KEY wired into the pod, so a system-role message landed AFTER the server prompt where recency favours it. Rather than filter per provider, ChatMessage.role is now Literal['user','assistant'] - the authority boundary is the request model. Both provider filters stay as defence in depth because stream_chat is reachable with raw dicts.

422 rather than a silent drop: the history endpoint already rejects those roles, so no caller has reason to send one, and quietly discarding an injection attempt hides it from the caller and the logs.

Verified no real flow breaks: the browser builds message history only from stored rows plus hardcoded user literals; chat_history.py:414 rejects non-user/assistant at persistence and add_message has exactly one caller, so no system-role row can exist to be replayed; fork copies roles from rows that already passed that check.

Corrected a false claim I had put in the bead and the docs: the chat API is NOT reachable with a per-user API token. auth_required accepts the IAP/oauth2-proxy header or a Bearer INTERNAL_API_SECRET resolving to identity 'mcp-tool'; per-user tokens are validated only by the internal-only /tokens/validate that the /mcp path consumes. The security argument is unaffected - any IAP-authenticated user could already do it.

Follow-ups filed: the tool-descriptions authz gap, and the assistant-role length bound.

title: mcp-server cannot reach db-api: all BigQuery-backed MCP tools fail
description:
The standalone mcp-server (/mcp path, used by external MCP clients) has NEVER been able to reach db-api, so every BigQuery-backed tool returns 'BigQuery API URL not configured'.

Confirmed failing live on daly (2026-07-21): query_bigquery, get_bigquery_schema, get_asm_qtl_by_gene, get_open_chromatin_by_gene, get_variant_effect_by_gene.

Two independent causes, BOTH must be fixed:
1. BIGQUERY_API_URL is set in k8s/deployments/chat-backend.yaml but has never existed in k8s/deployments/mcp-server.yaml (git log -S confirms no commit ever added it).
2. NetworkPolicy allow-ingress-db-api (k8s/network-policies/policies.yaml:137-151) admits only app=chat-backend; monitor-policy.yaml adds monitor. mcp-server is not permitted, so even with the env var set the call would be blocked.

Manifests are profile-independent => affects finngen AND daly equally.

chat-backend is unaffected (has the env var and is allowed by policy), so the web UI agent's BQ tools work; only the standalone MCP server is impacted.

Note these tools are BigQuery-by-design: results-api has no by-gene open_chromatin endpoint, so executor.py:824 resolves gene->coords via gene_annotations_v.

Decision needed: opening db-api to mcp-server is a network-isolation change, not just a config fix.
notes: Config fix committed cb18545 (BIGQUERY_API_URL on mcp-server.yaml + mcp-server podSelector on allow-ingress-db-api NetworkPolicy). Left OPEN: takes effect only after cluster rollout (scripts/rollout.sh mcp-server + re-apply NetworkPolicy). Close after deploy verifies BigQuery-backed MCP tools work.

After deploy: running mcp-server has BIGQUERY_API_URL set; allow-ingress-db-api NetworkPolicy admits app=mcp-server; from pod mcp-server-75fd7c8644 TCP connect to db-api:8080 succeeds (was TimeoutError), /health=200, and POST /query 'SELECT 1 AS ok' returns 200 rows=[[1]]. title: Phase 0: decide ChromBPNet row-scale thresholding policy
description: Count ChromBPNet variant-score rows (132 contexts x variants, potentially billions). Decide thresholding (significant/non-zero only, or top-N per context) before sizing tabix/BQ. Biggest scale risk. Gates the Marderstein munge task.
design:
RECOMMENDED DEFAULT thresholding policy (empirical cutoff + row counts to be CONFIRMED once data is downloaded — blocked on .1). Keep this task OPEN.
Problem: ChromBPNet = 132 contexts x all variants (~3 billion predictions in the paper). Do NOT store the full cross-product.
Default:
- ChromBPNet -> variant_effect (model=chrombpnet), LONG. Emit a row only for (variant, context) pairs that pass a significance/effect threshold, NOT all 132 contexts per variant. Prefer the per-context significance calls provided by the Synapse release if present; else keep per-context empirical mlog10p >= 3 (p <= 1e-3) OR abs(chrombpnet_logfc) in the top 1 percent per context. Always set is_significant and mlog10p so the cutoff is transparent and re-filterable.
- Retain a variant if significant in ANY context (so by_variant lookups return it); emit its passing contexts, plus optionally its single top context.
- FLARE -> variant_effect (model=flare): keep the FULL released FLARE prioritized-variant set (already curated and far smaller); pan-context rows with cell_type/tissue NULL.
Rationale: bounds storage to variants with a real predicted effect somewhere (millions, not billions) — exactly what the query needs. Empirical step (after .1): count rows at this cutoff, confirm the significance fields the release actually provides, adjust cutoff to a sane table size.
close_reason: Decision made: default thresholding policy adopted (recorded in --design). Empirical row-count confirmation happens inside the Marderstein munge task (.13), which applies and tunes the default; no separate gate needed.

title: Feature: open-chromatin (scATAC) + variant-effect data
description: Add two new data products to the platform: (A) open_chromatin — an atlas of accessible/active regions labeled by cell type/tissue/condition (variant/region/gene -> accessible contexts); (B) variant_effect — in-silico predicted variant effect on accessibility (ChromBPNet, FLARE). Onboard 6 datasets: Marderstein/Kundaje 2026 (A+B), Li 2023 brain, Zhang 2021 Catlas, EpiMap (ChromHMM active states + enhancer-gene links), Calderon 2019 immune stimulation, ROSMAP/Xiong 2023 AD brain. Full design in /home/jkarjala/.claude/plans/we-want-to-start-stateless-eich.md. Execution via beads-ralph-wiggum.
design:
TABIX INDEXING CONTRACT (surfaced by the .7 results-api open_chromatin review — the API overlap engine depends on this):
- open_chromatin files (.13 peaks, .14-.18): MUST be INTERVAL-indexed — tabix -p bed (i.e. -s1 -b2 -e3, distinct start/end columns). Do NOT point-index (-b2 -e2): the API point-query fast path would trigger and variant-overlap queries would SILENTLY MISS peaks whose interval contains pos.
- variant_effect files (.13 chrombpnet, flare): point-indexed — tabix -s1 -b2 -e2.
- ALL files: bgzip; sort -k1,1 -k2,2n before bgzip; chr-prefixed seqnames (chr1..chr22, chrX/chrY/chrMT); columns in the EXACT canonical order from the plan (open_chromatin 18 cols chrom..version; variant_effect 18 cols chrom..version). The API prepends `resource` itself; do not add it to the file.
- GCS paths: gs://finngen-commons/results_api_data/{open_chromatin,variant_effect}/<resource>/<dataset_id>.tsv.gz (+ .tbi) and the gs://daly-genetics-results/... equivalent. These must match the results-api profile config file paths added in .7/.8.
notes: Epic-level review (isolated resolver): all 21 non-optional children CLOSED. Feature fully implemented, merged, and DEPLOYED on both profiles: branch open-chromatin-variant-effect is an ancestor of master in every repo (genetics-results-suite, -api, -db, -munge, -mcp-server) — nothing unmerged. finngen (bzl.19) and daly (bzl.20) deploys both verified: open_chromatin_v ~232.7M rows / variant_effect_v ~21.7M rows, endpoints + MCP tools live. Only OPEN child is bzl.22 (optional full ChromBPNet common/rare/ldsc run) — data-completeness only, needs Synapse creds + ~48GB download + BQ reload, gated on explicit demand; NOT a code/feature gap (FLARE already answers the question). Epic left OPEN solely because of optional bzl.22; no autonomous code work remains. (Note: bzl.20 close_reason flags a separate pre-existing gap — standalone mcp-server lacks BIGQUERY_API_URL so its 5 BQ-backed by_gene tools are dead on both profiles; filed separately, out of this epic's scope.)
close_reason: Closed per owner: feature fully implemented, merged, and deployed+verified on both profiles (open_chromatin_v ~232.7M rows, variant_effect_v ~21.7M rows; endpoints + MCP tools live). All children closed (bzl.22 optional ChromBPNet run closed as won't-do).

title: create-secrets.sh treats MCP_API_KEY as optional, but mcp-server refuses to start without it
description:
A first deploy that does not export MCP_API_KEY leaves mcp-server in CrashLoopBackOff, by construction. Three places disagree about whether the key is optional:

- scripts/create-secrets.sh:118 runs it through reuse_optional and writes an EMPTY string when it is neither exported nor already in the cluster. The header comment calls it '(optional)'.
- k8s/deployments/mcp-server.yaml:33-37 marks the secretKeyRef optional: true, so the kubelet starts the pod with the variable empty.
- genetics-mcp-server/src/genetics_mcp_server/mcp_server.py:510-513 hard-requires it for the sse and streamable-http transports: os.environ.get('MCP_API_KEY','').strip() empty -> logger.error('MCP_API_KEY is required for remote transports - refusing to start without authentication') -> sys.exit(1). There is no escape hatch.

Measured on the staging bring-up, 2026-08-26: genetics-secrets held mcp-api-key as a present-but-zero-byte value, and both mcp-server replicas crash-looped for ~15 minutes until a key was generated and the secret rewritten.

The refusal itself is correct and should stay - a remote-transport server with no bearer secret is the failure 618 exists to prevent. What is wrong is that the deploy tooling advertises the key as optional and will happily produce the state the server refuses to run in.

Same class as 4h6.100: a gap only a genuine first deploy can surface.
design:
ORCHESTRATOR RULING 2026-08-27, after a probe rather than from memory.

OPTION (c) IS A NO-OP AND IS WITHDRAWN. This bead's own design field offered 'drop optional: true from the manifest so the pod stops at CreateContainerConfigError'. That cannot fire: create-secrets.sh:160 writes --from-literal=mcp-api-key="${MCP_API_KEY:-}" unconditionally, so the key is ALWAYS present in genetics-secrets, empty at worst. optional: true only governs an ABSENT key. The failure mode is an EMPTY value, which satisfies the kubelet either way and reaches the process. optional: true is therefore already a dead flag for any Secret this script creates - worth noting somewhere, but not the fix.

OPTION (b) (refuse up front) REJECTED: it makes a first deploy abort on a secret the deployment mints for ITSELF.

TAKING OPTION (a): generate when absent, i.e. move MCP_API_KEY from the reuse_optional group to the same reuse-or-generate treatment as internal-api-secret, sandbox-token-signing-key and gateway-identity-secret.

WHY (a) despite the script's header arguing against inventing keys: that argument is explicitly about THIRD-PARTY keys (openai, tavily, perplexity, cohere) where a random value is a plausible-looking credential that fails only at call time. MCP_API_KEY is not third-party - it is a shared bearer secret this deployment issues, so a generated value is authoritative by construction: it IS what clients must present. It is the same class as the three secrets already generated, and belongs with them.

PROBE-ESTABLISHED FACTS the implementation may rely on:
- The startup refusal is UNCONDITIONAL for sse/streamable-http. Straight-line control flow in mcp_server.py main(); nothing consults Keycloak/OAuth, GOOGLE_TOKEN_AUDIENCE, chat API tokens or any ConfigMap before sys.exit(1). Configuring the other bearer paths does NOT satisfy it.
- The value is ROTATION-SAFE: no manifest bakes a literal, no client config pins one, no test asserts a production value, no doc contains a real key. Only coupling is operational (an external client holding an old shared key must be re-issued).
- reuse_optional already carries an existing cluster value forward, so generate-on-first-install stays stable across re-runs.
acceptance_criteria: A first deploy with no MCP_API_KEY exported either produces a working mcp-server or fails with a message naming the variable BEFORE the pod is created - not a CrashLoopBackOff discovered afterwards. create-secrets.sh's header no longer calls the key optional if it is not.
close_reason:
LANDED as suite b27545c. Standard implementation + FULL-tier validation (sighted review + blind validation in parallel), one fix round.

WHAT LANDED: MCP_API_KEY moved from the reuse_optional group to reuse-or-generate, alongside internal-api-secret, sandbox-token-signing-key and gateway-identity-secret. openssl rand -hex 32 rather than the neighbours' -base64 32, deliberately: this is the one secret a human pastes into a client config, and hex avoids base64's +/= entirely. Header comments, README and project-spec updated.

OPTION (c) WITHDRAWN, NOT IMPLEMENTED - and this bead's own design field had proposed it. A probe established create-secrets.sh:176 writes --from-literal=mcp-api-key unconditionally, so the key is ALWAYS present and optional:true on the manifest secretKeyRef governs a state that cannot occur. Removing it would have fixed nothing. The flag is left in place and now documented as provably dead. Filing a fix on an unchecked premise is what the probe rule exists to prevent.

THE RISK THAT WAS RAISED AND DISPROVED: silent rotation. Both reviewers extracted the assignment shape into scratch scripts with a stubbed kubectl and ran it across seven cluster states (unreachable, unset context, kubectl absent rc127, RBAC denial, key present-and-valid, key malformed base64, secret NotFound). VAR="${VAR:-$(cmd)}" is a standalone assignment, so bash takes its status from the command substitution and set -e aborts. The file's own warning comment describes a DIFFERENT shape (substitution inside a command's arguments, as in printf -v) and this site is on the safe side of it. Only 'secret absent' and 'key empty' reach the generator, and neither can be a value a client holds, because an empty key is exactly the crash-looping state. Same reasoning retro-covers the three pre-existing secrets.

END-TO-END TRACED by both reviewers: script -> Secret -> Deployment env -> the mcp_server.py guard. 64 hex chars survive .strip() and split(','), yield exactly one key, and /healthz is served ahead of the bearer check, so the pod reaches READY rather than merely starting.

FIX ROUND (all four documentation facts this change itself made false; the repo treats an enumeration the code no longer matches as broken): project-spec's 'both replicas' - the manifest is replicas: 1, and what was actually observed on daly-staging was TWO REPLICASETS each holding one pod, i.e. a rollout that could not converge, which is a different failure and is now stated as such; the ASCII parenthetical that named only base64; code-execution-security still listing mcp-api-key among the optional keys that 'survive untouched', now false for the empty case this fix exists to repair; and a new comment enumeration naming four reuse-then-generate secrets where re-derivation from the code gives seven across three Secrets.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: no README instructions for reading the generated key back. Echoing it would violate CLAUDE.md's credentials-out-of-output rule, and README already steers clients to per-user API tokens. Both reviewers raised it as a usability gap; recorded here rather than fixed.

BOUNDED BY genetics-results-suite-aka (filed and iced): deploy.sh:369's secret preflight does not list mcp-api-key, so a cluster ALREADY holding the empty value is not self-healed by a plain deploy - only by re-running create-secrets.sh. First installs and re-runs are covered; the existing broken state is not. daly-staging was fixed by hand on 2026-08-26.

GATE NOTE for future cycles: check-doc-drift.sh inspects git diff --cached only, so running it against an unstaged tree is trivially green and proves nothing. It was re-run here after staging.

title: artifacts_retained_in_clear never reaches the model: executor.py renders a whitelist that drops it
description:
FOUND 2026-08-24 in the final fix round of genetics-results-suite-4h6.88, by the fix agent checking how
the response is consumed before choosing a field name. NOT a defect in that change - the supervisor half is
correct and committed (genetics-results-suite 2cc877b). This is the other half of the same signal.

THE SUPERVISOR NOW REPORTS A SECURITY RESIDUAL THAT NOBODY RECEIVES.
4h6.88 added a boolean `artifacts_retained_in_clear` to the /execute response. It is true exactly when the
supervisor could NEITHER encrypt NOR delete an execution's artifacts, i.e. when that execution's outputs are
sitting in plaintext on a flat /scratch readable by any process at the shared uid 65532 until the reaper
removes the directory. It is deliberately NOT folded into `artifacts_omitted`, so that "some artifacts were
omitted" cannot be confused with "your data is readable by anyone in this pod".

WHERE IT DIES, verified by reading both hops:
- genetics-mcp-server sandbox_client._result() validates only `status` and `execution_id` and returns the
  whole body, so unknown fields PASS THROUGH. Adding the field was backward-compatible. Good.
- genetics-mcp-server tools/executor.py then renders a WHITELIST into the tool result - success, status,
  output, output_truncated, artifacts, duration_ms, and artifacts_omitted only when > 0. Anything not on
  that list is silently dropped. `artifacts_retained_in_clear` is not on it.
So the field is correct on the wire and invisible to the model and to the user. A signal nobody receives is
not a signal.

THE FIX IS SMALL: add the field to that `rendered` dict (~3 lines - and consider rendering it only when
true, matching how artifacts_omitted is handled, so the ordinary case does not carry noise), plus the
enumeration at that repo's docs/project-spec.md:292 which LISTS the forwarded fields and would otherwise be
stale the moment this lands.

WORTH DECIDING RATHER THAN ASSUMING, and this is the actual content of the task: WHAT SHOULD THE MODEL DO
WHEN IT SEES THIS? The condition is adversarial-only in practice (measured during 4h6.88: ENOSPC does NOT
trigger it, because unlink succeeds when writes fail; the realistic route is a same-uid peer chmod-ing the
artifacts directory). Options range from surfacing it as a plain field, to wording in the tool description
telling the model to warn the user, to treating it as an operator-only signal that belongs in logs rather
than in the model's context. Do not just plumb the boolean through without answering this - a field the
model sees and cannot act on is only marginally better than one it never sees.

NOTE THE WHITELIST IS THE GENERAL HAZARD, not this field: any future response field added on the supervisor
side is silently dropped by default. Whoever picks this up should decide whether the whitelist should stay a
whitelist. That is the same shape as EXTRA_LOG_FIELDS in genetics-results-suite-4h6.65 - an allow-list where
forgetting to add an entry fails silently - so the two are worth thinking about together.
close_reason:
LANDED with 4h6.52 in one cycle - genetics-mcp-server c62f0d4 + genetics-results-suite 0e1da90 -
because both live in _render_analysis / executor.py and would otherwise have collided.

THE DEFECT: 4h6.88 added artifacts_retained_in_clear to the supervisor's /execute response, true exactly
when the supervisor could NEITHER encrypt NOR delete an execution's artifacts. executor.py's
_render_analysis rebuilds the response FIELD BY FIELD from a whitelist, so the field was silently
dropped and the model never saw it. A signal nobody receives is not a signal.

THE DESIGN QUESTION WAS THE TASK, not the plumbing, and the answer shapes the wording: THE EXPOSURE IS
TO OTHER TENANTS' CODE IN THE POD, NOT TO THIS USER - the user's own artifacts are theirs to see - so
"your results may be compromised" is wrong on both halves. The primary audience is the OPERATOR and
LOG.error already serves it. The model's job is narrow and the note says exactly that: report that the
run's output files could not be removed from shared scratch, and stop treating those artifacts as
trusted input, BECAUSE BYTES READABLE BY A PEER ARE WRITABLE BY ONE - the same condition
read_artifact's 409 catches. success stays true; the analysis result still stands.
Rendered ONLY WHEN TRUE, matching artifacts_omitted, so an ordinary run carries no noise. Verified
unforgeable: a model-supplied False / 'yes' / 1 / 'true' / None all render nothing (strict `is True`).

THEN BLIND VALIDATION FOUND THE SIGNAL WAS SUPPRESSIBLE BY THE ADVERSARY, which is the same defect class
one layer out. _render_analysis put script-controlled `output` third and the flag seventh, while
llm_service truncates the serialized result to a PREFIX at mcp_max_result_size = 50000 and the
supervisor permits 64 KiB of output. MEASURED: len(result_json) = 66569, and both the flag and its note
were gone from the truncated result. A script that provokes the condition AND prints ~50 KB of stdout
deleted its own warning, and the generic [TRUNCATED: ...] notice says nothing about a dropped security
field.
FIXED BOTH WAYS, and mutation proved neither subsumes the other: the security fields now precede
`output` in the rendered dict (cheap, but relies on json.dumps insertion order), AND _truncation_notice
re-attaches the note by reading the flag from the WHOLE PRE-TRUNCATION dict (order-independent).
Reverting the ordering fails the field-name assertion; disabling the re-attachment fails the standalone
notice assertion.

NOT DONE, deliberately and still open as a general hazard: _render_analysis IS STILL A WHITELIST, so the
next field added on the supervisor side will again be dropped silently. That is the same shape as
EXTRA_LOG_FIELDS in genetics-results-suite-4h6.65 - an allow-list where forgetting an entry fails
silently - and 4h6.65's notes now say to answer the question once, for both, rather than twice.

title: Shorten RETENTION_S from 900 to 300, cutting the measured same-uid artifact exposure window 3x
description:
AUTHORISED BY THE USER 2026-08-20, out of the feasibility probe for genetics-results-suite-4h6.88.
This is the one piece of the .88 decision that is INDEPENDENT of every other option - it cannot become
wasted work whichever way .88 goes, and it composes with encryption rather than competing with it.

WHAT AND WHY. RETENTION_S = 900 (sandbox/supervisor.py:238) with REAPER_POLL_S = 30 gives a measured
exposure window of [900, 930)s during which ANY same-uid process can read a completed execution's
artifacts/ - the primary vector in 4h6.88, MEASURED there:
    listdir(/scratch) -> ['.supervisor', '<victim-uuid>', '<own-uuid>']
    peer_entries: ['private.csv']   read: 'SECRET-VICTIM-DATA'
Shortening the constant does not close the vector, but it is the only lever that shrinks it for
approximately no work and no new mechanism, no new dependency and no new trust assumption.

THE WINDOW IS ~30x WHAT THE REAL FLOW NEEDS. READ, from genetics-mcp-server:
- The client fetches artifacts IMMEDIATELY, in the same await chain. tools/executor.py:6015 is
      return self._render_analysis(result, images=await self._fetch_analysis_images(result))
  and _fetch_analysis_images runs the moment the supervisor's 200 lands, fetching at most
  _MAX_ANALYSIS_IMAGES = 4 image artifacts sequentially, with NO retry and NO deferral.
- GENERAL ARTIFACT RETRIEVAL DOES NOT EXIST YET. sandbox_client.py:13 states "artifact retrieval over HTTP
  is 4h6.52's and no route for it exists", and the read_artifact MCP tool (tools/definitions.py:2483 ->
  executor.py:5623) reads a LOCAL directory via SANDBOX_ARTIFACTS_DIR, which is deliberately unset in the
  chat backend - so it is inert.
So for the flow that exists TODAY, ~30s would suffice. The cost lands entirely on the flow that does not
exist yet: docs/code-execution-security.md specifies 4h6.52 as the model calling read_artifact BY NAME
later in the conversation, with name collisions resolving to the most recent still-retained execution -
which needs an artifact to outlive several model turns and a user reading a plot.

DECIDED VALUE: RETENTION_S = 300 (5 minutes). Observable window becomes [300, 330)s, a 3x cut. It covers
today's immediate fetch with enormous margin, covers a handful of model turns for 4h6.52, and stays well
above the failure mode anyone would actually notice. 120s is defensible if 4h6.52 is never built; 60s is
the floor (a slow multi-image fetch plus a supervisor restart race). DO NOT go below 60.

=== THE DOCS ARE THE WORK, NOT THE CONSTANT ===
"900" / "15 minutes" / "fifteen minutes" is enumerated in AT LEAST 13 PLACES across
docs/code-execution-security.md and docs/project-spec.md. Under this repo's doc-ownership rule
(sandbox/** -> docs/code-execution-security.md AND docs/project-spec.md) that sweep is mandatory and
in-commit, and under its stale-enumeration rule the list must be RE-DERIVED by grep rather than trusted -
including this bead's own count, which is a floor and not a promise.
DISTINGUISH TWO KINDS OF MENTION and do not blindly replace: (a) the VALUE of the retention window, which
must change; (b) prose about the CONCEPT of a retention window, or arithmetic that happens to contain 900
for an unrelated reason (quotas, ceilings, timeouts, MAX_QUEUED_WAIT_S). Changing (b) is a defect.

=== ALSO CHECK, none of which should need changing but all of which must be looked at ===
- SANDBOX_RETENTION_S override machinery: supervisor.py:4518 validates 1..RETENTION_S and only ever
  SHORTENS, so it needs nothing - confirm rather than assume.
- scripts/test-supervisor.py: any test keyed to RETENTION_S or to a 900-second horizon. reap_expired and
  the retention tests must still pass; 325 passed / 2 skipped is the baseline.
- The retained-state accounting from 4h6.82 (RETAINED_STATE_CEILING_BYTES, _enforce_retained_ceiling):
  shorter retention means FEWER live rows, so this can only help - but say so rather than ignoring it.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, and the doc must not imply otherwise: it does not close the read vector (4h6.88),
does not affect the LIVE execution window at all, and does not change integrity (4h6.82) or the escapee
class (4h6.83). It shrinks one window by 3x. State it that way.
close_reason:
LANDED. genetics-results-suite 93ae8d0. RETENTION_S = 15 * 60 -> 5 * 60.

The measured same-uid artifact exposure window goes from [900, 930)s to [300, 330)s - a 3x cut in
4h6.88's primary vector. REAPER_POLL_S = 30 is unchanged, so the window stays a RANGE rather than an
instant, which the code comments already said and still say.

THE ONLY EXECUTABLE CHANGE IN THE ENTIRE DIFF IS THE CONSTANT. Everything else is comments and docs.

THE SWEEP TOOK THREE PASSES, AND THE REASON IS THE REUSABLE LESSON: every miss was FORM VARIATION, not a
missed file.
- Pass 1: 25 sites, well above the 13 this bead named as a floor.
- Pass 1 MISSED reap_expired's own docstring ("nothing persists beyond 15 minutes") because the
  supervisor.py grep used `fifteen|900|930|15 \* 60` while the docs grep used the digit form `15 minute`.
  The retention value was wrong in the docstring of the function that implements retention.
- Pass 2 found a second: a table row stating the window as `[15 min, 15 min + 30 s]` - the same [900, 930)
  arithmetic expressed in different units.
- An independent re-derivation then swept for LINE-WRAPPED forms no single-line grep can catch
  (`15\nminutes`, `fifteen\nminutes`) plus retention-context proximity matches, and confirmed nothing
  remains in any form: 900, 900.0, 15*60, 15 min, 15-minute, fifteen, "quarter of an hour".
IF THIS IS EVER REDONE, unify the pattern across every file before starting. Two greps with different
patterns is how both misses happened.

KIND-(b) MENTIONS WERE CHECKED ONE BY ONE AND LEFT ALONE - rewriting one would have been the real defect:
2900 MiB (RLIMIT_AS/OOM), 1900m/1930m/2376m (CPU allocatable), "14-day retention" (GCE snapshots),
"~line 900" (a citation into supervisor.py), the GKE autoscaler's ~15 min scale-down, a 900-character line
limit, and `time.monotonic() + 900` in the tests (arbitrary far-future deadlines, still correct as
literals because 900 > 300).
THE NEAR-MISS WORTH RECORDING: docs/code-execution-security.md documents a separate 300s TOKEN TTL, and
this task was changing values TO 300. Replacing it would have silently rewritten an unrelated security
constant to match. It was correctly left.

A COLLISION THIS CHANGE CREATES, handled rather than left implicit: RETENTION_S is now numerically EQUAL
to the token TTL, where previously 900 > 300.
- NO CODE PATH DEPENDS ON THE ORDERING. Verified by reading the route: GET /artifact reads no
  Authorization header, decodes no token and compares no exp - it authorizes on execution_id, and the
  sandbox token is the child's INBOUND credential to db-api/results-api, not the outbound fetch. Every
  RETENTION_S reference is inside supervisor.py; no other file reads it.
- MAX_QUEUED_WAIT_S (120s, commented as constrained by the token TTL) is unaffected, because the retention
  deadline is set at COMPLETION, not at mint. Worst case 120 queued + 120 running completes at t~240 with
  the token expiring at 300, and artifacts then live to t~540 instead of t~1140. NOTHING THAT PREVIOUSLY
  COMPLETED NOW FAILS; only the tail shortens.
- One doc line said "the shipped 300s constant" with no name attached - self-disambiguating at 900,
  ambiguous at 300. It now names RETENTION_S and notes the two are unrelated. Every other 300s/5-minute
  mention was checked and is disambiguated by its own clause.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, and no wording was allowed to drift toward "closes": it does NOT close the read
vector (4h6.88, still open and still stated as open at :1344), does NOT affect the live-execution window,
does NOT change artifact integrity (4h6.82) or the escapee class (4h6.83). The "what that does not close,
stated so the bound is not overread" paragraph survives verbatim.

docs/project-spec.md needed NO change - verified by grep, not assumed: its retention coverage is
qualitative and enumerates no window. The pre-commit doc-drift hook warned anyway (it is path-keyed and
warn-only); the warning is correct as a heuristic and there was nothing to update. Every
SANDBOX_RETENTION_S override in the tree is 45 or 2, so all stay legal under the narrowed 1..300 bound,
and nothing uses the now-forbidden 301..900 range. Sibling repos carry no falsified retention figure.

TESTS: 325 passed, 2 skipped - the pre-change baseline, which is what a constant-and-docs change should do.
RECORDED ON e8e, pre-existing and NOT introduced here: the suite would pass identically at 900 or 300. It
never exercises the shipped constant - test_retention_expiry reads the window dynamically off the harness
and skips without an override. The shipped value's only guard is human reading.

title: dev-stack.sh defaults SANDBOX_ENABLED=true but starts no supervisor, recreating the exact failure 4h6.56 prevents
description:
FOUND by blind validation of genetics-results-suite-4h6.56, 2026-08-20. VERIFIED by the
orchestrator by direct grep, not taken on report.

scripts/dev-stack.sh:199 does  SANDBOX_ENABLED="${SANDBOX_ENABLED:-true}"  and line 200 exports it.
start_chat_api inherits it (its `set -a; . "$MCP_ENV_FILE"` only overrides when the developer's own .env
names the variable). THE SCRIPT STARTS NO SANDBOX SUPERVISOR.

So `dev-stack.sh up` puts the local chat-backend in exactly the state 4h6.56 exists to prevent: the tool
is offered, the model is steered toward it, the sandbox is absent, and the failure classifies as
SandboxUnavailable / retryable: true - which looks transient and invites the model to retry.

Before 4h6.56 this variable did nothing in chat-backend, so the default was harmless. It is not harmless
now, and the default was chosen when it could not matter.

FIX, pick one deliberately: flip the dev-stack default to false; or have dev-stack start a supervisor
when it sets the flag true. The second is more useful for local end-to-end work (see 4h6.40/4h6.49) but
is real work; the first is one line and restores honesty.

NOTE the interaction with genetics-results-suite-4h6.23: a benchmark server launched via dev-stack.sh
inherits true and so KEEPS run_analysis, while one started by hand does not. That difference silently
changes what the code arm measures.
notes:
--- PARKED 2026-08-20 by the ralph-wiggum loop. SCHEDULING ONLY - the fix is still correct and still wanted. ---
DEFERRED so `bd ready` does not serve it while the user's genetics-results-suite-4h6.23 paired benchmark
is in flight. THE REASON IS THIS BEAD'S OWN CLOSING PARAGRAPH, which is easy to read as a footnote and is
actually a blocker:

    "a benchmark server launched via dev-stack.sh inherits true and so KEEPS run_analysis, while one
     started by hand does not. That difference silently changes what the code arm measures."

Read the other way round: FLIPPING THE DEFAULT TO FALSE MID-RUN REMOVES run_analysis FROM THE CODE ARM.
If the user's benchmark server was launched via `dev-stack.sh up`, landing the one-line fix while the run
is in progress changes the code arm's tool surface underneath the experiment, and the scorecard compares
ARMS, not dev-stack revisions - so nothing in the results would record that the arms were built from two

title: Nothing pins the browser's tool-profile list against the server's, and the two unknown-value fallbacks point opposite ways
description:
FOUND by the review of the browser tool-profile change (genetics-results-browser 6eca9a2), 2026-08-18. NOT a defect in that change - a coupling it makes load-bearing for the first time.

THE BROWSER AND THE SERVER EACH ENUMERATE THE TOOL PROFILES, AND NOTHING PINS THEM TOGETHER.
- server: TOOL_PROFILES (api/bigquery/rag) plus TOOL_PROFILE_TOOLS (code), genetics-mcp-server tools/definitions.py:1713,1735
- browser: TOOL_PROFILES, genetics-results-browser src/features/chat/chat.types.ts
Verified an exact match for all four TODAY, by reading both.

THE FAILURE MODE IS SILENT AND ASYMMETRIC. 6eca9a2 made a BROWSER-side omission a COMPILE ERROR - TOOL_PROFILE_LABELS is an exhaustive Record<ToolProfile, ...>, so a profile added to the constant fails tsc until the UI decides about it. That guard stops at the repo boundary. A SERVER-side rename or removal is still the original silent failure, one repo further out: the browser keeps offering the dead name, the server does not recognise it, and its unknown-profile path DEGRADES TO GENERAL-ONLY. So a user who explicitly selects the 7-tool code surface silently gets 23 tools, with no error anywhere and nothing in the UI indicating it.

title: The benchmark has no per-iteration or per-tool timing, and reports cost as a 12x-wide interval it no longer needs to
description:
FOUND by reading replay_benchmark.py and llm_service.py for the user's question "does the evaluation have granular timing so I can see where to improve performance" (2026-08-18). ANSWER TODAY: NO - TWO NUMBERS PER TURN. Both fixes below land on THE SAME SEAM, which is why they are one bead.

=== WHAT EXISTS ===
Per turn: ms_to_first_token and ms_to_done, both from a perf_counter taken just before the POST. That is all.
NOT per iteration: iterations_detail carries tokens and context per iteration and NO TIMESTAMPS AT ALL. You cannot say which iteration was slow.
NOT per tool: nothing times a tool anywhere in the chat path. _execute_tool logs the tool name and result size and no duration.
MODEL TIME AND TOOL TIME ARE NOT SEPARABLE: ms_to_done minus ms_to_first_token is model + tools + serialization mixed.
Only three clock reads exist in llm_service.py, and the one that survives (wall_ms into chat_turn_metrics) is ONE NUMBER PER TURN and is not written at all for secret chat - which is every benchmark request.

=== FIX 1, THE CHEAP HIGH-VALUE ONE: PER-ITERATION ELAPSED MS ===
Stamp an elapsed-ms field into the EXISTING `usage` SSE chunk (llm_service.py around 906-918). The chunk already exists, is already emitted per iteration, and is already parsed by the benchmark into IterationUsage/iterations_detail. About six lines across llm_service.py and replay_benchmark.py.
THIS IS WHAT ACTUALLY LOCALISES A BOTTLENECK: it turns "the turn took 92 s" into "iterations 1-3 took 6 s each, iteration 4 took 68 s". The epic's own 2026-08-07 measurement says median context grows 39k -> 117k tokens between iteration 1 and 7+ with the uncached share rising 11% -> 52%, and that the expected win is COST AND TAIL LATENCY rather than a median tool-call drop - a claim that per-TURN totals cannot confirm or refute.

=== FIX 2, SAME CHUNK, DIFFERENT FIELDS: EXACT USD ===
The harness reports cost as an INTERVAL, not a point - cost_usd_min prices all cached tokens as cache-read, cost_usd_max prices them all as cache-creation, and the two are MORE THAN 12x APART. It also cannot separate cache_read from cache_create, deriving cached_input_tokens by subtraction.
IT NO LONGER HAS TO. genetics-results-suite-n3p ALREADY ADDED cache_read and cache_create to the usage payload (llm_service.py:906-918) - the harness has simply not been switched over. ~10 lines in replay_turn/IterationUsage turns a 12x-wide interval into an exact figure.
A 12x-wide cost interval cannot decide a rollout whose stated win is cost. This is the cheapest accuracy win available and it is nearly free.

=== FIX 3, THE NEXT STEP DOWN: PER-TOOL TIMING ===
Wrap the body of LLMService._execute_tool (llm_service.py:1243) in a perf_counter and either log tool=<name> duration_ms=<n> or emit a `tool_timing` SSE chunk from the call sites (around 1075 and 1098) where tools are gathered concurrently. CAVEAT: those are asyncio.gather fan-outs, so per-tool wall time OVERLAPS and does not sum to the iteration's tool phase - capture the iteration's tool-phase span too or the numbers will mislead.

=== SECOND SOURCES THAT ALREADY EXIST, worth knowing before building anything ===
- results-api middleware_usage_logging.py times EVERY request with perf_counter and logs endpoint_access with duration_ms.
- db-api api/main.py logs duration_ms on its query/schema paths under the same log_type.
- THE SANDBOX ALREADY REPORTS ITS OWN EXECUTION TIME: sandbox_client.py logs duration_ms from the supervisor's response body and executor.py surfaces it into the rendered run_analysis result. So the CODE ARM is the one arm that already knows how long its work took - and that field reaches the model, not any benchmark metric.
Correlating the first two with a benchmark run is awkward: the harness sets session_id = replay-<run_id>-<case>-<arm> but that identifier DOES NOT PROPAGATE into the downstream services' access logs, so today it would be wall-clock-window matching. Propagating it is a fourth, larger option.

Related: genetics-results-suite-4h6.23 (the benchmark), genetics-results-suite-n3p (added the cache fields already).

genetics-results-suite-4h6.71 + 4h6.73: per-iteration timing, exact USD, and the script_result chunk

Two beads landed together because they share one seam: the per-iteration `usage`
SSE chunk and the harness that parses it. Implementation + sighted review +
INDEPENDENT blind validation + two fix rounds. Suite 1620 -> 1638 -> 1646 ->
1649 passed / 74 deselected. No billed benchmark run: everything is verified
with fabricated streams, unit drivers and a fake Anthropic stream.

THESE NUMBERS DECIDE A ROLLOUT (4h6.23), so the standard held throughout is the
harness's own: it prints NOT MEASURED rather than 0 so as not to hand an arm a
free win.

=== WHAT IS NOW MEASURABLE ===
The `usage` chunk gains `turn_elapsed_ms` (cumulative from turn start, sharing
the monotonic zero with chat_turn_metrics.wall_ms), `model_ms` (that iteration's
model call alone) and `model_attempts`. A new `script_result` chunk is emitted
per completed run_analysis. Cost becomes `cost_usd` + `cost_basis`
(exact/interval/unpriced) using the cache_read/cache_create split that
genetics-results-suite-n3p had already put on the wire and the harness had
simply never consumed.

=== THE DORMANT CONSUMER HAD NEVER EXECUTED, AND WAS WRONG ===
replay_benchmark.py already looked for `script_result` and already had the
retry-loop logic, but nothing had ever emitted the chunk, so none of it had run.
Treating it as suspect rather than as a contract found three defects:
- `exit_code` DOES NOT EXIST. The bead, the dormant harness and a pre-existing
  test all specified exit_code/timed_out/exception. The supervisor answers with a
  `status` string of ok/error/timeout/limit. Emitting an exit_code would have
  meant inventing a constant and reporting it as measurement.
- chat_api.py's SSE dispatch is an if/elif chain with NO DEFAULT, so the chunk
  would have been emitted and silently dropped - NOT MEASURED forever with the
  work apparently done. Now has a branch and a test that fails without it.
- The retry-loop logic itself was correct and was kept.

=== THE DEFECT BOTH REVIEWERS FOUND INDEPENDENTLY, AND IT FLATTERED THE ARM ===
`ran = isinstance(status, str)` treated "no status key" as "transport fault, says
nothing about the model's script". FALSE for two shapes, both measured against
the real executor:
- a blank/non-string `code` from the model, which arrived as a bare
  status "unknown" INDISTINGUISHABLE IN THE JSON from a genuine transport fault;
- SandboxRejected, whose own comment reads "a caller bug ... Actionable, because
  the model chose the value" - raised for a model-supplied timeout_s outside
  1..120 and for oversize code.
Both were removed from the numerator AND the denominator and printed as "sandbox
faults (not script failures)". Measured consequence: a model asking timeout_s 300
twice per case yields `script runs=N failures=0 rate=0.000, sandbox faults=2N` -
a reader concludes the scripts never fail and the sandbox is flaky. THIS IS THE
DIRECTION NOBODY HOPING THE SMALL ARM WINS WOULD CATCH.
Now classified on the `status` already on the wire via five disjoint categories;
blank code carries a real `EmptyScript` error_type; both are script failures on
both sides of the rate.

THE TWO REVIEWERS DISAGREED ON TurnBudgetExceeded - one called it the arm's
characteristic risk, the other genuinely infrastructural - AND THAT IS DISSOLVED
RATHER THAN DECIDED. Every shape is counted verbatim and individually, the rate
prints its numerator and denominator inline, and TurnBudgetExceeded sits in its
own bucket on neither side, on its own line. Either classification is
recomputable from numbers on the page.

=== THE LOCALISATION FEATURE POINTED ONE ROUNDTRIP TOO LATE ===
Found by the blind validator and measured. `iteration_ms[N]` was
`turn_elapsed[N] - turn_elapsed[N-1]` = model[N] + THE TOOL PHASE OF N-1, printed
on the same row as tool_phase_ms[N], which belongs to N. Ground truth
iter1 model=1000 / iter1 tools=5800 / iter2 model=2000 named iteration 2 as the
bottleneck at 7.8 s when its own work was 2.0 s, and slowest_iteration_ms is in
_TURN_DISTRIBUTIONS so it propagated per-arm.
Now `iteration_ms = model_ms[N] + tool_phase_ms[N]` - the row sums and
slowest_iteration names the roundtrip to go and look at. The old quantity
survives as `segment_ms`, epoch-honest, because pre_model_ms derives from it.
NOTE the reviewers did NOT contradict each other here: tool_phase_ms's own
attribution was independently verified CORRECT and untouched. Different field.

=== THE FINAL ITERATION IS NOT AN ABSENCE, AND ALMOST BECAME ONE ===
The first fix made iteration_ms None on the final iteration, citing "absence is
never imputed as 0". But two cases were collapsed: a turn that ended BECAUSE the
model stopped calling tools has a tool phase that is genuinely ZERO, while a turn
that hit the iteration ceiling ran tools that were never timed.
Enumerating every exit from the agentic loop shows the split is clean - the
max_tokens and unfilled-result continuations `continue` rather than `break`, so
they always emit another usage chunk and are never final. Therefore
tools-after-the-final-usage-chunk implies the ceiling, and the ceiling is exactly
what appends the notice. The imputation is additionally gated on status == "ok",
so an error, timeout or disconnect mid-turn yields None.
This mattered rather than being tidiness: ~36% of production turns are
single-iteration and would have contributed NOTHING, and the final iteration is
where the answer is generated against the largest context (median 39k -> 117k
tokens by iteration 7+, uncached share 11% -> 52%). A metric that structurally
cannot see it would systematically name the wrong roundtrip - the same defect
class as the off-by-one above.
`tool_phase_ms` deliberately stays None in both cases: the column means "a tool
phase that was measured", and seeding one 0 per turn would drag every by-index
median toward zero for a reason unrelated to how long tools take.
Version skew was the one real false-negative risk and is closed: the notice text
is hoisted to llm_service.MAX_ITERATIONS_NOTICE, the harness keeps its own
literal (it parses a REMOTE stream, so importing would be wrong), and the two are
pinned together by a test.

=== ALSO FIXED ===
The timeline silently merged across an untimed iteration; it now resets the
baseline and reports None. It printed one `n` per row while tool_phase_ms has a
different denominator, and never printed the unreliable_percentiles the harness
already computes - so a p90 over n=1 rendered as an ordinary number, in exactly
the tail rows a reader cares about. Now per-column n with a `*` flag.
`model_ms` is printed under a header that says what it contains: the timed span
encloses retry backoff and, being an async generator, downstream SSE
serialisation. `model_attempts` went on the wire so a retry-inflated figure is
IDENTIFIABLE rather than merely disclaimed.
retry_loops splits into script / disputed / infra, summing to the total. The
parallel-script over-count is documented as the safe direction rather than
solved.
The footer's ">12x" is restored to a true statement: the two cache CLASSES differ
>12x in price; the bracket is narrower because output and uncached input sit in
both endpoints.

=== VERIFIED SOUND UNDER ATTACK, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-LITIGATED ===
The exact cost is algebraically closed and was derived independently twice: the
usage chunk's context is input + cache_read + cache_create, so the harness's
subtraction-derived cached total is identically read+create; min prices all at
the read rate, max at the create rate, read < create, so cost_usd is ALWAYS
inside its bracket. The two cannot disagree. Mixed turns are demoted whole -
one chunk without the split and the turn is not exact - and absence is never
imputed as 0.

pytest.fail if reached, proving no request leaves the process and therefore that
the sandbox cannot be blamed for either shape; another raises a real
APIConnectionError and asserts model_ms >= 900, so the 1 s backoff demonstrably
sits inside the figure.
