title: The system prompt and the tool list are assembled independently: contradictory steering, an ungated run_analysis, and a documented tool that is switched off
description:
FOUND while deriving docs/chat-tool-reference.md from source (2026-08-18). Nothing is broken at runtime; the model is being given CONTRADICTORY AND UNREACHABLE INSTRUCTIONS, which is a tool-selection-accuracy problem in an epic whose entire premise is tool-selection accuracy.

=== 1. THE SYSTEM PROMPT AND run_analysis's DESCRIPTION DISAGREE, AND NOTHING ARBITRATES ===
The base system prompt tells the model to PREFER API TOOLS OVER THE DATABASE. run_analysis's description tells the model to use it INSTEAD OF CHAINING DATA-ACCESS TOOLS. Both are in front of the model on every turn.
THE SYSTEM PROMPT NEVER MENTIONS run_analysis AT ALL. So the arbitration between "prefer the API tools" and "prefer the sandbox" exists ONLY inside the tool descriptions, where it is invisible to anyone reading the prompt and cannot be tuned per instruction set or per verbosity.
This matters directly for genetics-results-suite-4h6.16: that bead's plan is to A/B a five-tool `code` profile against the current surface. An A/B whose two arms are steered by a prompt that only describes one of them does not measure what it appears to measure.

=== 2. run_analysis IS ADVERTISED ON EVERY TURN WITH NO FEATURE FLAG ===
launch_subagents, get_phenotype_report and get_credible_sets_stats are all gated behind deployment flags that default FALSE. run_analysis is not gated at all, while genetics-mcp-server docs/project-spec.md:230 states the sandbox is not deployed and every call fails at the transport.
This is the same hazard as genetics-results-suite-4h6.56, seen from the tool-definition side rather than the deploy-ordering side. 4h6.56 proposes a settings flag as option (b); this bead is the evidence that the flag mechanism ALREADY EXISTS and is already used by three other tools, so option (b) is cheap.

=== 3. THE SYSTEM PROMPT DOCUMENTS TOOLS THAT ARE NOT IN THE TOOL LIST ===
It carries a WHOLE SECTION on launch_subagents while ENABLE_SUBAGENTS defaults "false", which removes launch_subagents from the tool list. The prompt has NO CONDITIONAL ASSEMBLY - the section is emitted regardless. It also cites "the variant_list_analysis skill", equally unreachable.
So the model is told at length how to use a tool it has not been given. The known failure mode is that it plans around the absent capability and then improvises when the call is unavailable.

WHY THIS IS ONE BEAD: all three are the same defect - THE PROMPT AND THE TOOL LIST ARE ASSEMBLED INDEPENDENTLY AND NOTHING CHECKS THEM AGAINST EACH OTHER. A test that asserts every tool named in the system prompt is present in get_anthropic_tools() for the profile in force, and that every steering instruction has exactly one home, closes all three and stops the next one.

Related: genetics-results-suite-4h6.56 (deploy-ordering view of item 2), genetics-results-suite-4h6.16 (the A/B this distorts). Source of record: docs/chat-tool-reference.md.
close_reason:
genetics-results-suite-4h6.69 - all three items closed by one mechanism, plus the test that stops the next one.

ITEM 1 (contradictory steering): arbitration is now per-surface and stated in the prompt - None "Prefer the dedicated API tools over the database", api "The API tools are the data path here", bigquery "The database is the data path here", code "Scripts are the only data path on this surface", rag none. Exactly one per surface, verified by rendering all five.
ITEM 2 (ungated run_analysis): the FIX is 4h6.56's flag and was deliberately NOT implemented here. What landed is the mechanism that makes it free - see the common note.
ITEM 3 (prompt documents absent tools): fixed. The Subagent Orchestration section and the variant_list_analysis clause now drop when launch_subagents is absent; Phenotype Reports drops when flag-gated off. The tool_names=None fallback keeps the old unfiltered behaviour but is reachable ONLY from tests - chat_api's single production caller always passes an explicit set - so the item is fixed everywhere it applied.

=== THE DEFECT THE MECHANISM ITSELF INTRODUCED, FOUND INDEPENDENTLY BY BOTH REVIEWERS ===
THE GATE OVER-SUBTRACTED. A block was suppressed if it named ANY absent tool, so a PARENTHETICAL, ILLUSTRATIVE or NEGATED mention deleted unrelated science from the arms under test. Pseudo Credible Sets was gated by ONE parenthetical mentioning list_datasets, so the `code` arm lost "these are NOT statistically fine-mapped" and "Always tell the user explicitly" - A LABELLING OBLIGATION SILENTLY REMOVED FROM AN ARM THAT STILL REACHES credible_sets_v THROUGH THE SDK'S sql(). Also lost: the case-sensitive data_type list, "Membership is NOT the same as LD", "Re-query; do not answer from memory", and the HLA pval-underflow and low-`info` traps.
THE TWO REVIEWERS CONTRADICTED EACH OTHER ON HLA AND IT WAS RESOLVED BY RENDERING, not by preferring the more confident one. THE BLIND REVIEWER WAS RIGHT: the section IS dropped for bigquery/rag/code. The sighted reviewer's "not triggered by any profile today" is false; what is true is that the negated get_summary_stats mention is never the SOLE cause, because instructional get_hla_by_* names co-occur in the same block.
AN `ignore_names` ESCAPE HATCH WAS DELIBERATELY REFUSED: it would weaken the invariant both reviewers verified, since an emitted block could then name an absent tool and the independent tokeniser test would have to subtract the escape set - i.e. start trusting the gate it exists to check. Splitting keeps the invariant absolute. Rule now documented: SCIENCE AND GROUNDING GO IN BLOCKS THAT NAME NO TOOL; ONLY THE "WHICH TOOL" CLAUSE IS GATED.

=== FIX ROUND 2: THE RULE WAS NOT APPLIED TO THE ROUTING BLOCK ITSELF ===
Two arbitration bullets still named three tools in a parenthetical "(e.g. ...)". PROBED: remove ONLY get_gene_based_results - precisely what 4h6.56's flag will do - and the ENTIRE API-vs-database arbitration disappears at once. What remains is "Write one script with run_analysis..." AND NO COUNTERWEIGHT: THE PROMPT SILENTLY BECOMES PRO-SCRIPT, in the direction that manufactures the result this epic hopes for. Nothing caught it - heading present and non-empty, every required string surviving, tests covering only today's five profiles. Fixed with `requires_all`. title: PID 1 never reaps descendants adopted after the fork server dies, or where PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER does not take
description:
FOUND by the fix round of genetics-results-suite-4h6.49, while building a grandchild probe that could actually go red. MEASURED, not reasoned.

The supervisor runs as PID 1 in the container and waits ONLY on its own direct child (the execution). It never reaps anything else. A descendant that outlives its parent is re-parented to PID 1 - the supervisor - and when it dies nobody calls waitpid on it, so IT STAYS AS A ZOMBIE FOR THE LIFE OF THE CONTAINER.

MEASURED: after a wall-clock limit kill, the in-group grandchild was left in state Z and never disappeared. The 4h6.49 harness now FILTERS state Z explicitly, precisely so a permanent zombie does not masquerade as a working kill - which is the second-order hazard here: a naive "is the pid gone?" check reads a zombie as alive, and a naive "is it in /proc?" check reads it as alive too.

WHY IT MATTERS: zombies hold a PID SLOT. The pod is configured with a pids limit (--pids-limit 1024 locally, kubelet pod_pids_limit in the cluster). Every killed descendant that is never reaped is a permanent debit against that limit, in a pod whose replicas is 1 and which serves every subsequent user until it restarts. Enough executions that leave descendants and the pod cannot fork at all - and fork failure is exactly the state genetics-results-suite-4h6.63 shows leaks 6 fds per attempt, so the two compound.

THIS IS NOT THE SAME BEAD AS 4h6.66. 4h6.66 is that the group is never SIGNALLED on the completing path. This is that even a SUCCESSFUL kill leaves the corpse behind forever. Fixing 4h6.66 alone makes this WORSE, because it turns surviving processes into zombies at a higher rate.

FIX SHAPE: PID 1 needs a reaping loop - a SIGCHLD handler or a waitpid(-1, WNOHANG) sweep - that reaps ANY child, not just the tracked execution. The care needed is that it must not steal the wait status the execution path depends on: 4h6.41 deliberately uses waitid(P_PID, WEXITED|WNOWAIT) so the status can be read without consuming it, and a blind waitpid(-1) sweep racing that is exactly the kind of change that turns a clean timeout into an intermittently-lost exit status. Read _resolve_pgid and the waitid call before touching this.

A PID namespace per execution (genetics-results-suite-4h6.55 option (c)) makes the whole class disappear - the namespace's PID 1 dies and the kernel kills and reaps everything in it. Worth weighing alongside that bead rather than fixing twice.

Related: genetics-results-suite-4h6.66, genetics-results-suite-4h6.55, genetics-results-suite-4h6.41 (owns the waitid discipline), genetics-results-suite-4h6.63 (fd leak on fork failure - the same exhaustion state).
notes:
--- RESCOPED 2026-08-20 after bd415f9 (4h6.82/.83/.66). THIS BEAD'S ORIGINAL PREMISE IS NOW MOSTLY FALSE.
Established by probe, MEASURED unless marked READ. Do not work the original description - work this. ---

WHAT IS STILL TRUE (READ): the supervisor IS PID 1 in the deployed shape - k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml
declares no command:/args: and sandbox/Dockerfile's ENTRYPOINT is the bare interpreter with no CMD, so the
interpreter running supervisor.py is PID 1 once 4h6.50 wires it. And it still installs NO generic reaping:
there is no waitpid(-1) anywhere in the file, and main()'s only signal.signal calls are SIGTERM/SIGINT.
(SIGCHLD is set to SIG_DFL, but only inside _forkserver_main.)

WHAT IS NOW FALSE: "killed descendants become permanent zombies". They do not, on the ordinary path.
bd415f9 made the FORK SERVER a subreaper (PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER) and added a bounded re-enumerating
FS_OP_SWEEP, so descendants reparent to the FORK SERVER, not to the supervisor, and the sweep kills and
reaps them. MEASURED: after the execution child exits, an escapee shows ppid = the fork server's pid.
NOW REAPED: reparented zombies (ordinary unwaited Popen orphans), live escapees, in-group survivors the
success-path _kill_survivors missed, and chains up to FS_SWEEP_MAX_ROUNDS deep per execution.

WHAT IS LEFT OF THIS BEAD, AND IT IS REAL BUT MUCH NARROWER - THIS IS THE WORK:
PID 1 needs a BOUNDED waitpid(-1, WNOHANG) reaper for the orphan class that lands on the SUPERVISOR rather
than on the fork server. Two ways to get there:
 (i) THE FORK SERVER DIES. Its surviving descendants reparent PAST it to PID 1. MEASURED end to end:
        after fork server dies : S={'state':'S','ppid':<pid-1 analogue>}
        after S is killed      : S={'state':'Z','ppid':<pid-1 analogue>}
        one second later       : S={'state':'Z',...}   <- never waitpid()ed, permanent
     This is exactly the `stranded` path _execute_inner already handles (SIGKILLed fork server, poisoned
     control socket). Probe: scratchpad/probe-6887/q1_orphan_class.py.
 (ii) PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER IS UNAVAILABLE OR FAILS. Today that is only a LOG.warning (supervisor.py
     ~:1612/1616) and the sweep silently becomes inert - escapees reparent to PID 1 = the supervisor and
     are never reaped. Identical class. READ, not measured; gVisor behaviour is unverified (4h6.51).
Also still missed by the sweep, but NOT this bead's work - recorded on e8e: last-round collateral zombies
(cleared next execution), chains deeper than the round cap, an unreadable /proc, and a dead fork server
(which is case (i) above).

THE waitid(WNOWAIT) COLLISION HAZARD THIS BEAD WARNED ABOUT HAS SHRUNK WITH IT. The supervisor no longer
waits on execution children at all - they are GRANDCHILDREN now. So a blind waitpid(-1, WNOHANG) reaper's
only collision surface is ForkServer.alive/close on fs.pid (supervisor.py ~1931/2011/2023) and
_NoForkServer.reap (~:2040, the fallback path). That is a small, enumerable set - which is what makes this
tractable now in a way it was not when the bead was filed.

DO NOT CLOSE THIS AS "no change needed". The original claim is stale; the residual is not.
close_reason:
LANDED. genetics-results-suite 495b42a, batched with 4h6.62. TWO fix rounds - the cap - and BOTH rounds
fixed a demonstrated RECYCLED-PID KILL. Read that before touching this area.

THE RESCOPE WAS DONE BY PROBE BEFORE ANY WORK, and it was most of the value: bd415f9 had made the fork
server a subreaper, so the original premise ("killed descendants become permanent zombies") was already
false on the ordinary path. What was left is what reparents PAST the fork server to PID 1 - the fork server
dead, or PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER unavailable (today only a LOG.warning, after which the sweep silently goes
inert).

WHAT LANDED: ORPHAN_REAP_MAX_ROUNDS = 64 per SIGCHLD delivery, WNOHANG throughout, installed after
bring_up() so neither the fork server nor any execution child inherits it (_forkserver_main also sets
SIGCHLD to SIG_DFL explicitly - belt and braces against exactly the 4h6.41 waitid collision).

THE CENTRAL LESSON, and it is transferable: THE REAPER'S OWN REASON FOR EXISTING WAS THE STATE THAT BROKE
ITS SAFETY ARGUMENT. Its docstring said a collision was impossible because execution children are
GRANDCHILDREN. True ONLY WHILE THE FORK SERVER IS ALIVE - and the reaper exists BECAUSE the fork server can
die. When it dies mid-execution the child reparents to PID 1, the reaper takes its status, and the
invariant written verbatim at _kill_group ("a zombie keeps its pgid and its pid cannot be recycled until it
is reaped") no longer holds. MEASURED under `unshare -Urpf --mount-proc` with ns_last_pid:
    pre-change : bystander could NOT obtain the number (50 attempts)
    post-change: bystander got pid 117; _signal_group(job, SIGKILL) KILLED THE BYSTANDER
WHEN A SAFETY ARGUMENT IS "X CANNOT HAPPEN BECAUSE OF RELATIONSHIP R", ENUMERATE EVERY STATE IN WHICH R
DOES NOT HOLD - and check whether the change's own justification names those states. The sighted review
traced the call graph correctly and still missed this: the call graph is IDENTICAL in both states, only the
process TREE differs.

ROUND 2 FIXED THE SECOND PATH TO THE SAME HARM, WHICH ROUND 1'S OWN RESIDUAL PARAGRAPH HAD DENIED EXISTED.
_reap stamps job.reaped_pgid BEFORE the waitpid that can fail, so a fork server dying between the
FS_OP_WAIT and FS_OP_REAP replies leaves the pgid stamped, `reaped` False and the child reparented here -
the stranded branch is NOT taken and _execute_inner's else branch calls _kill_survivors UNCONDITIONALLY.
For a setsid() child that pgid IS the pid. MEASURED: the supervisor announced "its process group 117 still
has members; killing them" about an unrelated process and killed it.

THE SHAPE THAT WORKS, and it is the only one available: PUBLISH AFTER THE FACT. waitpid(-1) reports whose
status it took only AFTER taking it, so "skip fs.pid" is not implementable, and the peek alternative
(waitid(P_ALL, WNOWAIT)) wedges on a fork-server zombie and stops reaping everything else. So the reaper
hands every consumed pid to BOTH owners - ForkServer.note_reaped and the new Supervisor.note_child_reaped -
which record the status, mark reaped, and clear the pid AND the recorded pgid, so every signal path answers
"gone" at its first guard. Ordering is deliberate: reaped_pgid and reaped_status are cleared/set BEFORE
`reaped`, so a reader that sees the job reaped also sees the pgid gone. NO LOCK IS TAKEN - a handler
blocking on a lock a serving thread holds stalls PID 1 with no other thread to run it.

WHAT GENUINELY REMAINS, measured, not rounded: a _signal_group that has ALREADY passed its job.reaped check
delivers THAT ONE signal. Window = one _resolve_pgid, MEASURED at 3.1 microseconds. NOT CLOSABLE, and a
lock would serialise rather than reorder it. THE ESCALATION IS REFUSED - a second _signal_group answers
gone - so the 2s grace loop, its SIGKILL and every later signal are gone, which is where the exposure was.

THE HANDLER IS NOW ACTUALLY SILENT, which it was documented to be and was not. _sigchld -> _reap_orphans ->
note_reaped -> _mark_broken -> LOG.error. MEASURED with main()'s exact logging setup over a congested
stdout pipe: RuntimeError "reentrant call inside <_io.BufferedWriter>", swallowed by except BaseException,
which ABORTED THE DELIVERY (4 of 5 zombies left unreaped) AND LOST the most operationally important line in
the file permanently, because _mark_broken sets _broken BEFORE logging. Now log=False parks the reason and
alive() flushes it from a serving thread. NOTE, documented: alive() has exactly ONE caller, the /health
branch - so the reason surfaces on the next readiness probe and NOWHERE ELSE. A fork-server death during
shutdown, after the last probe, prints nothing.

CAP JUSTIFICATION WAS FALSE AND IS CORRECTED. "64 is far above what one execution can strand" - no:
PID_BUDGET 32 is enforced over process-GROUP membership only, and a setsid() descendant leaves that group,
so an execution can strand past 64, bounded only by pod_pids_limit 1024. The conclusion survives for a
DIFFERENT reason: SIGCHLD deliveries are not coalesced in practice. MEASURED both ways - 300 children
released at once leaves 0 zombies; with SIGCHLD blocked to force ONE delivery, 236 of 300 remain, which is
the documented residual.

TESTS 385 -> 412, 2 skipped. TEN controls now ship. THREE MUTATIONS THAT PREVIOUSLY LEFT THE SUITE GREEN
now fail: SIGCHLD->SIG_IGN (the end-to-end check had asserted an end state THE KERNEL'S OWN auto-reaping
satisfies - see e8e item 38), close() setting _closing last (the test hand-set the flag instead of driving
close()), and a publisher that clears job.pid without setting job.reaped.

title: The supervisor signals the process group only from _fire_limit, so a completing execution never kills what it left behind
description:
FOUND by the sighted review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.49, while establishing that that bead's own grandchild assertion was vacuous. The assertion was fake; THE UNDERLYING GAP IS REAL and was measured.

sandbox/supervisor.py:1951 is the ONLY call site of _kill_group, and it sits inside _fire_limit. SO THE EXECUTION'S PROCESS GROUP IS SIGNALLED ONLY WHEN A LIMIT FIRES.

CONSEQUENCE: an execution that COMPLETES NORMALLY (status: ok) never signals its process group. Anything it left behind - a plain fork that stayed IN the group, no setsid() and no escape attempt required - persists for the life of the container. The supervisor reaps the direct child and returns a clean result while the descendant keeps running.

MEASURED inside genetics-sandbox-local with a working probe (fork + setsid + prctl(PR_SET_NAME) + time.sleep, no exec - the shape 4h6.55 used):
  759797  755953  759792  E2EMARK-GRP   <- still IN the execution's pgid, survived a normally-completing execution
  759798  755953  759798  E2EMARK-DET   <- setsid escapee
The FIRST of those is this bead. The second is 4h6.55's finding 3, which this run CONFIRMS reproduces under plain Docker/runc with --pids-limit 1024.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY "ADD A KILL ON THE SUCCESS PATH": it may well be that simple, but it is a supervisor behaviour change on the path every ordinary user takes, and the ordering against reaping matters - 4h6.55 already records that once waitpid reaps the child the pgid is STALE AND THE PID IS RECYCLABLE, so a later killpg can hit an unrelated group, plausibly the NEXT execution's child. 4h6.41 dealt with that hazard for the limit path (_resolve_pgid, waitid with WNOWAIT); the success path needs the same care, not a bare killpg.

RELATION TO 4h6.55: a setsid() descendant leaves the group and is unreachable by ANY killpg, so closing this bead does not close 4h6.55 - only a PID namespace does. But this gap means a descendant does not even need to setsid() to survive an ordinary execution, which makes the cheap version of the attack cheaper than 4h6.55 assumed.

Related: genetics-results-suite-4h6.41 (built the reaper and owns _resolve_pgid), genetics-results-suite-4h6.55 (the escapee class), genetics-results-suite-4h6.62 (a continuously-writing escapee holding a drain thread).
notes:
--- RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-20 by a probe for 4h6.83. CLAIM IMPRECISE, DEFECT STANDS. ---
"signals the process group only from _fire_limit" is not quite right: there are TWO _kill_group call
sites - supervisor.py:2740 (_fire_limit) and :2523 (the stranded path added by 4h6.55, taken only when
job.pid is not None and not job.reaped, i.e. the reap failed).
THE DEFECT IS UNCHANGED, because a NORMAL completion has reaped=True and so hits neither. MEASURED: a
plain forked grandchild that stayed in the pgid SURVIVED a normally-completing execution
(`1197089 1197084 PRB-INGRP`).
This bead's own caution - "the success path needs _resolve_pgid-style care, not a bare killpg" - is now
cheap to satisfy: _signal_group/_resolve_pgid ARE the only way to signal, and they already carry the
reaped/own-group guards. See 4h6.83's correction note for why a success-path kill still does not reach a
setsid() escapee, and what does.
close_reason:
LANDED as part of the 4h6.82/.83 cycle. genetics-results-suite bd415f9.

THE DEFECT, restated precisely because this bead's original wording was imprecise: it is not that
_kill_group is only called from _fire_limit - there are TWO call sites (_fire_limit and the stranded path
added by 4h6.55). It is that a NORMALLY COMPLETING execution has reaped=True and therefore hits NEITHER,
so anything the script forked into its own process group simply survived. MEASURED: `1197089 1197084
PRB-INGRP` still running after a status=ok execution.

WHAT LANDED: _execute_inner's finally now has an `else:` arm calling _kill_survivors(job) on the reaped
path.

MY OWN FIX SPEC FOR THIS BEAD WAS WRONG AND THE IMPLEMENTER CORRECTED IT. I instructed routing the
success-path kill through _signal_group/_resolve_pgid "because they already carry the reaped/own-group
guards". That would have been a NO-OP: _signal_group's first guard returns _SIGNAL_GONE when job.reaped,
which IS the success path. The implementer kept the guards' SUBSTANCE instead - job.reaped_pgid is
captured inside _reap under kill_lock while the zombie is still held, so the pid cannot be recycled at the
moment of the read, and the own-group check is re-applied against the live os.getpgrp() before signalling.
VALIDATED INDEPENDENTLY: both _reap branches (waitid(WNOWAIT) and the WNOHANG loop) capture it under the
lock, neither is missed, and the residual recycling window cannot reach the supervisor, the fork server,
or the next execution's child (the slot is held from the reap to the call and nothing forks in between).

ALSO FIXED HERE: _kill_survivors used to `except OSError: pass` after SIGKILL and return True
unconditionally, so a group that survived escalation was indistinguishable from one that died - the one
place this new kill path could fail silently, while every other kill path in the file logs it. Now it
re-reads _group_members after a bounded 0.25s settle (SIGKILL delivery is asynchronous, so an instant read
would false-alarm) and logs surviving members at ERROR. It only logs; it takes no further action.

KNOWN, recorded on e8e not fixed: test_survivors' in-group assertion is satisfied by the SWEEP's reap
rather than by _kill_survivors alone - SIGTERM leaves a zombie and _fs_sweep reaps it - so this bead's
contribution is not INDEPENDENTLY asserted. The negative control disables both mechanisms together, so the
group as a whole is sound, but the per-bead attribution is stronger than what the test separates.

title: results-api's sandbox logging drops Rejection.code and the user, the two fields an operator needs
description:
FOUND during genetics-results-suite-4h6.49's end-to-end verification, and confirmed INDEPENDENTLY BY BOTH REVIEWERS by reading the source. Not a defect in 4h6.49 - it is a pre-existing results-api defect that the e2e harness ran into and had to work AROUND, which is how it was noticed.

TWO DEFECTS IN THE SAME SUBSYSTEM, both losing exactly the field an operator needs. Fix them together.

=== 1. Rejection.code NEVER REACHES A LOG LINE ===
genetics-results-api app/core/sandbox_budget.py:320-331 - log_rejection passes `code`, `limit` and `observed` in the record's `extra`.
app/core/logging_config.py:9-25 - EXTRA_LOG_FIELDS lists NEITHER of the three, so the JSON formatter DROPS them. `sid` and `jti` are in the list and do survive.
CONSEQUENCE: a `sandbox per-execution limit exceeded` line reaches the operator carrying WHO but not WHICH LIMIT. Rejection.code exists precisely to make a 429 actionable - to say concurrency vs request-count vs response-bytes - and it is the one thing that does not arrive. An operator seeing the line cannot tell a runaway script from a script hitting a ceiling that is simply too low, which are opposite responses.
MEASURED: the 4h6.49 harness could not read the code off the log at all and reads it off the 429 RESPONSE BODY instead. That workaround is in scripts/test-e2e-local.py and should be revisited once this is fixed - reading the body tests the client's view, not the operator's.

=== 2. endpoint_access LOGS user_email: null FOR A SANDBOX PRINCIPAL ===
app/middleware_usage_logging.py:120,132-133 - the access record stamps `sid` and `jti` for a SandboxPrincipal but leaves `user_email` null.
CONSEQUENCE: results-api's own log cannot attribute a sandbox request to a USER. The join is still closable - db-api's `sandbox request authorized` record carries `sub`, and the supervisor's audit stream carries it too (4h6.45) - but it requires a second source. Measured in the same run: `INTERNAL_API_SECRET` callers show `jti = None` AND `user_email: null`, so on results-api's log alone an accounted sandbox request and an unaccounted internal one differ only by the presence of `jti`.

WHY THIS WAS NOT FIXED INSIDE 4h6.49: that bead's job is to MEASURE the path, and a verification bead that quietly repairs what it was measuring destroys its own evidence. Both findings were recorded rather than worked around silently.

WORTH DECIDING: whether EXTRA_LOG_FIELDS should be an allow-list at all, given that adding a field to an `extra` and forgetting the list is silent - the log line simply arrives without it, and nothing fails. That is the same shape as the defect, not just its cause.
notes:
--- ADDED 2026-08-24. THIS BEAD IS NOT A SINGLE-REPO TASK, DESPITE NAMING ONLY results-api FILES. ---
It was considered for pipelining alongside 4h6.50 on the grounds that it lives entirely in
genetics-results-api. THAT IS FALSE, and the check that caught it was one grep.
THE SUITE'S OWN SECURITY DOC ENUMERATES BOTH OF THIS BEAD'S DEFECTS BY NAME:
  docs/code-execution-security.md:3344 - "`code`, `limit` and `observed`" ... "so `Rejection.code`, whose
                                          whole purpose is to make a 429 [actionable]"
  docs/code-execution-security.md:3347 - "`endpoint_access` records `user_email: null` for a sandbox
                                          principal even though `sid` and [`jti` survive]"
  docs/code-execution-security.md:4565 - describes the EXTRA_LOG_FIELDS allow-list mechanism itself
So FIXING this bead FALSIFIES three passages in genetics-results-suite, and they must be updated in the
same change. That makes this a two-repo task that WILL collide with anything else touching
docs/code-execution-security.md - which in practice is every sandbox bead.
DO NOT RUN THIS CONCURRENTLY WITH A SANDBOX BEAD. Run it alone, or batched with whatever else is editing
that doc.

WORTH FOLDING IN WHEN THIS RUNS, because it is the same defect class one layer out:
genetics-results-suite-4h6.97 records that genetics-mcp-server's tools/executor.py renders a WHITELIST of
sandbox response fields, so a field added on the supervisor side is silently dropped. EXTRA_LOG_FIELDS is
the same shape - an allow-list where forgetting an entry fails silently and the line simply arrives without
it. This bead's own description already asks whether EXTRA_LOG_FIELDS should be an allow-list at all. Answer
that question once, for both, rather than twice.
close_reason:
LANDED. genetics-results-api c815aa3, genetics-results-suite 36ca9d6. One fix round of the two allowed.
Tests 644 -> 678, confirmed independently after the fix round by a separate run (678 passed, 328s), not
taken from the implementer's report. ruff clean.

THE BEAD'S SECOND PREMISE WAS TOO BROAD AND THE OBVIOUS FIX WOULD HAVE BEEN A SECURITY REGRESSION.
"endpoint_access logs user_email: null for a sandbox principal" is true only where REQUIRE_AUTH=false, or
on an @is_public route with ANONYMOUS_SURFACE_MINIMAL off - i.e. the local e2e harness, which is where it
was observed. In the SHIPPED config (results-api.yaml REQUIRE_AUTH=true, ANONYMOUS_SURFACE_MINIMAL=true)
the auth dependency had ALREADY stored `sandbox:<user>` in state["authenticated_user"], because
get_verified_user returns SandboxPrincipal.identity. So the fix as literally requested - stamp the bare
address - REPLACED `sandbox:person@x` with `person@x` and made a sandbox row indistinguishable from a
human row in the ONE column that reaches BigQuery (terraform/logging.tf admits only
log_type="endpoint_access"), falsifying code-execution-security.md rule 5 in the direction the doc names
as the hazard. Fixed by stamping principal.identity: a no-op in production, a fill-in in the harness case,
and the doc stays true. FOUND BY THE SIGHTED REVIEW, which traced the whole chain rather than reading the
bead's premise; the orchestrator re-verified the chain by hand before ruling.

THE ALLOW-LIST QUESTION IS ANSWERED, ONCE, FOR THIS AND FOR 4h6.97: DELETE IT, do not extend it.
An allow-list is defensible when omission is loud, or when the excluded set is dangerous. Neither held.
The excluded set was "fields this codebase deliberately attached to a log record" - by construction things
somebody wanted logged - and omission was a no-op: the line simply arrived short. That is exactly how
code/limit/observed survived to production. Inverted to a deny-list of LogRecord's own attributes, derived
from a probe record at import so it tracks the interpreter. There is no longer a list to forget.
4h6.97 (mcp-server's response-field whitelist) is the SAME shape and the same answer applies, but nothing
was implemented there - it stays its own bead.

TWO GUARDS THE ALLOW-LIST HAD PROVIDED BY ACCIDENT, both found by BLIND validation, both restored:
1. RESERVED-KEY OVERWRITE. `log_entry.update(extras)` ran after the base keys, so extras won. MEASURED:
   extra={"severity":"DEBUG"} on a logger.info() emitted severity DEBUG, and trace/labels/httpRequest/
   logging.googleapis.com/* passed through top-level. On GKE those are reserved fields the ingester
   honours, so a caller could demote a WARNING below an alerting threshold from inside logger.warning().
   `message` was already protected by makeRecord; `timestamp` was already clobberable and is not a
   regression. Fixed with _merge_extras: base keys win, reserved names not overwritable, and a colliding
   extra is RE-KEYED to extra_<name> rather than DROPPED - dropping would have reintroduced the exact
   silent loss this bead is about. Two passes, because the naive one-pass version was order-dependent.
2. format() COULD RAISE AND LOSE THE LINE. json.dumps(default=str) does NOT cover a self-referential dict
   or list (ValueError: Circular reference detected), a tuple-keyed dict (TypeError), or an object whose
   __str__ raises. The line was lost and reappeared on STDERR unstructured via Handler.handleError - which
   on GKE is also ingested. Under the allow-list the four admitted names were all scalars so this was
   structurally unreachable; it became reachable by any future extra=. format() now degrades instead.
   THE FIRST TEST FOR THIS PROPERTY WAS VACUOUS: it used object(), which default=str handles, so it passed
   while the claim was false. Now parametrized over the four cases that genuinely raised.

NO CREDENTIAL LEAK, and it was checked rather than assumed. Three extra= sites in the whole service
(middleware.py:216, auth.py:188, sandbox_budget.py:323), all literal scalar keys; nothing builds an extra
from request data or headers. The one dangerous library source - google's GAPIC transport logging raw gRPC
metadata including `authorization: Bearer ya29...` - is triple-gated: DEBUG only while log_level is pinned
INFO, requires GOOGLE_SDK_PYTHON_LOGGING_SCOPE, and sets propagate=False so those records never reach the
root formatter. Net new emission on live paths is uvicorn's color_message on a few startup lines.

EACH FIX VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING by reverting the single line/block in place (backups outside the tree, byte
-compared on restore; no git stash/checkout): identity stamp 3 failures, reserved-key merge 8, degrade 5
with the plain_object case still passing - which is precisely the vacuousness the finding described.

METHOD NOTE WORTH KEEPING: the sighted review found the blocking finding, the blind validator found the
regression the sighted review had explicitly cleared ("blast radius is small, and I checked"). Both were
right about what they looked at. The reserved-key door was invisible to a reviewer asking "can a secret
get in" and obvious to one asking "what could a caller now overwrite".

title: A continuously-writing setsid() escapee holds a drain thread and its fd for the pod's lifetime
description:
FOUND by the sighted review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.45. NOT a defect in that change - a pre-existing shape it adds a third instance of. Reasoned, with the safe half measured.

sandbox/supervisor.py _drain checks the DRAIN_GRACE_S deadline ONLY in the `if not ready:` branch. A descendant that calls setsid() and writes CONTINUOUSLY to a pipe therefore keeps the drain thread alive indefinitely, because `ready` is never false.

WHAT IS SAFE, and it is the important half: the EXECUTION SLOT IS NOT HELD. `t_audit.join(DRAIN_GRACE_S + 5.0)` times out, an error is logged, the fd is leaked and the response is sent. `audit.close()` makes further feed() calls no-ops, so the escapee cannot get records onto the operator's stream after the execution it belongs to has ended. This is 4h6.39's drain deadline working as designed.

WHAT LEAKS PER ESCAPEE: one thread, one read-end fd, and the CPU to keep discarding. Replicas 1 and concurrency 1 mean these accumulate in the pod that serves every subsequent user, bounded only by a restart.

THE SAME SHAPE PRE-EXISTS ON THE STATUS PIPE AND THE OUTPUT PIPE. The audit pipe is the third, and it is the only one with NO `limit` at all (it is drained with limit=None by design, because a rate cap cannot be enforced on a buffer handed over at EOF). So a continuous writer on the audit pipe is the cheapest way to hold a thread.

WHY IT IS NOT FIXED HERE: an escapee is genetics-results-suite-4h6.55's territory, and the fix that closes it as a class - a PID namespace per execution - closes this too. A deadline check in the ready branch is a plausible narrower fix and would bound the CPU and the thread, but it does not bound the fd unless the read end is also closed, and closing a read end while a write end lives is how you turn a leak into a SIGPIPE in someone else's process. Decide alongside 4h6.55 rather than before it.

Related: genetics-results-suite-4h6.55, genetics-results-suite-4h6.39 (owns the drain deadline).
notes:
--- RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-20 by a probe for 4h6.83. STILL TRUE AS WRITTEN, no correction needed. ---
_drain checks the deadline only inside `if not ready:` (supervisor.py:1747-1751), so a CONTINUOUS writer
keeps `ready` truthy and `time.monotonic() >= deadline` is never evaluated. The safe half this bead
describes also still holds: t_*.join(DRAIN_GRACE_S + 5.0) at :2526-2528 bounds the wait, the fd is
leaked, the response is sent and the slot is released.

--- REACHABILITY NARROWED 2026-08-22 by probe. THE CODE IS UNCHANGED; WHAT CAN REACH IT IS NOT. ---
The 2026-08-20 re-verification above checked the _drain CODE and was right about it. It did NOT check the
new caller ordering, and that is what moved.

bd415f9 PUT _sweep_strays(job) BEFORE THE DRAIN JOINS, supervisor.py:3020-3026, with the stated reason
"BEFORE the drain joins, so an escapee holding the output pipe's write end stops being the reason _drain
waits out its grace". _sweep_strays (:2872) drives the fork server's bounded re-enumerating _fs_sweep
(:1633-1722), which SIGKILLs reparented escapees. So the continuous writer this bead describes is normally
DEAD before the join is reached, and the thread/fd leak does not occur.

THE LEAK NOW REQUIRES THE SWEEP TO MISS, and that residual set is EXACTLY 4h6.68's rescoped residual:
  - the fork server is dead, so descendants reparent past it to PID 1;
  - PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER was unavailable (supervisor.py:1619-1628 - WARNING ONLY, nothing fails);
  - the chain is deeper than FS_SWEEP_MAX_ROUNDS = 4 (:468);
  - /proc is unreadable.
DECIDE THIS BEAD AND 4h6.68 TOGETHER. They are the same root cause seen from two sides. Note a
supervisor-side reaper does NOT close this one: a LIVE continuous writer is not a zombie and reaping does
not touch it.

SIZE, unchanged in substance: ONE LINE to bound the CPU and the thread (move the deadline check out of the
`if not ready:` branch at :2110-2116). STRUCTURAL to bound the FD, because that means closing a read end
while a write end lives - this bead's own reason for deferring, and still the right caution.
The safe half still holds: :3028-3030 joins with DRAIN_GRACE_S + 5.0, and :3035-3040 leaks the read end
DELIBERATELY, with LOG.error("... leaking its read end") rather than closing it under a live writer.
close_reason:
LANDED. genetics-results-suite 495b42a, batched with 4h6.68 - correctly, because the probe established they
were ONE ROOT CAUSE SEEN FROM TWO SIDES.

ONE LINE: _drain's DRAIN_GRACE_S deadline is now evaluated on every pass instead of only inside
`if not ready:`, so a descendant that setsid()s and writes CONTINUOUSLY no longer keeps the thread alive
for the pod's lifetime by keeping `ready` truthy.

THE FD OUTCOME IS BETTER THAN THIS BEAD EXPECTED, AND BY EXISTING CODE RATHER THAN NEW. The orchestrator
ruled "bound the thread and CPU, do NOT close the read end, document the leak" - on this bead's own
reasoning that closing a read end under a live writer turns a leak into a SIGPIPE. What actually happens:
with _drain now RETURNING, _execute_inner's post-join cleanup closes the read end on the ordinary abandoned
path, which is the same path every already-reachable abandon took. No close was added and none was
suppressed.
AND THE SIGPIPE GOES NOWHERE IT SHOULD NOT: the supervisor closes its copies of out_w/st_w/audit_w after
the fork, and _fs_do_fork closes the fork server's, so the ONLY holders of a write end are the execution
child and its descendants - attacker-authored code, INSIDE the sandbox boundary. _child_main restores
SIGPIPE to SIG_DFL, so a non-Python escapee dies rather than merely erroring. That is a bonus, not a hazard.
The "leaking its read end" backstop branch still exists unmodified for the thread-still-alive case, and the
execution slot is still not held (joins remain DRAIN_GRACE_S + 5.0).

REACHABILITY, re-established before working it: bd415f9 moved _sweep_strays BEFORE the drain joins, so the
continuous writer is normally SIGKILLed before the leak can happen. What remains needs the sweep to miss -
dead fork server, PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER unavailable, a chain deeper than FS_SWEEP_MAX_ROUNDS, or an
unreadable /proc - which is exactly 4h6.68's residual set. A reaper does NOT close this bead: a LIVE
continuous writer is not a zombie.

CONTROL: SUPERVISOR_TEST_DRAIN_DEADLINE_IN_READY=1 restores the in-branch check and turns exactly two
checks red - `abandoned=False` and "gives up ON the deadline rather than merely eventually" (6.50s against
a 0.5s grace). The test's writer NEVER stops and never closes its write end, and the regime is sampled at
the instant the drain lets go, so it drives the continuous-writer path rather than an EOF - which matters,
because the previous cycle in this file shipped tests that passed vacuously by exercising the wrong regime.

RECORDED ON e8e, NOT FIXED (pre-existing, outside this bead): `abandoned` does not set `output_truncated`,
so an output cut short by the drain deadline is reported to the client as COMPLETE. Not reachable through
this change - with DRAIN_GRACE_S = 2.0 and a <=64 KiB pipe buffer the deadline cannot fire on a dead child.

title: db-api has no per-execution request-count or concurrency limit, unlike results-api
description:
FOUND during the review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.44, in a CORRECTED form. Two reviewers reported db-api as "attributable but uncounted"; a third agent read api/main.py and showed that is FALSE - db-api meters per execution by BYTES. This bead is the narrower claim that survives.

WHAT db-api DOES HAVE, keyed on the sandbox token's jti: SANDBOX_AGGREGATE_BYTES_BUDGET of 200 GB via _charge_aggregate, charged on the dry-run estimate and reconciled against actual bytes processed, across /query, /schema, /tables/{t}/sample and /stats. Plus SANDBOX_MAX_ROWS (25k) and SANDBOX_MAX_BYTES_BILLED (50 GB) per query for a SandboxPrincipal.

WHAT IT DOES NOT HAVE: any per-execution REQUEST COUNT and any CONCURRENCY limit. results-api has both - 1000 requests and 4 in-flight per execution, 8 pod-wide - and enforces them in MIDDLEWARE BEFORE ROUTING, so even unmatched paths count. db-api enforces in four handlers only, so its cheap paths (anything that is not one of those four) are neither counted nor gated.

THE CONCERN IS AVAILABILITY, NOT SPEND. A script can issue unbounded cheap requests at unbounded concurrency against db-api. db-api is replicas: 1. The sandbox is concurrency 1 with replicas 1, so this is one execution's worth of load rather than many - but one execution is enough to saturate a single pod that also serves the browser through results-api, and the sandbox's own wall clock (60s default, 120s ceiling) bounds the duration rather than the rate.

WORTH DECIDING RATHER THAN ASSUMING: whether db-api should grow the same middleware-level per-jti gate results-api has, or whether the asymmetry is correct because the two meter different things (BigQuery spend vs egress and pod memory) and db-api's expensive paths are already bounded by spend. The second reading is defensible. What is NOT defensible is leaving it undecided and undocumented, which is why this exists.

genetics-results-suite-4h6.49 could measure the actual behaviour cheaply while it has the stack up. NOT a blocker for it.
close_reason:
LANDED. genetics-results-db f0e636c, genetics-results-suite 922393e. One fix round of the two allowed.

THE DECISION THIS BEAD ASKED FOR, AND THE FACTS THAT SETTLED IT. The bead offered two readings and called
the "asymmetry is correct" one defensible. IT IS NOT, and the deciding facts were not in the bead:
db-api is replicas:1 at cpu 500m / memory 512Mi, and it is called by CHAT-BACKEND AND MCP-SERVER as well
as the sandbox (measured: BIGQUERY_API_URL in chat-backend.yaml:58, mcp-server.yaml:29, sandbox.yaml:182;
results-api does NOT call db-api). So one execution looping a free path does not degrade only itself - it
degrades the browser's chat. The bead framed this as "one execution's worth of load"; the missing half is
that the pod is shared.
Also decisive: db-api's auth is an APP-LEVEL DEPENDENCY (dependencies=[Depends(require_auth)] in the
FastAPI constructor), not middleware, and a dependency is solved PER MATCHED ROUTE - an unmatched path
404s out of the router without it ever running. That is why the gate had to be ASGI middleware and not
another dependency.
UNCOUNTED PATHS, enumerated from the decorators rather than assumed: /health, /docs, /redoc,
/openapi.json charge nothing; /schema charges nothing on a categorical-value cache hit; /stats' 15-
iteration bq_client.get_table loop is metadata-only. Eight routes total.

WHAT SHIPPED: api/sandbox_budget.py, a port of results-api's module rather than a fresh design - same
constant names and defaults (1000 requests, 4 in-flight per execution, 8 pod-wide, 4096 tracked), same
_env_int handling, same import-time refusal below 1 and of TOTAL < per-execution, same
{detail, code, limit, observed} 429 body and the same five code labels. Registered before the CORS
registration, which on the installed starlette makes it INNER of CORS and OUTER of the router: measured
chain ServerErrorMiddleware -> CORSMiddleware -> SandboxBudgetMiddleware -> ExceptionMiddleware -> router.
That is the correct side - a browser preflight is answered by CORS and can never be counted or 429'd,
while a 429 still carries Access-Control-Allow-* from the outer layer.

THE PROPERTY THAT MATTERS AND HOW HARD IT WAS PUSHED. "A non-sandbox request is untouched" is what keeps
chat up. Fuzzed with 18 hostile Authorization headers - absent, empty, bare `Bearer`, lowercase `bearer`,
internal-secret-shaped, `a.b.c`, non-UTF-8 bytes, RS256 JOSE header, alg:none, JSON-array header, iat as
a list, exp as a string, aud as a list, expired, empty jti, iat far past, wrong signing key, capitalised
header name. Every one returned None, none raised, _executions stayed {} . Structural, not luck:
is_sandbox_shaped catches ValueError/binascii.Error/UnicodeDecodeError and verify_sandbox_token wraps
jwt.decode in a bare except Exception, so nothing escapes as a 500.

MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED, by blind validation running real probes:
- Boundary: cap 3 gives [200,200,200,429,429]; the Nth is admitted, the (N+1)th refused. Same >=-before-
  increment shape for both concurrency caps.
- Admit/increment race: 16 threads x 400 cycles at cap 4 - no over-admission, residual in_flight 0,
  _in_flight_total 0. All check-and-increment is inside one threading.Lock with no await in between.
- Before routing: GET /nonexistent gives [404,404,404,429,429] at cap 3. The 404s ARE counted.
- Slot release across 404, 405, 422, a handler raising through ServerErrorMiddleware, and a
  StreamingResponse with a BackgroundTask - in_flight returns to 0 in every case. The background task
  observed in_flight == 1 WHILE it ran, i.e. the slot outlives the response body, which is correct.
- The sweep never evicts a live entry: with the bound at 2, a live entry survived 20 subsequent distinct-
  jti admissions with its counter intact and the newcomers were refused instead. The window is tight
  against verification: sweep needs expires_at < now - LEEWAY while PyJWT accepts up to exp + LEEWAY.

MUTATION MATRIX on the 24 (now 26) new tests: gate removed 12 fail / 12 survive; release() no-op 6/18;
sweep ignores in_flight 1/23; admit decrements requests 5/19. The 12 survivors of full removal are the
4 ungated-path tests (which assert ABSENCE of accounting, so surviving is correct), the defaults test,
the 5 _env_int params, and one tautology - see below.
ONE VACUOUS TEST WAS FOUND AND REPLACED: test_the_pod_wide_concurrency_bound_is_never_tighter_than_one_
executions asserted 8 >= 4 over constants the module already enforces at import, so an inverted pair
would error the whole file at COLLECTION and the assertion could never fail on its own. Replaced by
test_an_inverted_concurrency_pair_is_refused_at_import, parametrized (4,8) refused / (8,8) and (9,8)
accepted - the equal case pins the boundary against a <= typo.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, all recorded on 4h6.98 rather than filed:
- admit() creates the entry before the pod-wide check, so a jti the pod-wide cap rejects on its FIRST
  request leaves a zero-valued entry until its token expires. IDENTICAL ordering in results-api, so this
  is a faithful port, not a divergence. Bounded and self-clearing. (item 85)
- The raw-header scan assumes lowercase keys; a capitalised Authorization makes the gate a no-op. Correct
  under uvicorn, fails open FOR THE GATE ONLY, same assumption as results-api. A comment now sits at the
  line. (item 86)
- db-api now emits two different 429 vocabularies - the new gate's structured body and the byte budget's
  bare detail. Not aligned because the byte-budget shape is established behaviour a consumer may parse.
  (item 84)
- THE "_jti_bytes LRU CAN DROP A LIVE EXECUTION" CLAIM WAS CHECKED AND IS OVERSTATED. results-api's own
  module docstring says it, and the implementer repeated it as a live fail-open. Both _charge_aggregate
  and _charge_aggregate_spent call move_to_end(jti), so it is a TRUE LRU: an actively-charged execution
  is the most-recently-used entry and the LAST one evicted. Displacing it needs 1024 other jtis charged
  between two of its own calls, which concurrency-1/replicas-1 cannot produce, and chat-backend and
  mcp-server carry no jti at all. LATENT, NOT A DEFECT - so no bead was filed. (item 88, with what would
  make it real.)

TESTS: db-api 177 -> 203 passed, 17 skipped (skip set unchanged). Counts verified independently, not
taken from the implementer's report.

title: A stale gitignored sandbox/.sdk-src silently makes the stub generator and its test read an old SDK
description:
FOUND while discharging genetics-results-suite-4h6.44's cross-repo doc obligation, and it cost a wasted regeneration to find.

sandbox/.sdk-src is a GITIGNORED staged copy of the genetics-mcp-server SDK. scripts/build.sh creates it and removes it on an EXIT trap - so it only survives when a build was INTERRUPTED. It is also the DEFAULT --sdk-src for both scripts/gen-sandbox-docs.py and scripts/test-sandbox-docs.py.

THE FAILURE: run either script with the default while a stale .sdk-src is present and it silently operates on an OLD SDK. Measured this session - a regeneration written against the stale tree produced two files and left scripts/test-sandbox-docs.py STILL FAILING, which is a confusing signal because the regeneration appears to have worked. The fix was to pass an explicit --sdk-src at the live worktree, which is what build.sh itself does.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ANNOYANCE: the generated stubs are SHIPPED INSIDE THE SANDBOX IMAGE and are what a script author reads, and docs/code-execution-security.md's secrets-in-image analysis reasons about their content. A stale regeneration therefore ships a false statement about credentials into the image AND leaves the doc's premise wrong, while the test that exists to catch exactly that either passes against the wrong source or fails for a reason that looks unrelated.

THE OPTIONS: (a) drop the default entirely so --sdk-src must be given - loudest, and the scripts have exactly two callers (build.sh and a human); (b) refuse a .sdk-src whose mtime is older than the resolved SDK source, or that is not a directory build.sh created in this run; (c) have the scripts resolve the live checkout the way scripts/run-sandbox-local.sh already does - it gates each candidate on src/genetics_mcp_server/sdk existing, which is the check-worktree-paths failure class handled correctly. (c) plus (a) is probably right.

Related: genetics-results-suite-e96 (run-sandbox-local.sh is in neither CLAUDE.md's doc-ownership table nor check-doc-drift.sh).
close_reason:
LANDED with 4h6.36 in one cycle. genetics-results-suite 00a6281.

THE HAZARD WAS DORMANT WHEN FIXED - `sandbox/.sdk-src` was absent, verified before starting - which is
the normal state, because build.sh removes it on an EXIT trap and it survives ONLY when a build was
INTERRUPTED. That is exactly what made it dangerous: it is present rarely, and when it is present it
changes the answer silently.

WHY IT MATTERED MORE THAN A DEVELOPER ANNOYANCE: the generated stubs are SHIPPED INSIDE THE SANDBOX
IMAGE and are what a script author reads, and docs/code-execution-security.md's secrets-in-image
analysis reasons about their content. A stale regeneration ships a FALSE STATEMENT ABOUT CREDENTIALS
into the image and leaves the doc's premise wrong - while the test that exists to catch exactly that
either passes against the wrong source or fails for a reason that looks unrelated. The bead was filed
after a wasted regeneration did precisely this.

IMPLEMENTED (c)+(a) FROM THE BEAD'S OWN OPTIONS. `.sdk-src` is no longer a default for either script. A
shared `resolve_sdk_src()`, imported by the harness FROM the generator so the two cannot resolve
different sources, tries explicit --sdk-src -> GENETICS_SDK_SRC -> MCP_SERVER_DIR -> the live sibling
checkout with the worktree-matching candidate first, each gated on src/genetics_mcp_server/sdk existing.
A leftover .sdk-src is REPORTED ON STDERR AND IGNORED rather than read.
NOT pure (a) - README instructs a human to run the generator bare, so dropping the default with no
replacement breaks the documented path. NOT (b) - an mtime or ownership check keeps the stale tree as
the DEFAULT SOURCE and only tries to detect staleness, which is strictly weaker, and mtime on a `cp -r`
tree is not trustworthy.

TWO PREMISES IN THE BEAD WERE INCOMPLETE and are corrected in the code comments: run-sandbox-local.sh is
a SECOND producer of leftovers and a THIRD caller (the bead said "exactly two callers"), and
test-sandbox-docs.py already honoured GENETICS_SDK_SRC while the generator did not - that asymmetry is
gone.

VERIFIED BY EXECUTION: leftover ignored with a note; every precedence tier honoured in order; an env dir
without the sdk subdir falls through; no resolvable source exits 2, which is what the doc now claims;
the generator and harness printed the SAME path; and build.sh, build-all.sh and run-sandbox-local.sh all
pass --sdk-src explicitly and are unaffected. A bare run today is a byte-for-byte no-op (--check green,
16 schema files, 3 stubs).

RECORDED, NOT FILED (4h6.98 item 70): neither of these scripts appears in CLAUDE.md's doc-ownership
table or in check-doc-drift.sh, though the table explicitly covers the trees they GENERATE and says
those are not exempt because the security doc reasons about their content. So changing the generator
cannot flag the doc while changing its output can. That is now the THIRD instance of the same gap
(with e96 and docs/environments.md), which is enough to say the table's failure mode is missing rows
rather than wrong ones.

Tests: scripts/test-sandbox-docs.py 13 -> 14 checks, 0 failures (the new one plants a fake staged tree
and asserts the resolver does not choose it). test-supervisor.py 468 passed / 2 skipped.

title: Supervisor: BODY_READ_TIMEOUT_S does not cover the request line or headers, and its comment says it does
description:
FOUND by the BLIND validation of the 4h6.41/.42/.43/.46 batch. REPRODUCED against the running container. Pre-existing from 4h6.39, not caused by the batch.

sandbox/supervisor.py: BODY_READ_TIMEOUT_S's comment says it covers "request line to last byte -> 408". IT DOES NOT. `started` is taken in _execute, AFTER BaseHTTPRequestHandler has already read the request line and every header with NO TIMEOUT of any kind.

MEASURED: a connection that sent a single byte b'P' and then nothing was STILL OPEN AT 35 SECONDS.

TWO THINGS TO DECIDE, and they are separable:
1. THE COMMENT IS FALSE and now sits among controls that are real (the batch added the wall clock, both quotas, the pipe cap). A false comment next to true ones is worse than a false comment alone. At minimum, correct it to say what is actually covered.
2. WHETHER THE GAP ITSELF MATTERS. The supervisor's ingress is a NetworkPolicy admitting chat-backend alone, so the untrusted party here is not the one holding the socket - which is why this is P2 and not higher. But the server is threaded and an unbounded number of header-stalled connections is a slot-independent resource. Set a socket timeout before the handler reads, or accept it explicitly and say why.

Note the shape of this finding: it was found by an agent that was NOT told what the change was for, precisely by testing a claim rather than reading past it.
notes:
--- RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-22 by probe, AFTER f225944 (4h6.87). PREMISE STILL TRUE; THE FIX SITE MOVED. ---
The false comment is still there verbatim, supervisor.py:114:
    BODY_READ_TIMEOUT_S = 10.0            # request line to last byte -> 408
`started` is still taken AFTER the head is parsed (supervisor.py:4653-4654, inside _execute), and the
timeout is applied ONLY in _read_body (:4634-4645).

WHAT .87 CHANGED, and it matters for where the fix goes: _HeaderBoundedReader INTRODUCES NO TIMEOUT OF ITS
OWN. A stalled head now parks in _read_head's blocking recv_into(..., MSG_PEEK) at :4365 rather than in a
BufferedReader.readline. EVERY settimeout in the file is accounted for: :1491, :1860, :1899, :1909 are the
fork-server control socket; :4638 and :4645 are _read_body. _Handler sets no `timeout` class attribute and
socket.setdefaulttimeout is never called, so socketserver never arms one.
So the fix must arm a timeout in _Handler.setup() or around the head read - NOT merely in _read_body.

THE TRAP TO AVOID: _read_body's finally already does settimeout(None). If the head timeout is armed in
setup() and _read_body disarms it, the NEXT request on a kept-alive connection reads its head with no
timeout at all - a fix that works once and then silently stops working. Pair the two deliberately.

.87's own code already documents this gap: the _roll_tail docstring at :4345-4348 says "the connection has
no timeout outside _read_body, and _Server's threads are daemons".

NOTE THE BASE RATE BEFORE TOUCHING THIS FUNCTION: _read_head had a defect found by validation on TWO
CONSECUTIVE passes during 4h6.87, both fail-OPEN, and the blind validator found one the sighted review
missed. Treat this area as high-risk regardless of how small the diff looks.

--- CROSS-REPO RISK RAISED BY REVIEW AND CLEARED BY PROBE, 2026-08-22. Keep this: it is the one question
the supervisor repo cannot answer about its own change. ---
THE RISK: IDLE_READ_TIMEOUT_S = 65.0 is a NEW SERVER-INITIATED IDLE CLOSE that did not exist before. If
chat-backend held POOLED keep-alive connections to the sandbox with an idle timeout at or above 65s, it
could hand a POST /execute to a socket the server was closing, see httpx.RemoteProtocolError, and fail -
POST is not idempotent and is not retried transparently.

CLEARED. MEASURED against the mcp-server WORKTREE (/home/jkarjala/suite/genetics-mcp-server/.claude/
worktrees/db-only-architecture - NOT master, which is older and would give a wrong answer).
THE DECIDING FACT: THE CONNECTION POOL NEVER OUTLIVES A SINGLE REQUEST. sandbox_client.py:520-526 opens
`async with self._client(timeout) as client:` and sends the POST inside it, so the AsyncClient and its pool
are torn down per call. Same shape for GET /health (:299) and GET /artifact (:349). There is no second
client - sandbox_client.py is the only module that talks to sandbox_url.
The SandboxClient OBJECT is a singleton (tools/executor.py:5804-5814, @cached_property) but holds only a
base_url and a sleep callable - no pool, no socket. Even execute's own retry loop (:417-448) re-enters
_submit and builds a fresh client, so a connection does not survive a Retry-After sleep.
BELT AND BRACES: no `limits=` is passed anywhere, so httpx's default applies - keepalive_expiry=5.0
(verified against the installed httpx 0.28.1), which would evict a socket ~13x sooner than 65s anyway.

title: Supervisor: a SIGTERM between slot release and the response write truncates a completed execution
description:
FOUND by the BLIND validation of the 4h6.41/.42/.43/.46 batch. Reasoned, not reproduced. NOT a defect in those beads - pre-existing in the 4h6.39 skeleton, surfaced because the batch put real controls around it.

sandbox/supervisor.py _shutdown_when_idle polls supervisor.idle(). idle() goes true in run()'s `finally`, which runs BEFORE _send_json(200, result) in the handler. The server sets daemon_threads = True.

FAILURE: a SIGTERM landing in that window - after the execution released the slot, before the response bytes are written - lets the shutdown path win the race and the process exits with the response truncated or unsent. The client sees a connection reset for an execution THAT ACTUALLY COMPLETED, and its artifacts were retained. On the client side (sandbox_client, 4h6.47) a reset classifies as SandboxUnavailable with retryable: True, so the model is told to run the same script again - a script that already ran to completion and whose side effects already happened.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE WINDOW SUGGESTS: the pod has terminationGracePeriodSeconds 130 precisely so the supervisor can drain, reap, ANSWER THE IN-FLIGHT REQUEST and wipe. Answering is the step this race can skip. Any rollout, eviction or scale-down is a SIGTERM.

FIX SHAPE: idle() must not report idle until the response is written - i.e. the slot release and the response write need to be ordered, or the shutdown path must wait on an explicit in-flight-response count rather than on idle(). Do not simply widen a sleep.

Related: genetics-results-suite-4h6.39 (the skeleton that owns _shutdown_when_idle), genetics-results-suite-4h6.51 (deploy-window verification - a rollout is exactly when this fires).
close_reason:
LANDED. genetics-results-suite dd2bc03, batched with 4h6.63. ONE fix round, and that round fixed a
REGRESSION THE FIRST VERSION INTRODUCED - read that part before touching this area again.

WHAT LANDED: a distinct _responding count and a distinct quiescent() predicate
(_running is None and not _waiting and _responding == 0). idle() IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED - _release and
_waiting semantics are relied on elsewhere, so the shutdown path consults a NEW predicate rather than
redefining the old one. _Handler._execute became a three-line wrapper: begin_response(), the former body
renamed _execute_and_answer() verbatim, end_response() in a finally.

THE FIRST VERSION WAS A REGRESSION AND BLIND VALIDATION MEASURED IT END TO END. The counted region ends
only after _send_json writes to the socket, and THAT WRITE HAS NO DEADLINE - wfile is a _SocketWriter doing
a blocking sendall, and both _read_head's and _read_body's finally restore settimeout(None). MEASURED:
20000 PIPELINED POST /execute on ONE socket, SO_RCVBUF=1024, client never reading. Each answered 400
InvalidRequest (~292 B) and - UNLIKE the 415/413/408/503 paths - the 400 from parse_execute_request does
NOT set close_connection, so replies accumulate:
    t=115.0s gate_returned=False in_flight=1   (thread parked in _send_json -> end_headers -> sendall)
    pre-change gate, same scenario: returned=True after 0.0s
So the fix as first written converted ONE TRUNCATED RESPONSE into A PROCESS THAT NEVER EXITS and is
SIGKILLed at terminationGracePeriodSeconds 130 - losing the clean forkserver.close() and child reap on top
of the answer. The size-independent version needs no pipelining and no malice: a peer that stops ACKing
blocks even a 292-byte sendall for tcp_retries2 (~15 min) for an ORDINARY SINGLE RESPONSE.

THE CEILING IS WHAT MAKES THIS A FIX RATHER THAN A TRADE: DRAIN_DEADLINE_S = 125.0, after which the gate
proceeds to httpd.shutdown() REGARDLESS and logs at ERROR naming the in-flight count. BOTH BOUNDS ARE REAL:
not below 122s, because an execution already running at SIGTERM can need MAX_TIMEOUT_S (120) + KILL_GRACE_S
(2) before its answer can even be written; not above 130s, because shutdown(), server_close() and
forkserver.close() all still have to run after the gate returns. 125 leaves 3s of write margin and 5s of
exit margin. WORST CASE NOW DEGRADES BACK TO A TRUNCATED RESPONSE - exactly what it was before this bead -
instead of a SIGKILL.
A WRITE DEADLINE ON _send_json IS THE MORE PRECISE FIX AND WAS DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN: it changes socket
semantics mid-sendall, the measured hang was in flush_headers rather than the body write (send_response and
end_headers sit OUTSIDE _send_json's try/except OSError), and a partial write forces the connection closed.
Iced as genetics-results-suite-4h6.95 with the full fix shape.

THE TESTS DID NOT COVER THE ONE EXIT THE finally EXISTS FOR, and that is the second thing to carry forward.
Blind validation mutated end_response OUT of the finally and the whole new group returned FAILURES=0 - all
three counted error exits RETURN NORMALLY. The finally is genuinely load-bearing because
ConnectionResetError escapes the handler body when a client resets mid-execution. MEASURED with
SO_LINGER(1,0) closed 1s into a 3s execution: with the finally in_flight=0; without it in_flight=1 and a
permanent hang. That path now has a check.
Tests 365 -> 385, 2 skipped. FIVE controls now run across two cycles, each red on its own checks only:
COUNT_NO_FINALLY (1), SHUTDOWN_NO_CEILING (2), SHUTDOWN_ON_IDLE (1), PIPES_OUTSIDE_TRY (2), ARM_ONCE (1).

VALIDATION METHOD NOTE, recorded on e8e item 32 and worth repeating here because it decided the outcome:
THE TWO SEATS REACHED OPPOSITE CONCLUSIONS ON THE SAME QUESTION, each correct for what it tested. Sighted
measured ONE LARGE RESPONSE (66 KB completes at t=0.5s under stock buffers) and concluded "bounded in
practice". Blind measured MANY SMALL RESPONSES ACCUMULATING and got "never". Vary the axis, not the effort.

/health and /artifact are UNCOUNTED and the docs now say WHY that is safe rather than asserting it: both
are idempotent GETs with no side effect, so a reset cannot cause the duplicate-execution harm this bead
exists to prevent, and artifacts live in the pod's emptyDir and are lost to termination either way - a
retry against the replacement pod gets a terminal 404, not a wrong answer.

title: Suite security docs are stale after run_analysis landed: _mcp_disabled is no longer the sole control
description:
FOUND by the review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.48. The suite repo is the SPEC OF RECORD for the suite, and CLAUDE.md's cross-repo rule says adding an MCP TOOL requires updating this repo's docs - not only the docs of the repo that changed. run_analysis landed in genetics-mcp-server and these statements here are now false or stale.

MEASURED SITES, in genetics-results-suite (verify before editing, line numbers move):
- docs/code-execution-security.md around 2833 and 2843: "Add run_analysis ... run_analysis joins it with 4h6.16". IT LANDED WITH 4h6.48, not 4h6.16.
- docs/code-execution-security.md around 2884: "Membership of _mcp_disabled is the SOLE registration-layer control." NOW FALSE - THERE ARE TWO. run_analysis has NO @mcp.tool() block at all, and register_mcp_tools is a hand-enumerated list of decorated closures that never iterates TOOL_DEFINITIONS, so disabled_tools (which can only SUBTRACT) cannot re-add it by any configuration. This MATTERS rather than being pedantry: section 5 explicitly assumes layer 1 is defeatable, and the second control makes that assumption STRONGER than the doc claims - the section is arguing from a weaker position than it actually holds.
- docs/code-execution-security.md around 3510, the 4h6.16 row: it asks for an assertion that NO HTTP ROUTE on mcp-server's app (chat_api.py, routers/) reaches the sandbox client. THE SHIPPED TEST ASSERTS THE IMPORT GRAPH of genetics_mcp_server.mcp_server instead. That is sound - k8s/deployments/mcp-server.yaml runs `python -m genetics_mcp_server.mcp_server` and never mounts chat_api - but THE DOC AND THE TEST SAY DIFFERENT THINGS, and a later reader will not be able to tell whether the asked-for assertion was skipped or satisfied differently.
- docs/project-spec.md around 1105: "layer 2 of the THREE MCP-exclusion layers". The count is now arguably four.
- docs/code-execution-security.md around 1624: reasons about a count derived from the definitions minus _mcp_disabled.

RE-DERIVE THE NUMBERS RATHER THAN ADJUSTING THEM, per CLAUDE.md's enumeration-rot rule. Measured 2026-08-17: 65 TOOL_DEFINITIONS; 66 registrable blocks with an empty disabled set; 54 actually on /mcp. Better still, state the relationship and drop the counts.

ALSO WORTH RECORDING WHILE THERE, because it is the strongest evidence the boundary holds and it is nowhere in the docs: an adversarial review could NOT get run_analysis onto the MCP surface by any configuration, env var, empty-disabled-set, category, profile or dynamic-registration path. The only route back on is someone hand-adding an @mcp.tool() block, which _mcp_disabled and test_code_execution_tools_absent_from_the_registered_tool_list would both catch.

ONE RESIDUAL WORTH A SENTENCE, NOT A FIX: mcp_proxy.register_proxy_tools registers EXTERNAL MCP servers' tools with an OPTIONAL prefix and consults only EXTERNAL_MCP_EXCLUDE_TOOLS, never _mcp_disabled. An external server could therefore put a tool literally named run_analysis on /mcp. It proxies to that server and cannot reach our sandbox, so it is NOT a code-execution bypass - but it defeats name-based enumeration and is a shadowing hazard. Pre-existing. The fix, if wanted, is to union _mcp_disabled into exclude_tools; that is a separate decision.

title: sandbox_client's default SANDBOX_URL points at the local db-api's port, not at the sandbox
description:
FOUND by genetics-results-suite-4h6.40 when it brought the sandbox container up on this machine. FILE-ONLY, and it will bite the first person who tries the local end-to-end path.

THE COLLISION: genetics-mcp-server's sandbox_client defaults SANDBOX_URL to http://127.0.0.1:8080. ON THIS DEV MACHINE 8080 IS THE LOCAL db-api (python3 api/main.py). So a chat-backend started without SANDBOX_URL set will POST /execute AT db-api.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN A WRONG PORT: db-api is a real, running, authenticating service. It will not answer the sandbox contract, but it WILL answer something - a 404, a 405, or an auth error - and the client classifies unknown responses rather than crashing. The developer sees a confusing sandbox error rather than "nothing is listening", which is the diagnostic they need. A connection to a CLOSED port fails instantly and unambiguously; a connection to the WRONG SERVICE does not.

CONTEXT: 4h6.40 published the local sandbox on host port 8081 precisely because 8080 was taken, so the default is wrong for the only environment where the default is used. In the cluster SANDBOX_URL is set explicitly to the Service, so production is unaffected - this is purely a local-development defect, which is exactly the environment the current phase is about.

DECIDE BETWEEN, rather than assuming the first:
(a) change the default to 127.0.0.1:8081 to match what scripts/run-sandbox-local.sh actually publishes. Cheapest, but it hardcodes one script's choice into the client.
(b) REMOVE the default and require SANDBOX_URL to be set, failing loudly when it is not. Most honest - it makes the "nothing configured" case unambiguous instead of silently pointing at whatever occupies a common port - and it matches the fail-closed posture the rest of the sandbox client already takes for a missing signing key.
(c) keep the default but have the client refuse to treat a response that is not contract-shaped as a sandbox error, reporting "the configured SANDBOX_URL is not a sandbox" instead. Most work, best diagnostic.
(b) is probably right and is closest to the module's existing behaviour on SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY, but this is a judgement call, not a fix to apply blindly.

RELATED: genetics-results-suite-r9e records that the dev stack's config is gitignored and lives only in the main checkouts, so a worktree-started service comes up with NO env at all - which is exactly the situation that makes a wrong default dangerous rather than merely wrong. Whoever takes r9e or 4h6.49 will hit this.
notes:
CONFIRMED IN A LIVE CLUSTER after the fix landed, daly-staging 2026-08-26/27 — the first deploy anywhere to actually run with SANDBOX_ENABLED=true.

Independently re-derived the bead's central finding before seeing this bead: SANDBOX_URL was in no file under k8s/ and absent from deploy.sh's envsubst whitelist, so a deployed chat-backend had no way to learn the address. Symptom with the sandbox genuinely enabled and healthy: chat-backend logged 'sandbox is not reachable at http://127.0.0.1:8080' on every run_analysis while the sandbox pod reported supervisor ready, prewarm complete and answered kubelet /health 200 continuously. So the failure the bead predicted for production is exactly what an enabling deploy produces.

The NetworkPolicy was never implicated: allow-ingress-sandbox already admits app=chat-backend on 8080, and from inside the chat-backend pod both http://sandbox.genetics.svc.cluster.local:8080/health and http://sandbox:8080/health returned {"status": "ok", "busy": false, "queued": 0}. Only the address was wrong.

With 525f44d's manifest line in place the error stops. NOT yet exercised: no script has actually been RUN end to end - this confirms reachability and configuration, not a completed execution.

title: code-execution-security.md claims the image hides the dataset name, but db-api's 400 discloses it verbatim
description:
FOUND by the review of genetics-results-suite-3za, in the suite repo, about db-api behaviour. PRE-EXISTING; 3za did not cause it and was told not to widen scope into it.

TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS IN THE SAME PARAGRAPH, docs/code-execution-security.md around lines 735-742.

--- 1. THE MECHANISM SENTENCE IS STALE ---
It says db-api "rewrites a bare name in a table position to its own DATASET_ID before authorize_query sees it". THAT REWRITE WAS DELETED by genetics-results-suite-4h6.53 (genetics-results-db 05571dc), which removed _qualify_tables and its six helpers - 131 lines - and replaced them with `default_dataset` on both job configs. BigQuery now resolves bare names itself.
The paragraph's CONCLUSIONS survive (the allow-list still compares fully-qualified ids, because BigQuery reports referencedTables fully qualified whichever way the name was written). Only the mechanism sentence is wrong. Fix it to describe default_dataset.

--- 2. THE DISCLOSURE CLAIM IS FALSE, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT MATTERS ---
The same paragraph claims the sandbox image "no longer discloses which dataset backs the views". DB-API HANDS THAT DATASET NAME TO ANY CALLER THAT SUBMITS ONE BAD TABLE NAME.
`authorize_query`'s NotFound/BadRequest branch (genetics-results-db api/main.py, around line 777) returns BigQuery's `e.message` VERBATIM. For a bare name, with default_dataset now in force, the message reads:
    Invalid query: Not found: Table phewas-development:genetics_dev.foo was not found
i.e. PROJECT_ID.DATASET_ID, disclosed to whoever asked. A sandboxed script can obtain it in ONE query.
The allow-list 403 leaks the same class of information independently: it echoes the resolved fully-qualified `disallowed` ids back to the caller.

--- 3. THERE IS ALSO AN EXISTENCE ORACLE, WHICH IS SEPARATE FROM THE TEXT ---
THE STATUS CODE ALONE distinguishes the cases, whatever the message says:
    table does not exist                         -> 400
    exists, SA can read it, not allow-listed     -> 403
    exists, SA denied                            -> 403
So "does this table exist" is answerable by any caller, and no amount of message-muting closes it. This is worth recording because 3za's implementation originally justified muting BigQuery's denial text as CLOSING an oracle; it does not, and that justification has been corrected in the db repo's own docs to the plain ground that the caller has no use for the text. Do not re-introduce the oracle-closing rationale here.
