title: Add instruction-set CRUD endpoints
description:
genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/routers/llm_config.py, in the user-settings region (~lines 185-296), all Depends(auth_required) and user-scoped:

GET    /chat/v1/llm-config/user/instruction-sets -> [{id,name,body,updated_at}]
POST   /chat/v1/llm-config/user/instruction-sets {name, body} -> created set; 400 empty, 413 over char cap, 409 over count cap
PUT    /chat/v1/llm-config/user/instruction-sets/{id} {name?, body?, comment?}; 404 if not owned
DELETE /chat/v1/llm-config/user/instruction-sets/{id} -> archive, 204
GET    /chat/v1/llm-config/user/instruction-sets/{id}/history?limit=20 (mirrors the tool-description history endpoint ~lines 388-413)

Selection reuses the live GET/PUT/DELETE /user/settings/selected_instruction_set — no new endpoint for it.
notes:
From .4: the accessors raise typed errors so you can map them without string matching — InstructionSetBodyTooLong -> 413, InstructionSetLimitReached -> 409. create_instruction_set's -> InstructionSet annotation is now honest (it raises RuntimeError rather than returning None).
update_instruction_set now returns None for an ARCHIVED set as well as an unowned one, so PUT on a set the user just DELETEd must 404, not 200.
InstructionSet.body_over_cap flags a set whose stored body predates the cap; update() rejects an echoed-back over-cap body with InstructionSetBodyTooLong.
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit a617edf. Reviewer probed cross-user isolation empirically with a two-identity client: status, detail string and response shape are byte-identical for a foreign id versus a nonexistent one on all three id-taking endpoints, so there is no existence leak. Ownership is checked BEFORE the length cap, so an over-cap body aimed at a foreign id still 404s rather than 413ing. Error mappings come from the typed exceptions, not string matching. PUT on an archived set 404s.

A new accessor get_instruction_set_history plus an InstructionSetVersion dataclass were added; verified to meet all three of this file's hard-won conventions (_discard_stale_transaction on entry, _as_utc_or_epoch parsing, changed_at DESC + id DESC tiebreak) with user_id in the WHERE clause rather than a post-filter.

BLOCKING BUG CAUGHT IN REVIEW: the history endpoint's limit was unvalidated. ?limit=-1 returned the ENTIRE history because SQLite treats a negative LIMIT as unbounded, and a limit past 64 bits raised OverflowError out of the driver as an uncaught 500. Fixed with Query(20, ge=1, le=100). The pre-existing get_tool_description_history endpoint had the identical hole and was fixed in the same commit.

title: Emit a two-block cached system prompt
description:
genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/llm_service.py. stream_chat/_stream_anthropic (~lines 425-438, 519-531) gain user_instructions: str | None. Build system as two blocks at ~lines 577-581: block 0 = default_system_prompt + verbosity_prompt with cache_control (shared across all users, one entry per verbosity value), block 1 = instruction_envelope(body) with cache_control on the spare 4th breakpoint.

Measured: shared block is ~7.4K tokens; a full refragmentation costs ~$0.043 per event vs ~$0.0025 for the incremental per-user block, and leaving it uncached costs ~$0.05 across a 25-iteration turn. This uses the last of Anthropic's four breakpoints (tools, shared system, user system, last message) — update the cache-breakpoint comment at ~lines 549-556 to say so.
close_reason: Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit 1b0cf83 (batched with .7). Reviewer counted cache_control markers on the ACTUAL emitted request params rather than trusting the summary: 2 with neither tools nor instructions, 3 with either, exactly 4 with both - never more. Block 0 confirmed byte-identical across two users with different instructions, and the no-instructions path emits the identical single-element list as before, so nothing regresses for users without a set. All four Anthropic breakpoints are now in use (tools, shared system, user system, last message); any future breakpoint must displace an existing one, and the comment says so.

title: Resolve instruction_set_id in ChatRequest
description:
genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/chat_api.py. Add instruction_set_id: str | None to ChatRequest (near the verbosity field, ~line 221). In stream_chat (~line 383) resolve it to a body scoped to the authenticated user and pass it to service.stream_chat as a SEPARATE argument, not concatenated.

An id that does not resolve for this user is ignored, not 422'd — same rule as verbosity: a presentation preference must never fail a chat turn. A DB error must degrade to 'no instructions', never to a failed turn. Log the set id and name only, never the body.
notes:
HANDOFF FROM .4: .7 OWNS bounding the instruction body length - nothing below it clamps any more.
- get_instruction_set/list_instruction_sets return the AUTHORITATIVE stored body, which CAN exceed the cap (the .3 legacy import writes uncapped bodies, and a lowered cap strands existing rows).
- Truncate to INSTRUCTION_SET_MAX_BODY_CHARS yourself; import the constant from db.llm_config_db, do not hardcode 4000.
- InstructionSet.body_over_cap is a computed bool telling you it happened.
- Truncating must never fail the turn - degrade to the first N chars, consistent with the ignore-unresolvable-id rule. len() is code points, pinned by a test.
- Log the set id and name only, never the body.

FROM .6: instruction_envelope() now exists in config/defaults.py. Call it; do not rebuild the wrapper. Its fence length is computed from the body, which is what makes truncation safe - so truncate BEFORE wrapping and let the envelope fence the result.

FROM .6's review: chat_api.py:379-382 currently says the verbosity fragment 'is appended last so it reads as the final instruction'. That becomes FALSE the moment you append the envelope after it. .7 owns that file - update the comment in the same change.
close_reason: Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit 1b0cf83 (batched with .8). Suite 884 passed / 74 deselected across two seeds. Reviewer verified cross-user scoping empirically across 11 identity/id combinations (guessed uuid, null/empty user, case-variant, SQL-injection shaped, archived set) - only the owner resolves. The user comes from Depends(auth_required), never from the request body. Truncation-before-wrapping verified against 6 fence-straddle cases. Three nits fixed because they contradicted the task's own acceptance criteria: the try did not cover the slice or the envelope call so a non-str body could still raise; secret mode logged the user-authored set name; and 'Applying' was logged for a body that resolved to nothing.

title: Add instruction_envelope() to config/defaults.py
description:
genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/config/defaults.py, beside _VERBOSITY_PROMPTS (~lines 264-294). Build the fragment as: '## Your instructions (user setting)' preamble, the user body in a fence, then a guardrail postamble.

The postamble MUST follow the body — recency wins, and the existing comment at chat_api.py:379-382 reasons about the verbosity fragment being 'the final instruction', which inverts once arbitrary user text follows it. The envelope scopes the text to tone, audience, depth, units, default resources and language; it may not relax grounding, citation, truncation or out-of-scope rules, and says explicitly that the rules above win on conflict.
close_reason: Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit a18e3a2 (batched with .9). Suite 863 passed / 74 deselected across two seeds. Review found one BLOCKING issue: the envelope used a fixed three-backtick fence and interpolated the body verbatim, so a body containing ``` closed the wrapper early and could inject a heading at the same structural level as the real system sections; a body ending in a bare fence left the guardrail paragraph reading as fenced content rather than as an instruction. Not merely adversarial - .7 truncates the body before wrapping, so a cut landing in a backtick run does the same to a benign body containing a code snippet. Fixed with a fence computed from the longest backtick run in the body, verified against a CommonMark-accurate fence walker with both escape variants demonstrated contained.

title: Fix same-second tiebreak in user-settings reads
description: genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/db/llm_config_db.py get_user_setting/get_user_settings (~lines 452-506). They join on MAX(changed_at), but SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP has 1-second resolution, so two saves to the same key in the same second both match and an arbitrary winner is kept. Add ORDER BY changed_at DESC, id DESC (id is a true AUTOINCREMENT sequence). Needed because the selected-set pointer will live in this store.
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit 416e961. Suite 785 passed / 74 deselected across 5 runs including 2 random orderings. Blind validation killed all 8 mutants (HEAD revert of each of the 5 queries, MAX->MIN on both grouped forms, and dropping the user_id scope); 11 of 12 new tests fail against HEAD, the survivor being the one that pins preserved NULL behaviour.

The bug was user-visible, not latent: the index is scanned rowid-ascending within a tie, so get_user_setting returned the OLDEST tied write every time. Two clicks inside one second kept the first.

TWO ROUNDS OF REGRESSION CAUGHT IN REVIEW: (1) the first rewrite lost the index on both plural accessors — measured 26ms->1124ms at 60k tool rows and 5.5->214ms at 10k settings rows/user. Replaced with a grouped MAX(id) form that restores the plan and matches or beats HEAD. (2) A comment asserted a query plan that only occurs after ANALYZE; neither repo ever runs ANALYZE, so it was wrong in the deployed state. Two reviewers contradicted each other on it and the disagreement was resolved empirically across 44 database states.

SCOPE BEYOND THE TICKET, needs the user's awareness: the ticket named only get_user_setting/get_user_settings. Three tool-description accessors carried the identical defect and were also fixed — fixing only the singular one would have made it disagree with the history listing an admin reads as current, and a tie there could drop the NEWEST versions from a limited listing. Deliberately NOT touched: get_user_comments/list_all_user_comments (tie permutes a display list, no current value derived) — filed as genetics-results-suite-qdf instead.

Follow-ups filed: genetics-results-suite-2cl (singular accessors crash on NULL/blank changed_at while plural drop the key), genetics-results-suite-qdf (admin feedback pagination boundary shift).

title: Add instruction-set accessors with caps
description: genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/db/llm_config_db.py. Add list/get/create/update/archive_instruction_set. Every query scoped by user_id. update appends to user_instruction_set_history and updates the row. Caps enforced at write time AND re-checked at read time (a legacy row can exceed a later-lowered cap): ~4000 chars per body, ~20 non-archived sets per user.
notes:
From .2's review: SQLite DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP on updated_at fires only on INSERT, never on UPDATE. update_instruction_set MUST set updated_at explicitly, or the (user_id, archived_at, updated_at DESC) index orders by creation time and the 'newest first' listing is silently wrong. Also insert timestamps by omission rather than explicit NULL — the columns lack NOT NULL (consistent with every other table in the file) but the dataclass types them non-optional.

From .3's review: the legacy import's re-entry guard depends on the epic's archive-rather-than-delete decision. Do NOT add a hard delete accessor — a hard DELETE would let the legacy import re-run and resurrect an imported set the user deliberately removed.
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit 937cd74. Full suite 748 passed / 74 deselected, stable across 8 repeat runs; each new test mutation-verified to fail only against its own reverted fix. Three fix rounds; both round-3 reviewers concluded nothing blocked shipping.

Blocking bugs caught and fixed in review: (1) read-time body clamp destroyed 5000 chars of a 9000-char legacy set on an edit-form round trip; (2) the per-user count cap was a TOCTOU that 4 concurrent creates walked through, leaving 23 rows against a cap of 20; (3) BEGIN IMMEDIATE outside the try permanently poisoned a thread's cached connection after any failed DML; (4) update/archive lacked rollback guards, so a failed write was silently committed by the next successful one, breaking the append-only history invariant; (5) update returned success while persisting nothing and appending a phantom history row when racing an archive.

Responsibility moved OUT of this task: bounding the body length for the prompt now belongs to .7 (see .7 notes). InstructionSet.body_over_cap reports it.

Pre-existing defects found but deliberately NOT fixed here, filed separately: genetics-results-suite-y5d (the class's other 8 write accessors leave transactions open on failure) and genetics-results-suite-do8 (llm_config.db has no WAL, unlike chat_history.db).

title: Import and retire the orphaned user_instructions_history table
description:
genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/db/llm_config_db.py. user_instructions_history (created at ~line 158, migrated into at ~lines 95-113) is dead: commit 99fbdac removed its endpoints in Mar 2026 and it never reached prompt assembly. Its one-blob-per-user shape cannot express many named sets.

In _migrate_to_history_tables, do a one-shot idempotent import (guarded on user_instruction_sets being empty) of the latest surviving row per user into a set named 'Imported'. Stop creating the legacy table for new databases. Leave existing rows in place; do not drop the table in the same release.
close_reason:
Landed in genetics-mcp-server commit 5ac15b9. Full suite 686 passed (664 baseline + 22 new migration tests), review APPROVED round 2, blind validation found no functional defects.

DELIBERATE DEVIATION from this task's text: the guard is per-user (NOT EXISTS for that user_id), not 'guarded on user_instruction_sets being empty'. The literal reading was found to be a blocking bug — one user owning one set would have silently stranded every other user's legacy text forever, and nothing orders .11 after .3. Do not re-litigate.

Two round-1 blocking bugs fixed: one-arg SQLite TRIM strips spaces only so newline-only bodies were being imported; NULL changed_at suppressed the column DEFAULT and lost the ORDER BY comparison.

Known pre-existing issue found but NOT fixed (out of scope, needs user sign-off): docs/project-spec.md's Testing table is also missing test_credible_set_summary.py, test_disabled_thinking.py and test_stream_truncation.py, and CLAUDE.md's doc-ownership table has no tests/** row, so that table has no drift guard.

title: Feature: user-authored Instructions for chat
description:
Users can create and store multiple named sets of additional instructions (like Claude Desktop 'profiles', e.g. 'I'm a statistician') and select one per chat use case. The selected profile's text is appended to the LLM system prompt on each chat request.

UI lands beside the existing brief/detailed Answer selector in the chat options row (genetics-results-browser src/features/chat/LLMChat.tsx). Storage is per-user in the DB (genetics-mcp-server SQLite llm_config_db, which already has user_settings_history and an orphaned user_instructions_history table). Backend prompt assembly mirrors the verbosity_prompt() pattern in config/defaults.py + chat_api.py.

Spans repos: genetics-mcp-server (API + DB + prompt), genetics-results-browser (UI + types), genetics-results-suite (docs of record).

Naming to be decided as part of planning.
design:
Alternative 2 selected: first-class entity, server-resolved by id, split cached system block.

Name: UI label 'Instructions', code noun instruction_set. Rejected 'profile' (already means tool_profile in the same options row, the daly/finngen deploy config_profile, and results-api app/config/profiles/), 'persona' (the suite spec uses it for the APP_NAME assistant persona, and the text describes the user not the assistant) and 'context' (the same row renders a 'Conversation context' usage bar).

Key decisions:
- The chat request carries an id only; the server loads the body scoped to the authenticated user, so prompt text is never client-supplied and an answer is always attributable to a stored set.
- System prompt splits into two cached blocks: shared default+verbosity (one global cache entry per verbosity value) and the per-user envelope on the spare 4th breakpoint. ~$0.0025 per incremental write vs ~$0.043 for full-block refragmentation vs ~$0.05 per 25-iteration turn uncached.
- Selection: global-per-user default in user_settings_history, overridden per request, recorded per message on chat_messages. Per-session storage rejected: it needs a session-mutation endpoint and makes 'which wins' unanswerable when the selector moves mid-conversation.
- Archive rather than delete, so historical chat_messages rows stay resolvable.
- Unknown id is ignored, never 422 — same rule as verbosity.
- Folded in from the other alternatives: seeded clonable example sets in the dialog (from Alt 3), and the ORDER BY changed_at DESC, id DESC settings fix (from Alt 1).

Out of scope, documented rather than built: subagents (their reports are intermediate artifacts the main agent rewrites) and the MCP server path (no server-side system prompt, _validate_user_token discards identity, no llm_config.db volume mounted).

Not part of this epic, but decide separately: ChatRequest.system_prompt (chat_api.py:209) lets any authenticated user replace the entire system prompt with no gate — a strictly larger hole than the feature going in beside it.
close_reason:
All 21 subtasks closed. Feature complete and documented across genetics-mcp-server, genetics-results-browser and this repo's spec of record.

Shipped: users author named instruction sets, pick one per chat, and the selected set's text is appended to the system prompt in its own cached block. Named 'Instructions' rather than 'profiles' because tool_profile already sits in the same options row and the deploy config_profile and results-api app/config/profiles/ take the word twice more.

Architecture as chosen (Alternative 2): a first-class entity, resolved server-side by id so prompt text never travels on the request, with the system prompt split into a shared cached block and a per-user one. That keeps one cache entry per verbosity value instead of fragmenting per user, and consumes the fourth and last Anthropic breakpoint.

Blocking bugs caught in review that a green test suite did not: a read-time clamp that destroyed 5000 chars of a 9000-char legacy set on an edit round-trip; a per-user cap four concurrent requests walked straight through; BEGIN IMMEDIATE outside a try permanently poisoning a thread's cached connection; a fixed markdown fence a body could close early to inject a fake system section; an unvalidated LIMIT that returned entire histories on ?limit=-1 and 500'd past 64 bits; and a selector that silently reset on every session switch so messages went without the user's instructions.

Also fixed along the way, all pre-existing: rollback guards across both SQLite modules, WAL on llm_config.db, a same-second tiebreak that returned the OLDEST write, malformed-timestamp crashes, admin feedback pagination that could duplicate or skip an item, REQUIRE_AUTH read from two sources, and an importlib.reload that split the settings cache and made the suite's own green signal unreliable.

Deliberately not built, documented instead: instructions do not apply to subagents or to the MCP server path. Filed rather than fixed: genetics-results-suite-b3v (OpenAI branch drops instructions silently), -uvh (batched comment/doc accuracy), -eis (admin UI timestamp format), -avt (INTERNAL_API_SECRET), plus the still-open question of ChatRequest.system_prompt letting any authenticated user replace the entire system prompt with no gate.

title: [mcp-server] Serve MCP OAuth discovery (.well-known/oauth-protected-resource + WWW-Authenticate)
description:
Repo: ../genetics-mcp-server. File: src/genetics_mcp_server/mcp_server.py, in the ASGI auth_middleware (same place /healthz is special-cased).

Implement RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata so MCP clients (Claude connectors, ChatGPT, brainzzz) auto-discover the authorization server:
- Serve GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (and the path-suffixed /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp) returning JSON: { resource: OAUTH_RESOURCE_URL, authorization_servers: [OAUTH_ISSUER], scopes_supported: [...], bearer_methods_supported: ["header"] }. Serve it WITHOUT requiring a bearer token.
- On a 401 from the bearer middleware, add header WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="<resource>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource" so clients know where to look.
Only enable these when OAUTH_ISSUER is configured. The authorization-server metadata itself (/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server) is served by Keycloak, not here.

Depends on the settings subtask.

title: Feature: Direct OAuth (Keycloak) auth for MCP server — GeneGenie / brainzzz
description:
Let external web applications (first: brainzzz) connect to the GeneGenie MCP server via a standard OAuth 2.1 flow, instead of a shared api-token. Add this as a FOURTH bearer-validation path alongside the existing three (MCP_API_KEY shared secret, Google Identity Token JWT, per-user API token) — nothing existing is removed.

WHY: IAP/Google ID-Tokens don't fit a third-party app acting on behalf of its own users (audience-bound, no consent/refresh, users not on our email allow-list). MCP's HTTP transport defines an OAuth 2.1 profile where the MCP server is an OAuth *resource server* and clients auto-discover the *authorization server*. The daly/GeneGenie deployment already runs Keycloak as a full OIDC AS (https://auth.<domain>/realms/genetics, ENABLE_KEYCLOAK on for daly), so Keycloak is the authorization server and a 'web application type' OAuth client registered there is exactly what's needed.

SCOPE: GeneGenie (daly profile) only for now. finngen/FinnGenie has Keycloak OFF (Google-direct) and is out of scope.

DESIGN CONTRACT (shared across subtasks):
- Authorization server = Keycloak realm 'genetics'; issuer https://auth.<domain>/realms/genetics.
- MCP resource canonical URL (RFC 8707 resource indicator / RFC 9728 resource identifier) = https://genegenie.broadinstitute.org/mcp.
- Keycloak issues access tokens (JWT) with aud including that resource URL (via an audience mapper / dedicated client scope on the brainzzz client).
- MCP server validates: signature via Keycloak JWKS, iss match, aud includes resource URL, exp; THEN the existing email/domain allow-list (settings.allowed_emails / allowed_email_domains, already fed by the bearer-auth-allowed ConfigMap).
- Discovery: MCP server serves /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (RFC 9728) pointing at the Keycloak issuer, and returns WWW-Authenticate: Bearer with resource_metadata=... on 401. The authorization-server metadata itself is served by Keycloak (already on auth.<domain>).

Code work is split between the sibling repo ../genetics-mcp-server (validation + discovery + settings) and this repo genetics-results-suite (deployment env + auth-gateway routing + docs). Plus Keycloak client config (ops).

title: Phase 0: finalize EpiMap 18-state storage + open/active state set
description: Decide how the ChromHMM 18-state label is stored (score_type=chromhmm_18state + state token placement) and which states count as open/active (TSS/enhancer/transcribed). Gates the EpiMap munge task.
design:
EpiMap ChromHMM 18-state modeling for the open_chromatin product.
Model = Roadmap/EpiMap 18-state (observed_aux_18), 833 biosamples, hg38 CALLS.
INCLUDE (accessible/active regulatory subset) as open_chromatin rows:
  active promoter: TssA, TssFlnk, TssFlnkU, TssFlnkD
  active enhancer: EnhA1, EnhA2, EnhG1, EnhG2, EnhWk
  poised/bivalent (accessible, tagged): TssBiv, EnhBiv
EXCLUDE (not open peaks): Tx, TxWk, ZNF_Rpts, Het, ReprPC, ReprPCWk, Quies.
State storage (NO schema change): encode the exact state in score_type as chromhmm:<State> (e.g. score_type=chromhmm:EnhA1); assay=chromHMM; score=NULL (presence-based — ChromHMM is a categorical segmentation, so row existence = state called in that biosample).
Agent-facing regulatory_class grouping (map in the MCP tool description, NOT stored): Tss* -> promoter, Enh* -> enhancer, *Biv -> bivalent.
Labels: cell_type = verbatim EpiMap biosample name; tissue from EpiMap sample metadata (GROUP/Anatomy column); life_stage=adult unless the biosample metadata marks it fetal/embryonic; condition=unknown.
Do NOT import EpiMap DNase layer (that is the Meuleman DHS index, which was dropped).
close_reason: Resolved: EpiMap active/accessible state subset + state-in-score_type encoding decided. Decision recorded in --design.

title: Phase 0: confirm genome builds & liftOver needs
description: Confirm all sources vs hg38: Marderstein/Li/Catlas/ROSMAP snATAC and EpiMap ChromHMM CALLS are hg38; Calderon is hg19 (needs liftOver). Verify EpiMap hg38 CALLS are used, not hg19. Gates all munge tasks.
design:
Genome-build decision — platform standard = GRCh38/hg38 (GENCODE).
- marderstein (scATAC peaks + ChromBPNet + FLARE): hg38, native, no liftOver.
- li_brain_atac (Li 2023 Science): hg38, native.
- catlas (Zhang 2021 Cell): hg38, native (verify cCRE BED header at download).
- epimap (Boix 2021): USE the hg38 CALLS directory (ChromHMM observed_aux_18_hg38), NOT hg19.
- calderon_immune (Calderon 2019): hg19 -> liftOver to hg38 (UCSC hg19ToHg38.over.chain); drop unmapped and split/multi-mapping intervals, then re-sort.
- rosmap_brain (Xiong 2023): hg38, native.
RULE for every munge task: verify the source file build at download; if hg19, liftOver to hg38 and drop unmapped/multimapped before bgzip+tabix. Only Calderon is known-hg19 today.
close_reason: Resolved: builds determined (all hg38 except Calderon hg19->liftOver; EpiMap use hg38 CALLS). Per-file verification folded into each munge task. Decision recorded in --design.

title: Feature: Google token authentication for MCP server
description:
Currently the MCP server (genetics-mcp-server/src/genetics_mcp_server/mcp_server.py) only accepts MCP_API_KEY shared secrets and user-created API tokens (validated via local DB or chat-backend /v1/tokens/validate). It does NOT support Google Identity Tokens.

Goal: Bring MCP server bearer token auth to parity with results-api by adding Google Identity Token validation. This enables programmatic clients to authenticate to /mcp using gcloud-issued ID tokens, just like they already can with /api.

title: Dev environment strategy: local copy + sync script
description:
Solve the dev environment problem where each repo runs independently in separate tmux windows.

Approach: each service repo keeps a local copy of datasets.yaml (e.g., configs/datasets.yaml) that is used by default when running locally. The suite repo has the canonical version.

Implementation:
1. Add a Makefile target or script (e.g., `make sync-config` or `scripts/sync-datasets.sh`) in each service repo that copies from `../genetics-results-suite/configs/datasets.yaml` (assuming standard sibling directory layout)
2. The local copy is .gitignore'd OR committed as a known-good snapshot
3. Each service's code loads from a configurable path: env var `DATASETS_CONFIG_PATH` with a sensible default (e.g., `./configs/datasets.yaml`)
4. At deploy time, the suite repo's deploy.sh delivers the canonical version (ConfigMap or Dockerfile COPY)
5. Add a CI check that compares each service's local copy against the suite repo's canonical file to catch drift

Decision needed: should the local copy be committed (simpler dev onboarding, but risks drift) or .gitignore'd (forces sync, but slightly harder onboarding)?

title: deploy.sh's secret preflight omits mcp-api-key, so an already-broken cluster is not self-healed
description:
Found by the blind validator on genetics-results-suite-9xz, 2026-08-27. PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by that change, and it bounds what 9xz fixes.

scripts/deploy.sh:369 gates on internal-api-secret, sandbox-token-signing-key and gateway-identity-secret only. mcp-api-key is not in that list. 9xz makes create-secrets.sh GENERATE the key, so a first install and any re-run of create-secrets.sh are fine — but a cluster that already holds the present-but-zero-byte value keeps crash-looping mcp-server on a plain scripts/deploy.sh, because deploy.sh never inspects that key and create-secrets.sh is a separate command that additionally requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to be exported.

So the state 9xz repairs is repaired only by running create-secrets.sh, never by deploying.

NOT URGENT: the only cluster known to have been in this state (daly-staging) was fixed by hand on 2026-08-26, and any NEW environment gets a generated key. Iced rather than worked because nothing on the epic's frontier depends on it.
design: Likely one line: add mcp-api-key to the preflight list at scripts/deploy.sh:369. Check first what that preflight does on a failure — warn or abort — and whether aborting a deploy over a key that only mcp-server needs is proportionate. The three keys already listed are ones whose absence breaks several services.
acceptance_criteria: A deploy against a cluster whose mcp-api-key is empty either repairs it or refuses with a message naming the key, instead of rolling out a pod that will crash-loop.

title: db-api's aggregate-byte-budget 429 logs an endpoint_access line with no log_source and no service
description:
FOUND by the review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.24, which was a doc sweep and correctly did not widen into code. VERIFIED IN THE TREE before filing.

genetics-results-db api/main.py has FOUR dicts carrying "log_type": "endpoint_access" — at :125, :136, :200 and :481. THE FIRST THREE CARRY log_source. THE FOURTH DOES NOT, and it also omits `service`.

The fourth is _aggregate_budget_exceeded (:478-485), which is the 429 raised when a sandbox execution exhausts SANDBOX_AGGREGATE_BYTES_BUDGET (200 GB across one jti). So the line that records a SECURITY/SPEND CONTROL FIRING is the one line in the file that is not attributable.

WHY THAT IS A DEFECT RATHER THAN A COSMETIC INCONSISTENCY, in the code's own words: api/main.py:75 describes log_source as 'the service discriminator in the shared endpoint_access sink, where db-api's rows sit beside' results-api's. The sink is SHARED. A consumer filtering endpoint_access by log_source — which is what the discriminator exists for — will not see this line at all, and a consumer not filtering will see a row it cannot attribute to a service. Either way the aggregate-budget rejection is invisible in exactly the query someone would run to find it.

THE FIX IS ALREADY SHAPED BY THE FILE: :184 is a helper documented as 'The fields every db-api endpoint_access line shares with results-api's'. _aggregate_budget_exceeded simply does not use it. Merging those fields in is the change; check whether the other three go through the helper or hand-roll the fields, and make all four consistent rather than patching one.

CHECK WHILE THERE, do not assume: whether results-api has the same gap on any of ITS endpoint_access lines, and whether the monitor (scripts/monitor/ in genetics-results-suite) actually filters on log_source — if it does, name the query that would miss this line, because that turns the argument above from reasoning into a measurement.

NOT BLOCKING ANYTHING. genetics-results-suite-4h6's remaining children are all phase-blocked on a deploy window, and nothing depends on this. Filed and deferred per the filing gate: a real defect that nothing on the frontier needs.

title: Reopening a conversation adopts a server-known profile but never warns when the server has DROPPED one
description:
FOUND during genetics-results-suite-4h6.74's second fix round, 2026-08-25. Real, narrow, and nothing on the
frontier depends on it, so it is filed and iced.

4h6.74 made the browser probe GET /chat/v1/tools/resolved on three paths, but only two of them ask the
BROWSER->SERVER question (is this name still known?). applyFromConversation - opening an existing
conversation - adopts a server-known name, but does NOT call checkProfile, so it never renders the amber
"not recognised by the server" warning.

CONSEQUENCE: a conversation stored under a profile the browser DOES list (say `code`) that the server has
since renamed or dropped reopens with `code` selected, the server degrades it to general-only, and the UI
says nothing. Selection and load-restore both warn in that situation; reopening a conversation does not.

WHY IT IS SMALL: it needs a server-side REMOVAL of a profile the browser still lists, which the new pin
test in genetics-mcp-server (tests/test_unknown_profile_warning.py) now makes a deliberate act rather than
an accident - the whole point of that test is that removing a key fails CI until someone decides about the
browser. The server also warns once per distinct value, so an operator sees it even when the user does not.

FIX SHAPE: one checkProfile call in applyFromConversation. The in-flight set and the settled-answer cache
already make it free on a reopen. Cheap enough that the reason it was not done is scope, not difficulty.

title: The response-cap rejection line still names no `code`, and the e2e harness still reads it off the 429 body
description:
FOUND during genetics-results-suite-4h6.65's fix cycle, 2026-08-25. Both halves are about the SAME field -
the rejection code an operator needs - and neither blocks anything, so they are one bead and it is iced.

1. app/middleware.py:213-223 (genetics-results-api), the `sandbox response cap exceeded` line, passes
   path/status/limit/observed in its extra and carries NO `code`, while its own 429 RESPONSE BODY does.
   4h6.65 repaired the mechanism that was dropping those four fields, so the line now arrives - but it
   still names the observed value without naming the control that fired. sandbox_budget.log_rejection,
   which the bead named, does carry `code`. This is the one adjacent site that does not.

2. scripts/test-e2e-local.py:710-731 (genetics-results-suite) reads the rejection code off the 429
   response BODY as a workaround for the defect 4h6.65 just fixed. It is now removable: the harness
   already collects the `sandbox per-execution limit exceeded` records from results-api.log into
   `rejections` earlier in the same block, and those records now carry `code`, so the check becomes
   any(r.get("code") == "sandbox_concurrency" for r in rejections) and the whole probe/_hammer/bodies
   stanza - a second token mint and 12 extra HTTP requests - deletes.
   STRICTLY BETTER EVIDENCE, which is why it is worth doing eventually: reading the log tests the
   OPERATOR's view, which is what the check claims to be about; reading the body tests the client's.
   ONE PRECONDITION TO CONFIRM IN A REAL RUN: LogTail parses JSON lines out of results-api.log, so the
   local stack must be on the GCPJsonFormatter stdout path (dev-stack is), or the extras are not on
   those lines at all.

title: require_sandbox_config gates the signing key's length but not INTERNAL_API_SECRET's, in both verifiers
description:
FOUND 2026-08-24 while implementing genetics-results-suite-4h6.36, which added a minimum-length gate for
SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY. NOT a defect in that change - an asymmetry that change CREATED VISIBILITY OF.

THE GAP: `require_sandbox_config` - in BOTH verifiers, genetics-results-db `api/sandbox_auth.py` and
genetics-results-api `app/core/sandbox_token.py` - now refuses to start when SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY is
under 32 bytes, catching the whitespace-only / one-character / empty-file class. It applies NO such check
to INTERNAL_API_SECRET, which is validated by the same function at the same moment. A value of "   "
passes.

WHY IT WAS LEFT OUT OF 4h6.36, deliberately: INTERNAL_API_SECRET IS NOT AN HMAC KEY. 4h6.36's threshold
is 32 bytes because that is RFC 7518 3.2's minimum for HMAC-SHA256 and the point at which PyJWT stops
emitting InsecureKeyLengthWarning - a justification that simply does not transfer to a shared bearer
secret compared with ==. Picking a number for INTERNAL_API_SECRET needs its own reasoning, and 4h6.36
was scoped to the HMAC key.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH SOMETHING: a whitespace-only INTERNAL_API_SECRET is a GUESSABLE SHARED CREDENTIAL
that `is_internal_caller` accepts, and results-api serves an internal-secret caller UNACCOUNTED (see
docs/project-spec.md's anonymous-surface bullet - that is intentional for chat-backend, mcp-server and
bff, none of which is a per-execution tenant). So the blast radius of a weak one is larger than the
sandbox key's, not smaller. scripts/create-secrets.sh generates it with `openssl rand -base64 32`, so
nothing a correct install produces is near the boundary.

WHAT TO DECIDE IF THIS IS EVER PICKED UP - and it is a decision, not a patch:
- what minimum is defensible for a compared-with-== bearer secret (entropy, not a crypto standard);
- whether the check belongs in require_sandbox_config at all, since INTERNAL_API_SECRET is required
  whether or not the sandbox is enabled, while that function keys on SANDBOX_ENABLED;
- whether to also warn on a value differing from its stripped form, as 4h6.36 does - note the same
  DO-NOT-NORMALISE constraint applies for the same reason: the comparison is byte-for-byte against what
  the caller sent, so stripping on one side only would break every internal call.

ICED. Nothing on genetics-results-suite-4h6's frontier depends on it, no such key exists in a cluster
today (SANDBOX_ENABLED is false everywhere and the secrets are generated correctly), and the sandbox
epic's deploy path does not touch it. Filed so the asymmetry is not re-derived, and so that whoever
reads the new gate does not conclude the omission was an oversight.

title: Batched doc-accuracy and latent-hazard findings, part 2 (continues e8e, which hit the 64 KiB notes limit)
description:
CONTINUATION OF genetics-results-suite-e8e, WHICH IS FULL. Created 2026-08-24.

WHY THIS EXISTS, because a second batch bead otherwise looks like exactly the sprawl the batching rule
forbids: e8e's `notes` reached 62,196 characters across 75 numbered findings and the next append FAILED -
Dolt/MySQL Error 1105, the 64 KiB TEXT column limit. e8e's content is INTACT and must not be trimmed; it
simply cannot be written to again. This bead is where items 64 onward go.

THE RULE IS UNCHANGED: doc-accuracy, enumeration-rot and latent-hazard findings are APPENDED here, never
filed as their own beads. Read CLAUDE.md's "Findings that are not work" section and the global filing
gate before adding anything. Numbering CONTINUES from e8e's 63 rather than restarting, so a reference to
"e8e item 47" stays unambiguous across both beads.

OPERATIONAL LESSON WORTH KEEPING: a single-bead batch strategy has a hard ceiling of roughly 64 KiB, which
this epic reached in about three weeks of adversarial review cycles. Anyone continuing this pattern should
expect to split again, and should split by CREATING A SUCCESSOR rather than by pruning - the value of
these notes is that they record what was already investigated, and a pruned note is one a future session
re-derives from scratch.
notes:
--- APPENDED 2026-08-24 from the 4h6.67 cycle. Two doc sites, the SAME FAILURE CLASS as the bug that
    bead fixed: a doc promising a signal the code does not actually deliver. ---
64. docs/project-spec.md:1667 says of the dev-stack credentials: "Override any of the three to pin a
    value." That is imprecise in exactly the way 4h6.67 exists to correct. A SHELL EXPORT pins the value
    for all three services; setting it in MCP_ENV_FILE pins it FOR CHAT-API ONLY, because start_chat_api
    sources that file with `set -a` AFTER the exports - and chat-api is the MINTER, so the verifiers keep
    the generated key and every execution gets a 401 from both backends, which reads like a token bug
    rather than a precedence bug. docs/local-dev-vm.md was corrected in the 4h6.67 cycle; this sentence
    was not, so the two docs now describe the same mechanism at different precisions.
65. docs/local-dev-vm.md:118 says SANDBOX_ENABLED may be set "in the environment or in MCP_ENV_FILE", and
    the next clause promises that `up` probes SANDBOX_URL/health and warns if nothing answers. MEASURED:
    SET IN MCP_ENV_FILE IT DOES NOT WARN. The probe (dev-stack.sh:228-231) runs at TOP LEVEL, long before
    start_chat_api sources the file, so the variable is not set yet when the probe decides whether to run.
    Pre-existing, and NOT covered by the grep 4h6.67 added - that guard names only
    SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY and INTERNAL_API_SECRET.
    THE PATTERN ACROSS 64, 65 AND THE BUG 4h6.67 FIXED: this script has THREE variables whose effect
    depends on WHERE you set them, and the docs describe all three as though setting them were uniform.
    The durable fix is not three more warnings - it is either sourcing MCP_ENV_FILE BEFORE the exports so
    precedence is uniform, or saying once, in one place, that MCP_ENV_FILE is chat-api-only. Not filed:
    nothing on the frontier depends on it and the dev stack works.

--- APPENDED 2026-08-24 from the 4h6.52 validation. METHOD. ---
66. A FIX CAN LAND ON A CODE PATH PRODUCTION NEVER EXECUTES, AND EVERY GREEN TEST WILL AGREE WITH IT.
    On 4h6.52 the FIFO/blocking hazard was fixed by adding O_NONBLOCK to `_artifact_digest` - which runs
    ONLY in `build_manifest`'s `sealed is None` branch, and `build_manifest` is called from exactly one
    place (supervisor.py:4406) ALWAYS with `sealed=<dict>`. So the fixed function is UNREACHABLE IN
    PRODUCTION. The live path, `seal_artifact` (supervisor.py:1136), still had the identical
    check-then-open window and was untouched. A shipped, deadline-based regression test passed, and
    passed for a real reason - it exercised the path that was fixed.
    THE TELL, and it is checkable cheaply: the change came with a claim that the fixed path "became the
    ONLY read path". Whenever a fix is justified by "this is now the only path", COUNT THE CALLERS of
    the thing you changed and check the arguments they pass. Here one grep for `build_manifest(` would
    have shown a single call site with the branch-selecting argument always set the other way.
    GENERAL RULE: for a hazard that exists at several sites, enumerate the sites FIRST and fix them as a
    set. Fixing "the one the test reaches" is the failure mode, because the test was usually written
    against the same mental model as the fix.
67. A SMALL ONE WORTH THE HABIT: the implementer reported "~28 tests removed, ~30 added" with a total
    UNCHANGED at 1959. That arithmetic does not close, and it was worth one question. The review
    reconciled it by AST-counting the diff with parametrize EXPANDED - 26 removed defs (one x10) and 29
    added defs (one x7), 35 cases each way, net ZERO in a single file, no other test file touched. So
    the totals were right and the implementer's own count of its own work was wrong.
    Counting `def test_` lines does not count TESTS when parametrize is in play. When a reported delta
    does not reconcile, the cheap check is `pytest --collect-only -q` on the old and new file, not a
    re-read of the diff.

--- APPENDED 2026-08-24 from the 4h6.52 scoped re-check. ---
68. LATENT, pre-existing, comment-at-the-site material rather than work: `seal_artifact`'s copy loop
    READS TO EOF, so a setsid() escapee that APPENDS to a regular artifact as fast as the seal reads it
    makes the loop unbounded. Bounded in practice by the scratch disk quota
    (SCRATCH_AGGREGATE_CEILING_BYTES 480 MiB, ARTIFACT_QUOTA_BYTES 64 MiB), so it cannot run forever -
    but it can hold the execution slot for as long as the quota allows. Unrelated to the O_NONBLOCK
    change and present before it. Recorded so nobody re-derives it as new.
69. A MEASUREMENT WORTH KEEPING BECAUSE IT CONTRADICTS THE INTUITION THAT MOTIVATED A CHANGE. The
    4h6.52 fix round raised `_ArtifactManifests._MAX_EXECUTIONS` from 16 to 128 partly out of concern
    for memory. MEASURED afterwards: the binding term is row SIZE, not row COUNT. A row's name set is
    capped only by the supervisor's ARTIFACT_ENTRY_BUDGET (1024) x NAME_MAX (255), so a worst-case row
    is 328.4 KiB against a typical 487 bytes.
    The naive 512 x 128 product is 20.5 GiB against chat-backend's limits.memory 2Gi - AND THE OLD CAP
    OF 16 ALREADY PRODUCED 2.57 GiB ON THE SAME PRODUCT. So 16 -> 128 did not cross a safety threshold
    that 16 was on the right side of; `_MAX_EXECUTIONS` WAS NEVER THE BINDING TERM in either direction.
    What actually bounds it is THROUGHPUT: filling either product needs tens of thousands of executions
    inside one 300 s TTL through a sandbox that runs them one at a time. One session at the cap costs
    41 MiB.
    THE TRANSFERABLE POINT: when a bound is raised or defended on memory grounds, measure the SIZE of
    the thing being counted before arguing about HOW MANY. Both the original justification and the
    concern that replaced it reasoned about counts, and the counts were never what mattered.

--- APPENDED 2026-08-24 from the 4h6.60 + 4h6.36 cycle. ---
70. THE DOC-OWNERSHIP TABLE DOES NOT COVER THE SCRIPTS THAT GENERATE THE TREES IT COVERS. Neither
    scripts/gen-sandbox-docs.py nor scripts/test-sandbox-docs.py appears in CLAUDE.md's table or in
    scripts/check-doc-drift.sh - yet the table explicitly covers `sandbox/schema/**` and
    `sandbox/stubs/**` and says they are NOT exempt precisely because
    docs/code-execution-security.md reasons about their shipped content. So changing the GENERATOR
    cannot flag the doc, while changing its OUTPUT can. Confirmed by grep in this cycle.
    SAME CLASS AS genetics-results-suite-e96 (run-sandbox-local.sh is in neither) and as item 22 above
    (docs/environments.md has no row at all). That is now THREE instances of the same gap, which is
    enough to say the table's real failure mode is not wrong rows but MISSING ONES - it enumerates
    outputs and omits the tools that produce them.
    A table edit, so it belongs here rather than in a cycle.
71. results-api's OWN project-spec documented the sandbox startup gate NOWHERE AT ALL, while the suite's
    docs/code-execution-security.md:4696 says sys.exit(1) is used "in BOTH VERIFIERS by design". The
    4h6.36 cycle added the missing bullet. Recorded because of what it implies rather than for the fix:
    THE SUITE DOC WAS THE ONLY PLACE THE SECOND VERIFIER'S BEHAVIOUR WAS WRITTEN DOWN, so a reader
    working in genetics-results-api had no way to learn the gate existed, and the cross-repo rule in
    CLAUDE.md ("the sibling repos each document only themselves, so a feature that spans repos leaves no
    single repo's docs wrong in a way that repo can detect") describes exactly this - but the rule is
    stated for DATASETS, VIEWS, API ROUTES AND MCP TOOLS, and a startup gate is none of those.

--- APPENDED 2026-08-24, 4h6.36/.60 close. ---
72. SUITE README.md:560 says the services "refuse to start at all when SANDBOX_ENABLED=true and either
    secret is unset". Now INCOMPLETE - they also refuse on a SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY under 32 bytes
    (4h6.36). One clause, and it is the enumeration class this bead exists for.
73. A DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN TWO RECORDED FINDINGS THAT NOBODY HAS SETTLED, flagged so the next person
    checks rather than trusting either. e8e item 24 says db-api's verify_sandbox_token catches BARE
    `Exception` around jwt.decode WITH a written rationale, and that only results-api is narrow
    (`except jwt.InvalidTokenError`). The 4h6.36 reviewer reports that NEITHER verifier catches it and
    both are narrow. Both statements were written from reading, neither was re-measured in the 4h6.36
    cycle, and they cannot both be true.
    IT MATTERS because it decides whether a >=32-byte NON-UTF-8 signing key (measured: 40 x \xff passes
    the new length gate) yields a 500 or a 401 from each verifier, against a doc that says sandbox token
    failure is "always a hard 401". Unreachable from any shipped generator, so latent either way - but
    the cheap fix is one grep at each site, and whoever next opens either file should do it.

--- APPENDED 2026-08-25, from the 4h6.65 cycle. Three latent findings, none filed, per the gate. ---
74. THE DICT-MESSAGE BRANCH IS THE SAME RESERVED-KEY DOOR, LEFT OPEN. 4h6.65 stopped an `extra` from
    overwriting severity/timestamp/logger/trace/labels/httpRequest, but format()'s OTHER branch splats a
    dict message (`**msg`) with no such guard - and that branch is the PRODUCTION path for endpoint_access
    (middleware_usage_logging does logger.info(entry)). Not reachable today: the keys there are literals
    in our own middleware and only the VALUES are caller-influenced. It becomes real the moment any caller
    builds a log dict with a key it did not choose itself.
75. StripSensitiveFieldsFilter STRIPS full_path FROM DICT MESSAGES ONLY. A string-message record carrying
    a `full_path` extra now reaches the CloudLoggingHandler path with the query string intact; the
    formatter's own pop covers stdout but the filter is what covers the API handler. Nothing emits that
    today - the shape did not exist while the allow-list did.
76. sandbox_token.py DOES NOT NORMALIZE `sub`, so Person@Example.org and person@example.org are two
    identities in the user_email column; the header path lowercases, the token path does not. Deliberately
    left: normalizing would desync from get_verified_user's return and from db-api's verifier, both of
    which compare the raw claim. Cost is a split in log grouping, not an auth difference.

--- APPENDED 2026-08-25, from the 4h6.74 cycle. Enumeration rot, batched not filed. ---
77. docs/chat-tool-reference.md SECTION 1 "Where the definitions live" HAS SEVEN ROTTED LINE NUMBERS, and
    section 3 gives a THIRD, DIFFERENT set for the same two dicts. Measured against definitions.py during
    the 4h6.74 doc pass - actual vs documented: TOOL_DEFINITIONS 18/15, BIGQUERY_TOOL_DEFINITIONS
    1633/1616, SUBAGENT_TOOL_DEFINITIONS 1686/1669, TOOL_PROFILES 1730/1724, TOOL_PROFILE_TOOLS 1779/1773,
    get_anthropic_tools 1815/1748, register_mcp_tools 1896/1824. Section 3 separately cites 1713-1717 and
    1735-1745, disagreeing with its own section 1 table. Most of the gap (38 and 72 lines on the last two)
    PREDATES the 4h6.74 change, which added ~30 lines. The doc agent deliberately added no new line numbers
    rather than mix verified ones into a stale table - the right call, and it leaves the table uniformly
    stale rather than half-true.
    THE LESSON, not the entries: a doc that cites line numbers for a file under active development is a
    doc that is wrong by default. Whatever fixes this should cite SYMBOL names and let the reader grep.

80. IN-FLIGHT PROBE DEDUPE DROPS A SECOND CALLER'S ADOPTION. useChatOptions' profileChecksInflight is a
    Set, so a second caller asking about a name already in flight is dropped rather than joined to the

--- APPENDED 2026-08-26, from the 4h6.70/.80/.81 cycle. Three items, none filed. ---
81. uniprot.py's `size or _DEFAULT_SEARCH_SIZE` (search_uniprot) means size=0 silently returns 25 rows

83. THE PATTERN-FROM-A-VALIDATOR TRAP, recorded because it will come up again the next time somebody

--- APPENDED 2026-08-26, from the 4h6.61 / 4h6.32 validation round. ---
84. DB-API NOW EMITS TWO DIFFERENT 429 VOCABULARIES, and an operator diagnosing a throttled execution
    will meet both. The new per-execution gate (api/sandbox_budget.py) returns the results-api shape
    {detail, code, limit, observed} with code in {sandbox_request_count, sandbox_concurrency,
    sandbox_concurrency_pod, sandbox_execution_tracker_full}. The PRE-EXISTING aggregate byte budget
    raises HTTPException(429, detail=...) from _aggregate_budget_exceeded with NO code/limit/observed.
    Deliberately not aligned: the byte-budget response is established behaviour an existing consumer may
    parse, so changing its shape is a compatibility decision, not a tidy-up. Recorded so the asymmetry
    reads as a choice rather than an oversight.
85. admit() CREATES THE ENTRY BEFORE THE POD-WIDE CHECK, so a jti rejected by the pod-wide cap on its
    FIRST request leaves a zero-valued entry (requests=0, in_flight=0) that survives until its token
    expires and counts against SANDBOX_MAX_TRACKED_EXECUTIONS. Trigger: pod already at 8 in flight when a
    new jti first arrives. NOT a divergence - results-api's app/core/sandbox_budget.py has the identical
    ordering, so db-api is a faithful port. Bounded and self-clearing. Fix both or neither, and only if
    tracker-full pressure is ever observed in practice.
86. THE GATE ASSUMES LOWERCASE ASGI HEADER KEYS. api/sandbox_budget.py matches key == b"authorization"
    on the raw scope headers; a capitalised `Authorization` resolves to None and the gate becomes a
    silent no-op for that request. Correct under uvicorn, which lowercases per the ASGI spec, and it
    fails open FOR THE GATE ONLY - it can never wrongly reject chat-backend or mcp-server traffic. The
    test harness lowercases too, so the suite cannot detect a regression here. results-api's
    app/middleware.py has the same assumption. A comment now sits at the line; that is the right home
    for it, not a bead.
87. TWO PER-JTI MAPS WITH DIFFERENT EVICTION LIVE IN DB-API AS OF 4h6.61 - see the ICED bead filed
    alongside this entry for the fail-open half. Recorded here only so the next reader of
    api/main.py is not surprised to find _jti_bytes (OrderedDict, LRU 1024, no TTL) beside
    api/sandbox_budget.py's _executions (expiry sweep, refuses new on full). They are not redundant:
    they meter different things. They are also not consistent, and the LRU is the fail-open one.

88. THE "_jti_bytes LRU CAN DROP A LIVE EXECUTION" CLAIM IS OVERSTATED, AND IT IS CITED AS A DESIGN
    RATIONALE, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH CORRECTING HERE. genetics-results-api
    app/core/sandbox_budget.py's module docstring contrasts its own expiry sweep against db-api with:
    "db-api trims _jti_bytes to 1024 entries LRU, which *can* drop a live execution's counter and
    silently reset its budget". The 4h6.61 implementer repeated it as a live fail-open.
    MEASURED against the code: genetics-results-db api/main.py `_charge_aggregate` and
    `_charge_aggregate_spent` BOTH call `_jti_bytes.move_to_end(jti)` immediately after writing, so the
    structure is a TRUE LRU, not insertion-ordered. An execution that is actively being charged is the
    most-recently-used entry and therefore the LAST one `popitem(last=False)` will take. Evicting a live
    execution requires 1024 OTHER jtis to each be charged in the window BETWEEN two of that execution's
    own db-api calls.
    NOT REACHABLE IN THE DEPLOYED TOPOLOGY: jti entries are created only for a SandboxPrincipal (chat-
    backend and mcp-server carry no jti and never touch this map), and the sandbox is concurrency 1 with
    replicas 1, so distinct sandbox executions do not overlap, let alone 1024 of them inside one
    execution's inter-request gap.
    SO IT IS LATENT, NOT A DEFECT, and it was deliberately NOT filed as a bead. What WOULD make it real:
    raising sandbox concurrency or replicas above 1, or any future non-sandbox caller being given a jti.
    If either happens, revisit - and fix the results-api docstring at the same time, because a wrong
    rationale in a sibling repo is how this got repeated in the first place.

89. STILL-HARDCODED TEST COUNTS IN docs/project-spec.md, after 4h6.61's cycle removed one of them. The
    db-api "(26 tests)" figure was deleted rather than maintained, which is the right move under the
    enumeration rule; results-api's "(30 tests, offline lane)" for its own tests/test_sandbox_budget.py
    was NOT in that batch and survives. Same hazard, same fix (state the relationship, drop the number).
    Do it in whatever cycle next touches that paragraph; it does not deserve its own.
90. THE run-sandbox-local.sh OWNERSHIP ROW MAY BE TOO NARROW, and this is a judgement call left open
    deliberately. genetics-results-suite-e96 specified the row as
    scripts/run-sandbox-local.sh -> docs/project-spec.md, README.md, and that is what was added. But the
    script is referenced ~16 times in docs/code-execution-security.md against ONCE in README.md, so the
    doc most likely to go stale when it changes is the one the row does not name. Counter-argument, which
    is why this was not just widened: CLAUDE.md warns that a row broader than the doc concern it names
    fires where it can never apply and trains people to ignore it, and many of those 16 mentions may be
    incidental rather than descriptions of the script's behaviour. Someone should read the 16 sites once
    and decide; until then the row is defensible as written.
91. THE 4h6.16 -> 4h6.48 MISATTRIBUTION FOR run_analysis ALSO LIVES IN mcp-server's OWN COMMENTS, not
    only in the suite docs that bt8 corrected: genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/mcp_server.py
    ("run_analysis joins this set with 4h6.16") and near definitions.py's TOOL_DEFINITIONS block. Left
    alone because bt8 scoped itself to the suite repo and mcp-server was a read-only reference in that

92. check-doc-drift.sh CANNOT EXPRESS THE MAPPING THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT 4h6.32's STALE STUBS, and this
    is a structural gap rather than a missing row. The generated suite files sandbox/stubs/*.pyi are
    produced from genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/sdk/ - a path in a DIFFERENT REPOSITORY -
    while the script reads `git diff --cached` of the suite repo only. An SDK docstring edit therefore
    never enters `staged` and no rule in this script can fire on it. Nothing was invented to paper over
    it; a comment now records the gap at the site.
    WHAT DOES CATCH IT: gen-sandbox-docs.py --check, already invoked by build.sh, build-all.sh and
    run-sandbox-local.sh. THE RESIDUAL IS THAT NOTHING RUNS IT AT COMMIT TIME, so the stubs can be stale

93. docs/chat-tool-reference.md CARRIES ~30 `file.py:NNN` CITATIONS AND ONLY TWO HAVE EVER BEEN
    RE-DERIVED. 4h6.24 fixed the two in section 3 - definitions.py:1713-1717 / :1735-1745 had drifted to
    :1806 / :1855 - and replaced them with a `grep -n '^TOOL_PROFILE'` recipe rather than new numbers,
