    NOT FILED AS WORK. The right fix is not a re-derivation pass, which would rot again on the next
    commit to definitions.py - it is to replace line citations with grep recipes wherever the doc is
    pointing at a named symbol rather than at a specific line's content. Do that opportunistically in
    whatever cycle next edits that file.
94. scripts/gen-sandbox-docs.py IS NOT MATCHED BY ANY DOC-OWNERSHIP ROW. The `scripts/` row enumerates
    deploy.sh, rollout.sh, build*.sh, sync-datasets.sh, install-git-hooks.sh, check-worktree-paths.sh and
    lib/**; the generator matches none of them. Its OUTPUTS are covered via the sandbox/** row, so this
    is a gap in the rule's path pattern rather than a live doc error - changing the generator changes
    sandbox/schema/** and sandbox/stubs/**, which DO fire.
    Deliberately not added, for the reason CLAUDE.md itself gives: a row is owed only where changing the
    left-hand path can falsify the named doc without also touching something that already fires. Here it
    cannot, in practice, because a generator change that matters shows up in its regenerated output in
    the same commit. Recorded so the next person to notice the gap does not re-litigate it.
    RELATED AND NOT THE SAME THING: item 92's SDK -> sandbox/stubs/** mapping IS genuinely missing and
    genuinely unexpressible; this one is expressible and judged unnecessary.

95. THE STDIO TRANSPORT IS THE ONE PLACE mcp-server LOGS LINE-ORIENTED PLAIN TEXT, and it is worth knowing
    before anyone reasons about log injection in that repo again. genetics-mcp-server
    src/genetics_mcp_server/mcp_server.py:46-50 installs a "%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s -
    %(message)s" formatter on stderr for the stdio branch, while the sse/streamable-http branch installs
    logging_config.GCPJsonFormatter, whose json.dumps escapes control characters and makes injection
    impossible.
    genetics-results-suite-80n was closed NOT-A-DEFECT on that escaping (four executor.py logger.error
    calls interpolate a raw caller-supplied `resource`; measured, json.dumps neutralises it). THAT VERDICT
    IS TRANSPORT-DEPENDENT. It holds because k8s/deployments/mcp-server.yaml:20 pins
    `--transport streamable-http`. If anything ever runs the server over stdio with attacker-reachable
    tool arguments, the same four sites become genuine log injection.
    Not a bead: nothing deployed does this, and the manifest is the thing that would have to change first.
96. A BEAD'S OWN LINE NUMBERS ARE THE LEAST TRUSTWORTHY THING IN IT, and 80n is the sharpest example so
    far - it warned about this in its own text and was still wrong. It cited executor.py lines 1022, 1847
    and 1881; those hold row-shape checking, a resource_filter f-string, and a docstring. The real sites
    are 1498, 2328, 2362 and 3119 - and the bead MISSED THE FOURTH ENTIRELY. The file is 6609 lines.
    Every investigation prompt for this repo should say "re-locate by grep, the coordinates are stale",
    and every bead that cites a line should cite a SYMBOL alongside it.

97. genetics-mcp-server docs/project-spec.md HAS TWO ENV-VAR TABLES THAT ENUMERATE DIFFERENT SETS. The
    main table carries SANDBOX_URL (updated by 6um); a second, abbreviated table around :2195 lists
    SANDBOX_ENABLED and not SANDBOX_URL. Two tables purporting to describe the same configuration that
    disagree on membership is the enumeration hazard in its purest form - a reader consulting the second
    concludes the variable does not exist. The fix is probably to delete the second table and link to the
    first rather than to sync them, since syncing guarantees they diverge again. Not filed.
98. TWO SANDBOX PATHS DEREFERENCE self._sandbox WITH NO HANDLER FOR A CONSTRUCTION FAILURE, as of 6um.
    genetics-mcp-server tools/executor.py read_artifact (~5782) and _fetch_analysis_images (~6274) touch
    the cached_property directly; only run_analysis gained an `except SandboxNotConfigured`. So with
    SANDBOX_ENABLED=true AND SANDBOX_URL unset, those two would propagate a raw exception instead of the
    shaped, non-retryable operator error run_analysis now returns.
    LATENT BY CONSTRUCTION AFTER 6um: in the cluster k8s/deployments/chat-backend.yaml now sets
    SANDBOX_URL, and in the disabled configuration run_analysis is removed from the tool list while
    read_artifact returns not_found before touching _sandbox (the artifact manifest is empty because no
    execution ever ran). It requires a hand-broken configuration - enabled, with the address deleted.
    Not a bead. If a third caller of _sandbox is ever added, give the property itself the shaped-error
    behaviour rather than adding a fourth handler.

    --- SUPERSEDED IN PART, 2026-08-26, by 6um's fix round (genetics-mcp-server d9c0d7e). ---
    read_artifact NO LONGER dereferences the cached_property directly: both it and run_analysis now go
    through ToolExecutor._sandbox_or_operator_error, which catches SandboxNotConfigured by name and
    returns the shaped non-retryable operator error. The advice above - "give the property itself the
    shaped-error behaviour rather than adding a fourth handler" - is what was done, via a guarded accessor
    beside the property (a cached_property cannot itself return a shaped error, since callers await a
    client off it). _fetch_analysis_images remains unguarded and remains SAFE, because it runs only after
    a successful _sandbox.execute() has already populated the cache.
    WHAT SURVIVES AS A NOTE: any FUTURE caller of self._sandbox must go through the accessor, not the
    property. There is nothing that enforces this.
99. TWO PRE-EXISTING ruff ERRORS IN genetics-mcp-server, unrelated to any bead in this batch and left
    alone: F601 duplicate "pairs" key at src/genetics_mcp_server/scripts/pairwise_judge.py:741, and I001
    unsorted imports at tests/test_pairwise_judge.py:10. `ruff format --check` would additionally reformat
    much of tools/executor.py for long-standing reasons. Recorded rather than filed - fix opportunistically
    in whatever cycle next touches those files. The duplicate dict key is the one with actual behaviour
    behind it: the second "pairs" silently wins.

100. genetics-mcp-server db/chat_history_db.py `get_messages(session_id)` TAKES NO USER TERM and is safe
     only by CALL-SITE DISCIPLINE - every route calls get_session/get_session_for_access first, and those
     do carry `AND user_id = ?`. Established while auditing genetics-results-suite-dh3, whose whole defect
     was a lookup keyed on a session id with no owner term. This is the same SHAPE and is currently
     harmless, which is exactly why it is worth writing down: the protection lives in the callers, not in
     the function, and nothing enforces that a future caller repeats it.
     Not a bead - no reachable defect today, and the audit of every existing route came back clean (that
     audit is recorded in dh3's close reason). If a new route ever reads messages, give the function the
     user term rather than trusting the pattern to be noticed.
101. THE _ArtifactManifests BOUNDS PROSE STILL DESCRIBES THE OLD KEY. After dh3 the map is keyed on
     (sub, sid), but the long bounds discussion still calls _MAX_SESSIONS = 512 "an LRU cap on
     concurrently active chat sessions". It is now a cap on (user, session) PAIRS - which is the more
     conservative reading, so no arithmetic in that paragraph is wrong, but the noun is. The class's
     opening and key paragraphs were updated by dh3; this longer passage was left alone as out of scope.
     Fix opportunistically. Doc wording, not a behaviour claim.

102. THE ARTIFACT MANIFEST'S LRU IS REFRESHED BY WRITES ONLY, NEVER BY READS, so a manifest a user is
     actively reading can be evicted ahead of an idle one - and the eviction pressure comes from OTHER
     TENANTS' rows in a shared replicas:1 process. MEASURED during dh3's blind validation: record for user
     A, then 511 sessions for another user, then a successful resolve for A, then one more other-user
     session -> A's entry is gone despite the recent read, while the first attacker session survives.
     DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED. `record` calls move_to_end and `resolve` does not, which matches the class
     docstring's own framing ("LRU by last write"), so the behaviour is as documented rather than a
     divergence. The impact is AVAILABILITY ONLY - no misattribution, no cross-user read - and it is
     throughput-bounded, because every row costs a real serialized sandbox execution. A one-line
     move_to_end in resolve would make it least-recently-USED, which is the fairer reading; do it if
     multi-tenant eviction is ever observed to bite, not before.
103. TWO CLIENT-CONTROLLED TERMS FEED THE ARTIFACT MAP AND ONLY ONE IS BOUNDED, noted during dh3's blind
     validation. record() caps ROWS but not NAMES PER ROW - a probe stored 200,000 names in one row, the
     only real bound being the supervisor's ARTIFACT_ENTRY_BUDGET = 1024 on the far side of an HTTP
     boundary (the docstring admits record() "puts no cap of its own"). Both are throughput-bounded by one
     execution per row, so this is an observation about WHERE THE BOUND ACTUALLY LIVES rather than a
     demonstrated exhaustion. The session_id half was bounded as part of dh3's fix round; the names-per-row
     half was not, and is left as documented-but-unenforced-locally.

104. THE SIBLING configs/datasets.yaml COPIES ARE GITIGNORED, so "check whether those copies need
     regenerating" has a simpler answer than it looks and nobody should spend a cycle on it again.
     MEASURED 2026-08-26: genetics-results-db .gitignore:39 and genetics-results-api .gitignore:186 both
     ignore configs/datasets.yaml. The copies are LOCAL DEV ARTIFACTS, not committed generated files, so a
     change to the canonical creates NO cross-repo commit obligation - only a local refresh so a dev stack
     running out of those trees sees the new file.
     CLAUDE.md's cross-repo rule ("sibling repos hold generated copies - when you change it, check whether
     those copies need regenerating") is still right, but the check terminates at "they are ignored, copy
     them locally if you are running that service, and commit nothing".
     THE TRAP WORTH REMEMBERING: scripts/sync-datasets.sh deliberately resolves siblings next to the MAIN
     checkout and NEVER next to a worktree - its header says so and cites genetics-results-suite-e47. So
     running it FROM a worktree writes into the main checkouts, which are on a different branch. Copy into
     the sibling WORKTREES by hand instead when working on a branch; do not run the script for that.
     An agent reporting "the sibling copies need regenerating" after a datasets.yaml change is reporting
     something true-sounding and operationally empty. That happened on 4h6/dwp's doc pass.

105. THE BROWSER TEST SUITE HAS ~30 PRE-EXISTING FAILURES FROM AN msw/ENVIRONMENT BREAKAGE, and anyone
     running it will otherwise think they caused them. Observed 2026-08-26 while landing
     genetics-results-suite-r0v: full `npx vitest run` gives roughly 34 passed / 4 failed FILES and
     360 passed / 30 failed TESTS, every failure an `AxiosError: Network Error` from the msw interceptor,
     in src/test/msw/msw.test.ts, src/features/gene/GeneEvidenceTab.test.tsx,
     src/features/phenoSearch/PhenotypeSearchContainer.test.tsx and src/store/serverQuery.test.tsx.
     THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT SETTLES IT CHEAPLY: msw's OWN self-test fails on its own "supports per-test
     handler overrides" case. If msw cannot pass its own baseline, the other failures are environmental.
     Run `npx vitest run src/test/msw/msw.test.ts` before blaming a change.
     Not filed as work: it is a test-environment problem, nobody has asked for it, and no shipped
     behaviour depends on it. Worth fixing whenever someone next needs a trustworthy full browser run -
     at which point it becomes real work rather than a note.
     ALSO NOTE `npx tsc --noEmit` IS clean and there is NO lint script in package.json (scripts are dev,
     build, serve, typecheck, bff*, test*, e2e*), so "run the linter" has no meaning in that repo.
106. THE PHENOTYPE-PAGE CHAT SPANS PHENOCODES BY DESIGN, and r0v deliberately did not change that.
     <LLMChat> is not keyed on the phenocode there, so switching phenotype keeps the message list - and
     after r0v it keeps the session id too, which is the consistent choice: the conversation boundary is
     the message list, and the id now tracks it exactly. A new id is minted on mount and on a failed load
     (that branch unmounts the chat and discards its messages).
     IF A FRESH CONVERSATION PER PHENOCODE IS WANTED, that is a PRODUCT decision, not a defect: key
     <LLMChat> on the phenocode and mint a new uuid alongside. Recorded so the current behaviour reads as
     a choice rather than an oversight.

title: pairwise_judge's summary dict has the key "pairs" twice, so the deliberately-narrow per-pair list is discarded and the wide one ships in every report
description:
FOUND 2026-08-24 by ruff during the 4h6.79/.78 review, in code that cycle did not touch. VERIFIED FROM
THE SOURCE by the orchestrator rather than relayed - the reviewer reported it as "F601 duplicate dict key,
a real bug", and it is, but the interesting part is not the lint.

THE DEFECT: genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/scripts/pairwise_judge.py, `summarize_verdicts`
returns ONE dict literal containing the key "pairs" TWICE - at :627 and again at :741. Python keeps the
LAST, so :627's value is constructed and silently thrown away.
    $ uv run ruff check src/genetics_mcp_server/scripts/pairwise_judge.py
    F601 Dictionary key literal `"pairs"` repeated  --> pairwise_judge.py:741:9

WHAT IS LOST, AND WHY IT IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THE AUTHOR INTENDED:
:627 is a DELIBERATELY NARROW per-pair list - case_id, turn_index, outcome, winner, margin,
arm_identifiable - under a comment that states the design in as many words: "Kept deliberately narrow -
the judge's prose `reason` and the raw passes stay out, since this rides inside every saved report."
:741 is `[asdict(v) for v in verdicts]`, i.e. the ENTIRE PairVerdict dataclass - including precisely the
prose `reason` and the raw passes the comment says must stay out.
So the key that wins is the one the design excludes. Every saved report carries the judge's full prose
reasoning and raw pass data. The comment at :621-626 describes behaviour the file does not have.

THE RESULTS ARE NOT CORRUPTED. Every aggregate (wins, ties, sign test, bias diagnostics) is computed from
`verdicts` directly, not from this dict, so no benchmark number is wrong. The cost is report size and a
design intent silently inverted.

DO NOT "FIX" THIS BY DELETING :741 - THAT BREAKS THREE DOWNSTREAM READERS. `summary["pairs"]` is consumed
at :871 and :874 as `p["input_tokens"] for pair in summary["pairs"] for p in pair["passes"]`, and again at
:1050. `passes` exists ONLY on the asdict form, so those readers work today BECAUSE the wide version won.
Deleting the wide one turns a silent design inversion into a KeyError.
THE FIX IS A NAMING DECISION, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A BEAD AND NOT A LINT AUTOFIX: decide which of the two
shapes each consumer wants, give them distinct keys (e.g. "pairs" narrow for the saved report and
"pairs_detail"/"passes" wide for the token accounting), and update :871, :874 and :1050 to the right one.
Check whether any saved report on disk is read back by field name before renaming.

ICED. The user stated 2026-08-22 that the first benchmark set is done and benchmarking need not be taken
into account, so nothing on genetics-results-suite-4h6's frontier depends on this. It is filed so the
analysis is not re-derived, not because there is work to schedule.
Note also tests/test_pairwise_judge.py:10 has a pre-existing ruff I001 (import sorting) - trivial, fix it
in the same pass if this is ever picked up.

title: Supervisor: the response write has no deadline, so a peer that stops ACKing parks a handler thread for ~tcp_retries2 (~15 min)
description:
FOUND 2026-08-22 by the blind validation of genetics-results-suite-4h6.57. DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT OF SCOPE
of that cycle by an orchestrator ruling, and ICED because 4h6.57's drain ceiling closes the acute failure
this enabled. Filed so the number is not lost.

THE DEFECT: THE RESPONSE WRITE HAS NO DEADLINE. `_send_json` does `self.wfile.write(body)` on a connection
deliberately left at `settimeout(None)` - both `_HeaderBoundedReader._read_head`'s finally and
`_read_body`'s finally restore blocking mode. `wbufsize = 0`, so `wfile` is socketserver's `_SocketWriter`
doing a blocking `sock.sendall`. EVERY READ PATH GOT A DEADLINE IN 4h6.58; THE WRITE PATH NEVER DID.
That asymmetry is already stated as a residual in docs/code-execution-security.md and docs/project-spec.md
("Every read off the socket has a deadline - the response write has none").

THE NUMBER, and it is why this is filed rather than merely recorded: a peer that stops ACKing blocks even a
292-BYTE sendall for tcp_retries2 (=15 on the dev host), i.e. ROUGHLY 15 MINUTES, for an ordinary single
response. That needs no malice and no pipelining - node loss, a torn-down netns, or a conntrack drop
mid-response all produce it. Each occurrence parks one handler thread for that whole period, and nothing
caps concurrent handler threads (ThreadingHTTPServer, daemon_threads, one thread per connection).

WHY IT IS NOT URGENT: 4h6.57 gave the shutdown gate a hard ceiling, so a stalled write can no longer
prevent the process from exiting - the acute regression is closed. What remains is a resource hold, which
compounds with the already-documented "these bound duration, not count" residual from 4h6.58.

FIX SHAPE: arm `self.connection.settimeout(...)` around the write in `_send_json` the way `_read_body` does
for the read, and restore it in a finally. THE CARE NEEDED, and it is why this was not done inline:
- a socket timeout mid-`sendall` leaves a PARTIALLY WRITTEN response, so the connection must be closed
  rather than kept alive, and the handler must not then try to write an error onto the same socket;
- `_send_json` currently has `send_response()` and `end_headers()` OUTSIDE its try/except OSError and only
  `wfile.write(body)` inside, so the arming has to cover the header flush too - the measured hang in the
  4h6.57 validation was in `flush_headers`, NOT in the body write;
- `_read_body`'s finally already does settimeout(None); anything armed here must not be left behind for the
  next request on a kept-alive connection. That exact trap is documented on 4h6.58.

RELATED ASYMMETRY WORTH KNOWING WHEN THIS IS WORKED: the 400 from parse_execute_request does NOT set
close_connection, while the 415/413/408/503 paths do. That is what let blind validation accumulate 20000
pipelined replies on one socket. Bounded now by the drain ceiling, but it means a single connection can
still queue an unbounded number of unread responses.

title: Three keycloak-*.sh scripts hardcode the production issuer/audience as a default, stamping production values into a staging realm
description:
FOUND 2026-08-22 by the review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.93, and CORRECTED by the orchestrator before
filing - the finder's version said these scripts act "against production", which is not what they do. Read
the correction below before acting, because it changes both the severity and the fix.

THREE SCRIPTS HARDCODE THE PRODUCTION HOST AS A DEFAULT (all verified by grep 2026-08-22):
    scripts/keycloak-register-client.sh:50-51
        OAUTH_RESOURCE_URL="${OAUTH_RESOURCE_URL:-https://genegenie.broadinstitute.org/mcp}"
        OAUTH_ISSUER="${OAUTH_ISSUER:-https://genegenie.broadinstitute.org/auth/realms/genetics}"
    scripts/keycloak-register-brainzzz.sh:24  (OAUTH_RESOURCE_URL, same value; :119 prints both bare)
    scripts/keycloak-get-token.sh:29          (OAUTH_ISSUER, same value)

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO, stated first because the finder got this wrong and the wrong version is alarming:
IT DOES NOT MUTATE PRODUCTION. These scripts do NOT reach Keycloak over the OAUTH_ISSUER URL. They reach
it by kubectl - keycloak-register-client.sh:87-94 resolves the pod, reads keycloak-secrets, and runs
kcadm.sh via `kubectl exec`. So the TARGET is whatever the current kubectl CONTEXT points at, which for a
staging bring-up is correctly staging. keycloak-get-token.sh is the exception in the other direction: it
curls OAUTH_ISSUER directly, so run against staging without an override it drives a PRODUCTION login and
returns a PRODUCTION token. That is confusing rather than dangerous - it is the operator's own token.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES, and this is the defect: it writes the PRODUCTION audience and issuer INTO THE
STAGING REALM. Register a client during staging bring-up without setting the two variables and the
mcp-audience mapper carries aud=https://genegenie.broadinstitute.org/mcp. Staging's mcp-server checks the
audience, so staging logins fail - and they fail with an audience error pointing at a hostname that looks
correct, which is the worst possible symptom to debug.
NOT A CROSS-ENVIRONMENT AUTH BYPASS: a staging-issued token carrying the production audience is signed by
STAGING's realm keys, so production rejects the signature regardless of what the aud claim says.

WHY IT IS ICED RATHER THAN FILED AS WORK: nothing on the epic's frontier depends on it, and the cheap
mitigation is a documentation line rather than a code change. It becomes live the moment somebody works
the daly-staging bring-up checklist in docs/environments.md, which is why it is recorded on
genetics-results-suite-4h6.50 as well.

FIX SHAPE WHEN SOMEBODY DOES WANT IT, cheapest first:
(a) name the two overrides explicitly in docs/environments.md's "Bringing up daly-staging" checklist.
    Nearly free, and the checklist is where the person actually is. CLAUDE.md's doc-ownership table maps
    scripts/keycloak-*.sh to docs/keycloak-apple-signin.md AND docs/mcp-oauth-onboarding.md, so those two
    need the same treatment in the same commit.
(b) derive the defaults from DEPLOY_ENV / DOMAIN the way scripts/deploy.sh does (scripts/lib/env.sh knows
    daly, daly-staging, finngen) instead of hardcoding one environment's hostname.
(c) refuse to run when the kubectl context and the OAUTH_ISSUER host disagree. That is the only option
    that makes the class impossible rather than merely documented, and it is the most work.

THE GENERAL SHAPE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE INSTANCE: staging and production now differ by a single
character in a shared suffix (staging.genegenie... vs genegenie...), so every hardcoded production default
in this repo is newly easy to mistake for correct by eye. These three are the ones that exist today - a
grep for `genegenie.broadinstitute.org` outside docs/ finds exactly these three files.

title: Every supervisor response pays a ~40ms delayed-ACK stall because _send_json issues two sendall calls with Nagle enabled
description:
FOUND 2026-08-20 by blind validation of genetics-results-suite-4h6.87, as a side observation while
establishing that .87's MSG_PEEK header reader costs nothing. IT IS NOT .87's DEFECT - it is PRE-EXISTING,
on the WRITE path, untouched by that change and arm-independent by construction (both arms measured the
same). Filed so the number is not lost, and ICED because nothing on the epic's frontier depends on it.

THE DEFECT: every response the supervisor writes pays a ~40ms DELAYED-ACK STALL, because _send_json does
TWO sendall() calls - headers, then body - and the production _Handler does NOT set
disable_nagle_algorithm. Nagle holds the second small write until the peer ACKs the first; the peer's ACK
is delayed ~40ms; the response lands ~40ms late.

MEASURED, production settings, GET /health:  ~41.0 ms per request.
For contrast, the same path with disable_nagle_algorithm set in both arms measures ~816us (peek) and
~785us (buffered) - which is why .87's benchmark table sets it: WITHOUT IT A 40ms STALL SWAMPS THE SIGNAL
AND BOTH ARMS MEASURE ~41,357us. That is a measurement trap, and it is also, it turns out, the production
behaviour.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND /health:
- The kubelet readiness probe pays it on every tick. It will not FAIL the probe (timeouts are far above
  40ms) so nothing is broken today - which is exactly why this is iced rather than filed as work.
- Every /execute RESPONSE pays it too.
- The artifact fetch path pays it PER ARTIFACT: genetics-mcp-server's _fetch_analysis_images fetches up to
  _MAX_ANALYSIS_IMAGES = 4 images SEQUENTIALLY, so a 4-image analysis adds ~160ms of pure stall.

THE FIX IS ALMOST CERTAINLY ONE OF:
(a) set `disable_nagle_algorithm = True` on _Handler - it is a StreamRequestHandler class attribute, so
    this is one line, and it is what the benchmark already does;
(b) make _send_json build ONE buffer (headers + body) and issue a single sendall, which fixes the cause
    rather than disabling the algorithm.
(b) is the better fix - Nagle exists for a reason and disabling it globally is a bigger hammer than the
    problem needs - but (a) is trivially safe. MEASURE before choosing; .87's benchmark harness is the
    right instrument and its trap is documented above.

DO NOT confuse this with 4h6.87. .87 is about request-body bytes reaching the supervisor's HEAP before the
readiness check; this is about response LATENCY on the write path. They share only the benchmark.

title: A FIFO planted under a listed artifact name blocks os.open before the regular-file check, hanging a handler thread forever
description:
FOUND by blind validation of genetics-results-suite-4h6.82 on 2026-08-20, while probing the new
artifact-integrity binding. It is PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by .82 - and .82 NARROWS it - but it is the
one artifact-read failure mode that neither .82 nor .88 bounds, so it is filed rather than left implicit.

THE DEFECT, MEASURED: a FIFO planted under a name the manifest LISTED hangs the request FOREVER.
sandbox/supervisor.py, in the artifact read path:
    os.open(name, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW, dir_fd=dfd)     # ~:987
blocks in open(2) waiting for a writer, BEFORE the fstat that would reject a non-regular file ever runs.
The S_ISREG check is there and is correct; it is simply downstream of the block.
MEASURED: the client timed out, /health stayed 200, AND THE HANDLER THREAD NEVER RETURNED. Repeat the
request and threads accumulate with nothing to reclaim them.

WHY IT IS STILL LIVE AFTER .82: .82's digest binding makes a PLANTED name 404 before the file is opened,
which kills the easy version of this. But a name that WAS in the manifest is opened first and verified
after - it has to be, the verify hashes the bytes that would be returned. So the attack survives as:
unlink a listed artifact, mkfifo in its place, and every read of that execution's artifact hangs a thread.
The digest check is never reached.

THE ATTACKER CLASS IS THE ONE 4h6.88 DOCUMENTS: any process at uid 65532 can write into any execution's
artifacts/. So this is not a new capability - it is a new CONSEQUENCE of that capability, and unlike the
read and overwrite consequences it is a liveness failure of the supervisor itself rather than a
confidentiality or integrity failure of one user's data.

WHY IT IS ICED AND NOT ON THE FRONTIER: nothing in the 4h6 epic's acceptance criteria depends on it,
4h6.88 already gates the multi-user deploy on the same-uid class as a whole, and the fix is not free to
get right - O_NONBLOCK on the open changes the semantics for regular files and needs care with the
subsequent read, and the alternative (fstatat before the open) reintroduces a TOCTOU the current
open-then-fstat ordering was chosen to avoid. That is a real design decision, not a mechanical fix.

CANDIDATE FIX, not validated: open with O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, fstat, reject non-regular, then
clear O_NONBLOCK with fcntl before reading. O_NONBLOCK on a FIFO with no writer returns immediately with
ENXIO for O_RDONLY, which is exactly the discrimination wanted, and it is a no-op for regular files. Needs
measuring, including what it does under gVisor.

RECORDED AT THE SITE TOO: the implementer of .82 was asked to leave a comment at supervisor.py:987 noting
the hazard, because the docstring five lines above it still claims "no FIFO to block the read on" - which
is measurably false and is what would mislead the next reader.

DO NOT close this by pointing at 4h6.88. .88 is the accept-or-fix bead for READING; this is a
denial-of-service against the supervisor's own thread pool and would survive any fix to .88 that did not
also change the open.

title: test-e2e-local.py's results-api log join is racy: it reads before the after-response access record lands
description:
FOUND running scripts/test-e2e-local.py on 2026-08-19 to clear the benchmark's precondition. 44/45 checks passed; this one failed, and it is a defect IN THE HARNESS, not in results-api or the sandbox. The data path it was trying to prove is proven by the checks either side of it.

WHAT FAILED: "join: results-api recorded the same jti and sid - 0 records with jti fe471183-b836-4be4-a61c-0ce91e866662" (scripts/test-e2e-local.py:665-666, api_log.records() filtered on jti).

WHY IT IS A RACE, ESTABLISHED NOT ARGUED. The record EXISTS. Read back out of ~/.cache/genetics-dev-stack/results-api.log after the run:
  {"timestamp": "2026-08-19T12:25:19.420369+00:00", "severity": "INFO", "logger": "app.middleware_usage_logging", "message": "endpoint access", ..., "status_code": 200, "duration_ms": 1299.86, "sid": "sess-e704e64f", "jti": "fe471183-..."}
Exactly one occurrence, right jti, right sid. So the assertion's subject was produced; the harness read before it landed.

THE ORDERING THAT CAUSES IT:
- results-api logs this line AFTER the response. app/middleware_usage_logging.py computes duration_ms at :95 (after call_next) and calls logger.info(entry) at :136. The record therefore cannot exist until after results-api has answered the SDK.
- The harness synchronises on CHAT-BACKEND's response, which is downstream of that: SDK gets its rows -> script finishes -> supervisor returns -> chat-backend returns -> harness reads the log. Every hop is a chance for the read to win.
- db-api's equivalent check PASSES for the structural reason, not by luck: api/main.py:133 logs "sandbox request authorized" at AUTH time, immediately after request.state.principal is set, i.e. BEFORE the response. It is always on disk by the time anything downstream observes the request.
- The "accounting" checks on the SAME subsystem also passed in the same run, because they drive the per-execution concurrency limit to 429 first, which does enough extra work to let the earlier write land.

SO THE CHECK IS RACY BY CONSTRUCTION, and it will fail intermittently on a fast machine or a quiet log. It is not flaky in the sense of "unclear cause".

WHY THIS IS NOT A results-api DEFECT: logging an access record after the response is correct - duration_ms and status_code do not exist before it. Nothing should change in results-api for this.

THE FIX IS IN THE HARNESS: give the results-api log join a bounded wait/retry (poll api_log.records() for the jti for ~2-3s before failing) rather than a single read. Do NOT paper over it by asserting on db-api alone - the results-api join is the half that proves the sandbox token was attributable at the OTHER backend, which is the whole point of the check.

DO NOT confuse this with genetics-results-suite-4h6.65, which is about results-api's sandbox logging DROPPING Rejection.code and the user. Different defect, same subsystem: .65 is about fields that are never emitted; this is about a field that is emitted and read too early. Verified here that jti IS emitted on both the success path ("endpoint access", 17 lines carry jti) and the limit path ("sandbox per-execution limit exceeded", 16 lines).

ICED, per the filing gate: it blocks nothing on the epic's frontier. The benchmark's precondition is "the sandbox is reachable and attributable end to end", and that is established by the 44 passing checks - including both the accounting checks that prove results-api admitted the sandbox principal from the per-execution map, and the db-api join. Un-defer this when someone next touches test-e2e-local.py, or when the intermittency wastes a debugging session.

title: The phenotype-page embedded chat has no session at all, so run_analysis can never work there
description:
Found while fixing genetics-results-suite-vda. PhenotypeContainer.tsx renders <LLMChat> with no sessionId, no onEnsureSession and no persistence callbacks — it is an ephemeral chat. So every turn there sends session_id: null, and ToolExecutor.run_analysis refuses all of them with 'Code execution is not available in this context: no authenticated session.' Unlike vda this is not a first-turn race: it is permanent for that surface.

Reachable because the tool-profile selector lives inside LLMChat's options, so a user on a phenotype page can pick 'Code execution' and then hit a wall that never clears.

NOT FIXED as part of vda because the right answer is a decision, not a mechanical change:
- mint a client-side uuid per conversation, exactly as secret chats already do (ChatPage.tsx ~307, crypto.randomUUID) — the backend only needs a string for the sid claim and the logs; nothing there is persisted anyway. Cheapest, and consistent with an existing precedent.
- create a real session for the phenotype chat, which changes it from ephemeral to persisted and would start showing up in the session list.
- hide the code-execution profile on surfaces with no session, so the failure is not offered rather than not explained.

Files: genetics-results-browser/src/features/phenotype/PhenotypeContainer.tsx, src/features/chat/LLMChat.tsx.
close_reason:
LANDED. genetics-results-browser 7657b3b. No fix round needed.

TOOK OPTION 1 - mint a client-side uuid per conversation, as secret chats already do. Option 2 (a real
session) would turn an ephemeral surface into a persisted one appearing in the session list, which is a
product change nobody asked for; option 3 (hide the profile) removes the capability instead of delivering
it.

THE SAFETY QUESTION WAS PROBED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because "let the client choose the session id" is the
kind of thing that deserves a look before shipping. Two findings:
1. It is already the shipped precedent. session_id is client-supplied on EVERY surface - the backend does
   no ownership or existence check and treats a secret chat's crypto.randomUUID identically to a persisted
   id. Minting one here adds no new capability and no new guessable surface: a uuid4 is at least as
   unguessable as a persisted session row id, which is itself a server-minted str(uuid.uuid4()).
2. THE PROBE TURNED UP A REAL PRE-EXISTING HOLE ON THE WAY, which is the more valuable outcome: artifact
   read-back was authorized by that client-supplied session id ALONE, with no user term. Filed as
   genetics-results-suite-dh3, fixed and closed the same day (mcp-server 4dcfbb5) - artifacts are now
   keyed on (sub, sid) and read_artifact carries the same gateway-assertion gate run_analysis has. So the
   ordering worked out: the hole was closed BEFORE this bead widened the set of surfaces that mint ids.
   r0v did not cause it and was not blocked by it.
The 36-character uuid also fits the max_length=64 that dh3's fix round put on session_id.

onEnsureSession WAS NOT NEEDED and is not wired - established by reading LLMChat rather than assuming.
It resolves the turn id as `sessionId ?? null` and calls onEnsureSession only when that is falsy, so with a
non-null sessionId it can never fire. Same short-circuit ChatPage relies on for secret chats, and an
existing test already pins it.

SCOPE HELD: no persistence callbacks, no history save, no session-list entry. The surface stays ephemeral,
which is what it was.

ONE BEHAVIOUR LEFT DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED, recorded on 4h6.98 item 106: switching phenocode keeps both the
message list and the session id, because <LLMChat> is not keyed on the phenocode there. That is
pre-existing and now self-consistent - the conversation boundary is the message list and the id tracks it.
A fresh conversation per phenocode is a PRODUCT call, not a defect.

VERIFICATION: tsc --noEmit clean; src/features/phenotype passes; new test drives the real container
through two turns and asserts both request bodies carry the same uuid-shaped session_id.
THE FULL BROWSER SUITE HAS ~30 PRE-EXISTING FAILURES and they are not this change - every one is an
AxiosError: Network Error from the msw interceptor, and msw's OWN self-test fails all three of its own
cases the same way. That diagnostic is recorded on 4h6.98 item 105 so the next person does not spend a
cycle on it.

title: Syntax-highlight the expanded run_analysis script in the chat transcript
description:
genetics-results-suite-inp shipped the collapsible tool-call disclosure with the full script rendered as plain monospace in a <pre>. The option the user picked said 'syntax highlighted'; that part was deliberately NOT done because genetics-results-browser has no highlighter dependency today (checked: no react-syntax-highlighter, prism, shiki or highlight.js in package.json, and nothing in src/ highlights anything) and adding one is a bundle-size decision that is the user's, not a side effect of a display fix.

Options, cheapest first:
- rehype-highlight + a highlight.js theme, reusing the ReactMarkdown pipeline already in LLMChat.tsx (remarkGfm + rehypePlugins are wired) by rendering the code through a fenced block instead of a raw <pre>. Smallest delta, ships a CSS theme that must work in both MUI light and dark.
- react-syntax-highlighter with the light build and only the python language registered.
- a hand-rolled Python tokenizer, ~80 lines, no dependency. Ugly but zero bundle cost.

Files: genetics-results-browser/src/features/chat/ToolCallDisclosure.tsx, package.json.
notes:
--- PARKED 2026-08-26, awaiting a USER DECISION. Not blocked by any bead; blocked by a person. ---
This bead cannot be executed autonomously and should not be. Its own description says the syntax-
highlighting was deliberately left out of genetics-results-suite-inp because "adding one is a bundle-size
decision that is the user's, not a side effect of a display fix". That reasoning has not changed, and an
agent picking a frontend dependency on the user's behalf is exactly what it warns against.

THE DECISION NEEDED, and it is only the first one - the rest follows mechanically:
  (a) rehype-highlight + a highlight.js theme, reusing the ReactMarkdown pipeline already wired in
      LLMChat.tsx (remarkGfm + rehypePlugins), rendering the script through a fenced block instead of a
      raw <pre>. Smallest code delta. Ships a CSS theme that must be made to work in BOTH MUI light and
      dark, which is the part that will take the time.
  (b) react-syntax-highlighter, light build, Python only registered. Bigger dependency, less theming work.
  (c) a hand-rolled ~80-line Python tokenizer. Zero bundle cost, ugly, and one more thing to maintain.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS READY: the user picking one, OR stating a bundle-size budget that decides it.
Until then `bd ready` should not be offering it, which is why it is parked rather than left open.

Files when it does run: genetics-results-browser src/features/chat/ToolCallDisclosure.tsx, package.json.
NOTE the current state is not broken - inp shipped the collapsible disclosure and the full script IS
rendered, just as plain monospace. This is a polish bead, not a defect.

title: The rag surface keeps pseudo-credible-set science but not the membership and re-query rules, on an unstated distinction
description:
FOUND by the re-review of the genetics-results-suite-4h6.17/.69 fix round (2026-08-18). VERIFIED by rendering the `rag` profile. LOW severity: `rag` is not an arm of the genetics-results-suite-4h6.23 A/B, and nothing here is wrong for a user.

The fix round established the rule "science and grounding go in blocks that name no tool; only the 'which tool' clause is gated". Applied to the credible-set material it produced a split that is DEFENSIBLE BUT UNWRITTEN:
- `rag` KEEPS `## Data Sources and Resource Names` and `### Pseudo Credible Sets` - roughly 2 KB covering the labelling obligation ("not statistically fine-mapped", "always tell the user explicitly"), the r2 membership criteria and the PIP-caution rule.
- `rag` LOSES the Membership and Re-query rules, which are gated on having a data path.

Both are credible-set grounding. The implicit distinction is that the LABELLING obligation applies whenever the model PRESENTS such data (which a RAG surface can do from retrieved documents), while the MEMBERSHIP rules require ROWS the surface cannot fetch. That is a real and sensible line - it just exists nowhere in the code or the docs, so the next person to touch these blocks will not know which side a new sentence belongs on and will place it by feel.

WHAT TO DO: write the rule down where `_Block` documents the other gating rules, and check the existing blocks against it once. If the distinction does not actually hold for some sentence currently on the `rag` side, move it.

Do NOT let this turn into a rewrite of the credible-set sections; the science content was verified correct on every arm-bearing surface in the same review.
close_reason:
LANDED. genetics-mcp-server 2fd1b88 + genetics-results-suite 70a721e. Ran as ONE cycle with 4h6.78
because both deliver prose in the SAME _Block docstring paragraph; running them separately would have
collided, and 78 alone would have been a full round for one comment.

THE DELIVERABLE: three numbered rules now live in _Block's docstring - the top of the file every prompt
block is written in, which is the only place the audience for them looks. Rule 3 is this bead's:
gate on what a rule NEEDS, not on what it is ABOUT. The distinction had existed only as a comment in a
TEST (tests/test_system_prompt.py:442, "these presuppose a path to credible-set / MHC rows, which `rag`
does not have"), where the person writing prompt text would never meet it.

THE CHECK THE BEAD ASKED FOR, DONE ONCE: NO MOVE NEEDED. Rendered `rag` and read the whole
`## Data Sources and Resource Names` + `### Pseudo Credible Sets` region against the rule.
- Ungated and correctly so: the labelling duty, "approximate credible sets built around a lead variant",
  the FinnGen-LD-panel fact, the r2 membership CRITERIA, the PIP assignment, the filters, the PIP-caution
  distinction. All are construction facts and PRESENTATION obligations - a rag surface presenting a
  retrieved pseudo credible set obeys every one without fetching a row.
- Gated and correctly so: "Membership is NOT the same as LD ... ONLY if returned by
  get_credible_set_by_id / appears in credible_sets_v" (meaningless with no authoritative list to defer
  to), "Re-query; do not answer from memory", and the MHC/pval/info row-reading rules.
ONE BORDERLINE CASE EXAMINED AND DELIBERATELY LEFT: the list_datasets-gated provenance paragraph offers
"or by re-querying it" as the SECOND of two routes. The rule decides it via the word ONLY - a rule that
can ONLY be carried out by fetching is gated - and the primary route (read dataset_id/resource off the
result) works on rag, so moving the paragraph would strip a presentation obligation from that surface.
REVIEW'S CAVEAT, RECORDED HONESTLY: the whole decision for a MULTI-ROUTE rule rests on that one adverb,
and the docstring does not state the multi-route case explicitly. A careful reader gets there; a hurried
one may still place by feel. Judged not worth a fourth rule; if a second multi-route case ever appears,
add "if ANY route is obeyable without rows the rule stays ungated; split the row-needing clause into its
own block".

VALIDATION: review confirmed all seven checkable claims, including by RENDERING rather than reading -
prompt sizes re-derived and matching (unfiltered 35,420; None 29,112; api 29,109; bigquery 26,098;
rag 19,515; code 21,715), and the diff confirmed docstring-only with no block text, no gating field and
no rendered output changed. The docstring became an r""" string; verified the pre-existing body contained
no backslash, so the prefix is a no-op for it and REQUIRED for the new text (\w, \b).

TWO FIX ROUNDS USED, both finding something real, and the second found the worse defect - see 4h6.78's
close reason for the full list. Tests 1940 -> 1959 passed, 74 deselected.

title: The prompt gate and its test tokeniser both miss plural and suffixed tool-name forms
description:
FOUND independently by the sighted review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.17/.69 (2026-08-18). LATENT - no live instance today, verified by dumping every identifier-shaped token in the full prompt and checking it against the tool registry.

The gate matches `(?<!\w)NAME\b`, so a mention written as a plural or with a suffix - `get_hla_by_alleles` for `get_hla_by_allele`, or a pluralised bare mention - is NOT seen as a mention. Neither is it seen by test_system_prompt.py's independent tokeniser, which intersects tokens against the registry.

CONSEQUENCE IF ONE IS EVER WRITTEN: a block referring to a tool in a plural form is emitted on surfaces that do not have it, which is exactly the bug 4h6.69 was filed for - and the test cannot catch it, because the test's independence is on the ALGORITHM (tokenise-then-intersect vs per-name regex) and not on the NORMALISATION, which both share.

That shared blind spot is the point: two independent implementations of the same wrong normalisation agree with each other. Worth one line in `_Block`'s docstring at minimum, so the next person writing prompt text knows to name tools exactly.

RELATED STRUCTURAL SHARP EDGE, same file, also latent: a tool named only inside a PROHIBITION still gates its block POSITIVELY. The 4h6.17/.69 fix cycle resolved the live instance of this (the HLA block, where `get_summary_stats` appeared only in a negation), but the general property remains - remove a tool from a surface and any block that merely warns against that tool disappears along with whatever else it carries. Document it next to the plural caveat.
notes:
--- MERGED INTO THE 4h6.79 CYCLE, 2026-08-22. NOT a duplicate - the defects are different, the DELIVERABLE
