title: Nothing structurally guarantees chat_api resolves the same tool set for the prompt and for the model
description:
FOUND by the sighted review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.17/.69 (2026-08-18), deferred from that cycle as a hardening rather than a defect. Nothing is broken today.

genetics-results-suite-4h6.69's headline claim is that the prompt and the tool list can no longer drift apart. As shipped, that holds ONLY BECAUSE chat_api.py happens to pass the same `request.tool_profile` and `request.enable_tools` to BOTH `service.resolve_local_tool_names(...)` and `stream_chat(...)`. There is no shared object, no post-hoc assertion, and no test that pins the two call sites together.

SO A FUTURE EDIT THAT CHANGES ONE CALL SITE AND NOT THE OTHER REINSTATES 4h6.69 WITH THE ENTIRE SUITE GREEN - including the new test_system_prompt.py, which verifies the prompt against a tool set IT resolves itself rather than against the set the model was actually handed. The one test that crosses the boundary end-to-end (test_chat_api.py's profile test) would also pass, because it drives both sides from the same request.

FIX SHAPE, cheapest first:
(a) have `stream_chat` ACCEPT the already-resolved tool-name set instead of re-deriving it from the profile - one resolution, one source, the class removed rather than detected;
(b) failing that, assert in chat_api that the two resolutions are equal, and test that the assertion fires.
(a) is preferable: it deletes the second derivation rather than checking it.

NOTE THE ASYMMETRY THAT MAKES THIS WORTH DOING: the prompt is a function of the tool set, so a drift does not raise - it silently produces a model told about tools it does not have, or given tools nothing told it about. That is precisely the failure 4h6.69 was filed for, and it is invisible without a structural guard.
close_reason:
LANDED. genetics-mcp-server 4791569 (+ spec repo 54158dc for the doc). Batched with 4h6.75/.76 as one
commit; file-disjoint from them, so they ran concurrently.

STRUCTURAL FIX, NOT AN ASSERTION - and that was the ruling. An assertion is a DETECTOR; this bead exists
because a convention was mistaken for a guarantee, so a detector would have preserved the mistake in a
louder form. ResolvedLocalTools is a frozen dataclass holding `definitions` only, with `names` a COMPUTED
PROPERTY, so no object can exist whose names describe a different tool set than the one it carries.
chat_api resolves ONCE, builds the prompt from .names, and hands THE SAME OBJECT to stream_chat ->
_stream_anthropic. The second get_anthropic_tools call is DELETED - one call site remains, and the
local_tools=None fallback funnels through that same one, so it is one derivation rather than a
reintroduction.
THE list() COPY AT THE HAND-OFF IS LOAD-BEARING, measured: without it the external/RAG .extend() mutates
the caller's list and .names moves from 1 name to 3 AFTER the prompt was built.
resolve_local_tool_names survives as a one-line delegate - /chat/v1/tool-names still calls it.

THE TOLERANT FAKE HID A REAL BREAK, exactly as the brief warned. tests/test_chat_api.py's _CapturingService
stubbed resolve_local_tool_names, which the refactored endpoint no longer calls, so it would have
AttributeError'd at runtime while a **kwargs fake sailed past. Found by checking every real call site by
hand, not by the suite. WHEN A REFACTOR MOVES A BOUNDARY, THE **kwargs FAKES ARE WHERE THE BREAK HIDES.

TESTS 1889 -> 1892 for this bead (1940 with .75/.76). THE RECORDED BASELINE WAS 570 - stale by a factor of
three; see e8e item 42. Measure before starting.
The new test was verified decisive by restoring the pre-fix shape. Note the honest qualification the
reviewer added: "2 of 3 failed" is only reachable by reverting the call sites while KEEPING the dataclass -
a true pre-fix tree fails all three at collection - and one of the three is a tautology over dataclass
semantics, legitimate for its stated purpose but not evidence the derivation is single.

TWO LATENT ARGUMENT-DROPPING HAZARDS, recorded as comments AT THE SITE rather than as beads, per the filing
gate: custom_tool_descriptions is consulted only on the local_tools=None fallback, and a differing
enable_tools would give external+RAG tools with zero local ones. NEITHER IS LIVE - chat_api passes
request.enable_tools to both, and routers/llm_config.py:509 already records that nothing loads custom
descriptions into the chat path. The correct fix if either is ever wired in is stated at the site: pass
them to resolve_local_tools, which already accepts them, NOT to stream_chat.

MY OWN ERROR IN THIS CYCLE: I relayed a reviewer's citation (docs/project-spec.md:1296) without checking
it. The text is in docs/chat-tool-reference.md:276; project-spec.md:1296 is monitor-CronJob content. The
fix agent refused to edit a file that did not contain the quoted text rather than finding something nearby
to change - the right failure mode, and the reason nothing wrong landed.

title: The bigquery prompt forbids querying the database for consequence/AF/rsID but the block naming where they DO come from is gated away
description:
FOUND by the BLIND validator of genetics-results-suite-4h6.17/.69 (2026-08-18), deferred from that cycle. VERIFIED by rendering the `bigquery` profile.

The `bigquery` surface receives the block saying NEVER to query the database for consequence, allele frequency, rsID or pathogenicity. The block that names where those DO come from is gated on `get_variant_annotations` / `get_myvariant_annotations`, neither of which is in the `bigquery` profile, so it is dropped.

RESULT: a dead end. The model is told what not to do and is given no redirect - the prohibition survives while its remedy does not. The likely failure mode is not a wrong answer but an unnecessary refusal, or an improvised query against the very columns it was told not to trust.

This is the same defect class as the over-subtraction fixed in the 4h6.17/.69 cycle (a prohibition and its remedy separated by the gate), and the same fix shape applies: the prohibition is knowledge and should be ungated or given a per-surface variant naming a route the surface actually has - or, if `bigquery` genuinely has no route to annotation data, the prohibition should SAY SO rather than trailing off.

ESTABLISH FIRST, do not assume: whether the `bigquery` surface has ANY route to that data. If it does not, the honest text is "this surface cannot answer that; the data is not in the database", which is a different sentence from the one currently emitted.
notes:
--- WIDER THAN FILED. Established by probe 2026-08-22, by RENDERING the prompt per profile. ---
The bead names only `bigquery`. MEASURED: BOTH `bigquery` AND `code` get the prohibition
(defaults.py:325-329) and lose the remedy (defaults.py:330-333). The remedy's own TEXT names
get_variant_annotations / get_myvariant_annotations, so the text-level gate at defaults.py:554 drops it on
any profile lacking those tools - the requires_any is identical on both blocks, so the gate is not what
separates them.
AND THE HONEST WORDING IS NOT A REDIRECT: bigquery's 24 tools contain NEITHER annotation tool, so that
surface has NO ROUTE to consequence/AF/rsID at all. "This surface cannot answer that" is true; "use
get_variant_annotations instead" is not. `code`'s 7 tools need their own true sentence, not a shared one.
close_reason:
LANDED. genetics-mcp-server 4791569 (+ spec repo 54158dc). ONE fix round, and the fix round is the reason
this close reason is long: TWO SUCCESSIVE WORDINGS OF THE REMEDY WERE MEASURABLY FALSE.

THE DEFECT AS FILED, confirmed and WIDER: the prohibition ("NEVER query the database for consequence/AF/
rsID") is gated requires_any={query_database, run_analysis}; its remedy carried the IDENTICAL gate, but its
TEXT named get_variant_annotations / get_myvariant_annotations, so the TEXT-level gate at defaults.py:554
dropped it. Measured by rendering: BOTH `bigquery` AND `code` got the prohibition and lost the remedy. The
bead named only `bigquery`.

ERROR 1, MINE. I briefed the implementer that `bigquery` has NO ROUTE to these annotations. FALSE - its
resolved set contains run_analysis, and the SDK exposes genetics.variant_annotation(...). The probe's
finding ("bigquery's tools contain neither annotation tool") was TRUE BUT NARROW and I turned it into a
broader claim it did not support. The implementer caught it and shipped three gated variants instead of one.

ERROR 2, WHICH SURVIVED INTO THE FIRST IMPLEMENTATION. Its replacement wording said "there is no
variant-annotation tool on this surface". ALSO FALSE: `bigquery` has get_variant_protein_effect, and THE
SAME RENDERED PROMPT describes it as returning "curated UniProt/ClinVar annotation (disease, clinical
significance, population frequency, rsID)". So the block instructed the model to REFUSE what the prompt
above it explained HOW TO GET - and it fired on exactly one shape: `bigquery` with SANDBOX_ENABLED=false,
which is what k8s/deployments/chat-backend.yaml declares TODAY. UNNECESSARY REFUSAL IS THE EXACT FAILURE
THIS BEAD WAS FILED AGAINST, so the first fix would have shipped an inverted version of the bug.
The implementer's defence - "no variant-annotation TOOL" vs "no tool RETURNS them" - does not survive
contact with the prompt, which itself calls that tool's output "annotation". And the failing half was the
IMPERATIVE, not the descriptive clause.

WHAT LANDED: four arms, each naming the route that surface actually has. Naming get_variant_protein_effect
makes the bigquery-facing arms SELF-GATING under the existing text rule - the block then REQUIRES the tool,
which is exactly the intended precondition. Verified by rendering all five profiles x sandbox on/off:
    None sb/no proh=True [TOOL] | api sb proh=True [TOOL], api no proh=False []
    bigquery sb [SDK+PE] | bigquery no [DB+PE] | rag never | code sb [SDK], code no proh=False []
EXACTLY ONE remedy wherever the prohibition fires, zero where it does not, no orphan remedy, no dead arm.
The blanket "there is no variant-annotation tool on this surface" wording now matches NO SHIPPED PROFILE -
it survives only for a synthesised shape and its test builds that shape by subtracting the tool from a
resolved set.

THE DEFECT CLASS IS NOW PINNED GENERALLY, which is the most valuable thing this cycle produced:
test_no_prompt_refuses_what_the_same_prompt_explains_how_to_get asserts, over all ten renderings, that no
prompt carries a refusal sentence alongside the tool whose presence makes it false. Nothing had pinned it,
and it is what would have caught the shipped bug.

RECORDED, not filed: the UNFILTERED assembly (tool_names=None) now emits four mutually contradictory
annotation variants back to back, up from two. It is the documented pre-4h6.69 legacy path for callers with
no tool list, it already contained contradictions before this change, and chat_api always passes a set -
never None - so no production traffic reaches it.

title: Tool input schemas carry no minimum/maximum/pattern, so every documented numeric bound is prose only
description:
FOUND while deriving docs/chat-tool-reference.md from source (2026-08-18).

get_anthropic_tools() builds each input_schema from the `parameters` dict and emits ONLY type, description, default, items and enum. IT EMITS NO minimum, NO maximum AND NO pattern.

CONSEQUENCE: every numeric bound the tool descriptions state IN PROSE is unenforced at the schema layer. run_analysis's timeout_s is described as "1-120"; max_rows defaults are described per tool. The model is asked to respect these; nothing makes it. A model that emits timeout_s: 100000 produces a well-formed tool call that the schema accepts.

WHAT SAVES IT TODAY, and why this is P3 rather than higher: the server side validates independently - the supervisor clamps the wall clock to its own ceiling (genetics-results-suite-4h6.39) and results-api/db-api cap rows and bytes per execution (4h6.44's measurement). So an out-of-range value is REJECTED OR CLAMPED, not honoured. The cost is a wasted round trip and a confusing error rather than a breach.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH FIXING: the epic's whole premise is tool-selection and tool-call accuracy. A schema that declares its own bounds is the cheapest possible way to stop a class of malformed calls before they are made, and it costs one pass over the parameter builder plus the bounds that are already written down in the descriptions. It also removes prose that has to be kept true by hand - the "1-120" in a description is exactly the kind of enumeration CLAUDE.md warns rots silently.

Source of record: docs/chat-tool-reference.md.
close_reason:
LANDED. mcp-server 5964396 + 42d7d34, suite 597463f. One fix round of the two allowed.
Tests 1972 -> 1994. Against the unfixed builder 16 of 22 new tests fail; the 6 that pass are the
controls asserting ABSENCE (query_database unchanged, search_scientific_literature bare) and the three
that verify the ENFORCEMENT PREMISE rather than the fix - which is the right shape for a change whose
whole risk is claiming a bound that is not real.

THE RISK IN THIS BEAD IS NOT THE SCHEMA, IT IS THAT TWO SURFACES TREAT A BOUND DIFFERENTLY.
On the Anthropic surface `maximum` is advisory: the API does not validate tool inputs and the executor
still clamps. On the MCP surface pydantic REJECTS. So the same declaration is a hint in one place and a
hard error in the other, and the second one is a live-client contract.
Resolved by declaring on MCP only where the executor ALREADY rejects - the sql_int/sql_float sites and
the sandbox timeout - so the declaration moves an identical failure earlier. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not
by reading: all seven pre-change handlers raise at exactly the declared bounds, and every boundary value
(window=0, window=10_000_000, min_pip=0.0, min_pip=1.0, max_rows=1, max_rows=100_000) still passes and
reaches the query. The four CLAMPED parameters stay bare on MCP because le=10 would turn
`web_search(max_results=50)` - measured working today, returning 10 rows - into a validation error.
ONE OBSERVABLE CHANGE REMAINS AND THE COMMENT NOW SAYS SO: the rejection ENVELOPE differs. What was a
normal tool result {"success": false, "error": ...} is now a ToolError/isError protocol response. Neither
ever succeeded, so nothing that worked stops working, but a client branching on result["success"] sees a
different shape. The first draft of that comment said the change was "nothing observable", which was the
load-bearing justification for the whole decision and was wrong.

THE CLAMP/REJECT DISTINCTION WAS APPLIED TO CEILINGS AND NOT TO FLOORS, found in review.
`minimum: 1` was declared for three parameters whose enforcement is max(1, min(...)) - a CLAMP. The
server ACCEPTS 0. Two of those are honest (the floor really does apply to every value) and were kept.
THE THIRD WAS NOT: search_uniprot.size runs `size or _DEFAULT_SEARCH_SIZE`, and 0 IS FALSY, so size=0
returns 25 rows - not 1. The declared floor described a clamp the code never reaches. Dropped, with the
short-circuit recorded at the site. THE GENERAL RULE, now in the block comment: a clamped bound is only
honest if the clamp applies to EVERY value that reaches it.

TWO PROSE BOUNDS ARE NOT REAL AND WERE REPORTED RATHER THAN MADE TRUE BY FIAT:
- search_scientific_literature.max_results says "max 25". That clamp is on the EUROPE PMC path only
  (executor.py:3701). The DEFAULT backend is perplexity, which slices entries[:max_results] uncapped
  (:3819). So the stated bound is prose on the path most calls take. Left undeclared.
- query_database.max_rows has no local ceiling: fetch_max = max(max_rows, 100_000) WIDENS rather than
  caps, and the real limit is db-api's byte budget downstream.
(get_nearest_genes.n's "max 20" is enforced, if at all, inside genetics-results-api, which was out of
scope for this bead.)

NO `pattern` ANYWHERE, deliberately, and this is the reusable part: both candidates validate AFTER a
normalising step that WIDENS what is accepted. get_hla_by_allele strips a leading `HLA-` before matching
_HLA_ALLELE_RE, so a regex equal to the validator would reject `HLA-B*27:05`, which works today;
read_artifact.name is a strip-then-denylist, not expressible as a permissive regex. A regex copied from a
validator is only safe when nothing normalises before it. The builder supports `pattern` and a test
exercises it synthetically so the path is not dead code.

COVERAGE: TOOL_DEFINITIONS, BIGQUERY_ and SUBAGENT_ all flow through the single loop in
get_anthropic_tools, so one fix covers three lists. skills/sandbox_tools.py declares no numeric
parameter; mcp_proxy copies external inputSchema verbatim so external bounds survive and none are
injected. Verified, not assumed - "fixed one builder and left the others" is the exact shape of 4h6.74.

DOC-DRIFT HOOK CAUGHT WHAT THE FIRST COMMIT MISSED: tools/definitions.py -> mcp-server's own
docs/project-spec.md. The named concerns (tools table, profile categories) were untouched, but the rule
is "update it or say why", and 5964396 did neither. 42d7d34 adds the mechanism to that spec and points
at chat-tool-reference.md for the 12 bounds rather than copying them.

title: dev-stack.sh credential provisioning: MCP_ENV_FILE can silently override the minter's signing key
description:
FOUND by the sighted review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.49. Three small hygiene defects in the credential provisioning that 4h6.49 added to scripts/dev-stack.sh. THE PROVISIONING ITSELF WAS REVIEWED AND IS SOUND - files are 0600 under umask 077, in DEV_STACK_RUN_DIR outside every repo, reused rather than regenerated, and passed to services as inherited exported env so they never appear in ps output or a log. These are the edges around it.

1. THE ONE THAT CAN ACTUALLY BITE: start_chat_api sources $MCP_ENV_FILE with `set -a` AFTER the exports. So an INTERNAL_API_SECRET or SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY present in that .env silently WINS FOR CHAT-API ONLY - and chat-api is the MINTER. The verifiers (results-api, db-api) keep the generated key. A developer with either variable in their MCP .env gets a minter and verifiers that disagree, and the failure surfaces as a 401 from both backends inside every execution, which looks like a token bug rather than a config precedence bug. Not present in this checkout's .env, which is exactly why it would be missed. Either guard it or state the precedence.

2. scripts/test-e2e-local.py's --run-dir defaults to a HARDCODED ~/.cache/genetics-dev-stack and ignores DEV_STACK_RUN_DIR, which dev-stack.sh:59 honours. A developer who sets that variable must remember to pass --run-dir or the harness reads secrets from the wrong place - and the failure is a skip, not an error (see the skip-hygiene work in 4h6.49).

3. No lock around dev_secret, so two concurrent `dev-stack.sh up` runs could race the write. Trivial, listed for completeness.

ALSO WORTH A LINE SOMEWHERE: mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR" is outside the umask subshell, so the directory is 0775. The FILES are 0600 so the contents are protected; this is defence-in-depth only.
close_reason:
LANDED. genetics-results-suite 1308d2d. All three items plus the "worth a line" aside. One fix
round, and the fix round found the change did not achieve its own purpose - see below.

THE PROVISIONING ITSELF WAS NOT TOUCHED and did not need to be: 0600 under umask 077, in
DEV_STACK_RUN_DIR outside every repo, reused rather than regenerated, passed as inherited exported env
so it never reaches ps output or a log. The bead was right that these are the edges around it.

ITEM 1, THE ONE THAT BITES: guarded rather than merely documented, and NON-BLOCKING - a developer may
legitimately want to share one key across two stacks, and silence is what caused the bug. The grep
pattern was exercised against 13 constructed cases: it warns on plain, `export`, leading-whitespace,
EMPTY-VALUE (which overrides to empty, worse than a wrong key), CRLF and export+TAB; and stays quiet on
comments, `MY_INTERNAL_API_SECRET_PATH`, `OLD_SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY`, `KEY = value` (not an
assignment) and `export KEY` with no `=`. Zero false positives on anything constructible. Two false
negatives found and deliberately left: a second assignment on one line, and a UTF-8 BOM on line 1.

THE FIX ROUND IS THE PART WORTH CARRYING FORWARD. The first draft put the warning INSIDE start_chat_api,
whose subshell is redirected wholesale - `) >"$RUN_DIR/chat-api.log" 2>&1 &` - so `>&2` landed in the
log. chat-api.log is surfaced exactly twice: when the health check FAILS, and on an explicit
`logs chat-api`. In this bead's scenario chat-api starts FINE and passes health, so nothing points
anyone at it. MEASURED: the terminal saw nothing while the override was real. A change whose entire
purpose is to make a silent bug audible was silent. It now lives in preflight_svc's chat-api case,
unredirected, in cmd_up's loop before any service starts - which also makes
docs/local-dev-vm.md's "warns loudly" literally true rather than aspirational.

ITEM 3 (flock) INTRODUCED A FAIL-OPEN AND THE REVIEW CAUGHT IT. dev_secret is called as
${SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY:-$(dev_secret ...)}, and errexit does NOT propagate out of a command
substitution inside a parameter-expansion default. With flock absent: `flock: command not found`,
`K=[] len=0`, `SCRIPT CONTINUED PAST dev_secret` - an EMPTY signing key exported to all three services
with `up` carrying on, which per docs/local-dev-vm.md is the fail-open state. The MASKING IS
PRE-EXISTING (a failing python3 does the same) and was deliberately NOT addressed - out of scope, and
fixing the general pattern is a different task. What landed is a `command -v flock` preflight scoped to
COMMAND=up, the only path that calls dev_secret. Concurrency verified: 20 parallel calls on a fresh dir
yield ONE value, three rounds running; lock file 0600, fd 9 verified unused elsewhere.

A JUSTIFICATION THAT DID NOT SURVIVE CHECKING, recorded because it nearly entered the record as fact:
the new dependency was defended as "the script already hard-requires `ss` from the same package family".
`flock` is util-linux; `ss` is IPROUTE2 - different packages. The CONCLUSION holds anyway (the `ss`
preflight already makes this script Linux-only and flock is universal there), but when the fix agent
went looking for the comment carrying the false claim it found NONE - the claim existed only in an
agent's report, never in the tree. It correctly declined to "fix" something that was not there and wrote
the accurate reasoning instead.

EVERY CHANGE VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not by reading: the warning reaching real stderr and staying quiet
otherwise, preflight_svc with a missing/empty/nonexistent env file, the flock preflight firing and
staying quiet and correctly not firing on `down`, 20-way concurrent dev_secret, file modes, and
DEV_STACK_RUN_DIR's three cases including the empty-string one where Python's `or` and shell's `:-`
agree. bash -n clean.

TWO ADJACENT DOC IMPRECISIONS FOUND AND NOT FIXED HERE, recorded as items 64 and 65 on
genetics-results-suite-4h6.98 (the e8e continuation): docs/project-spec.md:1667's "Override any of the
three to pin a value", and docs/local-dev-vm.md:118's claim that SANDBOX_ENABLED set in MCP_ENV_FILE
gets a health-probe warning - it does not, because the probe runs at top level before the file is
sourced. THE PATTERN ACROSS ALL THREE: this script has three variables whose effect depends on WHERE
you set them, and the docs describe setting them as uniform. The durable fix is sourcing MCP_ENV_FILE
BEFORE the exports, or saying once that it is chat-api-only - not three more warnings.

title: Supervisor's log_message drops the stdlib control-char translation, and stdout is now the audit channel
description:
FOUND by the sighted review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.45. PRE-EXISTING and untouched by it, but that change RAISES THE STAKES, which is why it is filed now rather than left.

sandbox/supervisor.py's BaseHTTPRequestHandler.log_message override drops the stdlib's `_control_char_table` translation. The stdlib added that translation precisely so a raw HTTP request line cannot put control characters - ANSI escapes, carriage returns - onto the server's log.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE NOW: as of 4h6.45 the supervisor's STDOUT IS THE AUDIT CHANNEL. It is what the cluster logging agent collects and what an operator reads to answer "who ran what". An unsanitised request line lands on that same stream.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO, checked: it cannot forge an SDK audit record. The analyzer's SDK_CALL_RE is anchored, and log_message's format appends ` "<code> <size>"` after the request line, so a crafted request cannot produce a line the analyzer reads as a genuine call. Attribution is not at risk.

WHAT IT CAN DO: put terminal escapes and line breaks into the pod log, which is enough to make a `docker logs` or `kubectl logs` session misleading to a human reading it, and enough to confuse a naive line-oriented processor.

WHO CAN REACH IT: the supervisor's ingress is a NetworkPolicy admitting chat-backend alone, so the untrusted script is NOT the party holding this socket - which is why this is P3. It is reachable by anything that can make a malformed request from inside the namespace.

FIX: restore the translation, i.e. apply `str.translate(self._control_char_table)` as the stdlib does. One line, no behaviour change for well-formed requests.

Related: genetics-results-suite-4h6.58 (the same handler's BODY_READ_TIMEOUT_S covering neither the request line nor the headers) - these two are in the same object and should probably be fixed together.
close_reason:
LANDED. genetics-results-suite 2267836, batched with 4h6.58 - this bead's own description ends "these two
are in the same handler", which was correct.

_Handler.log_message dropped the stdlib's _control_char_table translation. Restored. Since 4h6.45 the
supervisor's STDOUT IS THE AUDIT CHANNEL, so an unsanitised request line landed on the stream operators
read to answer "who ran what".

THE TABLE IS VERIFIED DICT-EQUAL TO THE STDLIB'S, not merely similar - checked on both 3.10 and 3.12,
including the range endpoints (0x7e and 0xa0 untouched, so no off-by-one) and the `\\` override.
str.maketrans returns a plain dict so == is exact over all 54 entries.
THE FALLBACK IS DEAD CODE IN THE SHIPPED IMAGE and the comment now says so honestly. The first draft
justified it with "the image's distroless CPython is 3.11" - MEASURED: 3.10 ALREADY HAS
_control_char_table, so 3.11 certainly does and the stdlib table is always taken. Kept as defensiveness
against a future interpreter dropping a private attribute; that is the honest reason and it is what the
comment says.

THE FORGERY CLAIM IS TRUE BUT NOT FOR THE STATED REASON, which is worth correcting wherever it is repeated:
ANALYZER_SDK_CALL_RE is anchored only at `$`, NOT at `^`, and is used with .search(). What actually
prevents forgery is that log_message always appends ` "<code> <size>"` (size is always `-`) and the regex
tail requires the line to end in \d+, ` error: \S+` or ` cancelled` - none of which the fixed 7-char
suffix ` 404 -` can satisfy. MEASURED with a request line crafted as a complete fake SDK record:
search() -> False. The real mechanism is stronger than the word "anchored" implies; recorded on e8e item 28.

Test coverage added includes the one that matters most for an audit channel: a crafted request cannot
become TWO log lines (`"\x0d\x0a" in capture.lines[0]` and len(capture.lines) == 1).

title: Supervisor: the three os.pipe() calls sit outside _execute_inner's try, so EMFILE on the 2nd or 3rd leaks the earlier pair(s)
description:
FOUND by both reviewers of genetics-results-suite-4h6.45, confirmed PRE-EXISTING and unchanged in shape.

sandbox/supervisor.py _execute_inner creates its pipes BEFORE `os.fork()`, and the fork has no try. If it raises OSError every pipe created above it is leaked - both ends, permanently, for the life of the supervisor process.

IT WAS 4 FDS, IT IS NOW 6. 4h6.45 added a third os.pipe() (the audit stream), so each failed fork now leaks 50% more. That is an amplification of an existing hazard, not a new one, which is why it was not fixed inside that bead.

THE ONLY REALISTIC DRIVER IS PID OR FD EXHAUSTION - which is precisely the state in which fork() fails, so the leak compounds exactly when the process can least afford it. Each failure makes the next fork marginally more likely to fail.

FIX SHAPE: the pipe wiring needs restructuring so every fd created for an execution is owned by something that closes it on any exit path - a try/finally or a small context manager around the whole create-fork-dup-close sequence. This is not a one-line change, which is the other reason it was deferred; doing it carelessly risks closing an fd the child still needs, and the child-side dup2 ordering is delicate (see _relocate_above, which exists because dup2(status_w, 3) can silently close the audit write end when the kernel hands a pipe fd 3 or 4).

Low priority: reaching it requires the pod to be already failing. Recorded so the next person to touch that sequence fixes it rather than rediscovering it.
notes:
--- RESCOPED 2026-08-22 by probe, BEFORE working it. THE ORIGINAL PREMISE IS ~90% FALSE. Work this. ---
NEITHER bd415f9 NOR f225944 CLOSED IT - it was closed by 78cc9db (4h6.55), which this bead predates and
does not account for. git blame confirms supervisor.py:2920-2951 is 78cc9db, 2026-08-20 14:24.

WHAT IS NOW FALSE:
1. "the fork has no try". It does. supervisor.py:2925-2951 wraps the whole thing and closes ALL SEVEN fds
   on ANY exception:
       except BaseException:
           _fs_close_all([fd for fd in (payload_fd, out_w, st_w, audit_w, out_r, st_r, audit_r)
                          if fd is not None])
           raise
2. "os.fork() raises OSError". THE SUPERVISOR NO LONGER FORKS AT ALL. fork_child is a control-socket round
   trip to the fork server, so a fork failure arrives as a fork-server error INSIDE that try.
3. "needs the whole create-fork-dup-close sequence restructured" and "_relocate_above constrains it".
   _relocate_above (supervisor.py:1175-1192) NO LONGER CONSTRAINS THIS AT ALL - it now runs entirely on
   the CHILD side INSIDE THE FORK SERVER (:1296-1301, in _fs_do_fork's child), a different process from
   _execute_inner. Do not budget for a restructure.

WHAT IS LEFT, AND IT IS ONE LINE. The three os.pipe() calls are still OUTSIDE the try, at
supervisor.py:2915-2919:
    out_r, out_w = os.pipe()
    st_r, st_w = os.pipe()
    audit_r, audit_w = os.pipe()
If the SECOND or THIRD os.pipe() raises EMFILE - the exact fd-exhaustion state this bead names as the only
realistic driver - the earlier pair(s) leak. That is 2 or 4 fds, NOT 6, and only on the 2nd/3rd call.
FIX: move the pipe creation inside the existing try (payload_fd is already initialised to None above it,
and _fs_close_all already tolerates None), or wrap each pair. Nothing else.

SEQUENCING: do this BEFORE 4h6.62. Both live in _execute_inner and both are about fd ownership; an
fd-ownership wrapper written for this bead that also covered the READ ends would move 4h6.62's leak site
out from under it.
close_reason:
LANDED. genetics-results-suite dd2bc03, batched with 4h6.57. ONE LINE OF SUBSTANCE, as the 2026-08-22
rescope predicted - the bead's own description would have bought a restructure cycle for nothing.

THE RESCOPE WAS THE WHOLE VALUE HERE. 78cc9db (4h6.55) had already fixed the substance and neither this
bead nor the briefing knew it: _execute_inner has an `except BaseException` closing all seven fds and
re-raising, and THE SUPERVISOR NO LONGER FORKS AT ALL (fork_child is a control-socket round trip to the
fork server), so a fork failure already arrives inside that try. `_relocate_above` - which the description
cited as the delicate constraint - now runs in the FORK SERVER'S CHILD, a different process, and constrains
nothing here.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY LEFT: the three os.pipe() calls sat just OUTSIDE the try, so an EMFILE from the 2nd or
3rd leaked the earlier pair(s) - 2 or 4 fds, NOT the 6 the title claimed. Moved inside, with all seven
descriptor names bound to None in one chained assignment before the try so the handler cannot see an
unbound name. VERIFIED BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by reading: the chained assignment is seven STORE_FASTs,
none of which can raise, and it precedes `try:` - so entering the try implies all seven are bound; each
`a, b = os.pipe()` either raises before any store or completes both; and _fs_close_all filters None and
catches only OSError, so every value that can reach it is tolerated.

TEST: test_pipe_fd_ownership arms a fake os.pipe raising EMFILE on its 2nd then 3rd call and censuses
`pipe:` links in /proc/self/fd across a real POST /execute - counting PIPES rather than fds so the
request's own sockets do not perturb the census. Control SUPERVISOR_TEST_PIPES_OUTSIDE_TRY=1 restores a
genuinely unowned pair and turns exactly the two leak checks red (2 fds leaked each), leaving the four
"response given back" checks green.
Recorded on e8e, not fixed: the test swaps the PROCESS-GLOBAL os.pipe while the threaded server is live, so
a concurrent os.pipe() from another thread could consume the armed call. The supervisor is idle at that
point, so the risk is low, but it is a real hazard in that pattern.

title: Doc-accuracy pass over the supervisor after the 4h6.41/.42/.43/.46 batch
description:
FOUND by the sighted review AND the blind validation of the 4h6.41/.42/.43/.46 batch. Batched deliberately: per the cost rule, comment/doc-accuracy findings are collected rather than fixed in-cycle. NONE of these is a false claim about a security control (those were fixed in-cycle); each is a name, count or boundary that does not match the code.

1. ERR_MEMORY_LIMIT = "MemoryLimit" is DEFINED IN sandbox/supervisor.py AND NEVER EMITTED ANYWHERE. docs/code-execution-security.md lists it among "the supervisor's own reserved names". The RLIMIT_AS path surfaces the CHILD'S exception class instead, and the harness asserts error.type == "MemoryError". A client branching on "MemoryLimit" never matches. Either emit it or strike it from the reserved list - and note the batch made error.type validation reject unknown names, so this interacts with that.

2. SCRATCH_SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES is unused. The comment says so, which is honest, but a constant nothing reads is drift bait.

3. REAPER_POLL_S = 30 makes the "15 minute" retention TTL actually 15 min + up to 30 s. Harmless in itself - BUT genetics-results-suite-4h6.49 is instructed to assert that "artifacts survive to the 15-minute retention boundary and are gone after it", and the doc states the boundary as exact. Either state the tolerance in the doc or 4h6.49 will write a flaky assertion.

4. _retained_sizes calls _dir_bytes(<id>/artifacts) and os.scandir FOLLOWS the final path component, so a child that replaces artifacts/ with a symlink to another execution's directory makes the retained-ceiling accounting DOUBLE-COUNT. Deletion is safe (shutil.rmtree does not traverse the symlink), so this is misaccounting only. It is also squarely inside genetics-results-suite-4h6.55's territory - a child that can do this can already do worse - so fixing it here buys little until that is resolved. Recorded so it is not rediscovered as new.

DO THIS AS ONE PASS, and re-derive every count from the code per CLAUDE.md's enumeration-rot rule rather than adjusting the numbers in place.
close_reason:
Landed as genetics-results-suite 0de996b. Implementation + review + one fix round. NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: harness 184 in-process and 106 passed / 3 skipped in container, both unchanged. This bead BLOCKED 4h6.49 and now releases it.

MemoryLimit: THE CLAIM WAS CORRECTED, NOT THE CODE, and the reasoning is the deliverable. RLIMIT_AS is applied by the CHILD to itself and enforced by the kernel INSIDE the child, so the supervisor never observes it firing. Emitting MemoryLimit would mean either trusting the child's own status record to distinguish the ceiling from a plain `raise MemoryError` - exactly the trust _sanitise_error_type exists to refuse - or minting a second privileged exit code beside StartupFailure's 70, which is a wire-contract change and not a doc pass. Struck from the doc's reserved-name row; a new paragraph states what memory exhaustion actually looks like (status "error", type "MemoryError", limit null). ERR_MEMORY_LIMIT KEPT in RESERVED_ERROR_TYPES because forge-refusal is real use, so it is not the unused-constant shape. Doc now 8 names, constant 9, and the doc EXPLAINS the gap rather than leaving the two to disagree silently.
The latent _LIMIT_MESSAGES KeyError was left as-is (no behaviour change) with the invariant stated at the dict. Review re-derived it independently: _fire_limit is called with exactly Output, Timeout (x2), Pid, ArtifactQuota, ScratchQuota (x2); the dict holds exactly the four non-timeout ones; job.limit is assigned in one place, so the index cannot see a foreign value.

TWO OF THIS BEAD'S OWN FRAMINGS WERE WRONG AND WERE INVERTED, both re-verified against the code:
- The artifacts/-as-symlink double-count reads HIGH, not low. The aggregate over-reports, the ceiling evicts SOONER than needed, nothing is under-protected. Deletion stays correct (shutil.rmtree does not traverse the symlink; _remove_entry unlinks rather than descending). The cheap guard was priced - one lstat per measurement - and declined because it buys nothing until 4h6.55.
- The trim's newest-first policy does NOT spare the oversized file. It is considered LAST, but the loop's exit condition is the quota and no number of small deletions brings a tree under a quota one file alone exceeds. So the 50 small plots are deleted AND the 100 MiB CSV is deleted after them - the plots are lost for nothing. Worse than this bead described. Documented where a user-facing description of read_artifact would mislead; policy deliberately unchanged.

FOR 4h6.49, WHICH THIS BEAD BLOCKED - the retention numbers are now stated where that author will read them. The observable window is [15 min, 15 min + 30s] because REAPER_POLL_S is 30. SANDBOX_RETENTION_S shortens the TTL but NOT the poll (_reaper_loop is started with no poll argument), so the 30s term stays 30s however short the TTL. scripts/test-supervisor.py:test_retention_expiry already has the correct shape - retention_s + REAPER_POLL_S + 2 in container mode, direct reap_expired() in-process - and should be copied rather than reinvented.
REVIEW THEN CAUGHT THE PRESENCE SIDE STATED UNCONDITIONALLY: "guaranteed present until the deadline" is FALSE, because _enforce_retained_ceiling evicts oldest-first BEFORE a deadline when a later completion breaches the 256 MiB aggregate. Now qualified in both the doc and the code comment, with the caveat spelled out: 4h6.49's presence-side assertion is sound only while nothing else is retaining concurrently.

REVIEW FOUND ONE BLOCKING DEFECT AND THE DOC-DRIFT HOOK WAS ALREADY POINTING AT IT. docs/project-spec.md still described 4h6.41, 4h6.42, 4h6.43 and 4h6.46 as "each stubbed in place" and closed with "nothing yet kills a runaway child and nothing yet deletes a completed execution" - both clauses false since 09ed48d, which touched project-spec only to add the RLIMIT_AS number and left the bullet behind. That is precisely the shape this pass exists to remove, in the repo that is the SPEC OF RECORD for the suite. Rewritten from the code: the remaining stub was re-derived by grepping `STUB (` in supervisor.py, which returns exactly two hits, both naming 4h6.45. The cross-reference was repointed from the superseded "As built (4h6.39)" heading to "As built (4h6.41, 4h6.42, 4h6.43, 4h6.46)", whose text and location were verified rather than assumed. Also repointed "killing the escapee is 4h6.41/4h6.46 work" to 4h6.55, which all eight escapee references in supervisor.py already name.

artifacts_omitted was described as if a client could read the trim's deletion count out of it. It cannot - the field is omitted + trimmed, and build_manifest's half is a FLOOR past the scan limit, which the code logs in as many words. Now stated as a combined floor, not a trim counter.

ONE ITEM CLOSED WITH NO WORK, and checking was the instruction: this bead claimed SCRATCH_SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES was unused. STALE PREMISE - the second fix round of 4h6.46 derives SCRATCH_AGGREGATE_CEILING_BYTES from it. Verified before changing anything.

VERIFIED BY REVIEW AND WORTH KEEPING: no comment or doc line claims the process-group kill contains a setsid() escapee; the token file is still nowhere documented as an exposure bound; no stub describes a control the code does not apply; and the caveat added to "nothing writes to a retained directory, so the value cannot drift" is itself accurate - all three of its consequences (retained total, ceiling eviction, in-run aggregate check) do read low for an escapee, as claimed.

REPORTED, NOT FIXED - another repo, another bead: genetics-mcp-server tools/executor.py has a "MemoryLimit" hint that is DOUBLY dead. The name is never emitted, and the dict is only consulted under status == "limit", which a MemoryError (status "error") never produces. Whoever owns 4h6.44 may want a memory hint keyed on error_type == "MemoryError" in the error branch instead.

NOTE ON scripts/check-doc-drift.sh: it reads `git diff --cached` only, so it exits 0 silently against an unstaged tree. Its second sandbox check (sandbox/** -> docs/project-spec.md) is what would have caught the blocking finding above, and it is satisfied now that both docs are staged together.

title: run-sandbox-local.sh is absent from the doc-ownership table and check-doc-drift.sh
description:

title: rollout.sh has no `sandbox` entry, so build.sh prints a command that fails
description:
FOUND during genetics-results-suite-4h6.7's review, by BOTH validators independently. Pre-existing (the sandbox image build landed in 4h6.6), but 4h6.7 is what makes a single-service sandbox rollout meaningful, so it is worth fixing now rather than when someone first needs it in a hurry.

THE DEFECT: `scripts/build.sh:91` prints, as the next step after building the sandbox image,
    To roll out: REGISTRY=... ./scripts/rollout.sh sandbox ${TAG}
`scripts/rollout.sh`'s IMAGE_MAP (~lines 40-48) has NO `sandbox` key, so that exact command exits 1 with `Unknown service: sandbox`. The tool tells you to run something that cannot work.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: this makes the sandbox THE ONLY WORKLOAD WITH NO SINGLE-SERVICE UPDATE PATH. Every other service can be rolled individually; the sandbox can only be updated by a full `scripts/deploy.sh`, which also runs `terraform apply -auto-approve` and restarts everything else. That is a bad property for the one workload most likely to need a quick targeted redeploy, and neither README.md nor docs/project-spec.md says so.

THE FIX IS ONE LINE: add `[sandbox]=sandbox` to IMAGE_MAP. Both validators checked the shape - the image repo and the container name are both literally `sandbox`, so CONTAINER_NAME resolves correctly with no special-casing.

CHECK BEFORE COMMITTING, because the sandbox is not an ordinary service:
- rollout.sh restarts a Deployment. The sandbox Deployment is `strategy: Recreate` with `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 130`, so a rollout KILLS AN IN-FLIGHT EXECUTION and leaves no sandbox for up to ~130s. Confirm the script's rollout-status wait tolerates that, and that its timeout exceeds the grace period.
- The sandbox Deployment is GATED: `deploy.sh` only applies it when ENABLE_SANDBOX is on, derived from `sandbox_pool_enabled = true` in terraform.tfvars. Decide what `rollout.sh sandbox` should do when no sandbox Deployment exists in the cluster - a clear "not deployed" message beats a kubectl error.
- The doc-ownership table makes `scripts/*.sh` changes require updating docs/project-spec.md and README.md in the same commit.

NOT URGENT: the sandbox is not deployed, and nothing can be rolled out until 4h6.14 provides a supervisor for the image to run.
close_reason:
LANDED with 4h6.50 in one cycle. genetics-results-suite a582ee9. Batched because both are deploy
plumbing and both required docs/project-spec.md and README.md in the same commit.

THE ONE-LINE FIX WAS ONE LINE, exactly as filed: `[sandbox]=sandbox` in IMAGE_MAP, and
CONTAINER_NAME="${SERVICE}" resolves it with no special-casing, as both validators had predicted.
THE THREE CHECKS THE BEAD ASKED FOR WERE THE ACTUAL WORK, and one of them turned up a regression this
cycle introduced:
- GRACE PERIOD: tolerated, no change needed. Re-derived from the manifest - strategy Recreate,
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds 130, readinessProbe initialDelaySeconds 5 + periodSeconds 10, no
  liveness or startup probe. The 300s rollout-status timeout clears 130s drain plus schedule plus
  prewarm plus 5+10. Recorded at the site that the rollout KILLS AN IN-FLIGHT EXECUTION and leaves no
  sandbox for up to ~130s, which chat-backend surfaces as a tool error. ONE UNCOVERED CASE, worth
  knowing before the staging bring-up: a cold first pull of a multi-GB image on a fresh gVisor node
  could exceed 300s, and rollout.sh has no `|| true` where deploy.sh does - so a slow first pull
  surfaces as a non-zero exit on a rollout that is actually progressing. Non-destructive.
- NOT DEPLOYED: a generic existence pre-check now prints a clear message instead of a bare kubectl
  NotFound, with four extra lines for `sandbox` explaining the ENABLE_SANDBOX gate.

title: The sandbox startup gate accepts a blank-ish signing key - add a length check, but do NOT strip
description:
FOUND while validating genetics-results-suite-l7z and deliberately NOT fixed there - it is PRE-EXISTING (the pre-l7z import-time snapshot used the identical truthiness test), orthogonal to that task's claim, and the obvious one-line fix is WRONG in a way worth recording.

THE GAP: `require_sandbox_config` accepts any truthy string as SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY. Measured with SANDBOX_ENABLED=true, all of these pass startup: "   ", "\n", "x", "0". PyJWT itself warns - `InsecureKeyLengthWarning: The HMAC key is 3 bytes long`.
CONSEQUENCE: a whitespace-only or single-character secret - the classic `kubectl create secret --from-file` of an empty or near-empty file - passes the startup gate AND becomes a guessable HMAC key that mints valid sandbox principals. The startup check exists precisely to stop the sandbox reaching a misconfigured db-api, and this is a misconfiguration it does not catch.

THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG. Do NOT just add .strip() to `_signing_key()`. db-api VERIFIES with that value; chat-backend MINTS with whatever is in its own copy of the secret. A key deployed with a trailing newline signs as "key\n" and would then be verified against "key", so EVERY LEGITIMATE SANDBOX TOKEN WOULD 401. Any normalisation has to happen on both sides at once, which means a coordinated change in the minting repo - that is why l7z declined it rather than doing it cheaply.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY WORK, roughly in order of cost:
1. A MINIMUM-LENGTH GATE AT STARTUP ONLY, with no normalisation - e.g. refuse to start if the key is shorter than N bytes after stripping, WITHOUT changing the value used for signing or verifying. This catches the whole reported class ("   ", "\n", "x", "0") and cannot desynchronise anything, because the value that reaches jwt.decode is untouched. This is almost certainly the right answer, and it is self-contained.
2. Additionally warn (not fail) if the key differs from its stripped form, so a trailing-newline secret is VISIBLE rather than silently load-bearing.
3. Only if 1 and 2 are judged insufficient: coordinated normalisation across the minter and verifier, which needs both repos changed and deployed together and is the risky option.

WHERE: `api/sandbox_auth.py`'s `require_sandbox_config` in genetics-results-db. Note it runs at IMPORT and its remedy is sys.exit(1), which is correct there - the pod never passes readiness and the rollout stalls, so a bad key is caught before the pod serves.

NOT URGENT: the sandbox is not deployed (SANDBOX_ENABLED is "false" on both services and there is no k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml), so no such key exists yet. Do it before the sandbox ships, since after that a weak key is a live credential rather than a configuration hazard.

title: Document (or close by observation) the BigQuery remote-function egress residual in the SQL gate
description:
FOUND while validating genetics-results-suite-4h6.33's claim that db-api is a safe permitted egress target for the sandbox. It IS safe against every path that was checked - this is the one residual that was not, and it is not documented anywhere.

WHAT WAS VERIFIED AND HOLDS: db-api is a permitted egress target that executes SQL, and authorize_query (genetics-results-db api/main.py:370-414) dry-runs each statement through BigQuery and rejects statement_type != "SELECT" plus any table outside _ALLOWED_TABLE_IDS. That closes EXPORT DATA, EXECUTE IMMEDIATE, DDL and DML as outbound data paths.

THE RESIDUAL: a BigQuery REMOTE FUNCTION (or a remote-model/`ML.PREDICT`-style construct) invoked inside an otherwise-legitimate SELECT would pass BOTH gates - the statement really is a SELECT, and ROUTINES DO NOT APPEAR IN referenced_tables, which is what the allow-list is checked against. A remote function calls a Cloud Run/Cloud Functions endpoint with the row values, so it is an egress channel that neither the NetworkPolicy nor the SQL gate sees, because the call is made BY BIGQUERY, not by the sandbox pod.

WHY THIS IS LOW SEVERITY TODAY, and file it as hardening rather than a hole: creating a remote function requires CREATE FUNCTION, which is DDL, which the same statement_type gate blocks. So it only matters if a remote function ALREADY EXISTS in the project, or if something outside this path can create one. It also requires a BigQuery Connection, which is an IAM-governed resource.

WHAT TO ACTUALLY DO, cheapest first:
1. ESTABLISH THE FACT: enumerate existing routines and connections in the project and record the answer. If there are none, say so in docs/code-execution-security.md and the residual is closed by observation. Read-only: `bq ls --routines` per dataset, and list BigQuery connections.
2. If any exist, decide whether the dry-run gate should additionally reject statements whose referenced routines are not allow-listed - note dry-run metadata may or may not expose routines, so CHECK WHETHER IT IS EVEN DETECTABLE before designing on it.
3. Confirm no service account reachable from this path holds bigquery.connections.use or the ability to create routines in the datasets involved.

WHERE IT BELONGS: docs/code-execution-security.md owns the egress and SQL-gate analysis. Its section 3 currently reasons entirely about POD egress; a remote function is egress that does not originate in the pod, which is the reason it is not covered by anything written there.

NOTE THE SANDBOX IS NOT DEPLOYED, so this is design-time - the cheapest point to settle it.

title: api/sandbox_auth.py still snapshots two auth env vars at import - the hazard xi6 fixed for the third
description:
Split out of genetics-results-suite-xi6, which fixed this hazard for ONE of the three auth-related env vars and deliberately left the other two. Both the sighted reviewer and the blind validator raised it independently.

api/sandbox_auth.py:58 and :63 still snapshot SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY and SANDBOX_ENABLED AT IMPORT - exactly the pattern xi6 removed for INTERNAL_API_SECRET. So "whoever imports first decides" still holds for the sandbox credential path, which is the one path with ATTACKER-AUTHORED input.

CONCRETE CONSEQUENCES ESTABLISHED DURING xi6:
- tests/conftest.py's restore_auth_env fixture restores all three variables as if they were symmetric. Restoring the two sandbox ones buys NOTHING behavioural: they cannot change an already-imported module, so only a _reload() (which pops and re-imports them itself) ever sees them. The fixture's own docstring was corrected to say so, but the asymmetry remains in the code.
- A test that pops SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY affects no live app object, and popping it would fail CLOSED rather than open - so this is a correctness-and-clarity problem, not a security hole today.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING ANYWAY: the sandbox path is the one an attacker-authored script reaches. Leaving it on the pattern that just produced a seed-dependent red suite in the shared-secret path means the next person to add a module-scope import gets the same class of failure, in the harder-to-reason-about credential.

DO NOT COPY xi6's SOLUTION BLINDLY. xi6 needed a one-way latch and a tri-state return because its variable governs a FAIL-OPEN branch; the sandbox path has no fail-open equivalent (an unset signing key rejects every token), so a plain per-request read may well be sufficient. Establish that before designing.
Check also whether require_sandbox_config's invariant ("sandbox deployed => internal secret present") should be re-checked per request rather than only at import - xi6 left it asserted at startup only, which is recorded there as a known limitation.
close_reason:
Landed as genetics-results-db e7881bf. Blind validator + one fix round. db suite 148 -> 154 passed on the worktree's own .venv, stable at seeds 2662673150 (the historically red one), 12345 and 987654321. FILE-ONLY.
TIER NOTE, stated so the record is accurate: I ran the BLIND validator but NOT a sighted review alongside it. The blind pass was thorough and found everything below, but this was Standard-plus rather than the Full tier an auth path nominally calls for.

THE DESIGN CALL WAS "NO LATCH", AND IT SURVIVED DIRECT ATTACK. The bead warned against copying xi6 blindly and that warning paid: xi6 needed a one-way latch and a tri-state return because its value governs a FAIL-OPEN branch - "" means "authentication was never configured" and require_auth answers it with an early return that ADMITS the caller, so a plain read could DISABLE authentication in a running process. The signing key has no value with that meaning. verify_sandbox_token raises on an empty key and require_auth converts SandboxTokenError into a hard 401 with no fallthrough, so every state except the exact minting key rejects, and the only runtime transitions a plain read admits are unset->set (the hazard being removed) and set->unset-or-changed, both strictly STRICTER. A latch would have been a process global a future reader must trace before discovering it can never change an outcome.
MEASURED, not argued: unset / empty / trailing-newline / rotated / wrong-key tokens all 401; a non-ASCII but valid-UTF-8 key that MATCHES correctly returns 200 (key equality, no ASCII invariant needed here unlike the shared secret); an unset INTERNAL_API_SECRET - which IS fail-open - plus an INVALID sandbox token still 401, proving the sandbox path does not inherit the early return; and with two Authorization headers Starlette returns the first, so header stuffing can neither downgrade a failed sandbox token onto the secret path nor upgrade anything without already knowing the secret.

ONE FINDING WITH RUNTIME CONSEQUENCE, fixed. The catch was `except jwt.InvalidTokenError`. jwt.InvalidKeyError is a SIBLING under PyJWTError, NOT a subclass - a PEM pasted into the env var raises it - and PyJWT's prepare_key encodes a str key as UTF-8, so a key carrying the surrogates os.environ produces from non-UTF-8 bytes raises UnicodeEncodeError. Both escaped uncaught and surfaced as 500 RATHER THAN 401. Still fail-closed - nobody was admitted - but it falsified the function's own "always a hard 401" docstring and SUPPRESSED THE endpoint_access REJECTION LOG, so an operator saw an unattributed 500 instead of an auth failure. This is also the one place xi6's latin-1/utf-8 concern genuinely recurs, and the module had not addressed it.
Widened to `except Exception`, deliberately over the narrower tuple: the try block wraps exactly ONE call (jwt.decode), so the breadth cannot swallow surrounding logic, and only the broad form makes the "raises only SandboxTokenError" contract literally true against a future crypto-layer raise type. Justified in a comment. Two new parametrized tests pin it - one through the app asserting 401-not-500 and that the shared-secret caller is unaffected, one asserting the exception type directly. Nothing in the suite had pinned this before.

require_sandbox_config STAYS STARTUP-ONLY, and the question xi6 left open is now closed rather than deferred a third time. Reasons written into the docstring: its remedy is sys.exit(1), which is only correct at import (the pod never passes readiness, the rollout stalls, old pods keep serving) whereas from a request path it would kill a serving pod at a moment THE SANDBOX - the one attacker-authored caller - chooses; and SANDBOX_ENABLED comes from the pod spec, which cannot change without a new pod that re-runs the check.
MY FIRST DRAFT OF THAT ARGUMENT WAS WRONG AND THE VALIDATOR BUILT THE COUNTEREXAMPLE. It asserted "there is no runtime state this check could catch in which the service is serving fail-open with the sandbox deployed". That covers only the emptied-AFTER-startup transitions and omits the NEVER-CONFIGURED case, where _authentication_was_configured is False and _internal_api_secret() returns "" rather than None. Starting a process with both variables unset (so the check returns early) and then flipping SANDBOX_ENABLED=true reaches exactly that state. The CONCLUSION stands - pod-environment immutability rescues it - so the wording now depends on that rather than asserting the state cannot exist. Same edit in db docs/project-spec.md.

TESTS: the four simplified tests were checked for whether they still bite, and the honest answer is that only ONE of them does (the three-param startup test). The regression pressure comes from the two NEW tests, both of which fail against a reintroduced import-time snapshot. One simplified test - test_signing_key_unset_rejects_every_sandbox_token - was passing WITHOUT its delenv having any effect, since under a frozen empty key the sandbox path is already dead; it now asserts a non-401 BEFORE the delenv so it proves the path was live and the unset killed it.
The implementation reported "6 failed / 33 passed" when it verified the tests bite; independent re-measurement got 7/32 key-only and 9/30 for both variables. The conclusion is unaffected. Grepped tests/, docs/ and api/ - the figure was never written into a file, so there is nothing to correct.

WHAT THE BEAD GOT WRONG, two refinements: it framed SANDBOX_ENABLED as symmetric with the signing key, but only the signing key is on a request path at all - SANDBOX_ENABLED is read solely by the startup check, so moving it off the snapshot buys correctness of the CHECK, not any request-time behaviour. And it treated require_sandbox_config's scope as an open question inherited from xi6; it is closed by xi6's landed latch plus this change together, which is a conclusion xi6 could not have drawn before its own latch existed.

DECLINED, with a better reason than my instruction had, and filed separately: I asked for .strip() on the signing key so the startup gate would reject a whitespace-only secret. The fix agent refused correctly - stripping on the VERIFY side desynchronizes db-api from chat-backend's MINTING side, so a key deployed via `kubectl create secret --from-file` with a trailing newline signs as "key\n" and would then verify against "key", 401ing every legitimate sandbox token. That needs a coordinated change in the minting repo.

CONFIRMED CLEAN, so nobody re-derives it: no other module-scope auth-relevant env snapshot remains in api/ (only _startup_secret, by design, and CORS_ORIGINS whose middleware is constructed at import so a per-call read would be meaningless); no lru_cache/cache/cached_property anywhere in api/; FastAPI does not cache a plain function dependency across requests; and the per-call read costs 697ns against a 69.3us HMAC verify, i.e. 1%.

THE BEAD'S COORDINATES WERE FICTION, exactly as it warned about itself: lines 1022, 1847 and 1881 contain
no logger call at all (row-shape checking, a resource_filter f-string, and a docstring respectively). The
file is 6609 lines. Re-grep; never trust a line number in this file.
Everything else matching `{resource` is a URL segment built with _seg() (percent-encoded), a SQL filter
from quote_literal_list, or a RETURNED ERROR DICT rather than a log sink - so those are a different
question and not this one.

THE VALUE IS GENUINELY CALLER-SUPPLIED AND UNCONSTRAINED, so step 2 does not close it either. All four are
plain `str` MCP tool parameters (definitions.py 2076-2080, 2279-2281, 2289-2291, 2325-2330) whose JSON
schemas declare only {"type": "string"} with a prose description. No enum, no Literal, no dict lookup, no
datasets.yaml validation, nothing rejecting CR/LF. _seg() percent-encodes for the URL only and returns a
NEW string; the raw value is what reaches the f-string.

THE SINGLE FACT THAT CLOSES IT, MEASURED: the process formats every record through
src/genetics_mcp_server/logging_config.py's GCPJsonFormatter, whose format() ends
`return json.dumps(log_entry)` with the message as the STRING FIELD "message". json.dumps escapes every
control character, so CR/LF becomes the two-character sequence \r\n INSIDE the string. The record stays
one physical line, a second entry cannot be forged, and severity/logger/timestamp cannot be overwritten.
VERIFIED BY RUNNING THE REAL FORMATTER, not by reading it:
    {"timestamp": "...", "severity": "ERROR", "logger": "x",
     "message": "Error in f(ok\r\nseverity=CRITICAL fake)"}
The injected newline came out escaped and `severity` is still the genuine "ERROR".

AND THE DEPLOYED PROCESS REALLY USES THAT FORMATTER - traced end to end rather than assumed:
k8s/deployments/mcp-server.yaml:20 pins `--transport streamable-http`; mcp_server.py:41-42 calls
setup_logging for the sse/streamable-http branch; setup_logging (logging_config.py:49-55) CLEARS the root
handlers and installs a single StreamHandler(sys.stdout) with GCPJsonFormatter; mcp_server.py:525 passes
`log_config=None` to uvicorn so uvicorn does not reconfigure logging back; executor's module logger
propagates to root. The chat backend is the same - chat_api.py:27-29 calls setup_logging at import,
BEFORE every other package import, which is what makes mcp_proxy.py:26's plain-text basicConfig a no-op
there (it is guarded by `if not logging.getLogger().handlers`).

WHAT AN ATTACKER ACTUALLY GETS: their string, control characters visibly escaped, inside the message field
of one error record, on an exception path that already returns INTERNAL_ERROR_MSG to the caller. That is
log NOISE - unbounded length, mildly confusing to a human reading the rendered message - not injection.
The downstream sink question does not need chasing: the escaping happens before anything downstream sees
it. (For the record, terraform/logging.tf's BigQuery sinks filter on jsonPayload.log_type="endpoint_access"
and container_name="chat-backend", and mcp-server's entries match neither, so they land in Cloud Logging
only - but that is incidental to the verdict.)

THE ONE LATENT CAVEAT, recorded on 4h6.98 rather than filed: mcp_server.py:46-50's STDIO branch installs a
plain-text line-oriented formatter (%(asctime)s - %(name)s - ...) on stderr. The same code WOULD be
injectable under stdio transport. Nothing deployed runs it that way - the manifest pins streamable-http -
so by the filing gate it is a hazard note, not work.

These are the outcome-3 findings: each is real, none blocks the epic's acceptance criteria, and each was
DELIBERATELY LEFT UNFIXED in that cycle so the round stayed on the blocking sweep defect. All are in
sandbox/supervisor.py unless stated.

1. ForkServer.sweep()'s docstring understates the worst-case added response latency. _kill_survivors polls
   up to KILL_GRACE_S (2s) and _fs_sweep up to 2 x KILL_GRACE_S (4s), BOTH inside _execute_inner's finally
   with the execution slot held -> 6s, not the 4s the docstring accounts for. It is attacker-chosen: leave
   one SIGTERM-ignoring in-group process AND one setsid escapee. Separately, on the stranded path the fork
   server may be WEDGED rather than dead, and _sweep_strays then blocks on _round_trip for
   FS_CONTROL_TIMEOUT_S = 30s before the response is built - bounded, and it does free the slot, but it is
   30s of held slot that did not exist before. Checked and SAFE: the extra time sits between the reap and
   job.done.set(), and _fire_limit returns early on job.reaped, so a completed execution cannot be
   relabelled `timeout`.

2. A child whose fork reply never reached the supervisor stays in `pending` for the fork server's LIFETIME
   (deliberate - it is what _fs_kill_pending exists for). Consequence not previously written down: that
   child AND ITS WHOLE SUBTREE are invisible to every subsequent FS_OP_SWEEP, because `pending` is the
   sweep's exclusion set. Pre-existing for the child itself (4h6.55), newly relevant now that the sweep is
   the containment story. Worth one sentence in _fs_sweep's docstring, not a fix.

3. scripts/test-supervisor.py test_survivors, in-group case: the assertion `_proc_state(pid) is None` is
   satisfied by THE SWEEP'S REAP, not by _kill_survivors - SIGTERM leaves a zombie and the zombie is reaped
   by _fs_sweep. So 4h6.66's contribution is not independently asserted; disabling only _kill_survivors
   would still pass. The negative control disables both together so the group as a whole is sound, but the
   docstring's per-bead attribution ("The first is 4h6.66") is stronger than what the test separates.

4. A retained artifact that an attacker REPLACES WITH A LARGER FILE answers 413 ArtifactTooLarge (from
   st_size) rather than 409 ArtifactModified, because the size check precedes the digest check. Nothing is
   served either way, so this is honesty of the status code, not a hole; the doc's status table is accurate
   as written. Reordering would leak nothing but is not free to reason about, so it was left.

5. docs/code-execution-security.md phrasing to PRESERVE, not change: "that window is ... now narrower,
   because the process-group kill and the fork server's sweep both run before _retain and build_manifest"
   was checked against the code and is correct. Recorded so a later pass does not "tighten" it into an
   absolute - that is exactly the failure this cycle had to fix twice.

--- APPENDED 2026-08-20, second batch from the same cycle: RE-VALIDATION of the sweep fix. ---
These are behaviours MEASURED against the fixed code. None blocks; each is written down because the
next person to read _fs_sweep will otherwise re-derive it.

6. THE LAST ROUND'S COLLATERAL IS LEFT AS A ZOMBIE. Re-enumeration reaps collateral killpg victims for
   every round EXCEPT the final one, because reaping a round's victims is what the NEXT round's
   enumeration does. MEASURED with a depth-4 setsid() chain whose deepest level also forks an in-group
   (non-setsid) child, so the collateral only surfaces after round 4:
       after the execution: [('L1',None),('L2',None),('L3',None),('L4',None),('COLLAT','Z')]
       next sweep: swept=[] reaped=[1223622] -> ('COLLAT', None)
   At depth 1 the same shape is fully cleared inside one sweep. Impact is N pids held as zombies for
   exactly ONE execution, N bounded by the pod pid budget, and the "cannot claim the pod is clear" log
   line does fire, so it is observable rather than silent. The docstring sentence that failed to qualify
   this was FIXED in this cycle rather than batched, because it was false as written.

7. A SIGTERM-IGNORING STRAY THAT FORKS A FRESH setsid() DECOY EACH TIME IT IS SIGNALLED IS A FIXPOINT.
   MEASURED: it is never eliminated, and it taxes every subsequent execution ~8.2s.
       hostile execute: status=200 ok in 8.50s
       sweep 0/1/2: 8.2s swept=4 reaped=0   (identical every time)
       follow-up execute: status=200 ok out='ALIVE'
   The ROUND CAP binds here, not the wall-clock budget (4 x ~2.05s = 8.2s < FS_SWEEP_BUDGET_S = 10s).
   This is NOT a defect - the sweep is documented as bounding chain DEPTH per execution, not as a
   guarantee of elimination - but it is the worst case and it was not previously written down. The
   important half is what it does NOT do: the fork server survives and the next execution still works.

8. THE 30s ARITHMETIC, settled by measurement so nobody re-opens it: worst case is FS_SWEEP_BUDGET_S plus
   ONE round (the budget is tested at the END of a round), = 10 + 2*KILL_GRACE_S = ~14s, against
   FS_CONTROL_TIMEOUT_S = 30s. A round cannot exceed 2*KILL_GRACE_S because _fs_kill_set uses one batch
   grace per signal, not one per pid. Worst OBSERVED: 8.5s. It cannot convert a hostile script into a
   fork-server kill, which was the failure mode worth checking - overrunning the control timeout would
   poison the control socket.

9. LATENT, site-comment material at most: _enforce_retained_ceiling takes `sizes` and `mem` under TWO
   SEPARATE lock acquisitions, so the two snapshots can disagree. The only consequence is OVER-eviction
   (denial), never under-accounting, and execution concurrency is 1. Not filed as work per the filing gate.

10. CORRECTION TO A MECHANISM THIS CYCLE INITIALLY GOT WRONG, worth keeping because it is subtle. A
    subprocess.Popen the script never waits on does NOT become a reparented zombie - MEASURED, the fork
    server saw no stray. But the first explanation given (Popen.__del__ runs at interpreter shutdown) is
    ALSO wrong: the execution child exits via os._exit() (supervisor.py ~:1342) and never reaches
    interpreter shutdown or GC finalization at all. The real mechanism is that exec(compiled, {...})
    returns, the throwaway globals dict is released, the last reference to the Popen drops, and CPython
    REFCOUNTING runs __del__ -> _internal_poll -> waitpid(WNOHANG) right there, before os._exit. So the
    new INFO log line fires on raw os.fork() orphans, and on a Popen still held by a reference cycle at
    script end - not on ordinary Popen use.

39. `waitpid(-1)` CANNOT SKIP A PID - it reports which child it took only AFTER taking it. So "the reaper
    skips fs.pid" is not implementable, and the peek-shaped alternative (waitid(P_ALL, WNOWAIT)) wedges on a
    fork-server zombie and stops reaping everything else. THE ONLY WORKABLE SHAPE IS PUBLISH-AFTER-THE-FACT:
    hand every consumed status to whoever still cares, so no later code polls or kills a pid that is gone.
    Worth knowing before anyone redesigns this.
